recipes.name: Air Fryer Chicken Tenders
recipes.description: Panko-coated chicken tenders with a mayonnaise, honey and Dijon dipping sauce.
recipeIngredient: freshly ground black pepper, to taste
cooking spray, as needed for both sides of each batch
freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the chicken: Use chicken tenders, kosher salt, and freshly ground black pepper: pat the chicken dry with paper towels and season both sides. Keep the tenders a similar thickness; if using breast strips instead, cut them to match. Do not rinse raw chicken.

Mix the honey mustard: Whisk together mayonnaise, honey, Dijon mustard, hot sauce (if using), kosher salt, and freshly ground black pepper in a clean bowl before starting the breading, or use clean hands and utensils while the first batch cooks. Cover and refrigerate until serving.

Set the breading station and coat: Set out all-purpose flour, panko breadcrumbs, large eggs, and buttermilk. Put flour in one shallow dish, whisk eggs with buttermilk in a second, and put panko in a third. Coat each tender lightly in flour, shake off excess, dip in the egg mixture and let excess drip off, then press into the panko. Discard leftover flour, egg mixture and crumbs after raw-chicken contact; wash hands and utensils.

Air-fry in spaced batches: Follow the air fryer’s instructions for preheating to 400°F. Arrange chicken in a single layer with gaps; cook only what fits without overlapping. Apply cooking spray to the tops and cook 5 minutes. Flip, spray the second side and cook about 5 minutes more. Probe the thickest part of every tender from the side for 165°F / 74°C; continue cooking as needed. Repeat with remaining chicken. Keep finished pieces on a clean rack without stacking while the next batch cooks, and serve promptly.
Serve: Serve the hot tenders with the honey mustard. Check each batch independently; browned crumbs alone do not establish that the chicken is done.

recipes.name: Almond Zucchini Bread
recipes.description: Gina Matsoukas's almond-flour loaf uses banana and zucchini for a moist crumb. Squeeze excess water from the zucchini before measuring, then let the baked loaf cool completely before slicing; a warm, tender center can tear even when the loaf is baked through.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Grated Zucchini, squeezed of excess water before measuring

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a loaf pan with parchment paper.
The Squeeze: Grate the zucchini. Place in a clean towel and squeeze out excess water, then measure 1 cup of the damp shreds. They should no longer drip, but do not try to dry them out completely.
Dry: In a large bowl, whisk the almond flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
Wet: In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs, maple syrup, mashed banana, and coconut oil.
Mix: Fold the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir in the zucchini shreds.

Bake: Pour into the pan. Bake for 35-40 minutes until the top is browned, the center is set, and a tester has no wet batter. If the center is still wet, continue baking and check again; tent loosely with foil if the top is getting too dark.
Rest: Let cool in the pan on a rack for 5-10 minutes, then lift out carefully using the parchment. Cool fully on the rack before slicing; allow about an hour, longer if still warm.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi (Potato Cauliflower Curry)
recipes.description: Tender potatoes and cauliflower with toasted cumin, coriander and a thick tomato-spice coating. Give the potatoes a head start, then uncover briefly to remove excess moisture.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) yellow-fleshed potatoes, weighed after trimming; peel if desired and cut into 3/4-inch / 2 cm cubes
680 g cauliflower florets, weighed after removing leaves and the tough core; cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm pieces
100 g onion, peeled and finely diced
2 green serrano chiles, slit lengthwise; see the milder option
150 g ripe tomato, finely chopped, with its juices
1 tsp fine salt, for the vegetables
1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for the final seasoning; use only as needed
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, divided between the two vegetable stages
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only if the pan dries before the vegetables soften
1/4 tsp cayenne, optional for extra heat

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything: Wash, trim, weigh and cut the vegetables as listed. One large or two smaller cauliflower heads may be needed; weigh the florets after trimming. Drain the cauliflower well. Lightly crush the coriander seeds so there are no large, hard whole seeds. Measure the spices and divide the cooking water into two equal portions; keep the separate hot-water reserve aside. Finish all cutting and measuring before heating the oil.

Start the whole spices: Heat all the measured oil in the deep pan over medium heat. Add cumin and crushed coriander seeds and stir for about 20–30 seconds, until they sizzle and smell fragrant. Lower the heat if they darken quickly; do not let them burn.

Soften the onion and aromatics: Add the onion and cook for 6–8 minutes, stirring, until soft and beginning to turn pale gold. Add garlic, ginger and the slit serranos and stir for 30–60 seconds, until fragrant. For the milder powdered-chile option, leave the serranos out and add its cayenne in the next step.

Build the tomato coating: Lower the heat to medium-low. Stir in turmeric, ground coriander and the cayenne if using the milder powdered-chile option for about 20 seconds, then promptly add the tomato and its juice. Cook for about 5–7 minutes, stirring, until the tomato softens and the mixture looks thick rather than watery. Do not insist on dry-frying ground spices when they are beginning to catch.

Give the potatoes a head start: Add the potatoes and the initial fine salt, turn to coat for 1–2 minutes, then pour in the first half of the cooking water. Bring the liquid to a gentle simmer, cover tightly and cook over medium-low for about 12–18 minutes, gently turning once or twice. Test a cube: it should be partly cooked, with a tender exterior and some resistance at the center. If still hard all the way through, continue covered, adding 1 tbsp corrective hot water if the pan is dry, before adding cauliflower.

Add cauliflower and finish cooking: Fold in the cauliflower and the remaining half of the cooking water. Let the pan return to a gentle simmer, then cover and cook about 15–20 minutes, gently turning every five minutes. A knife should enter both a potato center and a cauliflower stem easily. If the pan dries before that point, use the corrective water a tablespoon at a time, within its separate listed allowance. Continue beyond the estimate when needed; avoid vigorous stirring that breaks up the florets.

Dry the coating and finish: Uncover and cook over medium heat for about 3–5 minutes, folding gently, until no loose liquid collects underneath. Stir in garam masala and the optional finishing cayenne and cook for 30 seconds. Turn off the heat, add the lemon juice gradually and fold in cilantro. Taste and use the reserved fine salt only as needed. Remove the slit chiles before serving if you do not want a diner to bite into one.

Serve: Divide into four main portions with bread, or six generous vegetable sides alongside dal. If serving with rice, remember that the potatoes already provide a substantial starch component; offer rice in smaller portions.

recipes.name: Anadama Bread
recipes.description: Molasses and a cooked cornmeal porridge give this New England bread its distinctive flavor and texture. Cool the porridge before adding it to the yeast, and let both rises reach their volume cues.
recipeIngredient: Oil, for coating the rising bowl
Butter, for greasing the loaf pan

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the porridge: In a small saucepan, whisk the first listed water portion and cornmeal. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring, and cook for about 5 minutes until thickened. Remove from the heat.
Cool: Stir in the measured porridge butter and molasses. Let the mixture cool until lukewarm before it meets the yeast.
Activate the yeast: In a large bowl, dissolve the active dry yeast in the listed warm water at 110°F. Let stand for about 10 minutes; look for a creamy, foamy surface.

Mix the dough: Stir the cooled cornmeal mixture into the yeast mixture. Mix in two thirds of the measured flour and all the salt, then gradually add the remaining measured flour until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Turn out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for about 8–10 minutes until smooth and elastic, using only enough dusting flour to keep it manageable. The dough should remain slightly tacky.
First rise: Lightly oil a bowl, place the dough inside and turn to coat it. Cover and leave in a warm spot until doubled in volume, about 1 hour.

Shape and heat the oven: Deflate and shape the dough. The original batch makes one loaf in a butter-greased 9 x 5-inch loaf pan. For larger batches, divide into original-size loaves in separate pans. For a smaller or partial loaf, choose a suitable smaller pan with similar dough depth and room to rise, and begin bake checks earlier. Begin preheating the oven to 375°F while the loaves rise.
Second rise: Cover and let the loaf double again, about 45 minutes. Wait until the oven has reached 375°F before loading.

Bake and cool: For original-size loaves, begin checking around 30 minutes. Bake until the crust is deep golden and firm, the sides are baked and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped. Carefully turn the loaves out onto a rack and let them cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Anelletti Al Forno
recipes.description: The ragù, fried eggplant, eggs, ham and two cheeses each have a place in the layers. The source-rich tomato-and-ham route below is distinct from the tomato-paste and pancetta-or-ham variation; its larger tomato and ham supplies are not equivalent yields.
recipeIngredient: 1 medium carrot, peeled and finely chopped
sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 1/2 cans (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes with their juices, coarsely chop tomatoes and reserve all juices
1 medium eggplant, about 12 oz for the original batch, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
vegetable oil, for a 1-inch frying layer in a suitable deep skillet, replenished as needed
2 lb dry anelletti or other small pasta
water and salt, for boiling pasta
6 oz fully cooked deli ham, cut into 1/4-inch cubes
12 oz primosale or provolone, cut into 1/4-inch cubes
1/2 cup finely grated caciocavallo or Pecorino Romano
olive oil or lard, for greasing the baking dishes

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the ragù: Use extra-virgin olive oil, medium carrot, medium celery stalk, medium onion, sea salt and freshly ground black pepper, ground beef, ground pork, dry red wine, ground cinnamon, finely grated nutmeg, whole peeled tomatoes with their juices, and frozen or fresh peas in this sequence. Heat the oil over medium heat in a roomy pot, add the carrot, celery and onion with some seasoning, and cook about 20 minutes until soft without requiring browned edges. Add the beef and pork, season and break up over medium-high heat until browned, about 5–8 minutes. Add all wine and scrape the pot; cook until most free wine evaporates, often about 6 minutes. Add cinnamon, nutmeg and all tomatoes and reserved juices. Bring to a simmer, partially cover and cook on low at a bare simmer about 2 hours until the meat is tender and sauce thickened, stirring as needed. Confirm ground meat reaches at least 160°F before tasting. Stir in all peas, heat through and adjust the listed seasoning.

Drain and fry the eggplant: While the ragù simmers, use medium eggplant, salt, and vegetable oil for the eggplant. Salt and toss the cubes in a colander, place a plate and clean weight over them and drain for 1 hour. Pat away surface moisture before lowering into hot oil. Use a deep skillet and its safe fill/headroom; heat the 1-inch oil layer over medium-high until shimmering, not smoking. Fry uncrowded rounds, turning until deep golden and tender, starting checks around 8–10 minutes per original-size round. Lift onto absorbent paper towels and repeat with all cubes, adding frying oil only as needed.

Cook and dress pasta: Heat the oven to 350°F. Use dry anelletti or other small pasta and water and salt for pasta cooking, stopping at al dente according to the actual package. Drain and return to a roomy pot. For the original batch, stir in 4 cups of the finished ragù and all the fried eggplant; scale that finished-sauce target proportionally with the listed dry pasta. Reserve any extra ragù separately for another use rather than forcing it into the baking dish. The cooked ragù volume is a source planning target, not a measured output guaranteed by the raw ingredient quantities.

Coat the dishes and layer: Use large hard-boiled eggs, fully cooked deli ham, primosale or provolone, finely grated caciocavallo or Pecorino Romano, bread crumbs, and olive oil or lard for the complete layered bake. For the original batch the source uses a greased 9-by-13-inch dish; check actual depth and headroom and use additional or smaller suitable dishes as needed. Coat the greased inside with the full crumb supply, shaking excess into a clean bowl to reserve for the top. Spread half the dressed pasta across the dishes. Distribute all chopped eggs and ham and half of each cheese over it. Cover with the remaining pasta, then all remaining cheese and any reserved crumbs. Divide every component between the dishes; do not overfill or discard layers to force a fit.

Bake and check: Bake at 350°F, beginning checks around 30 minutes for the original-depth warm assembly, until cheese is melted and the bake bubbles. Check several central locations in every dish reach at least 165°F; a melted top alone is not the casserole endpoint. Cold or deeper assemblies can take longer.
Rest and serve: Rest at least 15 minutes before serving. The layers settle, but the degree of clean slicing depends on pasta shape, moisture and dish depth; no firm cake-like slice is guaranteed.

recipes.name: Apple Banana and Carrot Muffins
recipes.description: Finely grated apple and carrot give these banana muffins small pieces of fruit through the crumb. Fold the flour only until moistened and check the center, since fruit size changes both moisture and batter volume.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the muffin cups
water, a little, for simmering the cooked-fruit variation, optional
1 apple, cored and finely grated for the raw-fruit method
1 large carrot, finely grated for the raw-fruit method
3 tbsp unsalted butter, melted and cooled to lukewarm

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the oven and tin: Preheat the oven to 350°F and set out butter or neutral oil and water (if using) for preparation. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with the pan fat; use the water only for the cooked-fruit variation below. Melt the batter butter and let it cool to lukewarm. For the cooked-fruit variation below, prepare the apple and carrot before making the wet mixture.
Prepare the grated fruit: Use the apple and large carrot, grating with the fine holes of a box grater. Squeeze off excess free juice; keep the shreds damp rather than trying to dry them completely.
Combine the wet ingredients: Whisk the large banana, large eggs, unsalted butter, and vanilla extract in a large bowl until evenly combined, then stir in the prepared apple and carrot.
Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the all-purpose flour, baking powder, ground cinnamon, and salt in a separate bowl so the baking powder and seasonings are distributed.

Fold and portion: Gently fold the dry mixture into the wet just until no dry flour pockets remain. The original batch makes about 12 standard muffins; for different quantities, use more or fewer standard cups at approximately the same portion size, rather than spreading every batch across twelve cups. Fruit size affects the batter volume; use extra prepared cups if necessary rather than filling to the rim.

Bake and cool: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, starting the center check at 20 minutes. The tops should be set and a tester through the central crumb should have no wet batter; continue baking if needed. Let the muffins stand briefly until firm enough to lift out, then transfer carefully to a rack. Cool before serving and cool completely before packing.

recipes.name: Apple Chai Oatmeal Cups
recipes.description: Rolled oats stay visible in these moist apple-and-banana cups. Whisk the spices into the melted coconut oil to distribute them, then combine with the wet ingredients and oats.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups Almond Milk or Whole Milk
Nonstick spray or a little oil for the muffin liners

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use a standard muffin tin, lining and lightly greasing enough wells for the listed planning cup count with the separate spray or oil allowance; the original batch plans twelve. Wash the apple, peel it and mince it finely; mash the banana.

Mix the spices and oats: Whisk all the cinnamon, cardamom, ginger, nutmeg and allspice into the warm melted coconut oil and let stand for 2 minutes while mixing the oats and baking powder in a large bowl. The measured coconut oil all belongs in the batter.

Combine the wet ingredients: Whisk the banana, eggs, milk and maple syrup until combined. Stir in all the spiced oil, then pour over the oats. Fold in all the minced apple until the oats are evenly moistened; this mixture keeps whole oat pieces.

Portion: Divide the mixture evenly across the listed planning number of prepared wells, redistributing fruit and liquid as needed. The original batch plans twelve cups. Leave room for the mixture to rise; if the actual wells cannot hold it, use additional prepared wells or another batch rather than discard batter.

Bake: Load only once the oven has reached 350°F. Bake for about 19–21 minutes, until the tops are firm and the centers are set without liquid egg mixture. Check the middle of a cup, rather than only its browned surface; an egg-dish center should reach 160°F. Tin size and extra batches can change the time.

Cool and store: Let the cups stand in the tin for 10 minutes before lifting them onto a rack. Serve warm or cool them further for cold service. Refrigerate promptly in a covered container once manageable.

recipes.name: Apple Cider Cream Pie
recipes.description: Reduce the cider to one-quarter of its starting volume, then cool it before whisking in the sour cream and eggs. The pastry has two stages at 425°F before the custard bake at 350°F.
recipeIngredient: 1 stick unsalted butter, chilled and diced

recipeInstructions.text: Make and chill dough: Pulse all-purpose flour, cornstarch, granulated sugar, kosher salt, unsalted butter, cold milk, and apple cider vinegar as follows: combine flour, cornstarch, crust sugar and crust salt, then pulse in all the cold butter until coarse meal with visible butter pieces remains. Mix all milk and vinegar, drizzle over the flour and pulse briefly until the dough holds together when pressed. Gather into a disk, wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Shape and blind-bake: Use all-purpose flour lightly on the work surface. For the original batch, roll an 11-inch circle and fit a 9-inch oven-safe pie plate, folding under the overhang and crimping. Chill until firm, about 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F. Line with oven-rated parchment and pie weights; bake in the lower third about 15 minutes until barely set. Carefully remove weights and parchment, shield the edge with foil and bake about 15 minutes more at 425°F until set but not browned. Gently deflate any puffed base and let the shell cool. Reduce the oven to 350°F.

Reduce and cool cider: Boil apple cider in a saucepan until one-quarter of its starting volume remains: 1/2 cup for the original 2-cup batch, scaled proportionally. Measure the reduction rather than relying on a roughly 10–12-minute estimate; pan width and batch size alter evaporation. Transfer to a bowl and cool completely before adding eggs.

Mix custard: Whisk granulated sugar, sour cream, salt, and large eggs into all the cooled cider reduction: start with sugar, sour cream and salt, then whisk in all the eggs until smooth. Keep raw-egg tools separate from the clean topping utensils.

Bake custard: Pour all the custard into the cooled shell, keeping the foil edge shield in place. Bake in the lower third at 350°F, starting checks around 35–40 minutes for the original pie. The edges should be set while the center moves slightly as one area, not sloshes. Probe the central custard for at least 160°F / 71°C and continue gently if needed. Shield browned pastry rather than stopping with an undercooked center.

Cool and chill: Cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate within 2 hours after baking, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Continue chilling until completely cold and set through the center; do not wait for several hours on the counter. Cooling and refrigerator performance determine the actual elapsed time.

Whip and finish: Beat heavy cream, granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon with clean tools until firm peaks form. Spread all the cream over the fully cold pie shortly before serving, then keep it refrigerated until needed.

recipes.name: Apple Pie
recipes.description: Cook the apples until they start to soften, catch every drop of their juice and reduce it to a syrup before returning it to the fruit. Cool the filling before enclosing it in cold pastry.
recipeIngredient: 14 tbsp unsalted butter, ice cold and cubed
3 lb baking apples, Granny Smith or Mutsu, washed before peeling, cored and sliced
1 egg, beaten for brushing; unused wash may remain
granulated sugar, for sprinkling the top

recipeInstructions.text: Make dough: Pulse all-purpose flour, unsalted butter, granulated sugar, kosher salt, ice-cold vodka, and ice-cold water in this order: flour, dough sugar, salt and butter until coarse meal and pea-size butter pieces remain; then add all vodka and measured water and pulse briefly until the dough holds when pressed. Gather by hand without kneading smooth. Wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. If the mixture cannot hold together with the listed liquid, stop and check the measurements rather than replacing vodka with an assumed equal egg mixture.

Cook apples: Use baking apples, granulated sugar, butter, and lemon juice as follows: toss all peeled, cored slices with lemon juice and filling sugar. Melt all filling butter in a large skillet over medium heat, add the apples and cook, stirring, starting checks around 7 minutes until they release juice and begin to soften. Continue as needed for the actual apple variety and slice thickness. Use suitable extra skillet rounds when scaling, retaining all fruit, butter and juice.

Reduce juices and cool: Strain apples in a colander over a clean bowl, catching all the juice. Return that juice to the skillet and simmer, beginning checks around 5–8 minutes, until thick and syrupy; stop before it scorches. Toss all the reduction and ground cinnamon and ground nutmeg back with the apples. Let the filling cool completely before assembly.

Roll and fill: Use all-purpose flour lightly on the work surface. Divide dough into equal halves for bottom and top. For the original batch, roll each half to roughly 11–12 inches and fit the bottom into a 9-inch pie plate, leaving enough overhang to seal. Add all cooled apples and syrup, mounding slightly if needed without forcing an overfull pan. Cover with the second round and seal/crimp the edges. Cut four steam vents; keep the dough cold, returning it to the refrigerator if it softens.

Wash and sprinkle: Use egg and granulated sugar to brush a thin coat over the sealed crust and sprinkle the separate topping sugar. Do not take sugar from the filling or dough. Discard unused raw egg wash and clean its tools before handling the baked pie.

Bake: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the lower third. Place the pie on a rimmed baking sheet to catch spills. Begin checking around 50 minutes for the original-size pie, continuing until the crust is well baked and golden and filling juices bubble through the vents. Cover a browning edge with foil if needed; a fixed 50-minute clock does not establish a finished crust in every oven.
Cool: Cool on a rack for at least 2 hours before slicing so the hot filling settles. Keep the cooked-apple juices in the pie; a short rest produces looser slices.

recipes.name: Arugula & Feta Salad with Strawberry Vinaigrette
recipes.description: Peppery arugula, sliced strawberries, feta and toasted sunflower seeds with a fresh strawberry, honey and rice-vinegar dressing.
recipeIngredient: 5 oz baby arugula, washed if needed and dried thoroughly
1 pint fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced, for the salad
4 large fresh strawberries, hulled, additional to the salad berries, for dressing
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare produce: Wash and dry arugula if needed. Wash berries, dry them and remove their hulls. Slice the listed salad berries and keep the additional dressing berries separate. Crumble feta and measure toasted seeds.

Blend dressing: Blend the dressing berries, olive oil, vinegar, honey and garlic until smooth. Taste with an arugula leaf and a small piece of feta, then season with salt and pepper as needed. If the blender cannot catch the small amount, use a narrower vessel or small food processor rather than adding water just to raise the level.

Dress lightly: Put arugula in a wide bowl and toss gently with about half the dressing. Add sliced berries and most of the feta, lifting carefully to avoid crushing fruit. Add more dressing only if the leaves need it; reserve any excess instead of automatically pouring it all over the salad.
Finish and serve: Scatter over the remaining feta and sunflower seeds. Divide into the intended side portions and serve immediately while leaves and seeds retain their texture.

recipes.name: Hoisin-Glazed Meatballs
recipes.description: Tender ginger-scallion meatballs with a thin, glossy sweet-tangy glaze. Includes separate temperature endpoints for beef and turkey.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) ground beef (80–85% lean) or ground turkey (93% lean)
2 scallions, finely sliced, whites and greens separated
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, plus more as needed
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the binder: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Line a rimmed sheet pan. Soak panko in milk for 5 minutes, then stir in the egg, half the garlic, half the ginger, soy sauce, scallion whites, and pepper.

Shape gently: Add the meat and mix just until evenly combined. Divide into 24 portions, about 35 g each including the binder, and roll gently. Arrange with gaps on the sheet pan. Wash hands and clean surfaces after handling raw meat.

Bake and check: Bake about 15–20 minutes. Check several of the largest meatballs through the center: beef must reach 160°F / 71°C; turkey must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking if needed; color alone is not the endpoint.

Reduce the glaze: Meanwhile, combine hoisin, plum sauce, vinegar, water, remaining garlic, and remaining ginger in a wide skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 4–6 minutes, stirring, until it lightly coats a spoon. Add water if it becomes pasty.

Coat and serve: Add the fully cooked meatballs and sesame oil. Toss over low heat for 1–2 minutes to coat. Taste the sauce and add a little water if too concentrated. Finish with scallion greens and optional sesame seeds; serve with plain rice and vegetables.

recipes.name: Napa Slaw with Edamame and Crispy Wontons
recipes.description: Napa cabbage and carrots with edamame, toasted sesame dressing and optional crisp wonton strips. Add the strips at the table to keep them crisp.
recipeIngredient: 6 cups napa cabbage, cored and thinly shredded
1 cup cooked shelled edamame, cooled and well drained
6 wonton wrappers, cut into thin strips
Neutral oil, enough for 1/2-inch depth in the frying pan
1 pinch salt, for the wonton strips

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the edamame: Use ready-to-eat cooked shelled edamame, or cook packaged shelled edamame according to its instructions first. Cool promptly under cool running water, drain thoroughly and measure the cooked beans. Keep refrigerated if preparing ahead.
Cut the vegetables: Core and thinly shred the napa, then measure it. Julienne the carrots and slice green onions. Combine in a large bowl with the cooled edamame.

Fry the optional strips: Cut the wonton wrappers into thin strips. Heat neutral oil to a depth of 1/2 inch in a dry, deep-sided pan with ample space above the oil. Bring to 350°F / 175°C. Fry a small batch, stirring gently to separate, until pale golden; start checking within seconds. Lift out with a slotted spoon, drain in a single layer and sprinkle with the pinch of salt. Repeat, allowing the oil to recover between batches. Let strips cool before topping the slaw.
Mix the dressing: Whisk or shake toasted sesame oil, vinegar, soy sauce, honey or agave, ginger, garlic and optional chile flakes until combined.

Dress and serve: Toss the vegetables and edamame with the dressing and toasted sesame seeds, lifting from the bottom to coat evenly. Taste a forkful before adjusting seasoning. Divide into four generous side portions and add the wonton strips just before eating.

recipes.name: Cabbage Slaw with Peanuts and Sesame
recipes.description: Green and red cabbage, carrots and scallions with ginger-soy dressing, roasted peanuts and toasted sesame.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp soy sauce or gluten-free tamari
1/2 tsp sriracha or chile-garlic sauce, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the vegetables: Thinly shred and measure both cabbages. Cut carrots into thin matchsticks and slice scallions. Put them in a large bowl; prepare the cilantro and peanuts separately.
Mix the dressing: Whisk or shake the vinegar, soy sauce or tamari, both oils, honey or maple syrup, ginger, garlic and optional chile sauce until combined. Stir again just before pouring.
Dress: Pour over the cabbage, carrots and scallions. Lift and turn from the bottom until evenly coated. Taste a complete forkful before adjusting any seasoning.

Finish: Fold in cilantro, peanuts and toasted sesame seeds just before serving. Divide into six side portions. If holding briefly, cover and refrigerate the dressed vegetables, adding the toppings at service; lift portions out of any pooled liquid.

recipes.name: Authentic Roman Alfredo (Fettuccine al Burro)
recipes.description: Fettuccine in a glossy butter and Parmigiano sauce. Learn how water, movement, and gentle heat keep it smooth.
recipeIngredient: 3 oz (85 g) Parmigiano-Reggiano, finely grated from a block
2 quarts (2 liters) water, for cooking pasta
1 tsp fine salt, for the cooking water
1 cup (240 ml) reserved pasta water, added as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the pasta: Bring the water and salt to a boil. Add fettuccine and stir so it does not stick. Begin tasting 2 minutes before the package time; stop when it is flexible with a slightly firm center. Reserve 1 cup cooking water before transferring the pasta.
Start the sauce: While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a wide skillet over low heat. Add 1/3 cup reserved hot pasta water and swirl until cloudy. Do not brown the butter.
Finish the pasta: Transfer pasta with tongs into the skillet. Toss over medium-low heat for about 1 minute, until the pasta reaches the texture you like. Add a splash of water if the pan looks dry.

Add cheese gently: Move the skillet off the burner. Wait until active bubbling stops, then add cheese in three small batches, tossing thoroughly after each. Add reserved water a tablespoon at a time until the sauce flows and coats every strand. If the cheese is not melting, use a few seconds of low heat while tossing, then remove again.

Taste and serve: Taste before adding salt; the cheese and cooking water already season the sauce. Add pepper if desired. Serve immediately in warm bowls, leaving the sauce slightly looser than you want on the plate.

recipes.keywords: Italian, rich, umami, savory, date-night, weeknight, boil, simmer

recipes.name: Avgolemono
recipes.description: Egg and lemon give this chicken soup its creamy body without dairy. Whisking hot broth gradually into the egg mixture warms it before it returns to the pot.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb cooked shredded chicken (rotisserie or properly refrigerated leftover)
1/2 cup dry long-grain rice or dry orzo
Salt and white pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the grain: Bring the measured chicken broth to a boil in a pot with room for the chicken and egg mixture. Add the chosen dry rice or orzo and reduce to a simmer. Use about 15 minutes as a first check for the rice, but follow the grain’s package timing and taste for a tender center; orzo may finish sooner.
Heat the chicken: Stir in the cooked shredded chicken. Heat while stirring until the chicken and soup reach 165°F / 74°C. Keep raw chicken out of this recipe’s cooked-chicken step.

Whisk the eggs: While the grain cooks, whisk the eggs until foamy, about 2 minutes as a starting guide, then slowly whisk in all the lemon juice. Keep utensils and surfaces that touched raw egg clean.

Temper: Reduce the pot to low heat. While whisking the egg-lemon mixture constantly, gradually ladle in about one-third of the measured broth from the soup, one ladle at a time: about 2 cups in the original 6-cup broth batch. This is a transfer from the pot, not additional broth. Use a bowl large enough for the expanded mixture.

Combine and heat: Pour the tempered mixture back into the soup slowly while stirring. Continue stirring over low heat until the soup reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout, checking after stirring and away from the pot bottom. Take it off the heat once the endpoint is reached. Aim for a creamy, opaque broth without a vigorous boil; a fixed 2-minute clock or opacity alone does not establish doneness.
Finish: Taste and season with the listed salt and white pepper. Serve promptly. Further high heat can make the egg texture grainy.

recipes.keywords: Greek, acidic, rich, comfort-food, weeknight, light-and-fresh, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Avocado Kale Caesar Salad
recipes.description: Shredded kale with a creamy avocado, lemon and miso dressing, diced avocado, Parmesan and toasted pepitas.
recipeIngredient: 5–6 cups lacinato kale leaves, tough stems removed, finely shredded
1 large ripe avocado, flesh divided equally between dressing and topping
1 tsp white miso paste or soy sauce
1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided and added to taste
2–3 tbsp water, plus more only as needed to thin the dressing
1 tsp olive oil, for softening kale
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the optional breadcrumb topping

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare greens and optional crumbs: Wash, dry and shred kale. If making the topping, melt its butter in a small skillet over medium-low. Add panko and stir about 3–5 minutes until golden. Transfer to a plate to cool; do not leave crumbs in the hot skillet.

Soften kale: Put prepared kale in a wide bowl. Add the measured olive oil and a small pinch taken from the measured salt allowance. Rub and turn gently with clean hands for about 1–2 minutes until leaves become darker and more flexible. Stop before they turn wet or mushy.

Blend dressing: Blend half the avocado with the initial water allowance, optional mayonnaise, garlic, lemon juice, Dijon, miso or soy and black pepper. Add further water only as needed for a smooth spoonable dressing. Taste with a piece of kale and some Parmesan before adding more of the remaining salt.

Dress and rest: Toss kale with about half the dressing, adding more only as needed to coat without leaving a pool. Fold in half the Parmesan and let stand about 5 minutes while dicing the remaining avocado. Reserve unused dressing.
Finish: Gently fold in diced avocado. Scatter with pepitas, remaining Parmesan and optional cooled breadcrumbs. Divide into side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, rich, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, snack, entertaining, blend, saute

citation.name: Adapted from Pinch of Yum, Avocado Kale Caesar Salad

recipes.name: Avocado Toast
recipes.description: Ripe avocado should yield gently under pressure. Mash it roughly with the full listed citrus juice, then spread it on sturdy, deeply golden toast.
recipeIngredient: 2 slices Thick-Cut Sourdough or Rustic Bread
1 tbsp Fresh Lemon or Lime Juice
Optional Toppings: everything bagel seasoning, soft-boiled egg, cherry tomatoes, radish slices, microgreens, pickled red onions

recipeInstructions.text: Toast: Toast all the listed bread slices until deeply golden with crisp edges and a sturdy surface, using the toaster’s suitable setting. Extra slices may need additional rounds.

Mash: Wash and dry the avocado before cutting. Halve it, remove the pit and scoop all flesh into a bowl. Add all the listed lemon or lime juice and some of the unmeasured flaky salt; mash with a fork, leaving some pieces.
Assemble: Divide all the avocado mixture among the listed bread slices.
Season: Drizzle the listed unmeasured olive oil over the toasts. Add flaky salt and red-pepper flakes to taste.

Choose toppings: Add any desired listed toppings, preparing them separately: washed cherry tomatoes, radishes or microgreens, prepared pickled onions, everything-bagel seasoning, or an already-cooked egg. For ordinary shell eggs, cook whites and yolks until firm; if choosing the soft-yolk variation, use shell eggs treated by pasteurization or another approved Salmonella-control method. Cut cooked egg into portions for the toasts. Egg cooking time is separate from the toast clock.
Serve: Serve promptly. The bread softens under the avocado and toppings; the avocado darkens with air exposure.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, acidic, rich, weeknight, light-and-fresh, quick-lunch, toast

recipes.name: Baby’s First Smash Cake
recipes.description: The banana cake and cream cheese frosting have separate vanilla amounts. Thawed apple juice concentrate goes into the frosting without added water; diluted juice makes a looser topping.
recipeIngredient: 3/4 cup oat flour, grind rolled oats then measure
Oil as needed, for greasing pans
1/2 cup apple juice concentrate, thawed and undiluted

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 375°F. For the original batch, lightly oil four mini tart pans plus 6–8 standard muffin cups, or two 8- or 9-inch round pans. These are alternative full-batch pan plans; four mini pans alone do not account for all the batter. Keep comparable shallow batter depth, leave rising room and use additional cups if needed.

Mash all the bananas. Whisk the whole wheat flour, measured oat flour, baking soda and cinnamon in a separate bowl. Mix all the applesauce, melted coconut oil and batter vanilla with the mashed bananas, then fold into the dry ingredients just until combined.

Divide all the batter among the prepared pans. Bake at 375°F, starting checks around 15–20 minutes for the original shallow cakes; centers should be set and a tester should come out without wet batter. Pan size and banana size change the clock; muffins or different pans may finish at different times. Cool completely before frosting. If using large rounds, cut smaller cake circles with an overturned bowl once cool; keep the offcuts for serving.

With clean tools, whisk all the softened cream cheese, thawed undiluted apple juice concentrate and frosting vanilla until creamy. Refrigerate while the cakes cool. If too loose to spread, chill 1–2 hours, then whisk again; the consistency of the concentrate and cream cheese matters.

Stack the completely cooled mini rounds with some frosting between them and spread the remaining frosting over the outside and any muffins you want to frost. Keep refrigerated until serving to the birthday guest.

recipes.recipeYield: Original batch: four mini cakes plus six to eight muffins
recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, bake, no-cook, blend

recipes.name: Baked Chicken and Broccoli
recipes.description: Lisa Gwock’s casserole combines split chicken breasts, broccoli and a mushroom-soup cheese sauce. Drain the broccoli well so its water does not thin the sauce.
recipeIngredient: 1 (10 3/4 oz) can cream of mushroom soup, undiluted

recipeInstructions.text: Continue: Place chicken in a 9-inch square pan and drizzle with butter. Bake at 375 degrees for 40 minutes.
Continue: While chicken is cooking, cook broccoli according to package directions; drain. Arrange around chicken.
Continue: Combine soup, milk and cheese; pour over chicken and broccoli. Sprinkle with bread crumbs and paprika.
Cook: Bake an additional 20 minutes. Check the thickest part of each chicken breast, away from bone, for 165°F / 74°C; continue baking if needed.

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Baked Chicken Parmesan
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets with toasted crumbs, melted mozzarella, and tomato sauce. Learn how to protect crisp edges while cooking the center properly.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 4–6 cutlets about 1/2 inch thick
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
6 oz (170 g) low-moisture mozzarella, thinly sliced
8 oz (225 g) dried spaghetti or rigatoni
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, for 3 quarts pasta water

recipeInstructions.text: Set up: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Put a rack over a rimmed sheet pan and grease with 1 tsp oil. Bring 3 quarts water and the pasta-water salt to a boil. Even the chicken to 1/2 inch thick and pat dry.

Toast the crumbs: Heat the remaining oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add panko and stir for 3–5 minutes until light golden. Spread in a shallow dish, cool briefly, then mix in Parmesan. Put beaten eggs in another shallow dish.

Bread: Season chicken with its measured salt and pepper. Dip each cutlet in egg, let excess drip off, then press into crumbs on both sides. Arrange on the rack without touching. Discard egg and crumbs that contacted raw chicken; clean hands and work surfaces.

Start baking and cook the pasta: Put the chicken tray in the oven and set a timer for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, add pasta to the boiling water. Stir and cook until just tender according to the package, then reserve 1/2 cup cooking water and drain. Warm marinara in a small pan or microwave-safe bowl.
Check the chicken: After 15 minutes in the oven, check the thickest pieces from the side with a thermometer. Continue baking until each reaches 165°F / 74°C, usually about 15–20 minutes total.

Melt the topping: Divide one third of the measured marinara over the centers of the cutlets, leaving edges exposed. Divide mozzarella over the sauced centers. Return to the oven for 3–5 minutes until melted; avoid prolonged baking once the cheese melts.

Serve: Toss pasta with the remaining marinara, adding reserved water a tablespoon at a time if needed. Divide pasta and chicken among four plates, finish with basil, and serve promptly with a green salad.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, acidic, umami, herbaceous, comfort-food, weeknight, kid-friendly, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Cod with Lemon Panko
recipes.description: Cod baked in lemon-garlic butter beneath a parsley-flecked panko crust. Keep the sauce around the fish so the topping stays crisp.
recipeIngredient: 4 skinless cod fillets of similar thickness, thawed if frozen and patted dry
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted, divided equally between the sauce and crumbs
2 cloves garlic, minced, divided equally between the sauce and crumbs
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Pat the thawed fish dry, check for pin bones and arrange the portions in a shallow baking dish to check the fit. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Melt the butter.
Make the base: Mix half the butter, all the lemon juice and half the garlic, with salt and pepper to taste. Pour into the dish and set the fish on top in one layer. Season the tops lightly.
Add the crumbs: Mix panko with the remaining butter and garlic, lemon zest, paprika and parsley. Distribute over the fillets and press gently into an even layer without packing it into a thick mound.

Bake and check: Bake on the center rack, beginning to check at 10–12 minutes; many portions take 12–20 minutes, depending on thickness. Insert a thermometer from the side into the thickest center of each portion: aim for 145°F / 63°C. The flesh should separate into opaque flakes. Remove thinner pieces as they finish. If the topping darkens too soon, shield it loosely with foil; do not keep fully cooked fish baking solely to darken pale crumbs.
Serve: Lift each fillet carefully onto a plate and spoon the lemon butter around or beneath it. Serve promptly with a vegetable and, if wanted, a separately prepared potato or rice side.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, acidic, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, light-and-fresh, bake

recipes.name: Baked Creamy Macaroni and Pimento Cheese
recipes.description: The roux thickens the milk before the cheddar goes in. Whisk out flour lumps while adding the milk gradually, then fold in the hot pasta and bake without chilling.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Sharp Cheddar Cheese, freshly shredded
Butter or oil, as needed to lightly grease the baking dish
Water, as needed to boil pasta
Water, a little as needed when reheating leftovers

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 13-by-9-inch baking dish with the listed pan-greasing allowance. Bring pasta water to a boil and cook the macaroni according to its package until al dente; drain. While the pasta cooks, begin the sauce.
In a large skillet with room to fold in all the cooked pasta, melt the measured butter over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking, about 1 minute; do not brown the roux.

Gradually whisk in the milk, salt, cayenne and garlic powder. Cook, whisking constantly, about 3–5 minutes, until smooth and thick enough to coat a spoon; continue as needed rather than stopping with a thin, floury sauce.
Reduce the heat and stir in all the cheddar and drained pimentos until the cheese melts and the sauce is smooth. Remove from the heat and fold in the drained pasta.
Transfer the hot mixture to the greased dish; do not chill it before this bake. Mix the full panko and Parmesan amounts and spread evenly over the pasta.

Bake about 15–20 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F /74°C, the pasta mixture is hot and bubbling and the topping is golden. If the topping darkens before the center is hot, shield it loosely with foil and continue checking. Serve hot.

recipes.keywords: Southern, spicy, umami, rich, comfort-food, bake, roast

recipes.name: Bakery Style Chocolate Chip Muffins
recipes.description: These chocolate-chip muffins start in a hot oven before finishing at a lower temperature. Have the oven and pan ready before mixing, use lukewarm melted butter, and fold only until the flour is moistened; the tops should rise while the centers finish without drying out.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the muffin cups and rims
1/2 cup unsalted butter, melted and cooled to lukewarm
granulated sugar or additional chocolate chips, for sprinkling, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the oven and pan: Heat the oven to 425°F before mixing the batter. The original batch uses a standard 12-cup muffin pan. For a different quantity, prepare more or fewer standard cups, greasing the cups and rims with butter or neutral oil, or line the cups and grease the rims. Keep the same standard cup size and very-full portion depth. Melt the batter butter and let it cool to lukewarm before mixing; additional pans or oven batches add time.

Mix the dry ingredients and chips: Whisk together the batter’s all-purpose flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and semisweet chocolate chips, adding the chocolate chips after the flour and leaveners are evenly mixed.
Mix the wet ingredients: In another bowl whisk the batter’s unsalted butter, granulated sugar, buttermilk, large eggs, and vanilla extract until evenly combined.

Fold the batter: Add the wet mixture to the dry mixture and gently fold until all the flour is moistened. Scrape the bottom so no dry pockets remain; small lumps are fine. Portion promptly rather than waiting for the oven to heat.

Fill the cups: Divide the batter among the standard muffin cups needed for the listed yield, keeping them very full. The original batch uses about 12 standard cups; a different quantity needs more or fewer cups, rather than the same twelve. Sprinkle with granulated sugar or additional chocolate chips (if using). Do not put a full original batch into smaller cups; additional pans or oven batches add time.
Start hot: Bake at 425°F for 5 minutes.

Lower the heat: Without opening the oven door, lower the temperature to 375°F. Continue baking for 12–15 minutes, until the tops are set and a tester through the crumb has no wet batter; avoid a melted chocolate chip when judging the tester. Check rather than extending the bake simply for darker tops.
Cool and release: Let the muffins cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Loosen the tops carefully, remove to a rack and serve warm or let cool completely before storing.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, kid-friendly, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Balsamic Peach Pork Chops
recipes.description: Keep the full balsamic–honey sauce, feta and basil with these peach-topped pork chops. Give the chops a gentle stove finish before the brief broiler stage instead of trying to finish a cold center while a thick glaze scorches.
recipeIngredient: 4 Bone-in pork chops, about 1 inch thick; keep thickness similar when scaling
Black pepper, to taste for chops
2 Fresh peaches, washed, pitted and sliced
Crushed red pepper flakes, to taste at serving

recipeInstructions.text: Heat broiler and mix sauce: Preheat the broiler to high using the oven’s instructions. Whisk Balsamic vinegar, Honey, and Fresh thyme leaves in a small clean bowl and keep separate from raw-pork utensils.

Sear and gently finish chops: Have Bone-in pork chops, Extra-virgin olive oil, Salt, and Black pepper ready. Season the chops with the listed salt and pepper allowances. Heat the measured oil in a broiler-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the chops about 3–4 minutes per side until golden, using more pan space or batches if crowded. Reduce to medium and continue gently cooking, beginning checks during the next 8–10 minutes. Check each thickest center away from the bone; allow longer as needed rather than adding a thick sweet glaze while the centers still require a long cook.

Add sauce and peaches: When the chops are close to their 145°F endpoint and need only a short finish, pour the prepared sauce over them and simmer gently about 2 minutes, watching its consistency. Remove the pan from the burner and arrange Fresh peaches over and around the chops.

Keep sauce from reducing too far: Keep Water (if using) ready as an optional whole-batch amount. Add only if the sauce is becoming too thick to remain saucy. If using multiple pans, divide the selected whole amount rather than adding it anew to each pan. Watch again during broiling; reduce exposure or remove the pan promptly if the glaze is blackening.

Broil and verify centers: Transfer the broiler-safe pan under the broiler and begin checking after a couple of minutes, using approximately 4–5 minutes only as a check window. Peaches should be lightly charred at the edges and every chop must reach at least 145°F /63°C in its thickest center, away from bone, before removal. If a chop is ready before the fruit, move it with clean utensils to a clean resting plate and finish the fruit separately; if fruit is ready before a chop, move the whole pan to gentle stove heat and finish the chop with the fruit and sauce still in the pan, watching the sauce instead of continuing to burn the glaze.

Add feta and rest: Top with Feta cheese, Fresh basil, and Crushed red pepper flakes. Rest every ready chop for 5 minutes after reaching 145°F, at least the minimum 3 minutes, then serve with peaches and all the pan sauce.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, spicy, sweet, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Banana Egg Oat Pancakes
recipes.description: Mash the ripe banana well, then whisk in the eggs and rolled oats. These small pancakes are delicate: let the first side set before moving them and use medium-low heat so the banana browns while the egg cooks through.
recipeIngredient: 1 large ripe Banana (the spottier the better)
1 tbsp Almond Butter or Peanut Butter
Butter or Coconut Oil for searing
Fresh fruit and maple syrup for serving (optional)
Chocolate chips for an optional add-in

recipeInstructions.text: Mash: In a medium bowl, mash the banana with a fork until mostly smooth.
Mix: Whisk in the eggs, rolled oats, nut butter, cinnamon, and salt until evenly combined. Small oat flakes may remain; this batter is mixed by hand rather than blended.
Heat: Heat a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add enough of the separate butter or coconut oil allowance to lightly coat the surface.

Cook the first side: Spoon small, roughly 3-inch circles into the pan, leaving room to flip. Add a few chocolate chips to the wet surface if using. Leave the pancakes undisturbed until the edges are set and the underside is golden, about 2–3 minutes. If the bottom darkens while the top is still loose, lower the heat; do not wait for bubbles as the only signal.

Flip and finish: Slide a thin spatula fully underneath each pancake and flip gently. Cook for about 30–60 seconds more, then continue as needed until the center is set with no liquid egg batter. A thin thermometer inserted from the side should read 160°F. Repeat with the remaining batter, refreshing the light coating of butter or coconut oil as needed.
Serve: Serve hot with fresh fruit and maple syrup if desired.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, quick-lunch, snack, weeknight, griddle

recipes.name: Banana Nut Bread
recipes.description: The Hamilton family banana bread creams softened butter with sugar before the eggs and banana go in. Very ripe bananas give the loaf its flavor; brief mixing after flour enters keeps the crumb tender.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pan
all-purpose flour, for dusting the greased pan
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, softened, not melted
3 (375 g) large very ripe bananas, peeled and mashed; gram equivalent is an approximate total
1/2 cup walnuts or toasted sunflower seeds, chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the oven and pan: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or neutral oil and all-purpose flour to grease and flour a 9-by-5-by-3-inch loaf pan for the original batch. Have the batter butter softened, not melted, before beginning.
Cream the butter and sugar: Beat the unsalted butter and granulated sugar until lighter and fluffy, scraping the sides and bottom so no dense butter remains.
Add the eggs: Beat in the large eggs one at a time, scraping the bowl after each addition.
Add banana and vanilla: Mix in the large very ripe bananas and vanilla extract. The mixture may look slightly curdled; stop once evenly combined rather than beating to make it perfectly smooth.
Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the all-purpose flour, baking soda, and kosher salt thoroughly in a separate bowl.
Fold the batter: Gently fold the dry mixture into the butter mixture until no dry flour pockets remain. Do not beat the flour mixture until perfectly smooth.
Add the nuts or seeds: Fold in the walnuts or toasted sunflower seeds just until distributed, then scrape the batter into the prepared pan.

Bake and cool: Bake for about 55–60 minutes, checking the center at 55 minutes. A tester should have moist crumbs but no wet batter; check another spot if it hits banana. If still wet, continue baking; tent loosely with foil if the top is darkening too quickly. Cool in the pan on a rack for 10 minutes, loosen the edges and turn out carefully. Cool completely on the rack before slicing; allow about an hour, longer if still warm.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Banana Oat Greek Yogurt Muffins
recipes.description: These banana muffins blend rolled oats with Greek yogurt and eggs, then fold in chocolate chips by hand. The oat batter makes a moist, somewhat dense crumb.
recipeIngredient: cooking spray, for greasing the muffin cups or paper liners
2 large ripe bananas, peeled and mashed
additional chocolate chips, for sprinkling over the tops, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat and prepare the pan: Preheat the oven to 400°F before blending. For the original batch, prepare a standard 12-cup muffin pan with cooking spray. For different quantities, prepare more or fewer standard cups, keeping the same three-quarter fill; additional tins or oven batches may be needed. If using paper liners, spray the liners too so this batter releases more easily.

Blend the oat batter: Put the plain full-fat Greek yogurt, large ripe bananas, rolled oats, large eggs, brown sugar, baking powder, and baking soda in a blender or food processor. Process until the oats are finely broken down and the batter is smooth and creamy, starting with about 1 minute. Stop and scrape safely as needed; use the texture rather than a fixed blending clock. For a larger batch, blend separately so the machine is not overfilled.
Fold in the chips: Stir in the dark chocolate chips by hand so they remain as pieces.

Fill the muffin cups: Divide the batter among the prepared cups, about three-quarters full. If the banana size leaves extra batter, use additional prepared cups rather than overfill. Add additional chocolate chips (if using) over the tops, then bake promptly.

Bake and cool: Bake for about 15–20 minutes until the tops are set and a tester through the central crumb has no wet batter. Melted chocolate on the tester is different from uncooked batter; check another spot if needed. Cool in the pan on a rack for 10 minutes, then remove carefully to a rack. Cool completely before packing.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, snack, bake, blend

recipes.name: Banana Pancakes
recipes.description: Ripe banana adds flavor and moisture to this buttermilk batter. Fold the wet and dry mixtures together until all flour is moistened, then stop while small lumps remain.
recipeIngredient: 2 large Ripe Bananas, mashed (about 3/4 cup total)
3 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted and slightly cooled
Butter or oil for the griddle
Maple syrup and sliced bananas for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the dry ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
Mix the wet ingredients: In another bowl, whisk together the buttermilk, mashed bananas, eggs, cooled melted butter, and vanilla until evenly combined.

Fold and rest: Add the wet mixture to the dry and fold gently with a spatula until no dry flour pockets remain, scraping the bowl bottom and sides. Small banana lumps and hydrated batter lumps are fine. Stop mixing and let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Heat the griddle: During the rest, heat a griddle or large nonstick skillet over medium heat, about 325°F for an electric griddle. Lightly grease with the separate butter or oil allowance.

Cook: Pour 1/3 cup batter per pancake, leaving room to turn them. Cook until bubbles form and begin to pop, the edges look set and the underside is golden, about 2–3 minutes. Flip gently and cook about 1–2 minutes more, until golden underneath and cooked through with no wet batter in the center. Lower the heat if the surface colors too quickly. Repeat with the remaining batter, refreshing the light coating of griddle fat as needed.

Serve or freeze: Serve with sliced bananas, maple syrup and optional serving butter. For freezing, separate cooked pancakes on a rack to cool promptly, layer between parchment and seal in a freezer bag. Freeze for up to 2 months for quality. Reheat in a toaster or oven until hot throughout.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, weekend-brunch, comfort-food, kid-friendly, griddle

recipes.name: Banana Pudding
recipes.description: Banana and vanilla pudding folded with whipped topping, layered with sliced bananas and vanilla wafers for a cool, creamy spoon dessert.
recipeIngredient: 3.4 oz (96 g) sugar-sweetened banana-cream instant pudding mix; a four-serving packet formulated for 2 cups milk
3.4 oz (96 g) sugar-sweetened vanilla instant pudding mix; a four-serving packet formulated for 2 cups milk
16 oz (454 g) frozen whipped topping, thawed in the refrigerator, divided
11 oz (311 g) small crisp vanilla wafer cookies, divided
3 medium ripe but firm bananas, sliced just before layering

recipeInstructions.text: Divide the topping and wafers: Keep half the thawed whipped topping, refrigerated for the top. Reserve 20 g of the wafers in a sealed container for garnish; use all the rest in the layers.

Mix the pudding: Pour the cold milk into a large bowl. Whisk in both pudding powders gradually, then whisk for about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl until no dry pockets remain. The base will be very thick. Blend in the condensed milk gradually until smooth, then stir in the vanilla.
Fold: Fold the other half of the whipped topping into the pudding with a flexible spatula, turning the bowl and lifting from the bottom. Stop when the color is even and no large white streaks remain.

Layer: Peel and cut the bananas into roughly 1/4-inch slices. In a 4-quart serving dish, layer half the unreserved wafers, half the bananas and half the pudding. Repeat with the remaining wafers, bananas and pudding, spreading it to cover the fruit. Spread the refrigerated half of the whipped topping over the surface.

Chill and serve: Cover the dish without pressing down the topping and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, until fully cold and the wafers are spoon-tender. Crush the reserved wafers over the top just before serving. Spoon into twelve dessert portions, reaching through the layers. Coffee or unsweetened tea suits its rich sweetness.

recipes.keywords: Southern, American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, entertaining, holiday, no-cook, assemble

recipes.name: Basic Crêpes
recipes.description: A thin, pourable batter makes crêpes that spread before they set. If needed, add milk one tablespoon at a time; tilt the hot pan immediately after pouring.
recipeIngredient: ½ cup milk, or more as needed
¼ teaspoon salt or to taste
Neutral oil or butter, for greasing the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: Whisk eggs, milk, water, and salt together in a large mixing bowl. Add flour and melted butter; whisk vigorously until batter is smooth and pourable.

Cook: Heat a lightly oiled griddle or frying pan over medium-high heat. Pour or scoop the batter onto the pan, using approximately 1/4 cup for each crêpe. Tilt the pan with a circular motion so that the batter coats the surface evenly.

Continue: Cook until the top of the crêpe is no longer wet and the bottom has turned light brown, 1 to 2 minutes. Run a spatula around the edge of the skillet to loosen the crêpe; flip and cook until the other side has turned light brown, about 1 minute more.

recipes.keywords: French, griddle

recipes.name: Basmati Rice
recipes.description: A controlled stovetop absorption method, with plain, cumin, or whole-spice options and clear checks before resting.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups (400 g) aged white basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
3 cups (720 ml) water, for the unsoaked stovetop method
1 tbsp ghee, butter, or neutral oil
1 small cinnamon stick, about 1 inch long, optional
2 tbsp hot water, only if needed to finish firm grains

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse rice in several changes of cool water until much of the loose starch has washed away. Drain thoroughly. Do not soak for this written method.

Heat fat and optional spices: In a 2–3 quart heavy saucepan, heat the ghee, butter, or oil over medium heat. If using spices, add them and stir for 20–30 seconds until fragrant. For plain rice, proceed directly to the next step.
Add rice and water: Stir in drained rice briefly to coat. Add the measured water and salt and bring to a gentle boil. Stir once, cover tightly, and lower heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cook and check: Simmer about 15–18 minutes. Check near the end that water is absorbed and taste a grain for an almost tender center. If it is still hard and the pot is dry, add the measured hot water, re-cover, and cook a little longer. If water remains and grains are firm, continue gently before resting.
Rest and fluff: Turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Remove visible whole spices and fluff gently with a fork. Serve promptly or cool safely for storage.

recipes.name: BBQ Chicken Sliders
recipes.description: Broiled BBQ chicken thighs with sharp cheddar, buttery Hawaiian rolls, pickles and crispy fried onions.
recipeIngredient: 2 lb boneless skinless chicken thighs, raw; fresh or fully thawed
1 cup BBQ sauce, divided; keep the glazing share separate from raw chicken
6 sharp cheddar slices, halved to fit sliders
dill pickle chips, as wanted for the sliders
additional BBQ sauce, as wanted for serving, separate from the measured marinade and glaze

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate in the refrigerator: Toss boneless skinless chicken thighs, 1/3 of the BBQ sauce, olive oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and black pepper together, using one-third of the measured BBQ sauce and leaving the other two-thirds in a clean container for glazing. Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours. Keep the clean sauce and utensils away from the raw chicken.

Broil the thighs: Set up a broiler-safe metal sheet pan and use the rack position permitted by the oven, about 6 inches below the broiler where the oven instructions permit. Lift the thighs from the marinade, shake off excess and discard the used marinade. Arrange in a single layer without overlap; cook in additional loads if necessary. Start checking at 6–7 minutes per side, turning as the surface browns. Check the thickest part of each thigh with a thermometer and continue until each reaches 165°F / 74°C. Watch sugary spots closely rather than waiting for heavy blackening. Move cooked chicken with clean utensils.

Glaze and melt the cheese: Use 2/3 of the BBQ sauce and sharp cheddar slices for the glaze and topping: brush the cooked thighs with the clean reserved sauce, then distribute all the cheese halves evenly over the chicken. The number of thighs need not equal the number of rolls. Broil for about 1–2 minutes, watching until the cheese melts; remove before the sauce burns.

Rest the chicken and toast the rolls: Let the chicken rest for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, use Hawaiian rolls and butter for the rolls: brush their cut faces with all the melted butter. Put the rolls cut-side up on a clean broiler-safe sheet pan and watch for 1–2 minutes, removing them as soon as the cut faces are golden.

Slice and assemble: Divide all the rested chicken and melted cheese into one bun-sized portion for each measured roll. Add dill pickle chips, crispy fried onions, and additional BBQ sauce to the sliders and serve while the rolls and onions are crisp.

recipes.name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Thin sirloin slices and broccoli with a glossy soy-oyster sauce, cooked in small batches and combined gently at the finish.
recipeIngredient: 680 g trimmed boneless top sirloin steak, weighed after removing tough outer membranes
450 g trimmed broccoli, florets about 1 1/2 inches wide and peeled stems sliced 1/4 inch thick
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, for steaming broccoli, divided
2 tbsp water, reserved for correcting dry broccoli or thick sauce
1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted beef stock or water
1 tbsp toasted sesame oil, added after sauce thickens
40 g scallions, white parts thinly sliced and green parts cut into 1-inch lengths
1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything: Pat the steak dry and cut across the grain into roughly 1/4-inch-thick, 2-inch-long slices. Divide into three batches of about 225 g. Cut the broccoli as listed and divide in half. Whisk soy sauce, oyster sauce, vinegar, stock or sauce water, cornstarch and white pepper together. Keep sesame oil separate. Mince garlic and ginger and separate scallion whites and greens.

Brown and steam broccoli in two batches: Heat the pan over medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and half the broccoli. Cook about two minutes, turning occasionally, until some edges brown. Lower the heat slightly, carefully add 2 tbsp of the steaming water and cover for 2–3 minutes. Check a thick stem; use a little reserved water and another short steam if still hard. Uncover and let remaining water evaporate, about 30–60 seconds. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the other half, another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the remaining 2 tbsp steaming water.

Sear three beef batches: Let the empty pan dry and regain medium-high heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp oil; it should shimmer without heavy smoke. Spread one beef batch in one layer. Leave for about one minute until browned underneath, then turn and stir-fry another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thick slices with a fine-tip thermometer inserted from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat twice with 1 1/2 tsp oil per batch. Turn the heat down if residue blackens; remove burned deposits before continuing. Allow the beef at least three minutes after reaching temperature before serving.

Make the sauce: Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil, garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, keeping the garlic pale. Re-stir the sauce and pour it in. Bring to a gentle bubble, stirring for about 45–90 seconds until glossy and lightly thickened. Stir in the separate tablespoon sesame oil. Use reserved water in small spoonfuls if the sauce is too thick. Pour half the sauce into a heatproof cup.

Combine in two rounds: Add half the beef and its collected juices, half the broccoli and half the scallion greens to the sauce remaining in the pan. Fold over medium heat for about 30–60 seconds to coat and rewarm, then transfer to a serving platter. Return the reserved sauce to the pan and fold in the rest of the beef, juices, broccoli and scallion greens. Once hot and coated, add this round to the platter. Do not keep boiling the meat to chase a thicker glaze.

Serve: Confirm at least three minutes have elapsed since the last beef batch reached 145°F / 63°C. Divide into four portions and scatter the optional teaspoon of sesame seeds over the full dish. Serve with plain rice prepared separately; the stir-fry already includes its vegetable portion.

recipes.name: Beef Chow Fun
recipes.description: Wide rice noodles, tender beef, ginger, scallions and bean sprouts with a thin soy coating, finished in four small batches for a home pan.
recipeIngredient: 450 g trimmed flank steak, sliced across the grain about 1/8 inch thick and 2 inches long
1 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the beef
1 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the beef
1 tsp neutral oil, for the beef coating
680 g fresh wide rice noodles (ho fun), about 3/4–1 inch wide
120 g fresh mung bean sprouts, rinsed and well drained
60 g trimmed scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
4 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
2 tbsp water, reserved for loosening noodles only if needed
2 tbsp regular soy sauce, for the noodles
2 tbsp Shaoxing wine, for the noodles

recipeInstructions.text: Coat the beef: Stir the beef's measured soy, wine, coating water, cornstarch and measured baking soda until dispersed. Add the thinly sliced beef, turn and gently mix until evenly coated, then mix in its measured coating oil. Cover and refrigerate for twenty minutes while preparing everything else. Do not rinse off this small-dose coating or add more baking soda.

Prepare flexible noodles: Separate supple fresh noodles gently. If they are cold and stiff, follow the package warming directions. Where the package permits microwaving, transfer noodles out of non-microwave-safe packaging to a microwave-safe plate, cover loosely and warm in short 20–30-second intervals, checking and turning between intervals until they separate without force. Work in manageable portions; one fixed thirty-second blast is not enough for every cold block. Cut whole sheets into 3/4–1-inch ribbons if necessary. Divide the prepared noodles into four 170 g portions.

Mix and portion: Whisk the noodle soy, Chinese dark soy, noodle wine, sugar and sesame oil, then divide the mixture into four equal portions. Prepare ginger, scallions and drained sprouts. Keep scallion whites and greens separate; divide each and the ginger into four portions. Set out clean bowls for the cooked sprouts and beef.

Cook sprouts separately: Heat 1 tsp of the cooking oil in the pan over medium-high heat. Add the sprouts and stir for about one minute. Add the measured sprout-cooking water, cover for 1–2 minutes, then uncover and let free water evaporate. The sprouts should be steaming hot and softened through their stems, not merely warmed on the surface; extend briefly if needed. Transfer to a clean bowl and divide into four portions.

Cook two beef batches: Let the pan dry and recover heat. Add 1 1/2 tsp cooking oil and spread half the beef in one layer, leaving excess loose coating in its raw-meat bowl. Cook about one minute until browned below, turn, and cook another 1–3 minutes as needed. Check representative thicker slices with a fine probe inserted sideways from the edge: at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 1 1/2 tsp oil and the other half. Discard leftover raw-contact coating and wash its bowl and tools. Divide the cooked beef and its juices into four portions; each has time to rest at least three minutes before serving.

Finish one noodle portion: Reduce heat if the pan is smoking heavily; remove any blackened deposits. Add 2 tsp of the remaining cooking oil over medium-high heat. Stir in one portion of ginger and scallion whites for about 20 seconds until fragrant. Add one noodle portion and lift gently to coat, then let it touch the pan for 15–20 seconds at a time, lifting and turning between contacts. Add one portion of noodle seasoning and fold until evenly coated. Add one portion each of cooked beef, juices, sprouts and scallion greens. Fold just until hot throughout, about 3–4 minutes for this whole finishing step. If firm noodles need moisture, use a little of the reserved water rather than adding extra soy; use no more than the full measured noodle-water reserve across the batch.

Plate and repeat: Serve the first portion promptly, confirming at least three minutes have passed since its beef reached 145°F / 63°C. Repeat step 6 three more times, letting the empty pan recover heat between portions before adding each fresh 2 tsp oil; add aromatics once that oil shimmers. Use the remaining measured ingredient portions. Serve as four moderate noodle-main portions. A separately prepared vegetable side can accompany them; extra rice is unnecessary because the noodles already supply the starch.

recipes.name: Beef Pad See Ew
recipes.description: This beef version uses Thai black soy sauce, oyster sauce and a little fish sauce. Loosen the noodles before they reach the wok, cook in manageable batches and use a clean plate for the seared beef.
recipeIngredient: FOR THE STEAK & MARINADE, YOU’LL NEED:
1 teaspoon Thai black soy sauce (or regular light soy sauce)
FOR THE REST OF THE DISH, YOU’LL NEED:
2 teaspoons Thai soy sauce (or regular light soy sauce)
1 pound fresh wide rice noodles (you can also use 8 ounces dried rice noodles)
3 cups Chinese broccoli (cut into 2-inch/5 cm pieces)
Water, a small splash for steaming broccoli if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Toss: Toss steak with its marinade soy sauce, one teaspoon oil and cornstarch. Mix oyster sauce, sugar, regular soy sauce, Thai black soy sauce, fish sauce and white pepper separately.

Continue: Loosen fresh rice noodles according to package instructions just before cooking. If using dried noodles, cook slightly short of package time, drain well and toss with one tablespoon of the measured cooking oil.
Cook: Heat one tablespoon cooking oil in a wok. Sear beef in a thin layer, then transfer to a clean plate. Work in batches as needed; keep the remaining noodle ingredients divided proportionately.

Continue: Add one tablespoon cooking oil, garlic and broccoli. Stir-fry about two minutes; add a splash of water and cover briefly if stems are still tough. Add noodles, sauce and beef. Toss gently until coated.

Continue: Push the mixture aside. Add the remaining cooking oil and eggs. Scramble until set, then fold through the noodles. Continue cooking until everything is hot and the beef reaches 145°F / 63°C; allow the beef three minutes before serving. Cook longer if necessary, using tenderness and doneness rather than the original brief timer.

recipes.name: Beef Hot Dogs with Corn Relish
recipes.description: Hot dogs made from beef tenderloin aren't a tradition - they're a luxury. The corn relish is the main event: fresh corn kernels provide sweetness and texture that store-bought relish can't match.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Center-cut Beef Tenderloin, cut into 4 long "dogs"
4 6-inch Baguette pieces or High-quality Brioche Buns
1 cup Roasted Corn (charred in a pan or oven)
1/4 cup Red Bell Pepper, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: The Relish: In a small bowl, whisk the vinegar, sugar, salt, and pepper. Toss with the roasted corn, peppers, and onions. Let marinate while you cook the beef.
The Beef: Rub the tenderloin strips with oil, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.

The Sear: Heat a cast-iron skillet or grill to high. Sear the beef strips until browned on each side, starting to check after 2-3 minutes per side. Insert a thermometer from the side into the center of each piece and continue cooking until it reaches 145°F / 63°C; lower the heat if the outside browns too quickly. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
The Bread: Toast the baguette or brioche buns until golden.
Assemble: Place a beef strip in each bun. Top generously with the corn relish.
