recipes.name: Beef with Snow Peas
recipes.description: Thinly cut flank steak and brief cooking keep this stir-fry tender. Divide the sauce before it touches raw beef and use a clean plate for cooked meat.
recipeIngredient: 1 tablespoon peeled and minced fresh ginger
1 1/2 pounds flank steak, trimmed of fat and sliced very thin against the grain
5 whole scallions, cut into 1/2-inch pieces on the diagonal
Jasmine or long-grain rice, cooked according to package directions

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: In a bowl, mix together the soy sauce, sherry, cornstarch, brown sugar and ginger. Add the beef to a separate bowl and pour one-third of the liquid over the top. Save the rest of the liquid. Toss the beef and set aside.
Cook: Heat the oil in a heavy skillet (iron is best) over high heat. Add the snow peas and stir for 45 seconds, getting as much color on them as possible. Remove to a plate.

Finish: Allow the skillet to get very hot again. With tongs, add half the meat mixture, leaving most of the marinade still in the bowl. Spread out the meat as you add it to skillet, but do not stir for a good minute. (You want the meat to get as brown as possible as quickly as possible.) Sprinkle half the scallions over the meat. Flip the meat to the other side and cook for another 30 seconds. Remove to a clean plate.

Continue: Repeat with the other half of the meat, allowing the skillet to get very hot again first. After flipping, add the first plateful of meat, the reserved liquid, the crushed red pepper and snow peas. Stir over high heat for 30 seconds, and then turn off the heat. Check the seasonings and add salt only if it needs it. The mixture will thicken as it sits. Use a clean plate for the first cooked batch. Discard the raw-contact marinade; the reserved sauce must have been kept separate. Check beef for 145°F / 63°C and allow three minutes before serving. Serve immediately over rice.

recipes.name: Cinnamon Rolls
recipes.description: These soft, pull-apart rolls have a buttery cinnamon spiral and tangy cream-cheese frosting. Cooking a small portion of the flour with water helps the dough retain moisture; cool the paste until just warm before mixing it into the dough.
recipeIngredient: 8 tbsp European-style Salted Butter (cool room temp)
2 tsp Vanilla Powder (optional, for the filling)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Refrigerate frosted leftovers in a covered container at 40°F / 4°C or below within 2 hours, or within 1 hour if the room is above 90°F / 32°C. Bring out only the portions you plan to serve.

itemListElement.text: The Tangzhong: In a small saucepan, whisk the tangzhong flour and water. Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until a thick paste forms, about 4–5 minutes. Scrape into a bowl and cool until just warm.

The Mix: In a stand mixer, combine the dough flour, granulated sugar, yeast and salt. Add the cream, milk, egg, dough vanilla and all the cooled tangzhong. Knead with a dough hook on low speed for about 2 minutes.

The Butter: On low speed, add the dough butter one tablespoon at a time, letting each addition incorporate. Knead for another 10–12 minutes, until smooth and elastic and a stretched piece forms a thin windowpane.
Rest the Dough: Shape into a ball, place seam-side down in a butter-greased bowl, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Make the Filling: During the rest, mix all the filling butter, brown sugar and cinnamon with the optional vanilla powder into a spreadable paste.
Shape: On a lightly floured surface, roll to a 15 x 21-inch rectangle with a 21-inch edge facing you. Spread all the filling over the dough, leaving a 1-inch clean border along the far 21-inch edge.

The Cut: Cut across the 21-inch width into twelve strips, each 1.75 inches wide and 15 inches long. Roll each strip away from you toward its clean edge and place in a parchment-lined metal 9 x 13-inch pan.
Final Rise: Cover and let rise until doubled, about 1–2 hours. Preheat the oven to 325°F during this rise and wait for it to reach temperature before baking.

Bake: Bake for about 30–35 minutes, until the tops are lightly golden and the center roll is set rather than wet dough. Check the center as well as the edges; continue baking if the middle is still doughy.
The Frosting: While the rolls bake, beat all the frosting cream cheese and butter until smooth. Mix in the powdered sugar, frosting vanilla and cream, beating until fluffy.
Finish: Cool the pan on a rack for 15 minutes. Spread all the frosting over the warm rolls, then let stand another 15 minutes before serving warm.

recipes.name: Brownies
recipes.description: These brownies have dense, fudgy centers, chewy edges, and a noticeable olive-oil flavor. Keep the 8-inch square pan: a wider pan makes a thinner layer that bakes faster.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Dark Chocolate Chips (60% cacao or higher)
Cooking spray, for the pan and parchment

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 325°F. Spray an 8x8 baking pan and line with parchment paper so it hangs over the edges. Spray the parchment too.
Dry Mix: In a medium bowl, whisk together the sugar, flour, cocoa, powdered sugar, chocolate chips, and salt.
Wet Mix: In a large bowl, whisk eggs, olive oil, water, and vanilla until well combined and slightly frothy.
Combine: Sprinkle the dry ingredients over the wet. Fold gently with a spatula until just combined. The batter will be very thick.
Bake: Spread evenly in the prepared pan. Bake for 40-45 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
The Finish: Allow to cool completely in the pan for at least 2 hours before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

recipes.name: Bibimbap
recipes.description: Bibimbap has roots in Korean royal court cuisine but became a peasant dish in the Joseon Dynasty, when farmers would mix leftover vegetables and rice in a bowl. The name means 'mixed rice,' and it reflects the Korean philosophy of balance - multiple flavors and textures coming together in harmony.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Have all your component recipes ready (Ribeye, Cucumbers, etc.).
Base: Scoop 1 cup of hot rice into each bowl. (Tip: For crispy rice, use the "Cast Iron Skillet Hack" mentioned in the Ribeye recipe).
The Clock: Arrange the prepared vegetables and meat in distinct piles around the perimeter of the bowl, moving clockwise.
The Crown: Place the fried egg in the center.
Sauce: Drizzle the mixed Gochujang sauce over the egg.
Serve: Mix vigorously before eating.

recipes.name: Big-Batch Chicken Chili Verde
recipes.description: Browned chicken thighs braised in roasted tomatillo and poblano sauce, with a small white-bean addition and measured fresh toppings.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1.35 kg (3 lb) tomatillos, weighed after removing husks, rinsed and halved
3 poblano peppers, about 450 g before trimming
2 jalapeños, optional or reduced for milder heat
2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, divided, plus up to 1 cup (240 ml) only if needed to loosen
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) plain white beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Roast peppers: Heat the broiler and position a rimmed tray about 6 inches from the element, following the oven's guidance. Broil whole poblanos and optional jalapeños, turning regularly, about 12–20 minutes until blistered. Put them in a heatproof bowl and cover for 10 minutes. Peel loose charred skin, remove stems and seed cores, and chop; handle hot chiles with care and wash hands before touching eyes.

Roast tomatillos: Arrange halved tomatillos cut-side down on the tray, retaining their juices. Broil about 10–15 minutes until soft with browned or blistered tops. Use two batches if they cannot fit in one layer. Watch rather than following the clock past burning.

Blend the sauce: Let vegetables cool enough for your blender's warm-liquid guidance. Blend tomatillos and collected juices with peeled peppers and 1 cup of the measured broth, in batches as needed. Vent as the appliance directs; do not seal steaming liquid in a personal blender. Have this sauce ready before beginning the chicken.

Brown chicken: Pat chicken dry and season with two-thirds of the listed salt. Heat 2 tsp oil in a roomy Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown one-third of the chicken on two sides, about 5–6 minutes, then transfer to a bowl. Repeat twice with 2 tsp oil per batch. The centers need the following braise; continue directly.

Build aromatics: Lower heat to medium and add the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Cook onion about 6–8 minutes until softened. Add garlic, cumin, coriander and optional cayenne and stir about 30 seconds. Pour in the remaining initial 1 cup broth and scrape up brown residue, then add the blended green sauce and chicken with its juices.

Braise and check: Bring to a gentle simmer, partly cover and cook about 25–35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and are tender. Add a little of the extra broth only if sauce is too thick before the meat is ready. Stir in drained beans for the final 5 minutes to heat through.

Finish: If sauce needs further reduction, remove finished chicken briefly and simmer the sauce alone, then return it. Turn off heat. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed. Stir in cilantro and start with just a little lime juice, adding more only if the sauce benefits.

Serve and portion: Divide into eight servings. Offer the listed sour cream, radishes and tortilla strips as optional full-batch supplies. Omit sour cream for a dairy-free version and check packaged ingredients. Bread or slaw is prepared separately.

recipes.name: Soft Black Bean Tacos with Lime Crema
recipes.description: Partly mashed black beans with softened onion, warm tortillas, lime crema and measured fresh toppings.
recipeIngredient: 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g drained total
1/2 cup (120 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth, plus a little only if needed
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste
1/2 cup (120 g) Mexican crema or plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed
1 tbsp water, only if needed to loosen yogurt
8 soft corn or flour tortillas, about 6 inches across
200 g tomatoes, diced and drained of pooled juice

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare toppings and crema: Shred cabbage, dice and drain tomatoes, chop cilantro and cut the serving lime. Stir crema or yogurt with the initial measured lime juice. Taste before adding the crema's optional salt and reserved juice; thin thick yogurt with up to the measured water allowance. Refrigerate while cooking.

Soften the aromatics: Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Add onion and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Add garlic for 30 seconds, then cumin, chili powder and smoked paprika for about 20 seconds. Lower heat if the spices begin to darken.

Build the filling: Add drained beans, broth and half the bean salt. Simmer gently 5–7 minutes, stirring. Mash about one-third of the beans with a fork or masher, then stir into a soft, thick filling. Add a little broth if stiff; simmer briefly if watery. Taste and add the remaining bean salt only if needed, remembering the optional cheese is salty.

Warm the tortillas: Cover beans off heat for the short warming period. In a second dry skillet, warm tortillas over medium-high for roughly 10–30 seconds per side until hot and pliable, then wrap in a clean towel. For one skillet, microwave four tortillas at a time between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, adding short bursts if needed.

Fill and serve: Divide beans among eight tortillas. Add cabbage, tomato, cilantro, a little lime crema and optional measured cotija. Serve two tacos per person, with wedges to adjust the lime at the table. Assemble at serving so the cabbage stays crisp and tortillas do not soak through.

recipes.name: Blackout Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This three-layer chocolate cake combines cocoa and espresso with tangy Greek yogurt, chocolate cream-cheese frosting and a chocolate-chip coating. Whisk the hot cocoa mixture smooth, then let it cool before the eggs enter; cool the baked layers completely so the frosting holds its shape.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pans and parchment
additional chocolate, for melting and drizzling, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the pans: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or neutral oil to grease three 9-inch round cake pans, line their bottoms with parchment and grease the parchment. Check that the pans fit in the oven with space for air to circulate; if baking in batches, allow extra time.

Bloom and cool the cocoa: Whisk the cake’s boiling water, unsweetened cocoa powder, and instant espresso powder together in a heatproof bowl until smooth. Let stand briefly, then cool until lukewarm before adding the eggs.
Mix the liquids: Whisk the cake’s plain full-fat Greek yogurt, vegetable oil, large eggs, and vanilla extract into the cooled cocoa mixture until evenly combined.
Mix the dry ingredients: In another large bowl, whisk the cake’s all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt thoroughly, breaking up lumps.
Combine the batter: Fold the dry mixture into the chocolate mixture just until no dry pockets remain. Divide evenly among the prepared pans.

Bake and cool: Bake for about 30–35 minutes, until the layers are set, the centers spring back lightly and a tester has no wet batter. Cool on racks for about 10 minutes in the pans, loosen the edges and turn out carefully. Remove the parchment and let cool completely.

Make the frosting: While the layers cool, beat the frosting’s butter, cream cheese, unsweetened cocoa powder, vanilla extract, salt, powdered sugar, and heavy cream until smooth: cream the softened butter and cream cheese first, mix in cocoa, vanilla and salt, then add powdered sugar gradually on low speed with the heavy cream. Beat until spreadable.

Stack and chill: Place one completely cooled layer on a cake board or serving plate. Spread frosting between the layers and over the top and sides. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to firm the frosting before applying the chocolate coating.

Coat with chocolate chips: Gently press the chocolate chips into the chilled cake’s sides over a tray to catch loose chips. Use as much of the listed coating allowance as needed for coverage; the remainder can be served alongside or saved separately.
Finish and serve: Melt additional chocolate (if using) and drizzle over the top. Let the cake lose its refrigerator chill before slicing; for cleaner cuts, slice before a chocolate drizzle hardens.

recipes.name: Blistered Shishito Peppers
recipes.description: Dry peppers and a single layer let the skins blister before the flesh becomes soft. Heat varies from pepper to pepper; a mild batch does not guarantee that every pepper is mild.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Shishito Peppers, left whole with stems on

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and heat: Wash the whole peppers under running water and dry thoroughly. Keep their stems on. Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high to high heat until hot, following the pan instructions; visible smoke is not required.

Blister: Use enough pan space for one loose layer. Divide the listed oil and peppers among batches if necessary. Add each batch’s oil, then the peppers. Leave undisturbed about 60–90 seconds until blistered and dark in spots, then toss and cook another 60–90 seconds. Continue briefly if needed until the skins have several blistered patches; reduce heat if oil smokes or peppers blacken all over.
Season: Transfer to a serving plate. Squeeze the listed lemon wedge over the peppers and distribute all the measured flaky salt and sesame seeds over the whole batch.
Serve: Serve promptly, picking peppers up by their stems and leaving the stems behind. Earlier batches soften while later ones cook.

recipes.name: Blueberry Oatmeal
recipes.description: Berries form a juicy layer beneath the oats, with a smaller amount on top. The toasted seeds are mixed through the oats, rather than added only as a topping.
recipeIngredient: 2/3 cup Toasted Sunflower Seeds or Pumpkin Seeds (Nut-Free option)
Butter or oil for greasing the baking dish
2 tsp Raw Sugar (optional, for pre-bake topping)
Plain or vanilla yogurt or whipped cream, optional for serving
Extra maple syrup or honey, optional for drizzling
Additional fresh fruit, optional for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and divide berries: Preheat the oven to 375°F and grease a 9-inch square baking dish for the original batch with the separate pan-fat allowance. Wash and drain fresh blueberries; use frozen berries without thawing. Use all the measured berries: reserve a small portion for the top and spread the rest over the bottom.
Mix the dry ingredients: Combine all the oats, toasted sunflower or pumpkin seeds, cinnamon, measured kosher salt and baking powder. Spread evenly over the bottom berries.
Mix the wet ingredients: Whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, vanilla and half the measured melted butter until combined. Keep the other half of the butter for finishing.

Hydrate and top: Pour the wet mixture evenly over the oats. Gently wiggle the dish to let the milk settle through, then press down any dry oats on the surface. Scatter all the reserved berries over the top. If using the optional raw sugar, scatter all its listed amount over the surface before baking.

Bake: Load only once the oven has reached 375°F. Bake about 40–45 minutes with fresh berries, or start checking around 45–50 minutes with frozen berries. Continue until the top is golden and the center is set without liquid egg mixture; an egg-dish center should reach 160°F. Berry temperature, dish material and deeper filling can extend cooking.

Finish and rest: Drizzle with all the remaining measured butter. Let stand for a few minutes so it holds together when portioned. Serve warm with optional yogurt or whipped cream, extra maple syrup or honey, and additional fresh fruit as desired. These serving allowances are separate from the measured batter. Refrigerate promptly for cold service.

recipes.name: Blueberry Banana Pancake Muffins
recipes.description: Blend the bananas, oats, full-fat cottage cheese and eggs until the oats and curds are smooth, then add the blueberries to the individual wells. These muffins have a soft, dense interior, with richness from the full-fat cottage cheese.
recipeIngredient: Oil or nonstick spray for the muffin wells

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease enough standard-size muffin wells for the listed planning count with the separate oil or spray allowance; the original batch plans twelve. Use ripe bananas and keep the frozen blueberries separate.

Blend: Blend all the bananas, oats, cottage cheese, eggs, maple syrup and vanilla until the oat pieces and curds are smooth, following the blender’s load instructions. Stop safely to scrape if needed. For larger batches, blend proportional smaller loads and recombine them before portioning.

Portion and add berries: Divide the mixture evenly across the listed planning number of prepared wells, with space for it to rise. Distribute all the measured blueberries across their tops and press them gently into the surface. Use the full listed berry amount; the original twelve-muffin batch uses half a cup. Berry size varies, so a fixed count is only a guide. Use extra prepared wells if the actual tin cannot hold the full mixture.

Bake: Bake about 25–30 minutes, until the muffins feel firm and the center is set. A skewer should show no wet batter; check beside a berry. An egg-dish center should reach 160°F. Puffing or browning alone does not establish a cooked center.
Cool: Leave in the tin for 5–10 minutes before lifting gently to a rack. They may settle as they cool. Serve warm, or refrigerate promptly for cold service.

recipes.name: Blueberry Date Oatmeal
recipes.description: Chop the pitted dates finely so they soften into the oats. Coconut oil adds richness to the porridge.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 cups Water (all or part may be milk of choice)
6 Medjool Dates, pitted and finely chopped
Additional water or milk, as needed to loosen the oatmeal

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Check the rolled-oat and frozen cauliflower and blueberry packages. If a frozen product requires cooking before eating, follow its cooking directions; do not rely on a brief off-heat thaw to satisfy them. Cook those products separately first if the oatmeal route will not meet their instructions, retaining all the listed amounts. Remove the date pits and finely chop the flesh.

Combine: Choose the stovetop OR microwave route. Combine oats, cauliflower, water or milk, chopped dates and all the coconut oil in a saucepan, or in a microwave-safe bowl with generous room for foaming. Use the prepared cauliflower if its package required separate cooking. Keep the berries aside until the finish unless they need cooking with the oats under their package directions.

Stovetop option: Bring to a gentle boil, then reduce to a simmer. Stir frequently and start checking at 5–7 minutes, following the actual rolled-oat package if it needs longer. Stop when the oats are tender and creamy. If too thick before the oats are tender, add a little of the additional water or milk allowance and continue gently. Skip the microwave step.

Microwave option: Follow the oatmeal package where it provides microwave directions. Otherwise heat on high for about 3 minutes as a first check, stopping earlier if it rises toward the rim. Carefully stir, then heat in short intervals, checking until the oats are tender and thickened; another 2–3 minutes is a planning range, not a guarantee for every microwave. If too thick before tender, stir in a little of the additional water or milk allowance before continuing. The bowl and steam will be hot. Skip the stovetop step.

Berry finish: If the measured blueberries already cooked with the oats, leave them in; do not add another amount. Otherwise, off heat, fold in all the measured blueberries if their package allows this use, or fold in the same amount cooked separately as required. Let any berries added frozen thaw and let the oatmeal become comfortable to eat before serving.
Season and serve: Add the pinch of salt and cinnamon to taste. Divide among the listed portions and serve.

recipes.name: Blueberry Oat Breakfast Bars
recipes.description: Press the coated oats firmly into the corners as well as the center of the pan. Baking to lightly golden edges is followed by cooling and a long cold rest; cut the bars only once the slab is firm.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Greek Yogurt or Coconut Cream

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 340°F (170°C). Line an 8-inch square baking dish with parchment for the original batch, leaving enough paper to lift the cooled slab. Wash and drain the fresh blueberries.

Melt: Gently melt all the measured coconut oil or butter, honey or maple syrup, and almond or peanut butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Stir until smooth and combined, then take off the heat.
Coat and fold: Stir in all the oats until evenly coated. Gently fold in all the drained blueberries without deliberately crushing them.
Press: Transfer the whole mixture to the prepared dish. Press firmly with the back of a spoon across the base and into the corners, making an even, compact layer.

Bake: Load only once the oven has reached 340°F / 170°C. Bake about 15–18 minutes, until the edges are just beginning to turn golden. The hot slab will still be delicate; browning is followed by cooling and chilling.

Cool and chill: Let the slab cool in the pan until manageable, then refrigerate promptly for at least 1 hour and until firm enough to cut; overnight chilling is an option. Keep the slab in its pan while it sets.
Drizzle: Whisk all the measured yogurt or coconut cream with all the orange juice until smooth. Drizzle over the cold, firm slab.

Cut and serve: Lift with the parchment and cut into the listed number of bars; the original batch plans eight. Serve cold, or let individual bars stand briefly for serving. Return the rest to the refrigerator.

recipes.name: Blueberry Pancakes
recipes.description: Whisk the eggs and milk until foamy, then stir the flour in briefly and let the batter rest for five minutes. Sprinkle berries onto each wet pancake so they stay evenly distributed.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Unsalted Butter, melted and cooled
Salted butter and maple syrup for serving (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat a griddle to 350°F, or a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Lightly grease with the separate butter allowance; the measured melted butter all goes into the batter.
Whisk the wet ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, and vanilla until light and foamy, about 2–3 minutes. Whisk in the cooled melted butter and honey until evenly combined.

Add the dry ingredients: Whisk the flour, salt, and baking powder together in another bowl, then add them to the wet mixture. Stir with a spatula just until no dry flour pockets remain. Small lumps are fine; scrape the bottom and sides, then stop rather than beating the batter smooth.
Rest: Let the batter sit for 5 minutes while the griddle finishes heating. Do not vigorously stir it again.

Portion and add berries: Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls, leaving room to turn each pancake. Immediately sprinkle 1 tbsp blueberries onto each wet surface. Distribute the listed berries across the batch; the original 3/4 cup supplies twelve tablespoon portions.

Cook and turn: Cook until the underside is golden and the edges begin to set, with bubbles forming and popping, about 2 minutes. Flip gently and cook about 2–2 1/2 minutes more, until the center has no wet batter. Lower the heat if the exterior darkens before the center cooks. Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly renewing the griddle butter as needed.

Serve: Serve immediately, with salted butter and warm maple syrup if desired. If finishing another griddle round, hold the cooked pancakes briefly on a covered oven-safe platter in a 200°F oven. Covered pancakes may soften; serve promptly once the batch is ready.

recipes.name: Peking Ravioli
recipes.description: Peking ravioli (also called potstickers) were popularized in Boston by Joyce Chen's restaurant in the 1950s-60s. The Boston style is distinctive for its thick, chewy wrapper - more like pasta than delicate dim sum.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Napa Cabbage, finely minced and squeezed dry
2 tbsp Chinkiang Black Vinegar (or Balsamic fallback)

itemListElement.text: Mix: Place flour in a bowl. Slowly pour in the boiling water while stirring with chopsticks until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Knead for 5-8 minutes until smooth. Cover with a damp cloth and let rest for 30 minutes.
Roll: Divide into small balls. Roll each into a circle about 3.5 inches wide. They should be significantly thicker than a standard wonton wrapper (about 1/8 inch).
Squeeze: Ensure the minced cabbage is salted and squeezed in a towel to remove ALL moisture. (Watery cabbage = soggy ravioli).
Mix: Combine all filling ingredients. Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until the meat is sticky and emulsified.
Portion: Place a large tablespoon of filling in each wrapper.
Seal: Fold in half and pleat only 3-4 times (the Boston style is more rustic and "chunky" than delicate). Press hard to seal.
Sear: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large flat-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat. Place ravioli in the pan and fry undisturbed for 2-3 minutes until the bottoms are dark golden.
Steam: Pour in 1/2 cup of water and immediately cover with a tight lid. Reduce heat to medium and steam for 6-8 minutes until the water is gone.
Crisp: Remove lid. Add 1 more tsp of oil. Fry for 1 more minute until the bottoms "crackle" and are perfectly crisp.

recipes.name: Boulevardier
recipes.description: Created in 1920s Paris by American expat Erskine Gwynne, editor of a magazine called 'The Boulevardier,' this cocktail embodies the era of Americans living the high life in post-WWI Paris. It's essentially a whiskey Negroni, swapping gin for bourbon or rye, and was popular at Harry's New York Bar, the legendary watering hole of Hemingway and F.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: Add the bourbon, red Italian bitter aperitif and sweet vermouth to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 20-30: seconds until properly chilled.
Strain into a chilled: coupe glass or over a large ice cube in an Old Fashioned glass.
Express an orange peel: over the drink and garnish.
Serve immediately.:

recipes.name: Braised French Lentils
recipes.description: French green lentils (lentilles du Puy) are the only lentils worth braising as a side dish. Unlike their brown or red cousins, they hold their shape beautifully and develop a firm, almost al dente bite.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups French Green Lentils (lentilles du Puy), rinsed and picked over
3.5 cups Low-Sodium Vegetable or Chicken Broth

recipeInstructions.text: Build the Base: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add the diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-7 minutes until the vegetables are softened and the onion is translucent. Add garlic and cook 1 minute more until fragrant.
Add Lentils and Aromatics: Stir in the lentils, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Pour in the broth and stir to combine. Bring to a boil over high heat.

Braise: Reduce heat to low, partially cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are tender but still hold their shape. They should be creamy inside with a slight bite. Most of the liquid should be absorbed -- if it evaporates too quickly, add a splash of water.
Finish: Remove the thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Stir in the Dijon mustard and red wine vinegar. Season with salt and pepper. Fold in the fresh parsley just before serving.

recipes.name: Breakfast Burrito
recipes.description: A good breakfast burrito is all about assembly order and restraint -- overfill it and it becomes an unwrappable mess. Cooking the peppers and onions first gives them time to soften and release their moisture before the eggs go in, preventing a soggy tortilla.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Red or Green Bell Pepper, diced small
1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Pepper Jack Cheese
4 slices Cooked Bacon or 1/2 cup Cooked Breakfast Sausage, crumbled
Optional: salsa, hot sauce, sour cream, avocado slices

recipeInstructions.text: Cook Vegetables: Melt butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add bell pepper and onion. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.

Scramble Eggs: Whisk eggs with milk and salt. Pour into the skillet with the vegetables. Stir gently with a spatula, folding from the edges to the center, until the eggs are just set but still slightly glossy, about 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat immediately.
Warm Tortillas: In a separate dry skillet over medium-high heat, warm each tortilla for 15-20 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted.
Assemble: Lay each tortilla flat. Layer in the center: a quarter of the scrambled egg mixture, a quarter of the cheese, and a quarter of the cooked bacon or sausage. Add optional toppings if desired.
Roll: Fold the bottom edge of the tortilla up over the filling, fold both sides in, then roll tightly away from you to seal. The cheese should melt from the residual heat of the eggs.
Serve: Serve immediately with salsa and hot sauce on the side. For meal prep, wrap each burrito tightly in foil before the cheese is added, let cool, and freeze.

recipes.name: Breakfast Carrot Cake
recipes.description: Fine carrot shreds distribute through the whole-wheat crumb, while the full oil and yogurt amounts keep the mixture rich. Whisk the wet ingredients thoroughly, then fold the flour mixture gently until moistened and mix in all the carrots and nuts.
recipeIngredient: 250 g carrots, finely grated; about 2 large carrots at the original batch size

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment for the original batch.
Grate: Wash and peel the carrots. Finely grate the carrots using the small holes of a grater. Use the listed weight; the original two-large-carrot description is only a shopping guide.

Wet ingredients: In a large bowl, whisk large egg, granulated sugar, brown sugar, canola or avocado oil, plain Greek yogurt, and vanilla extract for about 3–5 minutes until thoroughly blended and frothy.

Dry ingredients: Whisk whole wheat flour, ground cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and sea salt together to distribute the leaveners and spice, then fold gently into the wet mixture until moistened without dry flour pockets.
Fold: Add carrots and walnuts or pecans. Fold gently until evenly distributed, stopping once combined.

Bake: Spread the batter evenly in the prepared pan and tap lightly. Load only once the oven has reached 375°F / 190°C. Begin checking at about 25–30 minutes: the center should be set, spring back gently and give a tester without wet batter. Continue as needed; pan material, filling depth and oven temperature affect the time. Pan dimensions and baking time do not multiply with ingredient scale; use suitable smaller pans or additional pans to keep similar filling depth.
Cool: Let stand in the pan for 10 minutes, then lift gently onto a wire rack. Cool completely before frosting or wrapping; warm serving after the pan rest is also an option.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Egg Cups
recipes.description: Thin spinach ribbons and finely diced pepper distribute through the egg cups instead of forming large pockets. Whisk until the eggs and milk are blended, then stop; excessive foam is not needed.
recipeIngredient: 1 medium Red Bell Pepper, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat the oven to 375 °F. Generously coat standard muffin cups with the cooking spray, including the sides. The original batch makes about eight cups; keep extra greased cups available if the chopped pepper changes the volume.
The Base: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper until no separate streaks of white remain; do not whip to a thick foam.
The Veg: Wash and dry the pepper and spinach. Finely dice the pepper. Stack the spinach leaves, roll them together and slice thin ribbons.
Combine: Fold the pepper, spinach and shredded cheddar into the eggs until distributed throughout.

Fill: Divide among standard muffin cups, filling about three-quarters full. Stir the bowl gently between pours so the vegetables do not all land in the last cup. Use extra cups rather than overfilling; for a scaled batch, keep the cup size and fill depth the same.

Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until the centers are opaque and set, with no liquid egg when gently moved, and reach 160 °F / 71 °C. Measure a center without touching the metal tin. Continue baking if needed rather than relying on surface browning alone.

Cool and store: Let stand in the tin for 5 minutes, then loosen gently and remove. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and use within 3–4 days. Reheat the center to 165 °F / 74 °C; 30 seconds in a microwave is not a dependable endpoint.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, meal-prep, weeknight, quick-lunch, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Protein Biscuits
recipes.description: Greek yogurt and eggs make a thick, sticky dough with chopped spinach, chives and cooked ham. Fold the fillings and two thirds of the cheese through it so each biscuit gets a share, then use the remaining cheese on top.
recipeIngredient: A little flour for dusting your hands

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet, or additional sheets as needed, with parchment. Use cooked ham, diced small. Wash and dry the spinach and chives, then chop them finely.
Wet and dry: Whisk all the yogurt and eggs in a large bowl. Separately whisk all the measured flour, flaxseed, garlic powder, red pepper flakes, baking powder and sea salt until distributed.
Combine: Add the dry mixture to the wet mixture gradually, stirring until the flour is moistened and a thick, sticky dough forms without dry pockets.

Fold: Fold in all the spinach, chives, cooked ham and two thirds of the measured cheddar. Distribute the fillings through the dough, stopping once combined; use your hands gently if needed. Keep the remaining one third of the cheese for the tops.

Shape: Lightly dust your hands with the separate flour allowance. Divide the whole dough evenly into the listed number of biscuits; the original batch plans twelve. Form disks about 1 inch thick with space between them on the prepared sheets. Use additional sheets or oven loads rather than crowding them or discarding extra dough.

Bake: Scatter all the remaining measured cheese over the biscuits. Load only once the oven has reached 400°F. Bake at 400°F for 5 minutes, then reduce the oven setting to 350°F without opening the door and bake about 20 minutes more. Keep the same temperature sequence for additional oven loads; do not multiply the heat settings or make thicker disks when scaling.

Check and cool: The bottoms should be golden and the cheese browned, with set centers and no wet flour or egg mixture. Check the center of a thick biscuit; for this cooked-ham-and-egg bake, use 165°F as the casserole-style endpoint. Continue baking as needed. Let stand briefly until firm enough to move, then serve warm or cool promptly before packing.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, meal-prep, snack, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Breakfast Quesadilla
recipes.description: A breakfast quesadilla should be crispy on the outside, melty on the inside, and ready in under 15 minutes. The key is scrambling the eggs first and slightly undercooking them -- they will continue to cook inside the quesadilla from the residual heat and the time on the griddle.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Shredded Cheddar or Mexican Blend Cheese
Salsa and sour cream for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Scramble Eggs: Melt butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat. Whisk eggs with salt and pour into the skillet. Stir gently with a spatula until the eggs are just barely set -- slightly wetter than you would normally eat them. Remove to a plate.

Build the Quesadilla: Wipe the skillet clean. Lay one tortilla flat. Spread half the cheese on one half of the tortilla, top with half the scrambled eggs and jalapenos (if using), then add the remaining cheese on top. Fold the tortilla in half. Repeat with the second tortilla.

Cook: Place the quesadilla in the dry skillet over medium heat. Cook for 2-3 minutes, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bottom is golden brown and crispy. Flip carefully and cook for 2 minutes more until the other side is golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Slice and Serve: Transfer to a cutting board. Let rest for 30 seconds, then cut into thirds. Serve with salsa and sour cream on the side.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, American, savory, rich, spicy, weeknight, kid-friendly, quick-lunch, saute, toast

recipes.name: Brisket with Carrots and Onions
recipes.description: Flat-cut brisket braised in tomato juice with carrots, celery and plentiful onions, then sliced across the grain and served with soft vegetables and reduced tomato sauce.

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven and prepare the pan: Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Choose a heavy roasting pan that holds the brisket in one layer with the vegetables and has room for the full can of tomato juice below its rim.
Season the brisket: Mix the kosher salt, pepper, garlic and oregano. Rub the mixture over all sides of the brisket.
Layer the braise: Put the brisket in the pan. Arrange all the carrots, celery, onions and bay leaves on and around it.

Add the tomato juice and seal: Pour in the entire 46-ounce can of tomato juice. The pan geometry and vegetables determine how high it comes around the meat; it does not need to reach a fixed mark. Lay two sheets of parchment over the pan, then seal tightly with heavy-duty foil.

Braise until tender: Bake, covered, for about 3 1/2 hours. Check the thickest part with an instant-read thermometer: it must reach at least 145°F / 63°C, followed by a 3-minute rest, and it must also be fork-tender. If the temperature is safe but the fork meets resistance, re-cover and continue in 15-minute intervals until tender.

Rest and reduce: Transfer the brisket to a cutting board and tent loosely with foil. Remove and discard all bay leaves. If the roasting pan is approved for stovetop use across two burners, use it; otherwise transfer all vegetables and sauce to a wide saucepan. Boil over medium-high heat for 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glossy and thickened but still saucy.
Slice and serve: Find the direction of the meat fibers and slice across the grain. Serve the brisket with the reduced sauce, carrots, celery and onions.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, savory, acidic, umami, rich, holiday, bake, roast, braise

recipes.name: Broccoli all'Agro
recipes.description: Lemon juice and zest dress the steamed broccoli, with raw grated garlic for a sharp finish. Drain off surface water before gently tossing the hot florets with all the dressing.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Wash the broccoli and cut the listed florets to similar sizes. Wash the lemon, zest it before juicing, and grate the garlic into a paste. Set up a steamer following its instructions, with cooking water below the basket and enough headroom for the florets; bring the water to a simmer.

Make the dressing: Whisk all the measured olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic and salt in a large serving bowl. This dressing keeps the garlic raw; do not hold a garlic-and-oil mixture at room temperature for later storage.

Steam: Add the broccoli to the basket, cover and steam. Start checking at 4–5 minutes: a fork should enter the thickest floret stem with slight resistance and the florets should remain intact. Continue as needed for their actual size. Use separate loads if the steamer is crowded.

Drain and toss: Lift out carefully, keeping clear of steam, and let excess surface water drain briefly. Add the hot broccoli to the dressing and toss gently until coated, scraping the bowl so the measured dressing reaches the whole batch. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Italian, steam, toss

recipes.name: Broccoli Cheddar Quinoa Bites
recipes.description: Use cooked quinoa that is cool enough not to scramble the eggs, and chop the washed broccoli finely. Compress each scoop so the egg and cheese bind the grains together.
recipeIngredient: Oil spray, as needed for the lined baking sheet

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment and lightly grease it with the oil spray.
Mix: Toss all the cooked quinoa, finely chopped broccoli, cheddar and green onions in a large bowl.
Bind: Stir in all the beaten eggs, Parmesan, garlic powder, salt and pepper until the mixture is evenly combined. Start with already cooked quinoa.

Shape: Use a small cookie scoop or tablespoon and press each scoop firmly against the bowl before placing it on the sheet. Make similarly sized bites, aiming for roughly the listed count; use additional sheets or batches when needed rather than enlarging every scoop or crowding the sheet.

Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, checking for golden edges and a center that holds together. Check representative bites, including a larger one, for 160°F in the egg mixture; color alone does not show the center temperature. Additional sheet loads may take longer.
Rest: Rest on the sheet for 5 minutes before lifting with a spatula. Serve the rested bites; the listed count is approximate.

recipes.keywords: American, umami, herbaceous, entertaining, potluck, kid-friendly, meal-prep, bake

recipes.name: Broccolini, Chicken Sausage, and Orzo Skillet
recipes.description: Use fully cooked chicken sausage, then keep it and the sautéed broccolini aside while the orzo absorbs the broth. Return both only when the pasta is tender, and stir in the full Parmesan off heat.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz fully cooked hot Italian chicken sausage, sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
2 bunches broccolini (about 1 lb total), trimmed and coarsely chopped
1 cup frozen peas, optional replacement for the broccolini; do not add both
Hot water, as needed for firm or dry orzo
Additional grated Parmesan, for serving, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the cooked sausage: Heat all the olive oil over medium-high heat in a roomy skillet with a lid. Add the fully cooked sausage rounds and brown for about 3–4 minutes, then transfer to a clean plate. Raw chicken sausage needs its own complete cooking method and is not a direct substitute.

Cook the vegetable: Wash and dry broccolini, trim the woody ends and coarsely chop it. Sauté it in the same oil-coated pan with some of the listed salt and pepper for about 5 minutes, until the stems are tender-crisp; continue if still tough. Remove to the sausage plate. If choosing frozen peas instead, omit all broccolini and skip this sauté; keep the peas for the final simmer.
Toast briefly: Add all the dry orzo and minced garlic to the pan. Stir for 30–45 seconds until fragrant; stop before the garlic darkens.

Simmer the pasta: Pour in all the chicken broth. Bring to a boil, cover and reduce to a gentle simmer. Begin checking around 10 minutes, guided by the orzo package, until the center is tender with a little bite. If tender pasta has pooled broth, uncover and simmer briefly. If the pan is dry while the center is firm, add a little of the hot-water allowance and continue. When using the frozen-peas option, add the full chosen amount near the end and allow enough time to heat it through.
Return and enrich: Return all the reserved fully cooked sausage and broccolini, if used. Stir over low heat until hot throughout, then remove from heat and incorporate all the measured Parmesan.
Finish: Use a little hot water only if needed to loosen the pasta. Taste and adjust with the listed salt and black pepper. Serve promptly, with the separate optional extra Parmesan or chile flakes.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, spicy, umami, rich, kid-friendly, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Brown Butter Carrot Cake
recipes.description: Browned butter brings a toasted aroma to this carrot cake, alongside ginger, cinnamon and tangy cream-cheese frosting. Watch the milk solids rather than the foam, and pour the butter out of the hot pan as soon as it turns golden brown; keep those browned solids for the batter.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pans and parchment
3/4 cup unsalted butter, measured before browning

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the oven and pans: Heat the oven to 350°F. Use butter or neutral oil to grease two 9-inch round cake pans, line the bottoms with parchment and grease the parchment.

Brown and cool the butter: Melt the cake’s unsalted butter over medium heat in a light-colored saucepan. Stir and scrape the bottom as it foams; when the milk solids are golden brown and smell nutty, immediately pour everything, including the brown solids, into a heatproof bowl. Let cool to lukewarm while preparing the other ingredients.
Prepare the carrot mixture: Combine the carrots and buttermilk in a bowl.

Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the cake’s all-purpose flour, ground cinnamon, ground ginger, ground nutmeg, baking powder, baking soda, and light, hollow-flake kosher salt together thoroughly in a separate bowl.

Beat the eggs and sugars: Beat the cake’s large eggs, granulated sugar, light brown sugar, and vanilla extract for about 4 minutes until pale and thick. Reduce the mixer speed and gradually stream in the cooled brown butter, including its browned solids, just until incorporated.

Finish the batter: Add the dry mixture in three additions, alternating with the carrot-buttermilk mixture in two additions; begin and end with the dry mixture. Scrape the bowl and mix only until no dry pockets remain. Divide evenly between the prepared pans.

Bake and cool: Bake for 35–45 minutes, until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean. Set the pans on racks for 10 minutes, loosen the edges, turn out and remove the parchment. Let the layers cool completely before frosting.

Make the frosting: While the cakes cool, beat the frosting’s cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar, and vanilla extract: first smooth the cream cheese and softened butter together, then mix in powdered sugar gradually on low speed with the vanilla. Beat until smooth and spreadable.

Layer and frost: Spread frosting between the completely cooled cake layers and over the top and sides. Refrigerate the frosted cake until serving; let only the portion being served lose its refrigerator chill.

recipes.name: Brown Butter-Chocolate Soufflé
recipes.description: A shared chocolate soufflé with a browned-butter crust and a soft, airy center, served straight from the oven.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp granulated sugar, approximate coating amount; tap out excess
7 oz (200 g) bittersweet chocolate, 65–70% cacao, chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Separate the eggs and heat the oven: Separate large eggs, reserving all the whites in a clean, grease-free mixer bowl and all the yolks in a second bowl. Keep any yolk out of the whites. Set an oven rack in the middle and heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Have the remaining ingredients measured and plates ready before you begin mixing.

Brown and cool the butter: Melt unsalted butter in a small skillet over medium heat, swirling until the milk solids turn brown and smell nutty, about 4 minutes. Transfer immediately to a small heatproof bowl. Refrigerate for about 20 minutes, stirring halfway through, until opaque but soft enough to brush. Prepare the chocolate base while it chills.

Make the ganache: Use bittersweet chocolate, 65–70% cacao and heavy cream for the ganache. Put the chopped chocolate in a large heatproof bowl with room for folding later. Heat the cream in a small saucepan until steaming, about 2 minutes, then pour it over the chocolate. Stir occasionally for about 5 minutes, until smooth and slightly cooled.

Finish the chocolate base: Whisk Dutch-process cocoa powder, dark rum (if using), Morton kosher salt, and hot water into the ganache. Whisk in all the reserved yolks just until smooth; the base should be warm, not steaming hot.

Whip the whites: When the butter has chilled for about 10 minutes, add the meringue’s granulated sugar and cream of tartar to the reserved whites. Beat at medium-high speed until glossy medium peaks form, about 8–10 minutes. Lift the whisk to check: the peaks should hold but their tips should bend. Stop before the whites turn dry or clumpy.

Coat the dish: Brush the bottom and sides of the 1 1/2-quart soufflé dish generously with all the cooled, browned unsalted butter, including the browned solids, right up to the rim. Add the coating’s granulated sugar, turn the dish to distribute it, and tap out the excess. Refrigerate the coated dish while you fold the batter. If using a stand mixer, you can coat the dish as the whites finish whipping, watching their texture.

Lighten, then fold: Stir about one quarter of the meringue into the chocolate base until fully blended. Add the remaining meringue in three batches. For each, sweep a flexible spatula down through the middle and along the bottom, then lift the batter over itself as you turn the bowl. Stop once the batter is mostly uniform with no large white pockets; a few fine streaks are preferable to prolonged mixing. Scrape into the prepared dish and bake promptly.

Bake: Bake at 375°F / 190°C for about 35–40 minutes. Look for a risen top with a slightly darker, just-set surface and a gentle wobble in the center. Check near the end of baking that the center reaches at least 160°F / 71°C, without touching the dish with the probe. A liquid center needs more time; the clock and surface color alone do not establish doneness.

Serve immediately: Finish with powdered sugar and heavy cream: dust the top with the sugar, then spoon into dessert portions and pass the extra cream for drizzling. Reach through the airy top to the soft center. Some settling as you serve is normal.

recipes.name: Brownie Oatmeal
recipes.description: Blend the oats with the very ripe banana, egg and milk until smooth for a soft, cake-like chocolate center. Keep the full cocoa and chocolate-chip amounts.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 cup Milk of choice (Almond or Oat preferred)
Butter or oil for greasing the oven-safe dish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease an oven-safe ramekin or small baking dish with the separate butter or oil allowance. Choose a dish that can hold the entire batter with room above it; banana size changes the volume.
Blend: Add all the oats, ripe banana, egg, milk, cocoa, baking soda and pinch of sea salt to the blender. Blend until smooth, following the blender’s load instructions.

Fill and top: Pour the whole mixture into the prepared dish and add all the measured chocolate chips on top. If the vessel cannot hold the batter with headroom, use a suitable larger dish or additional prepared vessels; different depth or portion size changes cooking time.

Bake: Begin checking around 15–18 minutes. The center should be set and soft, with no liquid egg mixture or wet oat batter; an egg-dish center should reach 160°F. Check beside a melted chocolate chip. Continue as needed for the actual dish and filling depth.
Finish: Let stand briefly until the dish is safe to handle and the center settles. Finish with a pinch of the flaky sea salt if desired and serve warm.

recipes.name: Brownie Protein Balls
recipes.description: These no-bake bites prep in bulk for lunchboxes, pre-workout snacks, or yogurt toppings. Different protein powders absorb liquid at varying rates, so add milk one teaspoon at a time until dough reaches fresh brownie consistency.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp Ground Flaxseed or Chia Seeds
1-2 tbsp Water or Almond Milk (if needed)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a medium bowl, combine almond butter, protein powder, almond flour, cocoa powder, maple syrup, and sea salt.
Hydrate: Mix with a spatula until a thick dough forms. If it is too crumbly to hold a shape, add 1 tbsp of water or milk. If it's still too dry, add another tbsp.
Texture: Fold in the flaxseed (or chia) and the mini chocolate chips.
Roll: Scoop out 1-tbsp portions and roll between your palms into balls.
Set: Place on a plate and chill in the refrigerator for at least 20 minutes before eating.
Store: Keep in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week.

recipes.name: Cooked-Chicken Taco Bar
recipes.description: A measured six-person taco setup using already cooked chicken, warm tortillas, cabbage and fresh toppings, with a cooked-pork variation.
recipeIngredient: 600 g fully cooked chicken, bones and skin removed, shredded into bite-size pieces
1/4 cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) only if needed
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
1/2 tsp fine salt, only if needed
18 small soft corn or flour tortillas, about 5–6 inches across, total across both types
2 avocados, about 300 g edible flesh, sliced just before serving
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the avocado
1/2 cup (120 g) Mexican crema or sour cream
60 g cotija or queso fresco, crumbled, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cold components first: Shred cabbage, slice radishes, dice onion and chop cilantro. Portion crema, salsa, optional cheese and hot sauce. Slice the optional jalapeño and cut the serving lime. Keep perishables chilled until the bar is ready; leave the avocado whole for now.

Start the filling: Heat oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Stir cumin for 15–20 seconds, then immediately add the initial measured broth and cooked chicken. Toss, cover and heat gently, stirring every couple of minutes. Add extra broth a tablespoon at a time only if the pan is drying.

Verify and season: After roughly 6–10 minutes, check several portions with a thermometer; continue until the reheated chicken reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout. Remove the lid briefly if liquid pools. Taste before adding any measured lime or salt, since cooked chicken and broth may already be seasoned. Cover off heat for the brief tortilla warming period.

Warm tortillas and finish avocado: Warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high, about 10–30 seconds per side until hot and flexible, wrapping each batch in a clean towel. Alternatively, microwave stacks of four to six between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, adding short bursts if needed. Slice avocado and gently toss with its separately measured lime juice. This helps limit browning but does not preserve it indefinitely.

Set the bar and serve promptly: Set out hot filling, warm tortillas and the chilled toppings. Offer three small tacos per person, about 33 g cooked chicken per tortilla before toppings. A thin layer of cabbage and a small spoonful of sauce are enough to start. Taste a bite before adding lime or hot sauce.

Manage any longer serving period: Replenish small dishes rather than leaving all the food out at once. For an extended buffet, keep cooked meat at 140°F / 60°C or above and cold toppings at 40°F / 4°C or below. Refrigerate unheld perishables within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

recipes.name: Buttered Egg Noodles
recipes.description: Wide egg noodles soften quickly, so use their package time as a first check. Save the measured pasta water before draining, then toss the hot noodles with all the butter over low heat.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Kosher Salt (plus more for pasta water)
Water, as needed for boiling noodles

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Bring enough water for the noodles to move freely to a rolling boil in a large pot. Salt the cooking water using the extra salt allowance; keep the measured finishing salt separate. Add the noodles and cook according to the package, checking for tender noodles with a little resistance rather than a hard center. For wide egg noodles with a similar package time, start checking at 7–8 minutes; other shapes or brands may need a different time.
Reserve water: Before draining, scoop out the measured reserved pasta water.

Drain and toss: Drain and return the hot noodles to the pot over low heat. Add all the butter in pieces, the measured reserved water, finishing salt and pepper. Toss for about 30–60 seconds, until the butter has melted and the noodles look glossy. Keep the heat low enough that they do not stick or dry out.
Serve: Scatter with the measured parsley if using and serve promptly alongside braises, stews or saucy mains.

recipes.name: Buttermilk Cornflake Baked Chicken
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken in a tangy buttermilk marinade, baked with a cornflake, Parmesan and thyme coating. Allow at least three hours for marinating.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs (1360 g) bone-in, skin-on chicken pieces: 2 breast halves, 2 thighs, 2 drumsticks and 2 wings; back excluded
75 g peeled yellow onion, thinly sliced
12 g fine salt, for the marinade
150 g plain cornflakes, weighed before crushing into small crumbs

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate ahead: Whisk buttermilk, hot sauce, lemon juice and the twelve grams salt in a food-safe container; add onion, smashed garlic and thyme sprigs. Add the chicken without rinsing it. Use a snug covered container or a food-safe resealable bag set in a dish to keep the marinade against the pieces. Refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for three to twelve hours, turning the closed bag or pieces once if needed for coverage. Wash hands and clean raw-contact surfaces.

Set up the oven: Near the end of the soak, heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a shelf in the center. Line an 18-by-13-inch rimmed sheet pan with foil and place an oven-safe rack on top. Brush the rack with one teaspoon of the measured oil. Check the usable rack area before coating; have a second pan and oven-safe rack ready if all pieces cannot fit with the stated gaps. If using two pans, place shelves in the upper and lower thirds and plan to swap their positions halfway through baking.

Prepare the crumbs: Crush the weighed cornflakes in a bag with a rolling pin until mostly small crumbs, with some texture remaining. Mix in the remaining five teaspoons oil, rubbing lightly to distribute it, then add Parmesan, chopped thyme and pepper. Put half in a shallow dish and keep the other half in a clean bowl to add as needed. The marinade, cereal and cheese supply salt; do not automatically salt the coating as well.

Coat and arrange: Lift chicken from the marinade and remove clinging onion, garlic and thyme stems. Let excess buttermilk drip away, leaving a thin film. Press each piece into the crumb mixture on all sides, adding reserved crumbs to the dish as needed. Press on one thin, even coat and leave excess crumbs in the dish; do not heap them on just to use them up. Place skin-side up on the rack with roughly an inch between pieces. Use a second pan if they would touch. Discard remaining raw-contact marinade, aromatics and crumbs; wash hands and utensils before handling side dishes or cooked food.

Bake and check each piece: Bake without turning the chicken. After thirty minutes, check the breasts, wings and legs individually with a thermometer in the thickest meat, avoiding bone; check more than one spot in large breast halves. Continue baking and recheck as needed until every piece reaches at least 165°F / 74°C, commonly thirty-five to fifty-five minutes total. Remove finished pieces to a clean rack over a plate while the others continue. Thighs and drumsticks can stay longer if you prefer softer dark meat, but do not keep finished breasts in the oven for them. If the crust darkens too quickly, loosely shield that piece with foil. With two pans, swap their shelf positions and rotate front to back around halfway, allowing additional time if needed.

Rest and portion: Let the final pieces rest for five minutes, uncovered so steam can escape. Divide the meat among four diners, sharing breast meat and distributing thighs, drumsticks and wings by appetite; two pieces are not automatically equal portions. Serve the chicken beside the vegetables and mash rather than burying its crust under them. Mixed pieces may finish twenty minutes or more apart; a clean uncovered rack protects the crust but does not keep them hot indefinitely. Have the sides ready near the chicken finish. For closer finish times, use similarly sized bone-in thighs as described in the substitution.
