recipes.name: Chicken Piccata
recipes.description: Thin chicken cutlets with a bright lemon-caper pan sauce. This unfloured version finishes with butter off the heat.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken breasts, for thin cutlets
1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus more if needed
2 tbsp (28 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
2 tbsp brined capers, drained and briefly rinsed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Slice the breasts horizontally into four cutlets and pound between sheets of plastic wrap to an even 1/4 inch. Pat dry and season with the measured salt and pepper.

Sear in batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat. Cook half the cutlets about 2–3 minutes per side, until lightly golden. Transfer to a plate and repeat with the remaining oil and chicken. Lower heat if the pan residue darkens too quickly.

Deglaze: Reduce heat to medium. Stir garlic and capers in the pan for 30 seconds, then add broth. Scrape up golden residue and simmer for about 1 minute. Discard blackened residue rather than incorporating it into the sauce.

Check chicken: Check each cutlet by inserting a thermometer from its side into the center. If any are below 165°F / 74°C, return them and their plate juices to the broth and simmer gently until they reach that temperature. If all are already cooked, add only their plate juices to the broth and bring it back to a simmer. Transfer cooked chicken to a clean platter. Add a little broth if the pan is becoming dry.

Finish off heat: Turn off heat and let vigorous bubbling stop. Add lemon juice and swirl in cold butter a few pieces at a time until glossy. Stir in parsley. Taste before adding any additional seasoning, then spoon the sauce over the chicken and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Chicken Pot Pie
recipes.description: A double-crust chicken pie with tender vegetables, a measured milk-and-stock gravy, and cold butter pastry made from scratch.
recipeIngredient: 300 g all-purpose flour, plus a little for rolling
225 g cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
100–120 ml ice-cold water, added only as needed
450 g cooked boneless chicken, chilled and cut into bite-size pieces (weight after cooking)
1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Make pastry: Mix the 300 g flour and pastry salt in a bowl. Work in cold butter with fingertips or a pastry cutter, leaving a mixture of crumbs and flattened pea-size butter pieces. Toss with 100 ml ice water. Squeeze a handful: if it falls apart, add the remaining water a teaspoon at a time just until it holds. Bring together without kneading smooth. Divide into two discs, one slightly larger for the bottom, wrap, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Do not taste raw dough.

Prepare filling ingredients: While the dough chills, cut carrots and celery into small, even dice. Keep the cooked chicken refrigerated until needed. Measure the filling flour separately from any flour used for pastry or rolling.

Soften vegetables: Melt filling butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery; cook, stirring, about 10–12 minutes until onion is soft and carrot is almost tender. Lower the heat if vegetables begin to brown rapidly.

Thicken gravy: Stir in the 45 g flour, garlic powder, celery seed, salt, and pepper. Cook and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in broth, then milk, scraping the bottom and dispersing the flour mixture. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 3 minutes, stirring, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Fold in chicken and frozen peas. Taste for seasoning, then spread the filling in a shallow heatproof dish to release heat. Refrigerate promptly until cool, about 30–45 minutes in a shallow layer; do not leave it out for the whole dough chill.

Heat oven and roll: Put a sturdy rimmed metal baking sheet on the lower rack and preheat to 425°F / 220°C. On a lightly floured surface, roll the larger dough disc to about a 13-inch circle, roughly 1/8 inch thick. Ease into a deep 9-inch metal pie pan without stretching. Roll the second disc to about 12 inches. If either becomes soft, refrigerate briefly before continuing.

Fill and seal: Spoon cool filling into the lined pan, keeping it below the rim. If your pan cannot hold it, bake excess separately in a small ovenproof dish to 165°F / 74°C. Lay on the top crust, trim to about 1/2 inch beyond the rim, fold the edges together, and crimp. Cut four generous vents in the lid. Brush lightly with beaten egg; discard the remainder. Refrigerate the assembled pie for 10 minutes if the pastry has softened.

Bake through: Place the metal pie pan on the hot baking sheet. Bake 20 minutes at 425°F / 220°C, then reduce to 375°F / 190°C and bake about 30–45 minutes longer. Shield darkening edges with foil as needed. The pastry should be deeply golden and filling should bubble through the vents; also insert a thermometer through a central vent to verify 165°F / 74°C in the middle. Continue baking, loosely covered if necessary, until that endpoint is reached.

Rest and serve: Rest on a rack for 20 minutes, then cut into eight slices. The gravy will settle but remain soft rather than forming a firm slab. A lightly dressed green salad complements the rich pastry.

recipes.name: Chicken Quesadillas with Quick Pico
recipes.description: Folded chicken-and-cheese quesadillas with jalapeño, onion and a cold tomato pico; skillet and griddle routes use the same oil.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb cooked shredded rotisserie chicken or other cooked chicken
8 8-inch flour tortillas, ready-to-eat, for warming; cook raw tortillas separately according to their package before this recipe
2 cups shredded Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese, choose one; freshly shredded if possible
1 jalapeño, minced; seeds removed for a milder filling
Mexican crema or sour cream, as wanted; choose one for serving
lime wedges, as wanted for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Make and chill the pico: Combine ripe tomatoes, onion, jalapeño, fresh cilantro, lime, and kosher salt using the lime juice. Taste, then refrigerate until serving. Count preparation and serving time together: discard cut-tomato salsa left out longer than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C.

Warm the tortillas: Heat a dry skillet over medium-low heat. Warm 8-inch flour tortillas individually until pliable, then keep them wrapped in a clean kitchen towel while assembling. Start with the original 3–4-minute warming range; use pliability as the cue, and allow longer for more tortillas.

Fill and fold: Divide cooked shredded rotisserie chicken or other cooked chicken, shredded Oaxaca or mozzarella cheese, jalapeño, and diced onion evenly among all the measured tortillas, covering half of each and leaving a little border. Fold each tortilla over its filling. Each tortilla makes one folded quesadilla: the original eight tortillas make eight folded quesadillas for four planned portions. For some milder quesadillas, put only chicken and cheese in those and distribute the filling onion and jalapeño among the others; keep the pico separate.

Choose the skillet or griddle: Choose one of these methods and use the full measured vegetable oil across its cooking loads. For a skillet, heat over medium-high, spread a share of the oil in it and add only as many folded quesadillas as fit flat without overlap. Start with 2–3 minutes on the first side and 1–2 minutes on the second. For a griddle, spread the same total oil over its cooking area and start checking at 2–3 minutes per side, cooking in loads if they do not all fit. Use the remaining measured oil between loads. In either method, cook until both faces are golden and the chicken filling reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout; check the center of the filling with a thermometer. If the surface browns first, lower the heat and continue, covering briefly if needed to heat the filling.

Serve with the cold pico: Cut the quesadillas into triangles and divide among the planned portions. Serve promptly with the refrigerated pico and Mexican crema or sour cream and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.name: Chicken Sausage Pasta
recipes.description: Chicken sausage, peppers and spinach in a red-wine tomato sauce, tossed with long pasta and Parmesan.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Italian-style chicken sausage, raw or fully cooked; prepare according to the label and method
1 large bell pepper, stem and seeds removed, sliced into thin strips
9 oz fresh spinach, washed and drained
1 (28 oz) can petite diced San Marzano-style tomatoes, with their juices
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and heat water: Read the sausage label: slice fully cooked links into rounds about 1/2 inch thick, or remove casings from raw links. Slice pepper, mince garlic and grate Parmesan. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season moderately with salt.

Brown sausage: Heat olive oil in a large deep skillet over medium to medium-high. For fully cooked links, add the slices and cook about 5–7 minutes, turning, until browned in patches. For raw sausage, add the meat and break it into small crumbles; cook about 8–12 minutes, stirring, until representative thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. If crowded, brown in rounds with the oil divided between them. Transfer to a clean plate.

Build sauce: Add pepper to the same pan and cook about 4–6 minutes until starting to soften. Stir in garlic and dried basil for 30–45 seconds. Add wine, scrape up browned bits and simmer about 2 minutes. Add all the listed tomatoes and their juices. Simmer uncovered about 10–15 minutes, stirring, until lightly thickened and pepper is tender.

Time the pasta: During the tomato simmer, cook pasta according to its package, tasting near the end. Aim for tender with a little bite; a brief sauce toss follows. Reserve the listed cooking water before draining without rinsing.

Wilt and combine: Return sausage to the sauce and add spinach in handfuls, folding until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Heat the sausage throughout to 165°F / 74°C, then add pasta. Toss over low heat for about 1 minute, adding reserved water in small splashes only if needed for a coating sauce. Use the pasta pot for this stage if the skillet is too full.
Finish: Remove from heat and fold in Parmesan. Add black pepper and taste before adding salt; sausage and cheese already contribute plenty. Divide into the intended portions and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Chicken Scaloppine with Tomato & White Wine
recipes.description: Thin chicken thighs in a light tomato–white wine pan sauce with spinach, finished with a small amount of butter.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, opened flat
1/2 cup (60 g) all-purpose flour, for dredging
3/4 cup (180 ml) unsalted chicken broth, plus more if needed
9 oz (255 g) fresh baby spinach, washed if needed and well dried
1 tbsp (14 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare chicken: Open thighs flat and pound thicker sections gently to about 1/2 inch between sheets of plastic wrap. Season with salt and pepper, dredge lightly in flour, and shake off excess. Discard leftover flour after raw chicken contact.

Brown in batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in uncrowded batches, about 3–4 minutes on the first side and 2–3 on the second, distributing the remaining oil among later batches. Transfer to a plate; the chicken will finish in the sauce. Adjust heat to avoid burning the flour residue.

Cook paste and garlic: Lower heat to medium. Stir tomato paste in the pan for 1–2 minutes until slightly darker and fragrant. Add garlic and stir for 30 seconds. If the pan is dry enough to scorch, loosen with a tablespoon of the measured broth.
Deglaze: Take the pan briefly off the burner to add wine. Return to medium heat, scrape up golden residue, and simmer 2–3 minutes. Add the remaining broth and bring to a gentle simmer.

Finish the chicken: Return chicken and plate juices. Simmer gently about 3–5 minutes, turning pieces, until the thickest centers reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed, adding broth if the sauce becomes too thick. Transfer cooked chicken to a clean platter.

Wilt spinach and finish: Add spinach to the simmering sauce in handfuls, turning until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Simmer briefly if it releases excess water. Turn off heat, let vigorous bubbling stop, and swirl in the butter. Taste and adjust only if needed. Spoon spinach and sauce over the chicken and serve.

recipes.name: Shawarma-style Roast Chicken
recipes.description: Spiced roast chicken thighs finished briefly in a skillet for browned edges, with a measured tahini drizzle.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Reserve 2 tsp olive oil for finishing. Mix the remaining oil with lemon juice, garlic, ground spices, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken, cover, and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or below for 4–24 hours.

Roast and check: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Arrange chicken opened flat with gaps on a foil-lined rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking every thigh at its thickest part for 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed. Meanwhile, prepare the tahini sauce and measure out 1/2 cup for this meal.
Rest and slice: Transfer cooked chicken to a clean board, rest for 5 minutes, and slice across the meat into strips about 1/2 inch wide.

Brown briefly: Heat half the reserved oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the sliced chicken in one layer and leave briefly until some edges brown, about 1–2 minutes, then toss and remove. Repeat with remaining oil and chicken. Stop at browned edges; do not blacken the spices or dry all the strips.
Serve: Divide chicken among four plates and drizzle each with 2 tbsp tahini sauce, or offer the sauce separately. Add pita and a fresh salad if desired; these are additional components.

recipes.name: Chicken Souvlaki
recipes.description: Lemon-oregano chicken skewers with browned edges and a verified center temperature, plus a fresh lemon finish.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into even 1-inch pieces
1 tsp neutral oil, for brushing the grill grates

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Mix olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, garlic, salt, and pepper. Toss with chicken, cover, and refrigerate for 30 minutes to 4 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below.

Prepare grill and skewers: Preheat the grill to medium-high, with a cooler area available. Thread chicken onto about eight skewers without tightly bunching the pieces. Let excess marinade drip off and discard it. Brush clean grates lightly with the measured neutral oil.

Grill: Cook skewers with the lid closed between turns, turning every 2–3 minutes, until browned on several sides, usually about 10–15 minutes. Move them to the cooler area if garlic or oregano darkens too quickly or dripping marinade causes flare-ups.

Verify: Insert a thermometer into several of the largest chicken pieces, keeping its sensing tip in the meat and away from the skewer. Cook until each checked piece reaches 165°F / 74°C; continue as needed rather than relying on carryover from 160°F.
Rest and finish: Move to a clean platter and rest for 5 minutes. Serve with the lemon wedges for a fresh squeeze. A Greek village salad and pita make a fuller meal.

recipes.name: Paprika Chicken Kebabs with Chile-Yogurt Sauce
recipes.description: Skin-on thigh pieces coated with sweet paprika and a little oil, grilled to a measured endpoint and served with a separate tangy chile-yogurt sauce.
recipeIngredient: 1 3/4 lbs (790 g) boneless skin-on chicken thighs, trimmed of loose excess fat; net weight after deboning
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the chicken
6 g fine salt, for the chicken
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 cup (240 g) plain whole-milk Greek yogurt, for the sauce
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the sauce
1/4 tsp cayenne, plus up to 1/4 tsp more to taste
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the sauce
1 tsp neutral oil, for the grill grates or skillet

recipeInstructions.text: Start the grill: For gas, preheat with the lid closed, then set a cooking zone to medium and leave another burner low or off. For charcoal, light the coals and let them establish before arranging them on one side for a direct-heat zone and a cooler side. Follow the grill's lighting instructions. Begin the chicken and sauce while it heats.

Cut and season the chicken: Pat the boneless thighs dry without rinsing. Trim loose excess fat, keeping the attached skin. Cut about twenty-four pieces roughly 1 1/2 inches across, with similar thickness and no thick rolled bundles. Toss with the chicken's two tablespoons olive oil, paprika, six grams fine salt and half the pepper. Cover and refrigerate for fifteen minutes while making the sauce.

Mix a separate sauce: With clean hands and utensils, whisk yogurt, its tablespoon olive oil, lemon juice, the first quarter-teaspoon cayenne, red pepper flakes, sauce salt and remaining pepper in a clean bowl. Taste and add the extra cayenne only if wanted. Cover and refrigerate. Do not dip raw-chicken tools into this bowl or use its serving spoon for the skewers.

Thread and oil the grate: Divide chicken among eight skewers, about three pieces each, keeping pieces unfolded and skin facing outward rather than tucked between meat. Do not compress pieces tightly; leave exposed surfaces available for browning. Let excess oily coating drip back into its bowl and discard the residue. Brush clean grill grates lightly with the measured teaspoon cooking oil, using a folded paper towel held in long tongs. Put out a clean serving platter and clean cooked-food utensils.

Grill and measure: Lay the skewers over moderate direct heat with space between them, starting with the exposed skin toward the grate where possible. Grill about ten to fifteen minutes, turning every two to three minutes after the first surface releases. Move to the cooler zone if skin fat flares or paprika darkens sharply. Close the lid between turns. Begin checking around ten minutes: probe the thickest pieces on every skewer from the side, away from the metal, and continue until they reach at least 165°F / 74°C. Check any unusually large pieces separately. Remove finished skewers rather than waiting for all to reach the endpoint together.

Rest and serve: Transfer to the clean platter and rest five minutes. Serve two skewers per person with the sauce and lemon wedges. The sauce yields roughly one cup plus the oil and lemon additions; offer about a quarter-cup per diner, with any extra on the side. For four plates, add one full four-side batch of either couscous recipe and a vegetable or salad. Those are additional components and preparation time; the two couscous recipes are alternative starches.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, savory, spicy, tangy, entertaining, family-meal, grill

citation.name: Adapted from Jimmy Bannos Jr.'s Chicken Thigh Kebabs with Chile-Yogurt Sauce, published by Food & Wine

recipes.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.description: Broiled yogurt-marinated chicken in a rich tomato-and-cream sauce, with coriander, cumin and a fragrant dried-fenugreek finish.
recipeIngredient: 900 g (about 2 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, weighed after trimming large pieces of fat, cut into 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm chunks
3/4 cup plain full-fat Greek yogurt, unsweetened
1 tbsp finely grated garlic, for the marinade
1 tbsp finely grated ginger, for the marinade
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, for the marinade
1 tsp fine salt, for the marinade
1 tbsp Kashmiri red chile powder, pure ground chile rather than a seasoning blend
1 tsp garam masala, a salt-free ground spice blend, for the marinade
1 tsp neutral oil, for lightly brushing the two cooking racks
2 tbsp unsalted butter, for the onion
1 tbsp neutral oil, for the onion
250 g white or yellow onion, peeled and finely diced
1 tbsp minced garlic, for the sauce
1 tbsp minced ginger, for the sauce
3 cups (720 ml) plain unseasoned tomato passata
1 tbsp white sugar, for the sauce
1 tsp fine salt, for the onion and tomato base
1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for final seasoning; use only as needed
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, reserved only to loosen the sauce as needed
1 cup (240 ml) heavy cream, at least 35% milk fat
1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), measured loosely before crushing
1 tsp white sugar, optional for the final adjustment
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, optional for the final adjustment

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Trim and cut the chicken into pieces about 1 1/2 inches / 4 cm across. Whisk the yogurt, marinade garlic and ginger, marinade lemon juice, marinade salt, Kashmiri chile and marinade garam masala in a bowl. Fold in chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight up to 24 hours. Wash hands, board and tools after handling the raw chicken. Keep the separate rack oil out of the marinade.

Prepare the sauce and pans: Begin about 75 minutes before the chicken's four-hour marinade ends. Dice the onion, measure all sauce ingredients and set aside the finishing ingredients. Prepare the number of foil-lined metal pans and broiler-safe racks needed for your batch: two for the full recipe, one for half or quarter. Lightly brush the racks in use with the listed rack oil, dividing it between them. Keep the chicken refrigerated while making the sauce. Set out a clean covered platter and clean tongs for cooked chicken.

Cook the onion, paste and spices: Heat the onion butter and oil in the heavy pot over medium heat. Add onion and half the initial sauce salt. Cook for 15–20 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and golden. Add tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes, until a shade darker. Lower the heat; stir in the sauce garlic and ginger for 30–60 seconds, then coriander, cumin, turmeric and paprika for 15–20 seconds. Promptly add passata before the ground spices scorch.

Finish the sauce base: Stir in the measured sauce sugar and the remaining initial sauce salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, allowing a few minutes to heat, then cook uncovered for 15–20 minutes, stirring the bottom regularly. Use the water reserve a little at a time only if it becomes too thick to stir easily. The base should be thick and aromatic but still flow from a spoon. Turn off the heat and let bubbling stop. If blending, keep the immersion-blender head submerged and blend carefully until smooth, following the appliance's hot-food instructions; stop the motor before lifting it. Cover the pot off the heat while broiling. During the last ten minutes of the sauce simmer, preheat the broiler to HIGH according to the oven's instructions; do not load chicken until the sauce base is finished and the chicken has marinated four hours.

Load the first batch: Arrange up to about 450 g chicken on the first rack (half the full recipe; all the chicken for a half or quarter recipe) in one layer with spaces between the pieces. Lift it from the marinade, letting excess drip back into the bowl; retain a thin coating rather than wiping it clean. Keep the remaining raw chicken and marinade refrigerated. Place the top of the food about 5–6 inches below the broiler element. Broil only one tray at a time.

Broil through, then repeat: Broil the thighs for about 12–18 minutes total, turning after 6–8 minutes and rotating the tray if the element browns unevenly. Watch throughout. Start temperature checks early: insert a clean instant-read probe from the side into the center of several large pieces, avoiding the rack. Every checked center must reach 165°F / 74°C before removal; take ready pieces out as needed while thicker ones finish. If the surface darkens first, move the tray lower or use the oven finish in troubleshooting. Transfer with clean tongs to the clean platter and cover loosely. If raw chicken remains, load the second prepared rack and broil the same way. Discard any raw marinade once the last batch is loaded. Keep raw utensils away from the cooked platter. Allow a few minutes for loading and temperature checks between the two rounds; do not leave the broiler to prepare another dish. Discard the scorched tray drippings, keeping only the juices that collect on the clean cooked-chicken platter.

Combine and finish: Turn off the broiler. Reheat the sauce base, stirring, until bubbling throughout. Stir in the cream and bring back to a gentle simmer, using any remaining measured water only if necessary. Add all the cooked chicken and its clean-platter juices; stir gently for about 2–4 minutes, until the whole curry is hot and chicken centers reach 165°F / 74°C. Turn off the heat. Taste with a piece of chicken, then add the reserved salt only as needed. Use small amounts of the optional finishing sugar or lemon only if the sauce needs them. Stir in the finishing butter, crush the measured fenugreek leaves between your palms into the pot, and add the finishing garam masala. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

Serve: Divide the chicken evenly among the servings and spoon over the sauce, roughly 1 1/4–1 1/2 cups curry per person. Serve with plain basmati or naan, and small spoonfuls of cucumber raita if wanted. The full basmati recipe provides six rice sides; if also serving naan, start with smaller rice portions and one bread each.

recipes.name: Chicken Tinga
recipes.description: Cooked shredded chicken in smoky chipotle-tomato sauce with charred garlic, sautéed onion, oregano and the existing lime finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb cooked shredded chicken, already poached or rotisserie; cooking raw chicken is a separate preparation
3 garlic cloves, unpeeled for charring; peel before blending
cooking oil, a splash for sautéing the onion
fresh lime juice, a squeeze to finish

recipeInstructions.text: Char the tomatoes and garlic: Heat a heavy dry skillet over medium-high heat. Add large tomatoes and garlic cloves, tomatoes cut-side down. Start checking at 5–7 minutes, turning as needed, until the tomatoes soften with charred patches and the garlic softens inside its skin. Remove individual garlic cloves if ready before the tomatoes; avoid burning them while waiting for the tomatoes.

Cool and peel: Transfer the charred vegetables to a clean plate and let them cool to room temperature before using a countertop blender. Peel the garlic and discard the skins. Blend as soon as the vegetables have cooled; refrigerate them promptly if preparing ahead. Cooling takes additional elapsed time.

Blend the sauce: Blend chipotles in adobo and adobo sauce with all the cooled charred tomatoes and peeled garlic until smooth. Use the lower end of the listed chipotle range for a milder sauce; the adobo sauce remains its separately measured amount. Keep below the blender's marked working capacity and blend in batches if necessary.
Soften the onion: Wipe out the skillet. Add small onion and cooking oil and sauté until the onion is translucent and softened.
Bloom the oregano: Stir in dried oregano and toast for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, before it burns.
Simmer the sauce: Pour the blended sauce into the onion pan. Stir in chicken broth and salt and simmer for about 5 minutes until slightly thickened, stirring to keep the base from catching.

Heat the cooked chicken: Fold cooked shredded chicken through all the sauce. Start checking after about 5 minutes and continue, stirring, until the chicken and sauce reach 165°F / 74°C throughout. Check more than one part of the pan, especially thick clusters of chicken.
Finish and serve: Stir in fresh lime juice and serve the saucy chicken among the planned portions.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, savory, acidic, kid-friendly, saute, simmer, poach, blend

recipes.name: Chicken Tortilla Soup III
recipes.description: This creamy tortilla soup starts with fully cooked chicken and keeps all the half-and-half, condensed soup and creamed corn. Stir along the pot bottom as it heats.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of chicken soup
6 boneless chicken breast halves, fully cooked, skinned and shredded or cut into spoon-sized pieces
3 tbsp fresh cilantro, washed and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Soften aromatics: In a large pot over medium heat, sauté garlic cloves, onion, and margarine for about 5 minutes, until the onion softens. Choose a pot with room for all the liquid, chicken and corn, plus stirring headroom.
Cook flour: Stir in all-purpose flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute.
Add liquid: Gradually stir in chicken broth and half-and-half until the flour disperses. Bring to a boil while stirring along the bottom, then reduce heat to low.

Heat soup: Add condensed cream of chicken soup, fresh salsa, creamed corn, boneless chicken breast halves, ground cumin, dry fajita seasoning, and 2/3 of the fresh cilantro. Heat gently for about 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the finished soup reaches 165°F / 74°C throughout. Check after stirring so a hot edge does not stand in for the whole pot; cold cooked chicken may take longer.

Build bowls: Divide all 1/3 of the fresh cilantro, tortilla chips, and Monterey Jack cheese among the listed portions. Crumble some of the chips into the bowls and add half the cheese; ladle in the hot soup. Finish with the remaining chips and cheese and all the reserved cilantro. At the original eight-portion batch, each bowl gets 1 oz cheese total, half below and half above; use proportional shares for other batches.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, simmer

recipes.name: Chicken with Snow Peas Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Thin chicken slices and crisp snow peas in a light garlic sauce. Prepare separate marinade and sauce bowls before heating the pan.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz (340 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
1 lb (450 g) snow peas, ends and tough strings removed
1 tbsp peanut or neutral oil, divided
2 tbsp water, for briefly steaming the peas if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Coat chicken: Mix the coating teaspoon of cornstarch, teaspoon of soy, and teaspoon of oil. Toss with chicken and refrigerate for 10 minutes while preparing the remaining ingredients.
Mix sauce and trim peas: Whisk all sauce ingredients together in a bowl. Trim snow peas and dry them well. Keep the finishing sesame oil separate.

Cook chicken: Heat 2 tsp of the stir-frying oil in a wide skillet or wok over medium-high heat until shimmering. Spread chicken in one layer, cooking in batches if needed. Leave for about 1 minute, then turn and stir for another 1–2 minutes. Transfer to a plate; it will finish in the sauce.

Cook peas: Add the remaining teaspoon of stir-frying oil. Stir garlic for 15 seconds, then add snow peas and stir-fry 1–2 minutes. If the pods remain hard, add the measured water and cover for 30–60 seconds. Uncover and let excess water evaporate; taste a pea for a crisp-tender bite.

Glaze and verify: Return chicken and any plate juices. Re-stir the sauce so settled starch is suspended, then pour it in. Bring to a simmer, tossing, until glossy, about 1–2 minutes. Check several thick chicken slices from the side with a thermometer, avoiding the pan; they must reach 165°F / 74°C. Cook longer if necessary, removing peas temporarily if they are already tender.
Finish: Turn off heat, stir in sesame oil, and serve promptly with plain rice.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, stir-fry

recipes.name: Turkey and Sweet Potato Chili
recipes.description: Browned ground turkey, tender sweet potato and black beans in a smoky tomato chili, finished with staged lime and measured toppings.
recipeIngredient: 500 g peeled sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
2 tbsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
2 cups (480 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus up to 1 cup (240 ml) only if needed to loosen
2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g total drained
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
1 medium avocado, about 150 g edible flesh, diced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Brown turkey in two batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add half the turkey in loose clumps and leave briefly to brown before breaking it into coarse pieces, about 5–6 minutes total. Transfer to a bowl. Repeat with the remaining oil and turkey. Continue directly with cooking; browning is not the final safety check.

Cook aromatics: With turkey set aside, add onion and sweet-potato cubes to the pot. Cook about 5–7 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until onion softens. If the pan catches, add a small splash from the measured broth. Stir in garlic, chili blend, cumin, paprika and pepper for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add liquid: Return turkey and its juices. Add tomatoes and the initial 480 ml broth, scraping up browned residue. Bring to a gentle simmer. Keep the additional broth for consistency adjustments.

Simmer and check: Partly cover and simmer gently about 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until a potato cube yields easily to a knife. Check several substantial turkey pieces for 165°F / 74°C. Add a little reserved broth if the pot becomes thick before potatoes soften.

Finish beans and consistency: Add drained beans and simmer about 5 minutes until hot. If too thin, uncover briefly to reduce; if too thick, add reserved broth gradually. Avoid cooking until all the potato dissolves.

Season and serve: Turn off heat. Taste and add salt only if needed. Start with half the lime juice, then add the rest to taste. Divide into six bowls. Offer the listed optional topping quantities separately, divided across the whole batch; any bread or slaw is prepared separately.

recipes.name: Chimichurri
recipes.description: Keep parsley and oregano finely chopped but still visible in this Argentine-style herb sauce. Stir the garlic, oil and vinegar through the herbs rather than blending everything to a paste.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley (packed, stems removed)
1/4 cup Fresh Oregano Leaves (or 1 tbsp dried)
1/2 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (adjust to taste)

recipeInstructions.text: Chop: Finely chop parsley and fresh oregano by hand until they are fine, separate pieces. If using the listed dried oregano alternative, add it with the seasonings instead. Mince garlic separately.
Combine: Stir the herbs, garlic, oil, red wine vinegar, red pepper flakes, measured salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Rest: Allow 30 minutes before serving. Rest covered in the refrigerator if preparing ahead; a short room-temperature rest counts toward the total 2 hour limit (1 hour above 90°F /32°C).
Taste: Stir thoroughly and taste; adjust the seasoning only if needed.
Serve and store: Spoon out only what will be served and keep the remainder covered in the refrigerator. Use a clean spoon and keep the stored batch away from raw-meat utensils. Stir before serving.

recipes.keywords: Argentine, acidic, herbaceous, spicy, weeknight, entertaining, grilling, no-cook

recipes.name: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry
recipes.description: Chicken and crisp-tender broccoli with a glossy oyster-sauce coating. Cook the broccoli first and control the sauce thickness at the finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
1 lb (450 g) broccoli, cut into small florets with peeled stems sliced thinly
1/3 cup (80 ml) water, for steaming broccoli
2 tbsp peanut or neutral oil, divided

recipeInstructions.text: Coat chicken: Combine the coating wine, cornstarch, and light soy. Toss with chicken and refrigerate for 10 minutes while preparing broccoli and aromatics.
Mix sauce: Whisk oyster sauce, the sauce wine, dark soy, stock, sugar, and sauce cornstarch in a bowl. Set beside the stove.

Steam broccoli: Put broccoli and the measured steaming water in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Cover and steam about 2–3 minutes, until stems are nearly tender with a little resistance. Add another splash of water and more time if needed. Transfer broccoli to a plate, drain excess water, and carefully wipe the pan dry with a towel held in tongs.

Cook chicken: Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Spread half the chicken in one layer; cook about 1 minute before turning and tossing another 1–2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with 2 tsp oil and remaining chicken. Add the last teaspoon of oil, garlic, and ginger to the pan and stir for 20–30 seconds, reducing heat if needed to prevent scorching.

Finish together: Return chicken, its plate juices, and broccoli. Re-stir sauce thoroughly and pour it in. Bring to a simmer and toss 1–2 minutes until glossy. Check several of the thickest chicken slices reach 165°F / 74°C, probing from the side and keeping off the pan. Continue cooking if necessary, adding a tablespoon of water if the sauce thickens too far; lift broccoli out temporarily if already tender.
Serve: Transfer to a platter immediately. Serve with plain rice, with cucumber salad optional alongside.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, American, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, kid-friendly, quick-lunch, steam, stir-fry

recipes.name: Chicken & Broccoli with Lap Cheong Rice
recipes.description: A complete meal of savory chicken and broccoli over jasmine rice folded with cooked Chinese sausage.
recipeIngredient: 2 1/2 cups (600 ml) water, for the rice
3 oz (85 g) Chinese pork sausage (lap cheong), requiring cooking
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, for cooking the sausage, plus more if needed
2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
600 g broccoli, cut into small florets with peeled stems thinly sliced
2 medium yellow onions (about 300 g total), sliced
1/3 cup (80 ml) water, for steaming broccoli
1/4 cup (60 ml) dry sherry or Shaoxing wine
2 tbsp cold water, for the slurry

recipeInstructions.text: Start rice: Rinse rice in several changes of cool water and drain well. Combine with the measured rice water in a saucepan with a tight lid. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat, stir once, cover, and reduce to low. Cook about 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed. Turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes, then check a grain is tender. Follow the troubleshooting note if it needs more water or time.

Cook sausage separately: Meanwhile, place whole lap cheong links in a small lidded skillet with the measured sausage water. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook gently, turning occasionally, about 15–20 minutes or longer if the package requires it. Keep a little water in the pan. Verify the sausage centers reach 160°F / 71°C by probing from an end toward the center. Once cooked, transfer to a clean board, slice into thin coins, and fold into the finished rice. Keep covered briefly until the chicken is ready.

Prepare sauce and slurry: Mix soy, oyster sauce, and stock in a bowl. Keep the wine separate. In another small bowl, mix cornstarch with its cold water. Cut chicken and vegetables, using separate clean utensils and surfaces for ready-to-eat components.

Steam broccoli: Add broccoli and its measured steaming water to a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Cover for 2–3 minutes until almost tender through the stems, extending as needed for larger pieces. Remove broccoli, drain excess water, and dry the pan carefully.

Brown chicken and onions: Season chicken with pepper. Heat 2 tsp oil over medium-high heat and cook half the chicken for about 4–5 minutes. Transfer to a plate and repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken. Add the final 2 tsp oil and onions; cook 4–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and stir 30 seconds. Take the pan briefly off heat to add wine, then return to heat and simmer 1–2 minutes, scraping up golden residue.

Finish chicken: Add stock-sauce mixture, chicken, and plate juices. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 5–8 minutes, stirring, until several of the largest chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed before adding broccoli.

Glaze: Return broccoli. Re-stir slurry and add about half while stirring the simmering sauce. Simmer for 1 minute, then add more slurry only if needed for a light coating, simmering again after each addition. Taste before deciding whether additional seasoning is needed; soy, oyster sauce, and sausage already supply salt.

Serve: Divide the sausage rice among six bowls and top with chicken, broccoli, and sauce. Serve promptly. The wine is an ingredient in the sauce; a short simmer does not make it reliably alcohol-free.

recipes.name: Chili-Bean Eggplant with Pork
recipes.description: Tender eggplant with a small amount of ground pork, fermented chili-bean paste, garlic and a bright vinegar finish.
recipeIngredient: 600 g Chinese or Japanese eggplant, ends trimmed, cut into 1/2-inch-thick bite-sized pieces
4 tbsp water, for covered eggplant cooking, divided, plus more by the tablespoon if needed
1 tbsp (15 g) la doubanjiang, fermented broad-bean chili paste, chopped if coarse
30 g scallions, sliced, white and green parts separated
1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted vegetable stock or water
1 tsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured cold slurry water
2 tsp cold water, for the cornstarch slurry
2 tbsp unseasoned rice vinegar, divided and partly added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Cut the eggplant evenly and divide into two batches. Mix stock, soy sauce, wine and sugar in a bowl. Mix cornstarch with its separate cold water. Keep doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and scallion whites ready; reserve greens for finishing.

Cook the eggplant: Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high in a lidded skillet. Brown half the eggplant for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally. Lower to medium, add 2 tbsp water and cover for another 3–5 minutes, until the center yields readily to a fork. Add a tablespoon more water if needed. Uncover to evaporate excess, then transfer to a plate. Repeat with another tablespoon oil, the second half of the eggplant and remaining 2 tbsp water.

Cook pork: Add the final tablespoon oil and pork. Cook over medium-high about 4–6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until cooked through and reaching 160°F / 71°C. For a reading, gather a small mound and insert the probe without touching the pan.

Flavor the base: Lower heat to medium-low. Stir in doubanjiang and ginger for about 30 seconds, then garlic and scallion whites for another 20–30 seconds. Pour in the stock mixture before the garlic burns. Simmer about 1 minute.

Coat: Stir the slurry again and add half. Simmer 20–30 seconds, then fold in eggplant. Add the remaining slurry only if needed for a light coating and discard any unused portion. Cook gently another minute, adding a tablespoon water if the sauce becomes tight.

Finish and serve: Stir in 1 tbsp vinegar and the sesame oil, then fold in scallion greens off heat. Taste and add remaining vinegar only if wanted. Serve as four shared sides with plain rice and other vegetables; use the pork-free variation for a vegetable-only table.

recipes.keywords: Sichuan-inspired, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, comfort-food, saute, steam, simmer

recipes.name: Garlic-Ginger Stir-Fry Sauce
recipes.description: A cooked garlic-ginger sauce with measured soy, vinegar and a light starch body, portioned for vegetables or stir-fries.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup (120 ml) unsalted vegetable broth or water
1 tbsp oyster sauce or vegetarian mushroom stir-fry sauce
2 tsp cold water, for the slurry
Hot water, only as needed to bring the finished sauce to 240 ml

recipeInstructions.text: Measure: Mix broth, both soy sauces, oyster or mushroom sauce, wine, sugar and white pepper. In a separate cup, stir the cornstarch into the 2 tsp cold slurry water.
Cook aromatics: Warm neutral oil in a small saucepan over medium-low. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 30–45 seconds, until fragrant but still pale. Lower heat if the edges start coloring.

Simmer and thicken: Add the broth mixture and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook about 1 minute. Stir the slurry again and pour it in while stirring. Simmer 30–60 seconds, until lightly thickened with no chalky starch taste. Do not reduce to a sticky syrup.

Finish and measure: Take off heat; stir in vinegar and sesame oil. Carefully pour into a heatproof measuring jug. Add a little hot water, if needed, to reach 240 ml. If the sauce exceeds 240 ml, return it to the saucepan and simmer briefly to the stated yield, then measure again.

Use or chill: Use 120 ml as the starting portion for the linked 600 g garlic-eggplant recipe. For other cooked vegetables or protein, begin with a little sauce and add only enough to coat; their moisture and seasoning differ. Half this recipe makes the 120 ml needed for one eggplant batch. Chill unused sauce promptly in a shallow container.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American-inspired, savory, acidic, umami, sweet, weeknight, meal-prep, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Chinese Sausage Fried Rice
recipes.description: Cold, separated rice is easier to toss without crushing it. Cook the eggs into ribbons before combining them with the sausage and rice.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups cooked jasmine rice, cold, properly refrigerated
5 Chinese sausages (lap cheong), thinly sliced after any package-required preparation

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the rice: Break up cooked jasmine rice gently. Keep it cold until ready to add it to the pan. The listed amount is cooked rice, not dry rice.

Make the egg ribbons: Use large eggs, 1/2 of the toasted sesame oil, and 1/3 of the peanut oil for this stage. Whisk the eggs with their half of the sesame oil. Use the egg-stage peanut oil across the omelet batches. In a hot wok, cook thin omelets with roughly one-third of the original three-egg mixture at a time, adjusting the number of omelets for the listed quantity. Cook until fully set without liquid egg; an egg-dish center is 160°F / 71°C. Move to a clean board, roll and slice into ribbons. Set aside.

Cook the sausage: Use Chinese sausages (lap cheong), green onions, and 2/3 of the peanut oil for this stage. Add this stage’s peanut oil to the wok. Add the prepared sausage and all the green onions. Stir-fry over medium-high heat until browned and the labeled cooking requirements are met; 2–3 minutes is a browning check, not proof raw sausage is cooked. Reduce the heat if sugars scorch.
Add the aromatics: Add garlic cloves and red chili and stir-fry for about a minute until fragrant, lowering the heat if the garlic catches. Omit the chili or serve it separately for milder portions.
Fry the rice: Add the separated rice and turn it over high heat in an uncrowded pan, pressing out remaining clumps gently. Work in batches rather than packing the wok; 2–3 minutes is a first check.

Season and heat through: Add frozen peas, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and 1/2 of the toasted sesame oil, including the remaining half of the sesame oil. Toss until peas and rice are hot throughout, checking the cold-rice mixture at 165°F / 74°C in several places. Do not stop at a fixed two-minute clock if cold clumps remain.
Fold and serve: Fold in all the fully cooked egg ribbons and serve promptly among the listed portions. More omelets, sausage preparation or rice batches lengthen the schedule.

recipes.name: Steamed Fish
recipes.description: Whole steamed fish has a short, thickness-dependent cooking window. Ginger and wine season the fish before steaming; a separate clean soy mixture and hot oil finish it.
recipeIngredient: 1 (1 1/2 lb) Whole fish (snapper or sea bass), scaled, gutted, gills removed; original-size fish
1 Fresh ginger piece, original 2-inch piece, peeled and julienned
2 tbsp Peanut or other high-heat oil
3 tbsp Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine
Water for steaming, as needed with the plate above the water

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the fish: Prepare Whole fish (snapper or sea bass), 1/2 of the Fresh ginger piece, and 1/3 of the Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine. Keep fish cold until the steamer is ready and thaw frozen fish in the refrigerator, following any vacuum-package opening instructions. Rinse the ginger, scallions and cilantro under running water before cutting and drain well, keeping garnish tools separate from raw fish. Pat the cleaned fish dry. Place the ginger portion assigned here over the fish; retain its other half for the finish. Drizzle the wine portion assigned here over the fish; the remaining wine belongs to the sauce.

Mix the sauce: Combine Light soy sauce, 2/3 of the Shaoxing or Chinese rice wine, Water for sauce, Toasted sesame oil, Rock sugar, and White-pepper dashes in a clean bowl until the powdered sugar dissolves. This sauce is separate from the raw-fish plate; do not dip raw-contact utensils into it.

Steam: Use Water for steaming under a stable rack and heatproof fish plate, with a lid that closes. Bring the water to a boil before inserting the cold fish. Cover and begin checking around 8–10 minutes; continue until thick flesh reaches 145°F /63°C away from bone, is no longer translucent and separates easily. Fish thickness and plate loads change the time; use additional uncrowded plates or batches rather than piling fish.

Drain: Turn off the steam, lift the plate carefully with heat protection and discard the collected steaming liquid. Keep the cooked fish on a clean heatproof plate; do not return it to raw-contact dishes.
Add aromatics: Rinse and drain 1/2 of the Fresh ginger piece and Scallions well, then arrange over the hot fish. Use all the scallion threads and the retained half of the ginger.

Hot oil: Heat Peanut or other high-heat oil in a small dry pan over controlled heat until hot and shimmering, without keeping it smoking. Carefully pour over the well-drained aromatics, keeping face and hands clear of splashes.

Heat the sauce: Reduce the pan heat and carefully add the entire clean prepared sauce to the oil pan, allowing for splatter. Bring the sauce to a bubble and stir until the sugar is fully dissolved, then pour all of it over the cooked fish. Do not add another dose of oil or wine.

Serve: Garnish with Fresh cilantro leaves and serve promptly. Four portions are the original whole-fish planning yield, including bones. For larger batches use additional original-size fish with adequate plate capacity; smaller batches need appropriate fish portions and earlier center checks. Ingredient arithmetic does not multiply the steaming clock.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, entertaining, light-and-fresh, steam

recipes.name: Chinese-Style Snapper
recipes.description: This covered whole-snapper preparation uses ginger, garlic and a soy-wine dressing, followed by a hot peanut-oil finish. Slashes expose thicker flesh to the seasoning; they do not guarantee that every fish cooks in the same time.
recipeIngredient: 1.8 kg Whole Snapper, scaled and gutted

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat the oven to 425°F /220°C. Choose a roasting pan that holds the original-size whole snapper without bending it; for multiples use additional pans. Line it with foil and nonstick baking parchment rated for the temperature, keeping the paper inside the covered pan.

Slash: Use a scaled, gutted fish with the gills removed. Pat the inside and outside dry, keeping raw-contact tools separate from the serving platter. Cut three approximately 1-cm-deep slashes into the thick flesh on each side. Put it in the pan. Rinse fresh ginger, scallions and cilantro under running water as appropriate and drain thoroughly.
Season: Spread all the garlic and half the listed ginger into and over the slits. Mix all the soy sauce, broth, rice wine and sesame oil and pour over the fish.

Bake: Cover the pan tightly with foil. Begin checking before the original 45–50-minute planning range is complete and continue as needed until thick flesh on both sides reaches 145°F /63°C without touching bone, and is no longer translucent and separates easily. Fish thickness, starting temperature and pan load change the time.

Transfer: With broad spatulas, carefully move the cooked fish to a warmed heatproof platter. Reserve all the cooking juices in the roasting pan, taking care with steam. Put all the scallions and the remaining ginger on the fish.

Oil: Heat all the peanut oil in a small dry saucepan over controlled heat until hot and shimmering; do not maintain smoking oil. Carefully pour it over the well-drained scallions and ginger, keeping hands and face clear of splashes.

Finish: Check the reserved raw-contact pan juices at 145°F /63°C before pouring them over the cooked fish. If needed, return the pan to the oven or transfer juices to a saucepan to finish heating. Add all the cilantro and serve promptly. When scaling, use additional original-size fish and roomy pans; do not multiply the oven clock or assume a fractional fish has the same geometry.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, savory, umami, entertaining, weekend-project, bake, roast, steam

recipes.name: Chipotle Pork Bowls
recipes.description: This bowl pairs broth-cooked polenta with smoky ground pork, separately charred corn, cotija, cabbage and pepitas. Cook the frozen corn according to its package before the brief browning stage; char alone is not proof that a ready-to-cook product is cooked.
recipeIngredient: 1 Red bell pepper, washed, stemmed, seeded and diced
Cooking oil, as needed for the pork skillet
Salt, to taste in the cooked pork sauce
Black pepper, to taste in the cooked pork sauce
1 Lime, washed and cut into wedges
1 cup Green cabbage, washed and shredded

recipeInstructions.text: Cook and enrich polenta: Have Dry polenta or cornmeal, Chicken broth, Ground cumin, Unsalted butter, and Cotija cheese ready. Bring the measured broth to a boil, gradually whisk in the polenta and cumin, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Cook, whisking frequently to prevent sticking, until the grains are tender and no longer gritty. Begin checks after 15 minutes, using the actual polenta’s package cooking guidance; coarse grinds can take substantially longer. Once tender, stir in all the butter and cotija. Cover and keep gently hot while the pork finishes.

Cook then char corn: Cook Frozen sweet corn according to its package’s required instructions, then drain well if wet. Use a heavy skillet suitable for dry browning and spread the cooked kernels in a manageable single layer. Brown over medium-high heat, beginning checks after about 2 minutes, then stir to color another face. Stop before kernels turn black or dry out. Transfer the whole cooked corn amount to a clean dish; keep it separate from the polenta for this version.

Cook pork and pepper: Have Ground pork, Red bell pepper, and Cooking oil ready. Add the cooking-oil allowance to the skillet only as needed, then cook the pork and pepper over medium-high heat, breaking the meat into crumbles and turning to cook it evenly. Use manageable loads if crowded. Continue until the pork reaches 160°F /71°C, measured in several thicker clusters; browning or a 3-minute crust clock alone does not establish the endpoint.

Add aromatics and adobo: Lower the heat if needed and push the cooked meat aside enough to add Garlic cloves, Dried oregano, Chipotle peppers in adobo, and Adobo sauce to the skillet. Stir briefly until fragrant, starting checks after about 45 seconds; stop before the garlic darkens. Include the full measured adobo sauce as well as the minced peppers.

Simmer and season: Add Salt, Black pepper, and Fire-roasted crushed tomatoes, using the salt and pepper allowances after tasting the fully cooked sauce. Scrape the browned bits into the tomatoes and simmer gently, beginning checks after about 5 minutes, until the sauce coats the pork. Keep the pork hot while the polenta finishes; extend cooking as needed instead of serving gritty grains to meet the header time.

Assemble bowls: Divide the hot polenta and pork across the listed portions, add the separate charred corn and finish with Avocado, Lime, Green cabbage, Pepitas, and Sour cream. Offer the lime wedges at the table; Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, sweet, acidic, smoky, weeknight, comfort-food, fry, simmer

recipes.name: Chocolate Blended Oats with Raspberry Chia Jam
recipes.description: This is ideal for meal-prep breakfasts. Blending standard rolled oats transforms them into a smooth, cake-like batter.

recipeInstructions.text: The Jam: Place raspberries in a microwave-safe bowl. Heat until they break down into a compote. Stir in 1 tbsp chia seeds and let sit for 5 minutes to thicken.
The Base: Combine all blended oats ingredients in a high-powered blender. Blend for 60 seconds until perfectly smooth.
Layer: Divide the raspberry jam among 4 jars. Pour the blended oat mixture over the jam.
The Cap: Drizzle the melted dark chocolate over the top of each jar to create a Crunch layer.
The Finish: Seal the jars and refrigerate for at least 90 minutes (or ideally overnight). The mixture will firm up significantly as the oats and chia seeds absorb the liquid.
Serve: These keep for up to 5 days. Eat cold straight from the jar.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, umami, meal-prep, snack, weekend-project, blend

recipes.name: Chocolate Bread Pudding
recipes.description: Bread pudding is a way to honor stale bread - brioche is rich and tender, so it soaks up custard without becoming mushy. The double chocolate (bittersweet and white) creates complexity: dark chocolate for depth, white chocolate for sweetness.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spray eight 6-oz ramekins (or a 9x13 baking dish) with non-stick spray.
The Mix: In a large bowl, toss the brioche cubes with the chopped bittersweet chocolate and white chocolate chips.
The Custard: In a mixer, beat eggs, 1/2 cup sugar, and vanilla until pale. Gradually whisk in the heavy cream and milk until smooth.
The Soak: Pour the custard over the bread mixture. Toss gently to coat. Let stand for 15 minutes to allow the brioche to hydrate.
Assemble: Transfer the mixture to the prepared ramekins, spreading evenly. Drizzle the remaining 4 tbsp of sugar over the tops.
Bake: Bake for 15-20 minutes until the edges are golden and the custard is set in the center but still has a slight wobble.
Serve: Serve warm with a generous scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake, no-cook

recipes.name: Chocolate Chia Pudding
recipes.description: The secret to smooth chia pudding is the blender method. Many recipes leave the seeds whole, which can result in a gritty, uneven texture.
recipeIngredient: Fresh Berries, Chocolate Chips, or Chopped Nuts

recipeInstructions.text: Blend: Combine almond milk, chia seeds, maple syrup, cocoa powder, vanilla, and salt in a high-powered blender.
Pulverize: Start on low and gradually increase to high. Blend for 60 seconds until the mixture is completely smooth and the seeds have disappeared.
The Finish: Transfer the mixture to individual jars or a large bowl. Cover and refrigerate for at least 3 hours (or overnight) until thick and set.
Serve: Stir once before serving. Top with fresh berries and nuts for Textural Balance.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, comfort-food, blend

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Beet Muffins
recipes.description: Beet puree, cocoa and chocolate chips make a thick, scoopable batter. Fold only until the flour disappears, and check the center rather than judging doneness by the dark color.
recipeIngredient: Whole milk, a little more only if needed for a scoopable batter
Additional chocolate chips, optional, for topping
Butter or baking spray, as needed for greasing if not using liners

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line a standard 12-cup muffin tin, or grease it with the listed pan allowance. Use smooth prepared beet puree: blend drained plain canned beets, or blend already roasted beets once cool enough for your blender according to its instructions. Let any warm puree and melted butter cool before adding the eggs. Beet roasting and its cooling are separate advance preparation.
Wet mix: Whisk beet puree, eggs, melted butter, honey and brown sugar together, then whisk in the listed whole milk.

Dry mix: Whisk flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt together, then fold into the wet mixture just until no dry flour remains. The batter should be thick and scoopable. If it is too stiff to scoop, fold in a little of the separate extra-milk allowance at a time; stop before it becomes pourable.
Fold: Fold all the listed semisweet chocolate chips into the batter.
Fill: Divide among the muffin cups, filling no more than ¾ full. Sprinkle on the separate optional topping chips. Bake any excess batter in additional cups or a later batch.
Bake: Bake for 18–22 minutes, until a center tester comes out without wet batter; melted chocolate on the tester is different from raw batter.
Cool: Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Cool completely before sealing for storage.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, umami, rich, kid-friendly, meal-prep, weekend-project, bake, roast

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Cookie Cake
recipes.description: The key to a cookie cake is using chocolate discs rather than standard chips. This creates larger pools of molten chocolate that integrate into the dough.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (2 sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line a 14-inch round pizza pan with parchment paper.
Cream: In a large bowl, cream unsalted butter, light brown sugar, and granulated sugar until light and fluffy, about 3–5 minutes.
Add eggs: Add large eggs and vanilla extract and beat until combined.
Dry mix: Whisk all-purpose flour, baking soda, and sea salt together, then stir into the butter mixture until just combined.
Fold: Fold in semisweet chocolate discs and candy-coated milk chocolate candies.
Shape: Spread dough evenly onto the prepared pan, leaving a 1/2-inch border for expansion. Sprinkle candy-coated milk chocolate candies over the top, pressing them in lightly.

Bake: Bake for 20–25 minutes until the edges are deep golden brown and the center is set but still soft. Keep the same dough thickness when scaling; use additional pans, rather than multiplying pan dimensions or baking time.
Cool: Let cool completely in the pan before slicing so the structure can firm up.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Zucchini Muffins
recipes.description: Buckwheat gives these chocolate-chip muffins a nutty flavor; whole-wheat flour is a separate listed choice with a different crumb. Squeeze excess liquid from the shredded zucchini, then stir only enough to incorporate the flour and shreds.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Zucchini, shredded and squeezed in a towel to remove excess liquid
1/2 cup Milk of choice (Soy or Almond preferred)
Butter or baking spray, as needed for greasing if not using liners

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin tin with the pan allowance, or use liners. Prepare the listed shredded zucchini by squeezing excess liquid out in a clean towel.
Dry mix: Whisk the chosen buckwheat or whole-wheat flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon and salt together.
Wet mix: Whisk milk, egg, the chosen maple syrup or honey, the chosen avocado or canola oil, and vanilla together.
Combine: Stir the wet mixture into the dry just until no dry flour remains. Do not beat the batter or keep stirring to make it perfectly smooth.
Fold: Fold in all the chocolate chips and squeezed zucchini until distributed.
Bake: Fill muffin cups no more than ¾ full; use additional cups or a later batch for excess batter. Bake 16–18 minutes, until a center tester comes out without wet batter.
Cool: Leave in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack. Cool completely before sealing for storage.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, umami, rich, kid-friendly, meal-prep, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Chocolate Chip Walnut Cookies
recipes.description: Dissolve the baking soda in the listed hot water before adding it to this walnut-and-chocolate dough. Keep the portions similar in size and leave room for them to spread; browned edges and a center that has set are more useful than a timer alone.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F / 175°C. Set out ungreased baking sheets and a cooling rack.
Cream: Beat the softened butter with the white sugar and packed brown sugar until smooth and creamy, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then mix in the vanilla.
Dissolve: In a small cup, dissolve the baking soda in the listed hot water. Stir this mixture and the salt into the butter mixture.

Mix and portion: Stir in the flour just until no dry pockets remain, then distribute the chocolate chips and chopped walnuts throughout. Drop similarly sized large spoonfuls onto the ungreased sheets, leaving about 2 inches between portions. Keep dough waiting for later trays covered and refrigerated.

Bake: Load the oven only once it has reached temperature. Bake for about 10 minutes per tray, until the edges are browned and the centers have set but remain soft. Check the first tray closely; scoop size and your pan affect the time. Bake the remaining dough in further loads as needed.
Cool: Let the cookies firm on the sheet until they can be lifted intact, then transfer them to a rack. Let the sheets cool before loading more dough. Cool the cookies completely before packing them.

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Chocolate Crinkle Cookies
recipes.description: A firm, chilled dough is easier to portion and coat. Roll each ball in granulated sugar first and powdered sugar second, then bake until the coating cracks and the edges feel firm.

recipeInstructions.text: Melt: Set a heatproof bowl above gently simmering water, with its bottom clear of the water. Melt the chopped chocolate and salted butter together, stirring until smooth. Remove the bowl from the pan and let the mixture cool slightly before adding it to the eggs.
Dry mix: Whisk the flour, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and kosher salt until evenly mixed and free of lumps.

Beat: Beat the brown sugar, eggs, vanilla and one-third of the listed granulated sugar on medium-high until light and smooth, about 2–3 minutes. For the original batch, that sugar portion is 1/2 cup; reserve the other two-thirds for rolling.

Combine: Mix the slightly cooled chocolate-butter mixture into the egg mixture. On low speed, add the dry ingredients only until the dough is evenly combined. Cover and refrigerate for 2–4 hours, until firm enough to scoop and roll.

Prepare and coat: Near the end of chilling, preheat the oven to 350°F. Line baking sheets with parchment. Put the reserved two-thirds of the granulated sugar in one shallow bowl and all the powdered sugar in another. Scoop about 1 tablespoon of dough per cookie, form balls, and coat first with granulated sugar and then generously with powdered sugar. Leave about 2 inches between balls. Keep unportioned dough refrigerated while later trays wait.

Bake: Once the oven reaches 350°F, bake for 10–12 minutes per tray, until the tops have cracked and the edges feel firm. Use further loads as needed; do not crowd the sheets to force a particular count.
Cool: Leave the cookies on the sheet for 5 minutes, then move them to racks to cool completely. Let a hot sheet cool before loading another batch. Discard coating sugar that has contacted raw dough.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Chocolate Pie
recipes.description: This chocolate cream pie uses a cooked pudding filling. Stir until it bubbles and thickens, then take it off the heat before melting in the chopped chocolate.
recipeIngredient: 1 Pie Crust, baked and cooled (Use the [Apple Pie](/mise/recipes/apple-pie) Vodka Hack dough!)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: Have the baked, cooled crust and chopped chocolate ready before heating the filling. In a medium saucepan, whisk together sugar, cornstarch, and salt.
Emulsify: Slowly whisk in the milk and egg yolks until the mixture is perfectly smooth.

The Cook: Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the mixture begins bubbling and becomes thick and glossy like pudding. Start checking around 6-8 minutes, but continue if still thin; the texture, not the clock, determines when to stop.
The Melt: Remove from heat immediately. Stir in the chopped bittersweet chocolate, butter, and vanilla. Whisk until the chocolate is completely melted and the filling is uniform.

The Finish: Pour the hot filling into the cooled pie crust without overfilling; refrigerate any extra pudding separately in small dishes. Press a piece of plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the pudding to prevent a "skin" from forming.
Chill: Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, keeping the wrap against the surface, until the filling is cold and set.
Serve: Top with billowy whipped cream and shaved chocolate for contrast.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, boil

recipes.name: Chocolate Protein Zucchini Muffins
recipes.description: Measure the listed zucchini amount after grating, squeezing very dry and packing it tightly. This cocoa-and-protein-powder batter is different from the buckwheat zucchini muffins; fold briefly and check the center rather than relying on dark color.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup grated zucchini, squeezed very dry and packed tightly (measure after grating and squeezing)
¼ cup honey or maple syrup
¼ cup unsalted butter (melted, or use canola or avocado oil)
½ cup chocolate chips (or 1 cup blueberries or up to 1 cup chocolate chips)
Nonstick spray or butter, for greasing the muffin pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Grease a standard 12-cup muffin pan with the listed spray or butter. Grate zucchini, squeeze very dry in a clean towel, then measure the listed amount packed tightly.
Dry mix: Whisk flour, chocolate protein powder, cocoa, optional cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda and salt together.
Wet mix: Whisk squeezed zucchini, milk, the chosen honey or maple syrup, eggs, the chosen melted and slightly cooled butter or canola or avocado oil, and vanilla together.

Fold: Fold the dry mixture into the wet just until no dry flour remains. Fold in the chosen chocolate chips or blueberries. The original 12-muffin batch uses ½ cup chips, or 1 cup blueberries, or up to 1 cup chips; follow the corresponding listed scaled choice and use only one.

Bake and cool: Fill muffin cups no more than ¾ full, using extra cups or a later batch for excess batter. Bake about 16–18 minutes, until a center tester comes out without wet batter. Cool briefly in the pan, then transfer to a rack to cool to room temperature before storage.

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Chocolate Soufflé
recipes.description: This classic dessert requires careful technique. The secret to a tall, even rise is the thumb-run: after filling the dish, you must run your thumb around the inside rim to create a small channel.

recipeInstructions.text: The Ladder: Preheat oven to 375°F. Generously butter a 6-cup soufflé dish. Coat with 1 tbsp sugar, knocking out the excess.
The Base: Melt chocolate in a heatproof bowl over simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from heat and whisk in the egg yolks - the mixture will stiffen, which is expected.
The Meringue: In a clean bowl, beat egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add 1/3 cup sugar, beating until the whites are stiff and glossy.
The Lighten: Stir about 1 cup of the meringue into the stiff chocolate base to loosen it.
The Fold: Gently fold the remaining meringue into the chocolate using a "cut and fold" motion to preserve the air bubbles.
The Thumb-Run: Spoon the batter into the dish. Run your thumb around the inside edge of the dish to create a shallow groove.
Bake: Bake in the middle of the oven for 24-26 minutes until puffed and crusted on top but still having a slight "jiggle" in the center.
Serve: Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately with lightly sweetened whipped cream.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, rich, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, date-night, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Chocolate Vanilla Swirl Layer Cake
recipes.description: The white batter gets its own flour and milk additions, while the chocolate half gets cocoa and a separate milk addition. Equal alternating pours in the center create the swirls.
recipeIngredient: all-purpose flour, as needed for dusting pans
2 tbsp dark cocoa powder, level measures
white chocolate, as desired for drizzling, melted, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare pans: Use butter and all-purpose flour to grease and lightly flour two 8- or 9-inch round pans for the original batch. Heat the oven to 325°F.
Mix dry batter ingredients: Whisk all-purpose flour, cake flour, baking powder, and sea salt together. Keep the separate white-batter flour aside.

Cream and add eggs: Using unsalted butter, superfine sugar, large eggs, and vanilla extract, cream the softened butter and sugar until pale and fluffy, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs one at a time until incorporated, then the vanilla.
Combine and divide: Alternate the shared dry mixture and whole milk in several additions, beginning and ending with the dry mixture, just until smooth. Divide the batter equally between two bowls.
Finish white batter: Whisk all-purpose flour and whole milk into one half of the batter until smooth.
Finish chocolate batter: Whisk dark cocoa powder and whole milk into the other half until smooth.

Build swirls and bake: Alternate small equal scoops of white and chocolate batter directly into the center of each pan until both batches of batter have been used. About 1/3 cup per pour is an original-batch patterning guide, not a dose multiplied by the ingredient scaler. Bake at 325°F, starting checks around 35 minutes for the original pans; rotate partway through if the oven browns unevenly. Centers should be set and a tester should have no wet batter. Cool in pans on racks 5 minutes, then turn out and cool completely.

Make ganache: For bittersweet chocolate and heavy cream, heat the cream in a heavy saucepan just until about to boil. Pour over all the chopped bittersweet chocolate in a heatproof bowl and wait 5 minutes. Stir gently in one direction until smooth and glossy. Cool until spreadable; refrigerate if needed and while waiting for the cakes, stirring occasionally. Do not hold the cream ganache on the counter throughout a long cooling schedule.

Layer, frost and chill: Level the fully cool cakes, then cut each into two even layers for four layers altogether. Spread some ganache between each layer and all the remaining ganache over the top and sides. Drizzle white chocolate (if using) over the finished cake if desired. Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before slicing.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, entertaining, bake, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Cilantro-Lime Rice
recipes.description: Tender jasmine rice finished with cilantro and lime after a covered rest, with practical checks for water absorption and seasoning.
recipeIngredient: 180 g jasmine rice (about 1 cup), rinsed and well drained
1 1/4 cups (300 ml) water, plus water for rinsing
15 g fresh cilantro leaves and tender stems, finely chopped
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tbsp more to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water until noticeably less cloudy, then drain well in a fine-mesh strainer. A little cloudiness is fine; do not soak it while preparing the other ingredients.

Heat and cover: Put drained rice, the measured water and salt in a heavy 2-quart saucepan. Stir once, bring to a gentle boil, then cover snugly and reduce to low. Cook at a gentle simmer for about fifteen minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid.

Check the grains: Briefly lift the lid and part the rice near the edge. There should be no pooled water, and a tasted grain should be tender through the center. If hard and dry, add a little hot water as described in troubleshooting. If firm with water still present, cover and cook a few minutes longer.

Rest covered: Once the rice is tender and the free water is absorbed, move the pan off the hot burner. Leave covered for ten minutes. Prepare cilantro, zest and juice during the cooking or resting time.

Fluff and season: Uncover, fluff gently, and fold in oil, cilantro, zest and the first tablespoon of lime juice. Taste with the food it will accompany. Add the optional juice a teaspoon at a time only if it needs more acidity. Divide into four side portions.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, herbaceous, bright, aromatic, weeknight, meal-prep, boil, simmer, steam

recipes.name: Sweet Potatoes with Cinnamon
recipes.description: Thin orange sweet-potato rounds roasted with butter, glazed with honey and cinnamon, and finished with fresh lime.
recipeIngredient: 900 g peeled and trimmed orange-fleshed sweet potatoes, cut into even 1/3-inch rounds

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare pans: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C, with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Line two roughly 18-by-13-inch rimmed sheets with oven-safe parchment. Melt the butter and let it remain warm and fluid.

Slice and season: Peel and trim sweet potatoes to the listed weight. Slice crosswise into even one-third-inch rounds; halve unusually broad rounds if needed to handle them comfortably. Pat away surface water. Toss with all the melted butter, salt and pepper, then divide between the sheets in one layer with small gaps and no overlap.

Begin roasting: Roast for 15 minutes. Near the end of this first roast, warm the honey briefly in a microwave-safe bowl until fluid and stir in the cinnamon. Check the potatoes: bottoms should have some golden patches and centers should be beginning to soften. If still very firm and pale, give them another five minutes before glazing.

Turn, glaze and finish: Turn the rounds carefully with a thin spatula. Brush the upward-facing surfaces with all the honey-cinnamon mixture in a thin layer. Swap the sheets between shelves and rotate them front to back. Roast another 10–15 minutes, checking early, until several tested centers yield easily to a knife and the glaze bubbles lightly with brown edges. Remove ready pieces if some finish before thicker ones; do not wait for blackened sugar.

Add lime and serve: Drizzle the measured tablespoon of lime juice evenly over both pans. Transfer gently to a warm serving dish and serve promptly. Divide into four generous side portions, or six smaller holiday portions if the meal includes another starch. Avoid covering tightly while serving, which traps steam and softens the edges.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, tangy, buttery, weeknight, holiday, entertaining, comfort-food, roast

recipes.name: Beef Stew
recipes.description: Chuck braised to fork tenderness with vegetables and a rich pan sauce. Learn why browning and tenderness need different kinds of heat.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs (900 g) boneless beef chuck, cut into 1.5-inch cubes
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
2 oz (55 g) pancetta or bacon, diced
3 cups (720 ml) low-sodium beef stock, plus more as needed
1 lb (450 g) Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into 1-inch chunks
1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Dry and coat: Pat the beef dry, season with salt and pepper, and toss with flour. Shake off loose excess.
