Brown in batches: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef in three uncrowded batches, about 6–8 minutes each, turning to develop deep brown patches. Add the remaining oil as needed. Transfer each batch to a plate; reduce heat if the fond starts to blacken.

Cook the base: Reduce heat to medium. Add pancetta and cook 3–4 minutes until fat begins to render. Add onion and celery and cook 6–8 minutes until softened. Stir in tomato paste for 1 minute, then garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Deglaze: Add wine and scrape up brown fond with a wooden spoon. Simmer 5 minutes. This reduces wine but does not guarantee removal of all alcohol.

Braise gently: Return beef and accumulated juices. Add thyme and enough stock to nearly cover the meat. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and reduce heat to low. Cook about 2 hours, checking occasionally for slow bubbles and sufficient liquid.

Add vegetables when ready: Test several beef pieces. When they are beginning to soften but not yet fully tender, add carrots and potatoes. Simmer, covered, another 35–50 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the beef yields easily to a fork. If the beef is still quite firm at 2 hours, give it more time before adding vegetables.

Finish the sauce: Remove thyme stems. If the sauce is too thin, lift out meat and vegetables and reduce the sauce uncovered before returning them. Add peas and simmer 2–3 minutes until hot. Add balsamic vinegar gradually, taste, and adjust salt and pepper.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, acidic, umami, comfort-food, sear, braise, simmer

recipes.name: Classic Carrot Cake
recipes.description: Mercer Street Meals’ carrot cake uses a light brush of strained apple syrup on completely cooled layers. Keep the remaining syrup separate rather than soaking the cakes with the full batch.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp unsalted butter, for greasing pans
2 tbsp all-purpose flour, for dusting pans
1 1/2 lb carrot, peeled and finely grated
1 Granny Smith apple, washed, peeled and grated
1 lb brick-style cream cheese, cold, not softened

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare pans: Heat the oven to 350°F. For the original batch, use unsalted butter and all-purpose flour to grease two 8-inch round cake pans with all the pan butter, then divide the dusting flour between them, coating and shaking out excess. Dusting flour is separate from batter flour.

Mix batter: Combine all-purpose flour, granulated sugar, baking soda, baking powder, ground cinnamon, ground allspice, ground cloves, freshly grated nutmeg, salt, vegetable oil, large eggs, and carrot until the batter is smooth and all the carrot is distributed. Divide between the prepared pans, keeping similar depth and room to rise.

Bake and cool: Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 25–30 minutes for the original pans. Layers should begin pulling slightly from the sides, centers should be set and a tester should have no wet batter. Cool in the pans, then remove carefully once cool. Wait until fully cool before leveling and frosting.

Make and strain syrup: Bring Granny Smith apple, granulated sugar, and water to a rolling boil in a small saucepan, then remove from heat. Strain through a sieve and discard the apple solids. Keep the strained syrup for a light brush and reserve the excess separately; the cake does not absorb the whole syrup batch.

Mix frosting: Beat brick-style cream cheese, unsalted butter, powdered sugar, vanilla extract, and salt with a stand mixer or electric beaters until smooth, beginning slowly so powdered sugar does not scatter. Keep refrigerated while waiting for the cakes.

Glaze and assemble: Level the completely cool cakes with a serrated knife. Brush each cut surface lightly with apple syrup: about 1 tbsp per layer is the original-batch guide, not all the syrup. Reserve unused syrup separately in the refrigerator. Spread about one-third of the frosting on the first layer, stack the second and use all the rest over the top and sides. Refrigerate the finished cake.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: The chocolate chip cookie was invented by accident in 1938 when Ruth Wakefield, owner of the Toll House Inn in Massachusetts, ran out of baker's chocolate and chopped up a Nestlé chocolate bar instead, expecting it to melt into the dough. It didn't, and the chocolate chip cookie was born - becoming America's most beloved cookie.

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the Butter: In a small saucepan, melt the butter over medium heat. Continue cooking, swirling the pan, until the foam subsides and the solids turn a deep golden brown and smell like hazelnuts. Pour into a bowl and let cool until solid but soft.
Cream: Beat the cooled brown butter with the brown and white sugars until pale and fluffy (3-5 minutes). Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Mix: Dissolve the baking soda in 1 tsp hot water and add to the batter with the salt. Gently fold in the flour, chocolate chips, and seeds.
The Rest (Critical): Wrap the dough and refrigerate for at least 24 hours. This is the secret to the best cookies.
Bake: Scoop onto a parchment-lined sheet. Bake at 350°F for 10-12 minutes until the edges are golden but the centers are still soft.
Finish: Sprinkle with a tiny pinch of flaky sea salt immediately.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, kid-friendly, weekend-project, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Classic French Toast
recipes.description: The secret to French toast that is custardy inside without being soggy is the bread choice and the soak time. Challah and brioche have an enriched, egg-based structure that absorbs custard without disintegrating the way sandwich bread does.
recipeIngredient: 8 slices Thick-Cut Challah or Brioche Bread (3/4 to 1 inch thick)
2 tbsp Maple Syrup (plus more for serving)
Powdered Sugar, fresh berries, and warm maple syrup for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Make the Custard: In a wide, shallow dish (a pie plate works well), whisk together eggs, milk, cream, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until completely smooth. No streaks of egg white should remain.
Soak: Dip each bread slice into the custard for 20-30 seconds per side. Let excess drip off for a few seconds. The bread should be saturated but not falling apart.
Heat the Pan: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large nonstick skillet or griddle over medium-low heat. Swirl to coat.

Cook: Place 2-3 slices in the pan (do not crowd). Cook for 3-4 minutes until the bottom is deep golden brown. Flip and cook for another 2-3 minutes. The toast should feel slightly firm to the touch in the center -- a gentle press should spring back.
Repeat: Wipe the pan, add fresh butter, and cook remaining slices.
Serve: Dust with powdered sugar and serve immediately with fresh berries and warm maple syrup.

recipes.keywords: American, French, sweet, rich, weekend-brunch, comfort-food, saute

recipes.name: Classic Guacamole
recipes.description: Mash part of the ripe avocado into a creamy base and fold in the rest as chunks. Use the measured salt once, then taste the finished mixture before deciding whether it needs more.
recipeIngredient: Gluten-free corn chips, for serving, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare aromatics: If using a molcajete, grind the measured salt, jalapeño and one-eighth of the diced onion into a paste (1 tbsp onion at the original batch). Otherwise, finely mince the jalapeño and mix it with that same onion share and all the measured salt. Reserve the rest of the onion.
Add avocado: Halve the washed avocados, remove pits and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Add the aromatic mixture, measured lime juice and cumin. Do not add the measured salt a second time.
Mash: With a fork, mash about half the avocado into a creamy base, leaving the rest as rough chunks. Fold gently to combine rather than pureeing all the flesh.
Finish: Fold in the reserved onion, cilantro and optional seeded tomato. Taste after mixing; adjust only if needed, remembering that all the measured salt is already included.

Serve or chill: Serve with tortilla chips if using, ideally within 1 hour for color and texture. If waiting, cover directly against the surface and refrigerate promptly. Set out small dipping portions rather than keeping the whole batch on the table.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, savory, acidic, fresh, entertaining, game-day, weeknight, raw

recipes.name: Classic Manhattan
recipes.description: The Manhattan was created in the 1870s and is one of the oldest American cocktails, born during the golden age of pre-Prohibition bartending. Legend claims it was invented at the Manhattan Club in New York for a party hosted by Winston Churchill's mother, though this story is likely apocryphal.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz rye whiskey (or bourbon for a sweeter Manhattan)

recipeInstructions.text: Add the whiskey, sweet: vermouth, and bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 20-30: seconds until properly chilled and diluted.
Strain into a chilled: coupe or cocktail glass.
Garnish with a maraschino: cherry and optionally express an orange peel over the drink.
Serve immediately.:

recipes.keywords: American, rich, sweet, savory, entertaining, date-night, comfort-food, no-cook

recipes.name: Martini
recipes.description: A classic Martini is built on technique and temperature. We stir, never shake, to preserve the silkiness of the gin without introducing air bubbles or excessive dilution.

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Chill your glass in the freezer for 10 minutes prior to starting.
The Ice: Hold a large ice cube in your palm and crack it into 3-4 pieces using the back of a bar spoon. Fill a mixing glass with the cracked ice and additional large cubes.
The Stir: Add the gin and vermouth. Using a bar spoon, stir rapidly in a circular motion for 50 rotations. The outside of the glass should be frosted.
Strain: Double strain using a Hawthorne strainer into your chilled Nick and Nora or Martini glass.

The Express: Use a serrated knife or peeler to remove a 1-inch strip of lemon peel (aim for just the yellow zest, minimal white pith). Twist the peel over the glass to express the oils, rub the rim with the peel, and drop it in.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, smoky, entertaining, date-night, no-cook

recipes.name: Classic Peach Ice Cream
recipes.description: The secret to this heritage-style peach ice cream is keeping the skins on when you chop the peaches. During the maceration process, the pigments from the skin bleed into the sugar, providing a natural rosy color and a deeper, more complex peach aroma.

recipeInstructions.text: Macerate: Toss chopped peaches with 1/2 cup sugar and lemon juice. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours to draw out the syrup.
Custard: Place milk in a double boiler over medium heat. Bring just to a simmer.
Emulsify: In a bowl, whisk eggs, yolks, and 3/4 cup sugar. Slowly whisk 1/2 cup of the hot milk into the eggs to temper.
Thicken: Return the mixture to the double boiler. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 15 minutes until the custard is thick enough to coat the spoon.
Chill: Whisk in the heavy cream. Refrigerate until stone-cold (at least 4 hours).
Churn: Drain the peaches. Stir the accumulated peach syrup into the custard base. Pour into your ice cream maker.
Finish: Add the chopped peaches during the final minute of churning to maintain the fruit's texture.
Set: Freeze for 2 hours before serving.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, entertaining, comfort-food, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Classic Wonton Soup
recipes.description: Cantonese wonton soup features delicate pork wontons in clear, aromatic broth. Stirring the pork filling vigorously in one direction until it becomes sticky and tacky is a traditional technique that ensures the filling stays cohesive during boiling.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Light Soy Sauce, for the filling
1 tsp Shaoxing Wine, for the filling
40 small Wonton Wrappers (about 3.5 inches / 9 cm square)
1 liter prepared Wonton Broth (See note below)
Sesame Oil and Scallions for garnish
Salt and Ground White Pepper, to taste, for the broth
Water, for sealing wrappers and boiling wontons

recipeInstructions.text: The Filling: In a large bowl, whisk pork, scallions, ginger, soy, wine, and broth in one direction until sticky.

Assemble: Divide all the filling among the small wrappers, using only as much as each can seal securely; the count may vary with wrapper size. Wet the edges with water. Fold into a rectangle, then pinch the two corners together to form a "hat."

The Base: Bring the prepared broth to a boil in a separate saucepan, then keep it hot. In 4 serving bowls, add a few drops of sesame oil and white pepper to taste. Taste the prepared broth before adding salt; the linked broth is already seasoned.

Boil: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add wontons in uncrowded batches and stir gently to prevent sticking. Begin checking after 3-4 minutes; floating alone is not a doneness test. Check several wontons with a thin-tip thermometer inserted into the center of the filling and continue cooking until they reach 165°F / 74°C. Halve or quarter the bok choy lengthwise, rinse well, and cook it in the hot broth until its stems are tender-crisp; do not rely on 20 seconds for whole heads.
Bind: Bring the Wonton Broth back to a boil if needed. Ladle the hot broth into the serving bowls.
Serve: Transfer the wontons and bok choy to the bowls. Garnish with scallions and optional chili oil.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, savory, umami, weekend-project, entertaining, comfort-food, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Coconut Chicken Curry
recipes.description: An Indian-inspired curry-powder chicken stew with coconut milk, vegetables, and a measured mango-and-rice serving.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb (450 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
1 cup (240 ml) full-fat unsweetened coconut milk
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed
4 cups (about 780 g) cooked brown rice, prepared separately

recipeInstructions.text: Load vegetables: Put finely diced onion, small carrot pieces, garlic, and peppers in a 4–5 quart slow cooker. Keep the chicken refrigerated until ready to add.
Mix sauce: Whisk coconut milk, tomato paste, curry powder, and the measured salt. Place chicken over vegetables and pour sauce over it. Cover and start cooking immediately.

Cook and check: Cook on HIGH about 3–4 hours or LOW about 5–6 hours, until several of the largest chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and the carrots are tender. Keep the lid closed between checks. Extend cooking as needed; do not rely on color alone.

Finish: Stir in garam masala and cook another 5 minutes. Stir gently, taste, and add salt only if needed. If the sauce is excessively thin, reduce some liquid separately as described in troubleshooting.
Serve: Divide the prepared brown rice among four bowls. Add curry and finish with cilantro. Serve mango and lime wedges alongside, letting diners add lime to taste.

recipes.keywords: Indian, acidic, umami, rich, comfort-food, slow-cook

recipes.name: Coconut Chickpea Curry
recipes.description: Chickpeas in a creamy coconut-and-tomato sauce, warmly spiced with garam masala and finished with lime.
recipeIngredient: 2 (15 oz) cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed; about 250 g drained chickpeas per can
150 g red or yellow onion, peeled and finely diced
1 (14 oz / 400 g) can finely chopped tomatoes, with their juice
1/2 tsp fine salt, for the onion and tomato
1/4 tsp fine salt, reserved for the final seasoning; use only as needed
1 1/2 tbsp garam masala, a salt-free ground spice blend
1 tsp mild, salt-free Indian-style curry powder
400 ml full-fat unsweetened canned coconut milk, stirred together before measuring
2 tsp coconut flour, optional for a thicker sauce
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste; about 1 small juicy lime
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional for heat
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only if the curry becomes too thick

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the ingredients: Drain and rinse the canned chickpeas. Finely dice the onion, mince the garlic and measure all spices. Stir the coconut milk together before measuring. If using coconut flour, whisk the measured amount into a few spoonfuls of that milk and keep it with the remaining milk. Juice the lime into a small bowl so you can control the final addition.

Cook the onion and tomato base: Heat the coconut oil in the wide pot over medium heat. Add onion, tomatoes with their juices, the initial fine salt and the black pepper. Cook uncovered for about 10–12 minutes, stirring regularly, until the onion is soft and the tomatoes have formed a thick, moist mixture. Turn down the heat if it starts sticking. Some canned tomato pieces may retain their shape; press them with the spoon rather than waiting for every piece to dissolve.

Add the spices: Stir in garlic, garam masala, curry powder, cumin and optional red pepper flakes for 30–60 seconds, until aromatic. Keep the base moist and do not let the spices blacken. Promptly stir in the drained chickpeas and all the coconut milk, scraping in all of the prepared coconut-flour mixture if using it.

Simmer: Bring to a gentle simmer, allowing a few minutes for the whole pot to heat. Reduce to medium-low and cook uncovered for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally. The chickpeas should be hot throughout and the sauce creamy and spoonable. Use the reserved hot water a tablespoon at a time only if it becomes too thick. If it is still watery, give it a few extra uncovered minutes rather than serving a thin layer of liquid around the beans.

Balance and serve: Turn off the heat. Stir in half the measured lime juice, taste, then add the remainder in small amounts as needed. Add the reserved fine salt only after tasting; canned chickpeas and tomatoes vary in saltiness. Fold in the optional cilantro. Divide into four portions, about 1 1/4 cups each, with plain rice or bread to catch the sauce.

recipes.keywords: Indian, rich, aromatic, tangy, weeknight, meal-prep, saute, simmer

citation.name: Adapted from Jessica Hylton, Jessica in the Kitchen

recipes.name: Coconut Curry Shrimp
recipes.description: Large shrimp, zucchini and mushrooms in a honey-sweetened coconut curry sauce with fresh basil and lime.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb raw shrimp (U10 or U12), peeled and deveined, tails removed
1 (13.5 oz) can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred together
1 large zucchini, trimmed and cut into 1/4-inch half-moons
1 lime, juiced, juice divided to taste
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Chop the vegetables, garlic and basil and measure the sauce ingredients. Juice the lime. Pat the thawed shrimp dry; season lightly with salt and pepper.

Cook the shrimp: Melt half the butter in the skillet over medium to medium-high heat without browning it darkly. Add shrimp in a single layer, using batches if crowded and sharing this butter allocation between batches. Cook about 2 minutes on the first side, turn and continue about 1–3 minutes, checking early. They should be firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer cooked shrimp to a clean plate.

Soften the vegetables: Reduce to medium and add the remaining butter, onion and mushrooms. Stir for about 5–7 minutes until the onion is softened and the mushrooms have released moisture. Add garlic and curry powder; stir for 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Lower the heat if the spices begin sticking or darkening.

Build the sauce: Stir in coconut milk and honey, scraping the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, add zucchini and cook about 4–6 minutes, until tender with a little bite. Keep the sauce fluid; add a little water if it reduces too far.

Finish: Return shrimp and their juices only long enough to warm through, about 30–60 seconds. Turn off the heat. Stir in basil and half the lime juice. Taste with a piece of vegetable, then add remaining lime, salt, pepper and optional hot sauce as needed.
Serve: Spoon over separately prepared rice and divide shrimp evenly among the bowls. Plain Basmati Rice balances the rich sauce; coconut rice makes a richer meal.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, saute, simmer

citation.name: Adapted from Ree Drummond, The Pioneer Woman, Coconut Curry Shrimp

recipes.name: Coconut Jasmine Rice
recipes.description: Jasmine rice gently cooked in coconut milk and water, with a full covered rest and optional pandan fragrance.
recipeIngredient: 360 g jasmine rice, rinsed and well drained
400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred smooth
1 cup (240 ml) water, plus water for rinsing
2 pandan leaves, washed and tied in a knot, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse jasmine rice in several changes of cool water until less cloudy. Drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer; do not leave a bowlful of rinse water clinging to the batch.

Combine liquid and seasoning: Stir coconut milk, measured water, salt, optional sugar, and optional pandan in a heavy 3-quart saucepan. Warm over medium-low heat, stirring until smooth and the salt dissolves.
Add rice: Stir in drained rice, bring to a gentle boil, cover tightly, and reduce to low. Use only enough heat to maintain a gentle simmer.

Cook and check: Cook about 18–22 minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid. At the end, gently part the rice at the edge to check for pooled liquid. Taste a grain: it should be tender through the center. If hard and dry, use the small hot-water addition in troubleshooting; if liquid remains and rice is firm, cover and cook a few minutes longer.
Rest: Once rice is tender and free liquid has absorbed, take the pan off the burner. Leave covered for 10 minutes. Remove pandan, fluff gently, and divide into six side portions.

recipes.keywords: Southeast Asian, aromatic, rich, mild, weeknight, meal-prep, boil, simmer, steam

recipes.name: Jamaican Rice and Peas (Kidney Beans)
recipes.description: Rice and fully cooked kidney beans steamed in coconut milk with thyme, scallion, garlic, and optional Scotch bonnet.
recipeIngredient: 200 g dried red kidney beans, or 500 g canned kidney beans weighed after draining and rinsing
1.5 liters fresh water for cooking dried beans, plus water for soaking and topping up
360 g long-grain white rice, rinsed and well drained
400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred smooth
320 ml reserved liquid from fully cooked beans, or water for canned beans
Optional: 1 whole Scotch bonnet pepper, left unpierced; keep whole at any batch size

recipeInstructions.text: Soak dried beans: Sort and rinse dried kidney beans. Cover generously with water and soak in the refrigerator for about 8 hours or overnight. Drain and discard soaking water. If using canned beans, drain, rinse, weigh 500 g, and skip to step 3.

Boil, then finish beans: Put soaked beans in a large pot with 1.5 liters fresh water, adding more if needed to cover them by about 2 inches. Bring to a full rolling boil and maintain it for at least 30 minutes. Add boiling water as needed to keep beans submerged. Then reduce to a simmer and cook until fully tender throughout, often another 30–60 minutes. Do not taste before completing the full boiling stage. Drain, reserving at least 320 ml cooking liquid; measure exactly 320 ml for the rice, topping up with water if needed.

Infuse the measured liquid: In a heavy 3–4 quart pot, combine cooked beans, coconut milk, the measured 320 ml bean liquid or water, scallions, thyme, garlic, allspice, black pepper, optional coconut oil, and one-half teaspoon of the measured fine salt. Add the optional intact Scotch bonnet. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 5 minutes.

Add rice: Carefully lift out the chile to a small dish while stirring drained rice evenly into the pot; then place the intact chile back on top. Return to a gentle simmer, cover tightly, and reduce to low.

Cook and rest: Cook about 18–22 minutes, until rice is tender and free liquid has absorbed. Make one brief check near the end; use the hot-water correction if the pot is dry but rice is hard. Take off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes.

Finish: Carefully remove the whole chile, thyme stems, and scallions. Fluff gently without crushing beans. Taste and add the remaining salt only if needed, especially with salted canned beans. Serve as six to eight side portions.

recipes.keywords: Caribbean, savory, rich, aromatic, herbaceous, weeknight, family-meal, meal-prep, make-ahead, boil, simmer, steam

recipes.name: Classic Creamy Coleslaw
recipes.description: Thin cabbage and carrot shreds, lightly salted and drained before a measured mayonnaise, mustard and cider-vinegar dressing.
recipeIngredient: 800 g trimmed green cabbage, core removed, very thinly shredded
150 g carrot, peeled and coarsely grated
6 g fine salt (about 1 tsp), for draining
1 tbsp sugar, added gradually to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Salt and drain: Put prepared cabbage and carrot in a large colander over a bowl. Toss evenly with the measured 6 g salt and leave for 30 minutes, tossing once halfway through.

Dry the vegetables: Press handfuls gently to release loose liquid without grinding the shreds into a pulp. Spread briefly on a clean towel and pat away surface moisture. Taste a shred; if unusually salty, rinse briefly in cold water, drain again and dry thoroughly before proceeding.

Dress: Whisk mayonnaise, mustard, half the vinegar, half the sugar, optional celery seed and pepper in a large bowl. Fold in the vegetables. Taste, then add the remaining vinegar and sugar gradually only if needed. Do not add extra salt automatically.

Chill: Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes. Stir gently and check the seasoning again before serving. If liquid has collected, lift out the slaw with a slotted spoon rather than repeatedly diluting the dressing through the pool.
Serve: Divide into eight side portions. For four diners, make half a batch. Keep chilled until serving; its creamy, cool crunch pairs with a burger, wings or barbecue.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, sweet, savory, bbq, entertaining, comfort-food, no-cook

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Coq au Vin
recipes.description: Boneless chicken thighs with pearl onions, mushrooms and carrots in a savory beefy-onion sauce with a little red wine. Serve over rice.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs (900 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed
16 oz (450 g) cremini mushrooms, thickly sliced
6 medium carrots (about 450 g total), peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 envelope Lipton Recipe Secrets Beefy Onion Soup Mix
Cooking spray, for the crock and skillet as needed
Optional extra thickener: 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tsp cold water

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the vegetables: Lightly spray a 5–6 quart slow-cooker crock. Put the 1/2-inch carrot pieces on the bottom, then add pearl onions, mushrooms and garlic. The pearl onions can go in frozen; keep the chicken refrigerated until the pan is ready.

Brown the chicken: Pat the thighs dry and season with the 1/2 tsp black pepper. Heat a lightly greased skillet over medium-high heat. Brown in uncrowded batches, about 2–3 minutes per side, until golden patches form. Transfer directly to the vegetables. Do not refrigerate or pause the recipe with partly cooked chicken.

Deglaze: Take the skillet briefly off the heat and pour in the measured 1/2 cup wine. Return to heat and scrape up brown bits for about 30–60 seconds; do not reduce the wine by half. Pour into the cooker, leaving any black, burned residue behind.

Season: Mix the 1 tsp cornstarch with 1 tsp cold water until smooth. Stir it into the cooker with the 1 tsp Worcestershire, 1 tsp thyme, one envelope Lipton Beefy Onion Soup Mix and 1 tsp garlic powder. Distribute seasoning through the liquid as best you can. No stock is needed by default; the vegetables and chicken release liquid. Cover and start cooking immediately.

Slow-cook: Cook on HIGH, beginning checks at 2 1/2 hours. The original range is 2 1/2–3 hours, but use the food as the endpoint: several thighs must reach at least 165°F / 74°C in the thickest part, separate easily with a fork, and carrots must yield to a knife. Continue if necessary. If chicken is ready first, lift it out and finish firm carrots in a saucepan with some sauce.

Check the sauce: If you like its consistency, leave it alone. If watery, lift out the chicken and vegetables, transfer cooking liquid to a saucepan and bring to a simmer. Re-stir the optional 1 tsp cornstarch plus 1 tsp cold-water slurry; add gradually while stirring and simmer about 1 minute, stopping at a light coating consistency. Do not reduce an already salty sauce to thicken it.

Serve: Taste a bite of chicken, sauce and cooked rice together before adjusting pepper, garlic powder or salt. Return chicken and vegetables to the hot sauce if separated and serve over rice. Wine remains an ingredient after cooking; this is not an alcohol-free dish.

recipes.keywords: French, savory, comfort-food, sear, slow-cook, simmer

recipes.name: Corn Bread Dressing
recipes.description: Dried cornbread pieces baked with browned mushrooms, shallots, celery and herbs, with a moist center and crisp exposed edges.
recipeIngredient: 700 g fully baked and completely cooled cornbread, weighed before drying, cut into 3/4-inch pieces; about one 8-inch-square batch
115 g button mushrooms, wiped clean and diced
120 g peeled shallots, finely chopped, about 4 small shallots
40 g celery, finely diced, about 1/4 cup
1 1/2–2 1/2 cups (360–600 ml) unsalted chicken stock, as needed
1/4 tsp fine salt, plus up to 1/4 tsp more after tasting
1 tsp softened unsalted butter, for greasing the dish

recipeInstructions.text: Dry the cornbread: Heat the oven to 300°F / 150°C. Spread the 3/4-inch pieces in one layer on a large rimmed sheet without crowding; use two sheets if necessary and switch their positions halfway through. Dry about 30–40 minutes, turning carefully once, until a cooled sample is firm and dry through the middle. Avoid deeply browning the bread at this stage. Cool on the sheet for 10 minutes. Prepare the vegetables while the bread dries.

Brown the mushrooms: Melt two tablespoons of the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add mushrooms and cook about 6–8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until their liquid has evaporated and the pieces have brown patches. Lower the heat if the butter begins to scorch.

Soften the shallots and celery: Reduce heat to medium and add shallots, celery and a quarter-teaspoon of salt. Cook 6–8 minutes, stirring, until the shallots are translucent and the celery is tender. If the pan is dry, take one tablespoon from the remaining measured butter. Add garlic and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.

Add herbs and remaining butter: Stir in parsley, thyme, sage, pepper and all the remaining measured butter. As soon as the butter melts, remove from heat. There should be no watery mushroom puddle, though melted butter is expected.

Fold and moisten: Heat the oven to 350°F / 177°C. Grease a roughly 3-quart 9-by-13-inch baking dish with the separate teaspoon of butter. Transfer cooled dried bread to a large bowl and fold in the mushroom mixture with a broad spatula. Add one and a half cups of stock in two additions, folding gently between them. Wait five minutes, then break open a piece. If its middle is firm or dry, add more stock a quarter-cup at a time until moist through, stopping before liquid pools in the bowl. Taste a cooled spoonful and add the remaining salt only if needed.

Bake immediately: Spread loosely in the dish, leaving an uneven surface and some exposed pieces. Bake uncovered about 30–40 minutes, until the center reaches at least 165°F / 74°C and the top is golden. If the surface browns first, cover loosely with foil and continue until the center is ready.
Rest and serve: Rest 10 minutes, then spoon into eight side portions. Serve beside roast turkey or chicken, with cranberry sauce or a tart green salad to balance the butter.

recipes.keywords: Southern, American, savory, herbaceous, rich, holiday, entertaining, bake, saute

recipes.name: Corn Casserole
recipes.description: Glenna Johnson’s corn casserole combines cream-style corn, drained whole kernels and the full butter and sour cream. Let the melted butter cool until lukewarm before whisking it into the eggs.
recipeIngredient: 8.5 oz sweet corn muffin mix containing wheat flour, cornmeal, sugar, fat and leavening
1 can (15.25 oz) Whole Kernel Corn, drained
Butter, as needed for greasing the dish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9×13-inch oven-safe dish for the original full-can batch with the separate butter allowance. Check its actual depth and leave headroom. A 2-quart dish is another current option only when its actual load leaves adequate headroom; divide excess batter among additional greased dishes rather than assuming it all fits. Scaling uses separate dishes or an appropriate smaller dish, with similar batter depth.
Wet mixture: Whisk all the lukewarm melted butter, beaten eggs and sour cream together until smooth.
Add corn: Stir in all the cream-style corn and drained whole-kernel corn. Fold in all the listed optional green chiles if using them.
Fold: Sprinkle all the muffin mix over the wet mixture and fold just until combined.
Fill: Divide all the batter among the prepared dishes. If using the optional cheddar, divide its full listed amount over their tops.

Bake and rest: Bake for about 35–45 minutes, beginning checks at 35 minutes, until the center is set, the edges are golden and the casserole center reaches 165°F in each dish. A deeper load can need longer; tent a browning top if its center is not ready. Rest for 5 minutes before serving the listed planning portions.

recipes.keywords: Southern, spicy, sweet, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Corn-Shrimp Dumplings
recipes.description: Corn and shrimp dumplings are a modern dim sum creation showcasing summer sweetness. The key to bouncy texture: stir the shrimp mixture vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes before adding the corn.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb Shrimp, peeled, deveined, and finely chopped
1 ear Fresh Corn, kernels cut off the cob
Soy Sauce and Chili Oil for dipping

recipeInstructions.text: The Paste: In a large bowl, combine the chopped shrimp, scallions, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, and white pepper. Stir vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes until the mixture is sticky and pale.
Add Snap: Fold in the fresh corn kernels.
Shape: Place a wrapper in your palm. Spoon 1 tbsp of filling into the center. Moisten the edges with water. Fold into a half-moon and pleat the edges to seal tightly.
Steam: Place in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment. Steam over boiling water for 4-5 minutes until the internal temp is 165°F and the wrappers are translucent.
Option (Boil): Alternatively, drop into boiling water for 3 minutes until they float.
Serve: Serve immediately with a side of soy sauce and quick Pickled Red Onions or chili oil.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, sweet, savory, umami, weekend-project, entertaining, boil, steam

recipes.name: Buttermilk Cornbread
recipes.description: A lightly sweet cornmeal-and-flour bread with a tender crumb, baked in one defined square pan.
recipeIngredient: 140 g fine yellow cornmeal, not corn flour or self-rising cornmeal mix
6 tbsp (85 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled until just warm
1 cup (240 ml) cultured buttermilk, with the refrigerator chill taken off
1 tsp softened butter, for greasing the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Grease an 8-inch square metal pan with the measured teaspoon of butter. Melt the batter butter and let it cool until just warm. If buttermilk is very cold, warm it briefly until the chill is gone, not until hot.
Whisk dry ingredients: Combine cornmeal, flour, baking powder, baking soda and salt thoroughly in a large bowl, breaking up any powder lumps.
Mix wet ingredients: In another bowl, whisk eggs, buttermilk, brown sugar and honey until combined. Whisk in the just-warm melted butter.
Fold: Pour wet mixture into dry. Fold with a spatula until no dry flour streaks remain; a few small lumps are fine. Scrape into the prepared pan, level gently and put it straight into the hot oven.

Bake and check: Bake about 20–25 minutes, until golden at the edges, the center springs back lightly and a toothpick inserted in the middle shows moist crumbs but no wet batter. Extend a few minutes if the center is not set; tent loosely with foil if the top colors too early.

Cool and portion: Cool in the pan on a rack for 10 minutes before cutting nine squares. For a small accompaniment to a starch-containing chili, cut twelve smaller squares instead and serve one per person; cool and freeze spare pieces.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, sweet, rich, weeknight, entertaining, holiday, bbq, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Banana Oatmeal Protein Pancakes
recipes.description: Blend the oats and cottage cheese smooth before cooking this small batch. Medium-low heat gives the egg-rich centers time to set as the banana sweetens and browns the outside.
recipeIngredient: Fresh Blueberries or Dark Chocolate Chips
Greek yogurt or peanut butter for serving (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: Blend: Place the oats, banana, cottage cheese, egg, baking powder, cinnamon, and vanilla in a blender. Blend for about 30–45 seconds until smooth, stopping and scraping with the blender off if needed. Use a small blender cup if a wide jug cannot catch this small amount of batter.
Heat: Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Lightly coat it with oil spray suitable for the pan, following the spray and pan instructions.

Pour: Drop batter by 1/4 cupfuls, leaving room to slide a spatula underneath. If using blueberries or dark chocolate chips, sprinkle them onto the wet surface now. The original batch makes roughly 3–4 pancakes; the count depends on scoop size.

Cook and flip: Cook until the underside is golden and the edges look set, about 2–3 minutes; there may be only a few bubbles. Slide a spatula fully underneath and flip gently. Cook about 2 minutes more, until the middle is set with no wet batter. Lower the heat if the outside colors before the center sets. If checking with a thin thermometer from the side, the center should reach 160°F.

Repeat: Between batches, move the skillet off the heat and carefully remove browned residue with a heatproof utensil and a folded towel held with tongs. Reapply a light coating of spray as directed, then return the pan to medium-low heat and cook the remaining batter.
Serve: Serve immediately, with Greek yogurt or peanut butter if desired.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, snack, quick-lunch, weeknight, blend, griddle

recipes.name: Cranberry Apple Crunch
recipes.description: This family crisp uses butter instead of margarine for a richer oat topping. Tart Granny Smith apples and fresh cranberries cut through the buttery sweetness naturally.
recipeIngredient: 3 cups Apples, peeled and sliced thin (Granny Smith preferred)
1/2 cup (1 stick) Unsalted Butter, melted (Replaces Margarine)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish with butter or oil spray.
Fruit Base: Arrange the sliced apples and cranberries in the bottom of the dish. Sprinkle the granulated sugar evenly over the fruit and toss gently to coat.
Topping: In a medium bowl, combine oats, brown sugar, flour, and chopped pecans. Pour the melted butter over the mix and stir until it looks like wet sand.
Layer: Spread the topping evenly over the fruit. Press down lightly to ensure it adheres to the sugar-coated fruit.
Bake: Bake for 45-60 minutes until the fruit is tender and bubbling and the topping is a deep golden brown.
Cool: Let cool for 10 minutes before serving. This allows the fruit juices to thicken into a glossy syrup.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Cream of Mushroom Soup
recipes.description: Cook the sliced mushrooms in butter until their released liquid evaporates and their surfaces turn golden. Set aside a proportional garnish portion before puréeing the rest with stock.

recipeInstructions.text: The Sear: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, melt butter over medium-high heat. Add all mushrooms. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the released liquid has evaporated and the mushrooms are golden, about 10-20 minutes depending on the pot and moisture. Reduce the heat if the butter begins to scorch; browning, not an eight-minute timer, is the endpoint. If the mushrooms crowd the pot too deeply, work in batches, dividing the total measured butter among them and recombining the cooked mushrooms; extra batches add time.

Reserve: Set aside a proportional portion of the browned mushrooms for the garnish: 1 cup in the original batch with 16 oz cremini and 2/3 cup sliced shiitake. Increase or decrease that garnish portion with the measured mushroom quantity when scaling; keep the rest in the soup pot.

Aromatics: Add the minced shallot to the remaining mushrooms. Cook about 1 minute as a first check and continue until softened, stirring; add garlic and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Stir in all the dried thyme and salt and pepper to taste.
Simmer: Pour in all the vegetable stock. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer about 10 minutes until the mushrooms are very tender.

The Emulsion: Take the pot off the heat. Use an immersion blender according to its hot-liquid instructions, starting on low with the blade guard submerged; stop the motor before lifting it out. For a countertop blender, use only a container approved for hot liquids, let the soup cool to the manufacturer’s permitted temperature, and follow its fill and venting instructions in small batches. Never blend hot soup in a sealed personal-blender cup. Return the puree to the pot.
Finish: Stir in all the measured heavy cream and dry sherry. Simmer gently for about 1 more minute, stirring; taste for salt and pepper. Avoid leaving the cream soup at a hard boil.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and distribute the reserved browned mushrooms among them. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, comfort-food, saute, simmer, boil, blend

recipes.name: Avocado Pasta
recipes.description: Ripe avocado, basil, spinach and the full olive-oil amount make this sauce creamy without cream. Blend while the pasta cooks, then toss in a bowl off the heat.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
1 cup pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
Cherry Tomatoes, halved, optional for serving
Fresh basil, chopped, optional for serving
Water, as needed to boil pasta

recipeInstructions.text: Wash the avocados under running water before cutting. Rinse fresh basil, spinach and optional tomatoes under running water; produce labeled prewashed or ready-to-eat may be used as directed. Drain the leaves. Cook pasta in a large pot of salted water until al dente according to its package. Use some of the listed salt allowance for the pot and keep the rest for the sauce. Reserve the listed pasta-water amount before draining.
While pasta cooks, scoop avocado flesh into a blender. Add basil, spinach, garlic, lemon juice and some of the remaining salt allowance.

Start on low, drizzle in the full olive-oil amount and blend until smooth, about 1 minute. If the blender needs help turning, add a little of the shared reserved water. Follow the actual blender instructions for warm liquids; cool any water destined for a sealed or heat-restricted blender first.
Put hot drained pasta in a large bowl off the heat. Add the green sauce and toss until the noodles are coated.
Add more of the same reserve a little at a time if needed, tossing after each addition. You may not need it all. Season with the remaining salt as desired and the listed black pepper.
Serve immediately, offering halved cherry tomatoes, Parmesan shavings and chopped fresh basil as optional toppings.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, snack, boil, blend

recipes.name: Garlicky Shrimp Fettuccine
recipes.description: Fettuccine and shrimp in a generous Parmesan cream sauce with roasted red peppers, garlic and smoked paprika.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw medium shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
1 (12 oz) jar roasted red peppers, drained, then sliced into 1/2-inch strips
1/2 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
Kosher salt, for the pasta water and to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and boil: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it. Drain and slice the jarred peppers, slice garlic, grate cheese and dry the prepared shrimp. Cook fettuccine until about 1 minute short of its package al dente time. Before draining, reserve the listed pasta water. Begin the sauce while the pasta cooks.

Warm the peppers: Melt butter in the deep skillet over medium heat. Add peppers and cook about 2 minutes. Add garlic and paprika and stir about 30–45 seconds, until fragrant without darkening the garlic.
Simmer the cream: Add heavy cream and bring just to a simmer. Reduce to medium-low and cook gently for about 3–4 minutes, stirring, until it lightly coats a spoon. Avoid a hard boil.

Cook the shrimp: Add shrimp, separating them in the sauce. Simmer gently about 3–5 minutes, stirring so all pieces cook evenly, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. If the pasta is not ready, lift cooked shrimp onto a clean plate and turn down the sauce rather than leaving them simmering.

Combine off heat: Add drained hot pasta to the sauce and turn off the heat. Add Parmesan gradually while tossing. If the coating becomes too tight, add reserved pasta water a small splash at a time; you may not need all of it. Return any removed shrimp and toss briefly to warm.
Season and serve: Taste before adding salt, because the cheese and pasta water already supply it. Add black pepper and parsley, and serve promptly. The sauce thickens further as the pasta stands.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, sweet, umami, rich, herbaceous, smoky, weeknight, quick-lunch, date-night, boil, simmer

citation.name: Adapted from Food Network Kitchen, Creamy, Garlicky Shrimp Skillet

recipes.name: Creamy Polenta
recipes.description: Soft, spoonable polenta enriched with milk, butter and Parmesan. Gentle heat and a tenderness check give the cornmeal time to hydrate without catching on the bottom.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup coarse-ground polenta or coarse yellow cornmeal, not instant
4 cups water, plus warm water as needed for loosening
1 cup whole milk, plus warm milk as needed for loosening
1/2 cup Parmesan, finely grated; choose vegetarian-labelled hard cheese for a vegetarian dish

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the liquid: Combine the measured water, milk and salt in a heavy 3–4-quart saucepan. Bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally and watching that the milk does not boil over.
Whisk in the cornmeal: Reduce to medium-low. Pour the cornmeal in a slow, thin stream while whisking continuously. Continue whisking for about 2 minutes so no dry pockets remain.

Cook gently: Reduce to low so the mixture barely bubbles. Cook about 35–40 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom and corners. Add small splashes of warm water or milk if it becomes too stiff to stir before the grain is tender. Stir more often as it thickens.

Check both texture and thickness: Cool a small spoonful before tasting. It should taste tender and creamy, without grit, and spread softly from the spoon. If gritty, loosen and continue cooking. If tender but watery, stir over low heat a little longer.
Enrich: Remove from heat. Stir in butter and Parmesan until incorporated. Add black pepper, taste, and adjust seasoning only after the cheese is mixed in.
Serve: Divide into four generous side portions and serve promptly. If the polenta tightens while plating, stir in a little warm water or milk until it is spoonable again.

recipes.keywords: Italian, savory, rich, umami, comfort-food, entertaining, weeknight, simmer

recipes.name: Creamy Slow-Cooker Chicken and Wild Rice Soup
recipes.description: Check the rice product before starting: whole wild rice, processed grain and rice blends do not share an identical cooking window. Use the dry wild rice listed here.
recipeIngredient: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup dry wild rice, not instant rice
Additional half-and-half, as needed to loosen the finished soup

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Start with fully thawed chicken kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual 6-quart cooker’s fill instructions, allowing room for later mushrooms and dairy. Check that the dry rice is suitable for this long-cooking route; instant rice or a blend cannot simply inherit its 6–8 hour clock. Season the chicken with part of the salt/pepper allowance and put it in the cooker.

Start the soup: Add all the measured stock, dry wild rice, garlic, onion, carrots, celery, thyme, rosemary and bay leaves. Add seasoning as wanted from the unmeasured allowance, cover and start promptly on LOW. Plan 6–8 hours, checking actual rice tenderness and vegetables as well as chicken; processed rice may finish sooner than unprocessed grain.

Add mushrooms and check doneness: Add all the sliced mushrooms for roughly the final 30 minutes, covering again. The rice and vegetables must be tender, the mushrooms cooked and the thickest chicken pieces must reach 165°F /74°C before removal and shredding. Continue if any endpoint is unmet; do not infer safe chicken from tender rice.
Shred: Transfer the cooked chicken to a clean board and shred with two forks. Remove and discard all the bay leaves from the soup.

Make the sauce: Melt all the measured butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in all the flour and cook until lightly golden, about 1 minute. Gradually whisk in all the measured milk and half-and-half; cook while whisking until slightly thickened, about 4–5 minutes after adding them, allowing longer if the mixture has not heated and thickened. Season from the salt/pepper allowance to taste.

Combine and serve: Stir all the chicken and hot milk mixture into the cooker. If too thick, add a little additional half-and-half from its separate allowance. Stir until the soup is hot throughout; cold added dairy can require more heating. Taste before adding more seasoning and serve with the measured parsley if wanted.

recipes.keywords: American, slow-cook

recipes.name: Spinach Lemon Chicken
recipes.description: At the original four-portion batch, four large breasts make eight cutlets: keep them comparable in thickness and give each room in the pan. Cook the chicken and broth together before finishing the sauce with yogurt and lemon off the heat.
recipeIngredient: 4 large chicken breasts, halved horizontally into cutlets
9 oz fresh spinach, washed and drained

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Prepare large chicken breasts, halved horizontally into cutlets, salt, and black pepper. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Halve the breasts horizontally into cutlets and, if needed, pound to an even approximately ½-inch thickness. At the original batch this makes eight cutlets. Season with the salt and pepper. Use a skillet rated for the oven temperature, with room to arrange the cutlets without overlapping; use additional pans or batches as needed.

Sear in batches: For this stage use 1/2 of the olive oil. Heat half the olive oil over medium-high heat. Sear the cutlets in uncrowded batches, dividing this oil among the batches, for about 2–3 minutes per side until golden; browning does not establish center doneness. Move them to a raw-contact plate while making the broth base.

Build the broth base: Build the broth base with 1/2 of the olive oil, garlic cloves, dried oregano, low-sodium chicken broth, and fresh spinach, washed and drained. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining oil, garlic and oregano; stir 30–45 seconds until fragrant, without scorching the garlic. Add all the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Fold in all the spinach until it begins to collapse. Keep the yogurt and lemon out of the pan for now.

Finish cooking the chicken: Arrange every cutlet without overlapping in enough oven-safe skillets or baking dishes, dividing the entire broth-and-spinach base and all collected juices among them. Transfer the vessels to the oven. Start checking after 10–12 minutes; continue until each cutlet reaches 165°F in its thickest part, checked without touching the pan. Smaller or thicker cutlets and different pan loads change the time. Transfer cooked cutlets to a clean platter and rest for 5 minutes. Before finishing the sauce, verify the raw-contact broth base in each vessel also reaches 165°F.

Finish the yogurt sauce off the heat: Finish with Greek yogurt, full-fat preferred and lemon, zested and juiced. Remove the pan from the heat. If using multiple vessels, gather all their fully cooked broth-and-spinach bases in one saucepan off the heat. Put all the yogurt in a clean bowl and gradually whisk in several spoonfuls of the fully cooked hot broth to temper it. Gently stir this mixture into the cooked base, then add all the lemon zest and juice. Keep the finished sauce off a boil; rapid heating and acid can make yogurt separate. Taste with a clean spoon and adjust the existing salt and pepper allowances.

Serve: Divide all the rested cutlets and spinach among the listed portions and spoon over all the sauce. At the original batch, four portions each have two cutlets; breast sizes vary. Rice or greens are separate accompaniments. Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F). Use within 3–4 days, or freeze portions for later. Reheat hot leftovers to 165°F throughout. For reheated yogurt sauce, USDA also recommends bringing sauces to a rolling boil. Stir for even heating and keep the boil brief rather than prolonged; yogurt can separate and the sauce can concentrate. Retain the full yogurt and lemon quantities. These handling limits do not promise unchanged texture.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, savory, acidic, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, bake, roast, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Whole-Wheat Mac and Cheese
recipes.description: Use the full cheddar and Parmesan amounts, and separate the cream before heating: the larger portion goes in with the butter and the smaller finishing portion finishes the sauce. Melt cheese over low heat, stirring; if the sauce starts bubbling hard, take the pot off the heat while continuing to stir.
recipeIngredient: Water, as needed to boil pasta
Salt, as needed for pasta water, separate from the measured finishing salt
Water, a little as needed when reheating leftovers

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the dry macaroni in boiling water seasoned with the separate pasta-water salt allowance until al dente according to the package. Drain without rinsing.

Return the hot noodles to the pot. Add all the butter and the larger cream portion (⅓ cup in the original batch), keeping the smaller finishing cream portion separate. Stir over medium-low heat until the butter melts and coats the pasta.

Turn the heat to low. Add all the cheddar and Parmesan gradually, stirring until melted. Take the pot off the heat if the cheese mixture bubbles hard; return briefly to low heat only as needed to finish melting.
Stir in the remaining cream (1 tbsp in the original batch), measured sea salt, black pepper and nutmeg. Do not spend the finishing cream twice.
Serve immediately; the sauce thickens as it stands.

recipes.keywords: American, umami, rich, comfort-food, kid-friendly, boil

recipes.name: Crispy Baked Chicken Sliders
recipes.description: Pickle-brined chicken with a panko coating, served on sweet slider buns with mayonnaise and pickles.
recipeIngredient: cooking spray, as needed to coat the rack
cooking spray, as needed to coat the breaded cutlets
12 sweet slider rolls or slider buns
dill pickle chips, as needed for the sliders
mayonnaise, as needed for the sliders

recipeInstructions.text: Brine in the refrigerator: Use boneless skinless chicken breasts and dill pickle juice: slice the breasts horizontally into cutlets about 1/2 inch thick. Put chicken and pickle juice in a food-safe bag or covered container and refrigerate for 1–4 hours. Turn the bag or pieces during the soak so the measured juice reaches all surfaces; do not leave it on the counter.

Prepare the baking station: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set an oven-safe wire rack over a rimmed sheet pan and coat it with cooking spray. Have a second rack and pan ready if the cutlets will not fit in one layer with gaps.

Dredge and bread: Set out all-purpose flour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne pepper, kosher salt, black pepper, eggs, and panko breadcrumbs. Mix the flour with paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, salt and pepper in one dish; beat eggs in a second; put panko in a third. Remove chicken from the brine and pat dry with paper towels. Discard the used brine. Dredge in seasoned flour, shake off excess, dip in egg and let excess drip off, then press into panko. Discard leftover coating ingredients after raw-chicken contact and wash hands and utensils.

Bake and measure: Arrange cutlets on the rack in one layer with gaps. Apply cooking spray evenly to the tops. Bake about 18–20 minutes, until the coating is golden and the thickest part of each cutlet reaches 165°F / 74°C, probing from the side. Continue baking as needed. If using two pans, rotate their positions as needed for even browning; allow more time if the oven is crowded.
Rest and portion: Rest cooked chicken on the rack for 5 minutes. On a clean board, divide the cooked chicken into one bun-sized portion for each roll in the ingredient list, trimming pieces to fit.

Assemble: Use sweet slider rolls or slider buns, dill pickle chips, and mayonnaise: split the rolls, spread mayonnaise on the cut sides and add chicken and pickle chips. Serve immediately while the coating is crisp.

recipes.name: Roasted Black Bean Tacos with Avocado Crema
recipes.description: Roasted beans with crisp edges, a soft center and avocado crema, served in warm soft tortillas.
recipeIngredient: 2 cans (15 oz / 425 g each) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 510 g drained total
2 tsp reduced-sodium soy sauce or tamari
1 ripe avocado, about 150 g edible flesh
1/2 cup (120 g) sour cream or plain Greek yogurt
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
1 tbsp pickled jalapeño brine, added gradually to taste
2 tbsp water, plus 1 tbsp only if needed to loosen
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed
12 small soft corn tortillas, about 5 inches across
30 g drained sliced pickled jalapeños, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and dry: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with a rack in the center. Rinse and drain beans, then spread on a clean towel and blot thoroughly. Measure the crema ingredients and toppings.

Season without making a paste: On an 18-by-13-inch rimmed sheet, lightly crush about one-third of the beans with a fork, leaving coarse pieces and many whole beans. Toss with olive oil, soy sauce, cumin, smoked paprika and garlic powder. Spread into one layer; avoid thin mashed smears at the pan edges. No extra salt is needed before the salty sauce and optional cheese are considered.

Roast and check texture: Roast 20–25 minutes, gently turning after about 12 minutes. Begin checking around 18 minutes: cool a small sample before tasting for dry, crisp edges with a tender center. Remove before small pieces blacken or the centers become hard. Toss with lime zest after roasting; keep lime juice off the tray.

Make the crema while beans roast: Blend avocado, sour cream, 1 tbsp lime juice, half the brine, the crema cilantro, garlic and 2 tbsp water until smooth. Add the remaining brine, extra teaspoon of lime and optional salt only after tasting. Add the extra tablespoon of water only if too thick. Keep cool until serving.

Finish the accompaniments: Shred cabbage, portion optional cotija and jalapeños, chop the serving cilantro and cut lime wedges. Near the end of roasting, warm tortillas in a dry skillet over medium-high for about 10–30 seconds per side, or microwave stacks of four to six between damp paper towels for 30–45 seconds, extending briefly if needed. Wrap briefly in a clean towel.

Build at the table: Divide beans among twelve small tortillas, three per person. Add cabbage, a modest spoonful of crema and the chosen toppings. Serve immediately with optional hot sauce and lime wedges. Keep unassembled beans spread out briefly rather than trapping their steam in a covered bowl.

recipes.keywords: Mexican-inspired, smoky, savory, acidic, rich, umami, weeknight, entertaining, meal-prep, game-day, roast, blend

recipes.name: Crispy Gold Potatoes with Smoked Salt and Paprika
recipes.description: Petite gold potatoes with deeply browned cut faces, creamy centers and a finishing butter finish, garlic, smoked sea salt and sweet paprika.
recipeIngredient: 3 lb petite gold potatoes, scrubbed and thoroughly dried
1 1/4 tsp fine smoked sea salt, plus more to taste
3 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into small pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and cut: Heat the oven to 400°F convection, with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Set out two bare metal rimmed half-sheet pans. Halve the dry potatoes lengthwise; quarter larger ones so pieces are roughly 1–1 1/2 inches across.

Season and arrange: Toss potatoes with the olive oil, garlic, smoked sea salt, black pepper and sweet paprika. Divide between pans with space around each piece, setting a cut face flat against the metal. Scrape the coating from the bowl onto the potatoes; avoid piles of loose garlic on the pans.

Roast: Check after 20 minutes, rotating pans front to back and swapping racks. Turn potatoes once their undersides are golden and release with a thin spatula; leave pale or stuck pieces a little longer. Start checking tenderness at 30 minutes. They are ready when browned and a thin knife slides easily into the largest centers, usually 35–45 minutes total. If garlic darkens quickly, lower to 375°F convection and continue until tender.

Butter and serve: Add butter in small pieces to the hot potatoes and toss gently on the pans until melted. No extra roasting is needed. Taste before adding more salt. Serve promptly; avoid covering tightly or piling into a deep bowl, which traps steam.

recipes.keywords: crispy, buttery, smoky, savory, family-meal, entertaining, roast

recipes.name: Crispy Oven Zucchini Fries
recipes.description: Zucchini fries are the gateway vegetable for kids who resist anything green - they look like legitimate fries but deliver actual nutrition. The trick is removing excess moisture (zucchini is 95% water) by salting the cut pieces and letting them sit.

recipeInstructions.text: Remove Moisture: Cut zucchini lengthwise into quarters, then cut each quarter into fry-sized sticks (about 1/2-inch thick). Place on a paper towel-lined plate. Sprinkle generously with 1/4 tsp salt. Let sit for 5 minutes while the zucchini weeps water. Pat completely dry.

Set Up Stations: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Set up three shallow bowls: one with flour mixed with salt and pepper; one with beaten egg; one with panko mixed with Parmigiano, garlic powder, and Italian seasoning.
Coat: Working with a few zucchini sticks at a time, coat in the flour mixture (shake off excess), dip in egg, then roll in the panko mixture, pressing gently so the coating sticks.
Arrange: Place breaded zucchini on the prepared baking sheet in a single layer, not touching.
Brush: Lightly brush or spray each stick with olive oil on all sides. This is crucial for crisping.
Bake: Bake for 18-22 minutes until golden brown and crispy, flipping halfway through.
Serve: Serve hot with marinara sauce, ranch dressing, or a squeeze of fresh lemon for dipping.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, crispy, herbaceous, weeknight, kid-friendly, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Crispy Pancetta, Sweet Pea & Lemon Ricotta Pasta
recipes.description: Orecchiette with crisp pancetta, cooked sweet peas and a lemon-ricotta sauce finished away from direct heat.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz dry orecchiette or similar short pasta
1 cup sweet peas, fresh or frozen
1/4 cup dry white wine or unsalted chicken stock
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, taken from the zested fruit if possible
Water, a small splash if needed for sticking shallot
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and heat water: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Mince shallot and garlic, zest the lemon and measure its listed juice amount, and grate Parmesan. Season pasta water moderately, remembering the pancetta and cheese.

Render pancetta: Put pancetta in a cold skillet and set over medium heat. Cook, stirring, about 8–12 minutes, or as its package directs, until cooked through and crisp. Remove with a slotted spoon to a clean plate. Pour off excess fat into a heatproof container, retaining about 1 1/2–2 tablespoons of fat for each 4 ounces of pancetta cooked, or what it releases if less. This is a ratio: retain proportionally less for a smaller batch and more for a larger one.

Build the base: Over medium-low, soften shallot in the retained fat for about 3–5 minutes. If there is very little fat and it sticks, add a small splash of water. Add garlic for 30–45 seconds, then wine or stock. Simmer about 2 minutes, scraping browned bits, until reduced by roughly half. Turn off heat while pasta finishes.

Cook pasta and peas: Meanwhile boil pasta according to package directions until tender with a little bite; do not drain early for an unheated finish. Cook frozen peas according to their package, or simmer fresh peas separately until tender, then drain. Reserve the listed pasta-water amount before draining pasta. Combine cooked hot pasta and peas with the aromatic base.

Finish away from heat: Move the skillet completely off the burner and wait until it no longer sizzles; transfer to a large bowl if the pan stays very hot. Stir in ricotta, Parmesan, lemon zest, half the measured lemon juice and half the reserved pasta water. Toss gently until creamy, adding more water in small amounts only if needed.
Taste and plate: Add black pepper, then taste before adding salt and the remaining lemon juice. Divide into the intended portions and top with the crisp pancetta. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Crispy Parmesan Roasted Broccoli
recipes.description: Tender broccoli with browned edges and a nutty cheese crust. Learn to control surface moisture and add garlic before it burns.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs (680 g) fresh broccoli, cut into 1.5-inch florets with flat stem sides
1/4 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
1–2 tsp fresh lemon juice, to finish
Pinch of red pepper flakes, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and dry: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with a rack in the upper middle. Wash broccoli, drain, and towel-dry thoroughly. Cut thick stems to a similar size so they finish with the florets.
Season and arrange: Toss broccoli with 2 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan, placing flat cut sides down with space between pieces. Use a second pan if necessary.
Roast: Roast undisturbed for 15 minutes. Check the undersides: they should have golden patches. Turn the pieces and roast another 3–5 minutes if the stems still feel very firm.

Add the delicate ingredients: Mix garlic with the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Toss it through the broccoli, then sprinkle with Parmesan. Roast 3–5 minutes more, until the cheese is golden and a knife pierces the stems easily. Check early; do not wait for black garlic.
Finish: Taste a floret. Add lemon juice a little at a time and adjust salt only if needed. Add optional pepper flakes and serve immediately, uncovered, to preserve the edges.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, savory, umami, crispy, weeknight, entertaining, comfort-food, roast

recipes.name: Crispy Shallots
recipes.description: Crispy shallots (hành phi in Vietnamese, hom jiao in Thai) are a cornerstone condiment across Southeast Asia, adding texture, sweetness, and aroma to soups, salads, and stir-fries. The secret to perfect shallots is the cold-oil start.
recipeIngredient: 4 large Shallots, peeled and sliced into thin, uniform rings
1 cup Neutral Cooking Oil (Canola or Vegetable)

recipeInstructions.text: Slicing: Peel the shallots. Slice them into thin, uniform rings (about 1/16-inch thick) using a mandoline or a very sharp chef's knife. Uniformity is crucial for even browning.
Cold Start: Place the sliced shallots in a cold, small saucepan. Pour in the neutral oil until the shallots are just submerged.

Slow Fry: Turn the heat to medium. Once the oil begins to gently bubble around the shallots, reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally to ensure they do not clump or burn.

The Pull: Watch the shallots closely towards the end. The moment they turn a pale, light golden brown, immediately pour the contents of the pan through a fine-mesh strainer set over a heat-proof bowl. Do not wait for them to look dark brown in the oil, as carryover heat will continue to cook and darken them as they cool.

Drain and Salt: Spread the hot shallots in a single layer on a paper towel-lined plate. Immediately sprinkle with a pinch of kosher salt while they are still wet with oil. This helps them dry crisp and seasons them.
Store: Allow them to cool completely. Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. Use the leftover shallot-infused oil in the fridge for cooking.

recipes.keywords: Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, sweet, savory, caramelized, crispy, nutty, everyday, meal-prep, entertaining, fry

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Gnocchi & Veggies
recipes.description: Roast the gnocchi and vegetables with room between the pieces. The tomatoes provide some pan juices while the gnocchi edges color; check the centers for tenderness as well.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Fresh or Shelf-stable Potato Gnocchi
12 oz Mini Bell Peppers, cut into 1-inch chunks
1 small Red Onion, cut into chunks
1/4 tsp kosher salt, optional alternative to salt to taste; choose one salt route
1/2 lb shrimp or fully cooked chicken sausage, optional; choose one
Water, for separately cooking raw shrimp, if using

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare: Heat the oven to 450°F. Use rimmed metal sheets with room for one uncrowded layer. Leave them bare or line with suitable foil; use parchment only if its actual label permits this temperature. Wash the peppers, tomatoes, onion and herbs before cutting, and dry the produce.

Toss: In a roomy bowl combine the full gnocchi, peppers, tomatoes, onion and smashed garlic. Add all the olive oil and rosemary, plus the salt from your chosen seasoning route and black pepper to taste. Toss to distribute the oil. Keep all the basil and Parmesan for finishing; keep the optional protein separate.

Spread: Spread in one layer with gaps, using more sheets or successive rounds rather than piling the mixture. Divide the same full oil-coated mixture between the pans; a larger batch does not need a hotter oven.

Roast: Roast, stirring halfway through and exchanging tray positions if using more than one shelf. Begin checking around 18–20 minutes for the original-size uncrowded load; continue until gnocchi centers are tender and their edges golden, and vegetables have softened with browned edges. Actual gnocchi product, oven and tray load may need longer.

Prepare optional protein: If using the listed shrimp, peel and devein raw shrimp, thaw in the refrigerator if needed, and keep raw-contact tools separate from the finishing cheese and herbs. Cook the full chosen shrimp separately in gently simmering water until the flesh is firm, pearly and opaque throughout; check thick centers with a thin probe for 145°F. Drain and use clean utensils to add it to the finished vegetables. If choosing chicken sausage instead, use fully cooked product and heat it separately according to its package before adding; refrigerated cooked leftovers must reach 165°F throughout. Raw chicken sausage needs a complete separate method to 165°F and is not a direct substitute. Cooked shrimp may instead be reheated to 165°F before adding. Do not add both proteins.
Finish and serve: Toss the finished gnocchi and vegetables with all the chopped basil and all the measured Parmesan, then fold in the chosen cooked or heated protein if used. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, herbaceous, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, bake, roast, boil, steam

recipes.name: Smashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Boil the skin-on baby potatoes until soft, then flatten them gently to expose uneven edges. Let surface steam escape before coating with all the measured oil.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs Baby Potatoes (Red or Yukon Gold)

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Scrub whole baby potatoes and keep the skins on. Place in cold water and salt it with the listed allowance. Bring to a boil and cook about 15–20 minutes after boiling, until the centers yield easily to a fork. Drain. Start preheating to 425 °F while they boil.

Smash: Line a baking sheet with oven-suitable parchment. Arrange with space between potatoes; use additional sheets if needed. Gently press each with a heavy glass bottom or masher to about 1/2 inch thick, keeping the skin-on pieces together.
Dry: Let the smashed potatoes stand about 5 minutes so surface steam can escape.

Season: Distribute all the measured olive oil across the total batch, including any extra sheets. Add all the garlic powder and chosen dried rosemary or thyme; salt and pepper to taste. Do not repeat the full measured oil/seasoning amount on each tray.

Roast: Roast at 425 °F for about 25–30 minutes as a first window, flipping carefully halfway through. Continue until edges are deep golden and crisp and centers remain tender. Extra trays may need rotation and longer; judge the edges by color and crispness as well as the tenderness of the centers.
Finish: Add the flaky sea salt finish to taste and serve hot. Refrigerate leftovers promptly; reheat to 165 °F and use the oven to help restore edges rather than expecting microwave crispness.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, herbaceous, comfort-food, roast, boil

recipes.name: Hot Chocolate
recipes.description: While serious chocolatiers prefer the stovetop, the slow cooker is an excellent tool for gentle tempering. The low, consistent heat prevents the chocolate from seizing and allows the espresso and vanilla to infuse deeply into the dairy.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Bittersweet Chocolate (60% cacao), finely chopped
1 teaspoon Instant Espresso Powder (Brings out the chocolate depth)
Marshmallows and Shaved Chocolate for garnish
8 oz Irish Cream Liqueur (Optional, for adults)

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk: In a 6-quart slow cooker, whisk together the sugar, cocoa powder, espresso powder, and salt.
Incorporate: Gradually pour in the milk and heavy cream, whisking constantly until the powder is mostly dissolved.
Melt: Stir in the chopped bittersweet chocolate and vanilla extract.
Slow Cook: Cover and cook on LOW for 2 hours. Whisk vigorously every 30-45 minutes to ensure the chocolate emulsifies with the dairy.
Finish: Just before serving, stir in the liqueur (if using).
Serve: Ladle into mugs. Top with fresh marshmallows and shaved chocolate.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, slow-cook

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Mac and Cheese
recipes.description: Regular uncooked elbow pasta cooks in the full milk-and-cheese mixture on LOW. Check and stir after the first hour rather than leaving it unattended for a fixed two hours.
recipeIngredient: 1 pound elbow pasta (uncooked, regular - not quick-cook)
12 ounces extra-sharp cheddar, freshly shredded (about 3 cups)
4 ounces American cheese, shredded (about 1 cup - from the deli, not slices)
Non-stick cooking spray, for the cooker

recipeInstructions.text: Set up: For the original batch, use the source’s 6-quart slow cooker only if its actual instructions permit the load. Aim for a suitable fill between half and two-thirds full, with a lid that closes; scaling may require smaller, larger or separate cookers, not the same vessel at every amount. Keep milk and cheese refrigerated until preparation. Spray the insert with the listed cooking-spray allowance. Rinse regular uncooked elbow pasta in cold water and drain well.

Build: Add all the drained uncooked pasta, whole milk, evaporated milk, both cheeses, salt, pepper, dry mustard, garlic powder and cayenne. Stir thoroughly so the pasta is submerged as much as possible. Dot with all the cubed butter. Start cooking immediately; do not use a delayed-start timer.

Cook on LOW: Cover and cook on LOW for 1 hour, then quickly uncover and stir, reaching the bottom and edges. Check a cooled pasta sample: it should be tender without a hard center. Return the lid promptly if it needs longer. Keep LOW for this method; HIGH is not an equivalent shortcut.

Check and finish: Continue on LOW as needed, checking and stirring about every 30 minutes as in the saved method, or sooner as it approaches tenderness. Total cooking may take about 1–3 hours depending on the actual cooker and pasta. Stop when the pasta is tender and sauce creamy; check several central locations reach 165°F before serving. That casserole-temperature check and pasta tenderness are separate endpoints, not a claim that a timer alone makes it safe.

Rest and serve: Let stand 5–10 minutes before serving; it thickens as it cools. If holding for service, use a suitable hot setting and verify at least 140°F rather than assuming WARM is sufficient. Refrigerate leftovers promptly rather than leaving the switched-off cooker to cool.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, rich, entertaining, game-day, potluck, slow-cook

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Three-Bean Vegetable Chili
recipes.description: Three kinds of cooked beans with sweet potato and peppers in a smoky tomato base, finished with cider vinegar and optional fresh toppings.
recipeIngredient: 180 g red onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
300 g mixed red and green bell peppers, seeded and diced
300 g peeled sweet potato, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) kidney beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
2 cans (4 oz / 113 g each) mild diced green chiles, with juices
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) diced tomatoes, with juices
1 can (8 oz / 227 g) plain tomato sauce
2 tbsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
1 cup (240 ml) low-sodium vegetable broth, plus a little only if needed to loosen
1 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, added gradually to taste
1/2 cup (120 g) plain yogurt or unsweetened plant-based yogurt
1 medium avocado, about 150 g edible flesh, diced just before serving
