recipeInstructions.text: The Emulsion: Preheat oven to 350°F. In a blender, combine bananas, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, egg, yogurt, and milk. Blend on high for 30 seconds until perfectly smooth.
Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the whole-wheat flour, baking soda, and baking powder.
Combine: Pour the wet ingredients into the dry. Stir with a spatula until just combined (do not over-mix, or the whole-wheat will turn tough).
Bake: Pour into a greased loaf pan. Bake for 50-55 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 15 minutes before slicing.
The Freeze: To store, slice the loaf into 1/2-inch rounds. Place parchment between slices and freeze in a zip-top bag. Reheat individual slices in the toaster for a Crunch finish.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, weekend-project, bake, blend

recipes.name: Freezer Date Cookies
recipes.description: These are nutritious cookies designed for long-term freezer storage. The key to their texture is processing the Medjool dates directly with the melted butter in a food processor to create a smooth, caramel-like paste that acts as the primary sweetener.

recipeInstructions.text: The Date Paste: Place the pitted Medjool dates and melted butter in a food processor. Pulse on high until a completely smooth, thick paste forms.
The Emulsion: Add the egg, yogurt, and vanilla to the processor. Pulse for 10 seconds until perfectly integrated.
Dry Mix: In a separate bowl, whisk together buckwheat flour, whole wheat flour, oats, baking soda, and cinnamon.
Combine: Pour the date mixture into the dry ingredients. Mix with a spatula until a thick, sticky dough forms.
Shape: Preheat oven to 350°F. Roll the dough into small balls (about 1 tbsp each). Place on a greased cookie sheet and press down firmly with your palm to create a 1/2-inch thick disk.
Bake: Bake for 12-15 minutes until the edges are lightly browned.
The Freeze: Let cool completely. Transfer to a freezer bag. These are at their Kitchen Standard when eaten straight from the freezer.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, snack, quick-lunch, kid-friendly, bake, blend

recipes.name: Slow Cooker French Dip Sandwiches
recipes.description: Chuck needs time to become easy to pull apart. The broth, soy sauce, Worcestershire and rosemary make the dipping liquid; keep all their measured quantities.
recipeIngredient: Oil, as needed for optional searing

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and optionally sear: Start with fully thawed beef, kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the cooker’s capacity and meat-size instructions. If searing, brown the roast on all sides in a hot skillet with the optional oil allowance, then transfer immediately to the cooker to continue cooking. Otherwise place the roast directly in the cooker.
Combine: Add all the sliced onion, garlic, measured stock, soy sauce, Worcestershire and rosemary. Cover and start cooking promptly; do not use a delayed start.

Cook until tender: Cook on LOW for about 8 hours or HIGH for about 4–5 hours as planning ranges, until the beef pulls apart with a fork. Check that the roast has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with a three-minute rest before serving; shreddable chuck usually needs substantially more cooking than that minimum. Continue if it remains tough.

Shred and strain: Remove the cooked beef to a clean board and shred into large chunks, or slice thinly if preferred. Strain the cooking liquid into a heatproof vessel and keep it hot for dipping. The softened onions can be served with the beef if wanted rather than discarded automatically.

Assemble and broil: Split the listed rolls or baguette pieces and distribute the beef and measured provolone among them. Put them on a broiler-safe pan, keeping within the actual oven instructions. Broil about 1–2 minutes as a first check, watching continuously until the cheese bubbles and the bread toasts; remove individual sandwiches if ready sooner.
Serve: Divide the hot jus among individual dipping bowls and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, umami, comfort-food, slow-cook

recipes.name: French Toast
recipes.description: The secret to restaurant-quality French toast is the bread choice. We exclusively use challah or brioche for their high egg and butter content, which creates a custardy texture that regular white bread cannot mimic.

recipeInstructions.text: The Spice: In a small bowl, whisk cinnamon, nutmeg, and warmed honey until no clumps remain.
The Custard: In a shallow dish (like a pie plate), whisk together the honey-spice mix, eggs, milk, and vanilla until perfectly smooth.
The Sear: Heat 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium.
Dip: Working in batches, dip a slice of bread into the custard for exactly 2 seconds per side. Let the excess drip off.
Cook: Immediately place in the skillet. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden brown and slightly crisped at the edges.
Serve: Serve immediately with warm maple syrup and fresh berries for the mandatory Acid/Sweet Finish.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, acidic, rich, comfort-food, fry

recipes.name: Fresh Cabbage, Cucumber and Radish Kimchi
recipes.description: This is fresh kimchi ready to eat immediately. The key to crisp, non-watery kimchi is salting the vegetables heavily for an hour to draw out excess moisture that would otherwise dilute the spice paste.
recipeIngredient: 3 lbs Napa Cabbage, halved and cut into 2-inch pieces
1 1/4 lbs Daikon Radish, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/4 cup + 2 tbsp Rice Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)

recipeInstructions.text: The Cure: In four separate large bowls, divide the cabbage, cucumbers, daikon, and radishes. Sprinkle 2 tbsp of salt into each bowl and toss well. Let stand for 1 hour at room temperature.
The Paste: In a high-powered blender, combine ginger, garlic, gochugaru, rice vinegar, sesame oil, fish sauce, scallions, and sugar. Puree until almost smooth.
The Rinse: Drain the vegetables thoroughly. Gently squeeze each handful to remove all remaining water.
The Bind: In one massive bowl, toss all the vegetables with the kimchi paste until every piece is uniformly coated in the deep red glaze.
The Finish: Transfer to glass jars. Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours (ideally 24) to allow the flavors to meld and the fermentation to begin.
Serve: This fresh kimchi (Geotjeori style) is at its best within the first week.

recipes.keywords: Korean, sweet, acidic, weekend-project, make-ahead, blend

recipes.name: Fresh Egg Pasta
recipes.description: A yolk-enriched dough for rolled ribbons, with measured water adjustments, a covered rest, and thickness cues that work across pasta machines.
recipeIngredient: 290 g all-purpose flour, plus a little for dusting
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the dough
2 tbsp cool water, only as needed for the dough
2 tbsp fine semolina or all-purpose flour, for dusting cut pasta
4 quarts (3.8 liters) water, for cooking pasta
1 tbsp fine salt, for the pasta water

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: Pulse the measured flour and dough salt in a food processor. Beat eggs, yolks, and oil together, add, and pulse until evenly crumbly. Squeeze a small handful: if it holds together, stop. If it falls into dry crumbs, add the measured water a teaspoon at a time, pulsing briefly and checking again. You may not need all of it. Do not taste the raw mixture.

Knead: Tip onto a clean work surface and press together. Knead for about 5–8 minutes until firm and reasonably smooth. Use very little dusting flour. If still dry and cracked, knead with lightly damp hands; if tacky, dust sparingly.

Rest covered: Wrap tightly or place in a covered container so the surface cannot dry out. Rest for 1 hour at ordinary room temperature. Refrigerate instead if the kitchen is very hot or preparation will be delayed.

Roll gradually: Divide into four pieces and keep three covered. Flatten one piece, dust lightly, and pass through the roller's widest setting. Fold in thirds and repeat once or twice to form an even strip. Progress through narrower settings without skipping several at once, stopping at about 1 mm for fettuccine. Rest a resistant piece covered for 5–10 minutes rather than forcing it.

Cut: Let a tacky sheet sit just briefly until its surface no longer sticks, then cut into ribbons. Dust with the measured semolina or flour, shake off excess, and arrange in loose nests on a lined tray. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cook promptly, or refrigerate/freeze as described below.

Boil and finish: Bring the cooking water and its salt to a full boil. Add noodles, separating them gently, and cook until no floury center remains, generally 2–5 minutes depending on thickness and drying. Taste only after cooking. Reserve a little cooking water before draining, then combine promptly with the chosen sauce.

recipes.keywords: Italian, weekend-project, mix, shape, boil

recipes.name: Pasta Dough
recipes.description: Traditional pasta dough from Northern Italy uses just flour and eggs - the simplicity lets you taste the quality of each ingredient. The 30-60 minute rest period is essential: it allows the gluten to relax fully so the dough rolls smoothly without springing back.

recipeInstructions.text: The Mix: Place flour and salt in the bowl of a stand mixer. Create a well in the center. Add the eggs and olive oil.
The Hook: Use the dough hook on speed 2. Run until a shaggy dough forms and starts to climb the hook (about 3-4 mins).
The Knead: Continue on speed 2 for 8-10 minutes. The dough should transform from lumpy to completely smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky.
The Rest: Remove from the bowl. Wrap tightly in plastic wrap. Let rest for at least 30 minutes (up to 24 hours in the fridge) before rolling.
Shape: Cut, roll, and shape as desired. See Fresh Egg Pasta for rolling settings.

recipes.keywords: Italian, herbaceous, weekend-project, no-cook

recipes.name: Strawberry Vinaigrette
recipes.description: A berry-forward dressing with balsamic vinegar, honey and olive oil, blended after a short rest to soften the sliced fruit.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup fresh strawberries, hulled and sliced
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare fruit: Wash the strawberries, remove their hulls, slice and measure the listed amount.
Rest: Stir vinegar and honey together in a bowl, coat the berries with the mixture and leave for 30 minutes. Keep all the released juice.

Blend: Transfer berries and liquid to a small processor or suitable blender vessel. Add olive oil and a little salt and pepper; blend until the fruit is finely broken down, stopping to scrape safely if needed.

Taste and dress: Taste a small amount on a leaf. Adjust with a little honey if sharply tart or a little vinegar if too sweet, then check salt and pepper. Toss into dry greens gradually just before serving and reserve excess dressing for another salad.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, light-and-fresh, blend

citation.name: Adapted from Rachel at Grow a Good Life

recipes.name: Wonton Wrappers
recipes.description: Homemade wonton wrappers have a delicate, silky texture that's hard to match with store-bought. The dough should be quite firm after kneading, then rested for 30-60 minutes to relax the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin.
recipeIngredient: Cornstarch (for dusting - Do not use flour for dusting!)

recipeInstructions.text: Mix: In a large bowl, whisk the flour and salt. Make a well in the center. Add the egg and water. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Turn out onto a clean surface and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be quite firm.
Rest: Wrap in plastic and let rest at room temperature for at least 30-60 minutes. This relaxes the gluten so you can roll it paper-thin.
Roll: Divide dough into 4 pieces. Use a pasta machine (recommended) or a heavy rolling pin. Roll until the dough is thin enough to see your hand through it (Setting 6 or 7 on most pasta machines).
Cut: Dust generously with cornstarch. Cut into 3.5-inch squares.
Store: Stack with plenty of cornstarch between layers. Wrap tightly in plastic. (Can be refrigerated for 2 days or frozen for 3 months).

recipes.keywords: Chinese, weekend-project, boil

recipes.name: Fried Sweet Plantains (Maduros)
recipes.description: Maduros use very ripe sweet plantains rather than the firm green fruit used for tostones. Mostly black skins and yielding flesh are useful cues; ripening time varies with the starting fruit and room.
recipeIngredient: 3 very ripe Plantains (skins should be mostly black with yellow patches)
3 tbsp Neutral Oil (vegetable, canola, or coconut)

recipeInstructions.text: Choose the listed very ripe plantains: mostly black skins with some yellow and flesh that yields to gentle pressure. If firm and yellow, allow more room-temperature ripening and check daily; there is no guaranteed one- or two-day finish. Reject fruit with visible mold or spoiled flesh rather than treating every black mark as proof of readiness.
Wash the skins under running water and dry before cutting. Score lengthwise, peel and slice diagonally into roughly 1/2-inch pieces.

Heat all the listed oil in a large skillet over medium heat until shimmering without smoking. Add only enough slices for one uncrowded layer, keeping space to turn; the oil is the total pan-frying supply, not a fresh 3 tbsp dose for each round.

Start checking around 3–4 minutes per side, and flip gently with a thin spatula once the underside is golden. Continue until the centers are soft; lower heat if the surface darkens before the center softens. Remove finished pieces while thicker ones continue.

Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and divide the listed salt pinch and optional cinnamon pinch over all the cooked slices as each batch finishes. Repeat with the remaining slices using the oil left in the pan; adjust heat between rounds so sugary residue does not scorch.
Serve promptly for the clearest contrast between browned edges and soft centers. More plantains require more rounds or separate pans, dividing the same full oil supply among them.

recipes.keywords: Caribbean, sweet, caramelized, rich, weeknight, family-meal, kid-friendly, pan-fry, fry

recipes.name: Frozen Blueberry Muffins
recipes.description: Frozen blueberries make these buttery muffins practical year-round, with a nutmeg-sugar finish. Fold in the fruit without thawing and keep mixing brief so berry juice does not spread through the batter; look for cooked crumb around the fruit rather than a perfectly dry berry stain on the tester.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the muffin cups if not using liners
2 cups frozen unsweetened blueberries, keep frozen until folding

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the oven and pans: Heat the oven to 375°F. For the original batch, line two standard 12-cup muffin tins or use butter or neutral oil to grease the cups. For a different quantity, prepare more or fewer standard cups, keeping the same cup size and about two-thirds fill. Plan oven space with air circulation; additional oven batches add baking and pan-cooling time.
Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the batter’s all-purpose flour, baking powder, and sea salt together in a bowl.

Cream the butter and sugar: In another large bowl beat the batter’s unsalted butter and granulated sugar for about 3–5 minutes, until light and fluffy. The topping sugar is separate; none is subtracted from the batter sugar.
Add the eggs: Beat in the large eggs one at a time, scraping the bowl between additions.
Add the milk and vanilla: Mix in the 2% milk and vanilla extract until incorporated.

Fold in the flour mixture: Fold the dry mixture into the butter mixture just until moistened. Scrape the bottom of the bowl so no dry flour pockets remain; do not keep beating to remove every small lump.

Fold in the frozen berries: Gently fold in the frozen unsweetened blueberries with as few strokes as needed to distribute them. Portion into standard muffin cups about two-thirds full, using the listed muffin yield as a guide rather than forcing every batch into 24 cups. The original batch uses about 24 cups; use more or fewer cups and additional pans or oven batches for different quantities.
Add the topping: Combine the topping’s granulated sugar and ground nutmeg and sprinkle it evenly over the muffins.

Bake and cool: Bake for 20–25 minutes, until a tester through the crumb has no wet batter; berry juice on the tester is different from uncooked batter. Check muffins from both tins. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then remove to racks. Let cool completely before packing for storage.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, meal-prep, kid-friendly, entertaining, weekend-project, bake

recipes.name: Funfetti Cake
recipes.description: Whip the egg whites in a clean, grease-free bowl, then fold them and the sprinkles into the batter gently. Jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles retain their colors better than nonpareils.
recipeIngredient: 4 1/8 cups (516 g) all-purpose flour, all into batter; separate pan flour below
1/2 cup (80 g) jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles
butter, as needed for greasing pans
all-purpose flour, as needed for dusting pans

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare pans: Heat the oven to 350°F. Use butter and all-purpose flour to grease and flour three 8-inch round pans for the original batch, shaking out excess flour. All the listed batter flour goes into the cake; pan dusting uses a separate supply.

Cream cake ingredients: Using unsalted butter, granulated sugar, vegetable oil, and vanilla extract, beat the softened cake butter until creamy, then add all the sugar and oil and beat until combined. Scrape the bowl and mix in all the cake vanilla.
Mix dry ingredients: Whisk all-purpose flour, baking powder, and sea salt together in a separate bowl.

Combine batter: Alternate the dry mixture and whole milk into the butter mixture, beginning and ending with dry. Stir until each addition is nearly combined and scrape the bowl; stop once no flour pockets remain.
Whip whites: In a clean, dry, grease-free bowl, beat large egg whites to stiff peaks. Peaks should stand when the beaters lift; avoid continuing until the foam looks dry or broken.
Fold whites and sprinkles: Fold all the whipped whites and jimmies or flat confetti sprinkles into the batter gently with a spatula, reaching the sides and bottom without beating out the foam.

Bake and cool: Divide all the batter among the prepared pans. Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 35–40 minutes for the original three 8-inch pans. Rotate partway through if browning is uneven. Each center should be set, with a clean tester or a few dry crumbs rather than wet batter. Cool in pans 15 minutes, loosen edges and turn onto racks; cool completely.

Make buttercream: Using unsalted butter, salt, powdered sugar, heavy cream, and vanilla extract, beat the softened frosting butter until smooth, then mix in all the frosting salt. Gradually beat in all the powdered sugar, then add all the heavy cream a little at a time and all the frosting vanilla. Scrape the bowl and beat until smooth and spreadable.

Layer and finish: Frost between all three completely cool layers, then apply a thin crumb coat. Freeze about 10–15 minutes until that coat is firm, then use all the remaining buttercream for the final top and sides. Refrigerate while waiting to serve.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, holiday, entertaining, kid-friendly, comfort-food, bake, no-cook

recipes.name: Gambas al Ajillo
recipes.description: Gambas al ajillo puts garlic and chile into the olive oil that becomes the sauce. Have everything ready before heating the pan: pale golden garlic can turn bitter quickly, and shrimp need to come off the heat as soon as their centers are cooked.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Large Shrimp (16-20 count), peeled and deveined, tails on
2 Dried Guindilla Peppers (or 1 tsp red pepper flakes)
1 tsp Smoked Paprika (pimenton de la Vera)
2 tbsp Fresh Flat-Leaf Parsley, roughly chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Prep Everything First: Thaw frozen shrimp in the refrigerator, then pat dry with paper towels. Season with the measured salt and smoked paprika. Have sliced garlic, your chosen dried peppers or pepper flakes, sherry, parsley and measured lemon juice beside the stove. Keep the shrimp refrigerated until the pan is ready.

Heat the Oil: Pour the full measured olive oil into a cast-iron skillet or a cazuela suitable for your hob over medium heat. When it shimmers, add the garlic and dried guindilla peppers, or the alternative pepper flakes. Cook for 30–45 seconds, swirling, until the garlic is pale golden; lower the heat if it colors too quickly.

Add the Shrimp: Increase to medium-high. Add the shrimp in a single layer, cook for about 1 minute, then turn and begin checking after another 30 seconds. These are first checks, not a required stopping point. For a larger batch, use additional suitable pans or cook separate proportionate batches, dividing all measured oil, seasonings and liquids among them.

Add the Sherry: Pour in the measured sherry carefully and let it bubble, about 30 seconds as a first check. Continue only as needed for the thickest shrimp to reach 145°F, with firm, pearly, opaque flesh through the center. Lower the heat if the garlic darkens before the shrimp finish. A brief simmer does not remove all the alcohol.
Finish: Take the pan off the heat as soon as the shrimp are cooked. Add all the measured lemon juice and parsley. Curl and outside color alone do not establish that the centers are done.
Serve: Serve promptly with crusty bread and all the garlicky oil and sherry sauce. Set a hot skillet on a heatproof trivet and keep its handle out of reach.

recipes.name: Garlic Bread
recipes.description: A measured garlic, parsley and Parmesan butter on a crusty loaf, baked until the edges crisp while the middle stays tender.
recipeIngredient: 400 g crusty Italian-style bread or baguette
4 cloves garlic, finely grated or minced
1/4 tsp fine salt, or less if bread and cheese are salty

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare oven and bread: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Halve the loaf lengthwise and put both pieces cut-side up on a rimmed baking sheet. Use already softened butter; allow extra time if starting with a cold block.
Mix spread: Stir butter, garlic, parsley, Parmesan and the measured salt until uniform. Use less salt if the bread and cheese are already strongly seasoned.
Spread evenly: Divide all the butter mixture across the two cut surfaces, reaching the edges in a thin, even layer. Avoid large isolated clumps of garlic.
Bake: Bake about 12–15 minutes until the edges are golden and the center is hot with melted butter. Thick loaves may need a few more minutes; cover loosely with foil if the edges brown too soon.

Optional top color: If wanted, broil briefly for about 20–60 seconds, watching continuously and stopping as soon as the top colors. Keep the pan at least 6 inches from the element and follow the oven's broiler guidance. Do not put parchment close to a broiler.

Portion: Cut each half into six pieces, making twelve pieces total, or two pieces per side portion. Serve hot. For a small accompaniment to a pasta-containing soup, make half a batch and share its six pieces among six diners.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous
recipes.description: Small semolina pasta toasted in butter, simmered with broth and finished with parsley and optional lemon zest.
recipeIngredient: 225 g (about 1 1/2 cups) dry pearl couscous, not fine instant couscous
2 1/4 cups (540 ml) low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, with package-specific adjustment if needed
1/4 tsp fine salt, added only as needed
1 tsp finely grated lemon zest, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Toast gently: Melt 1 tbsp butter in a 2-quart saucepan over medium. Add pearl couscous and stir 2–3 minutes until a few pearls turn golden. Reduce heat if the butter darkens quickly.

Add garlic and broth: Stir garlic for about 30 seconds, then carefully pour in the measured broth. Add black pepper. Bring to a simmer; hold the salt until you know how salty the broth tastes after cooking.

Cover and cook: Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer about 10–15 minutes, or according to the package’s absorption method, until tender with slight chew. Check near the end. If dry and firm, add hot water 2 tbsp at a time; if tender with excess liquid, uncover briefly to reduce it without overcooking.
Rest and finish: Take off heat and leave covered 5 minutes. Fluff gently, fold in the remaining tablespoon butter, parsley and optional zest. Taste and add the measured salt only if needed.
Portion: Divide into four normal sides or use the smaller portion specified by a composed meal. This recipe already contains its finishing butter; add no extra oil automatically at the table.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, savory, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Green Beans
recipes.description: Cook the beans to the texture you want before the short garlic-butter finish. The blanched route keeps the garlic cooking brief; the direct route adds garlic only after the raw beans have softened.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and blanch: Wash and trim the beans. For the blanched route, bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it to taste separately from the measured finishing salt. Cook beans about 3–4 minutes until barely tender-crisp, checking a thick bean; drain well. To prepare ahead, cool and refrigerate promptly as described below. For the direct route, skip the boiling water and continue with raw trimmed beans.

Prepare almonds: Set aside the already-toasted sliced almonds. If starting with untoasted sliced almonds in the same listed amount, toast in the dry skillet over medium-low heat for about 2–3 minutes, stirring until fragrant and lightly golden; transfer to a plate.

Cook the chosen route: For blanched beans, melt all the cold butter with the sliced garlic over medium heat, stirring about 60–90 seconds until fragrant without deep browning. Add drained beans and toss about 1–2 minutes until hot. For raw beans, melt all the butter over medium heat, add the beans first and cook, tossing, about 7–8 minutes or longer until a thick bean is tender enough to eat. Reduce heat if the butter darkens; then add all the garlic and toss about 60–90 seconds until fragrant. Use more skillets or rounds rather than crowding; divide the same butter and garlic among them.
Season: Season the whole batch with all the measured kosher salt and black pepper. The separate blanching-water salt is an unmeasured preparation allowance, not part of this finishing amount.
Finish: Toss in all the toasted almonds and transfer to a serving dish. Add the listed unmeasured flaky finishing salt to taste and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: French, American, savory, herbaceous, nutty, weeknight, entertaining, comfort-food, saute

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Salmon with Potatoes and Asparagus
recipes.description: Garlic-lemon butter salmon with roasted baby potatoes and asparagus. Give the potatoes a head start, then remove each component when it is ready.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/4 lb skinless salmon fillet, cut into 4 similar portions
1 lb baby Yukon Gold potatoes, halved; quarter larger ones into pieces about 1 inch across
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, divided equally between potatoes and asparagus
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Carolyn Casner’s recipe at EatingWell.

itemListElement.text: Heat and cut: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Halve baby potatoes; quarter larger ones so the pieces are about 1 inch across. Pat salmon dry and check for pin bones. Keep it refrigerated while the potatoes start.

Start potatoes: Toss potatoes with half the olive oil, salt and pepper. Spread cut-side down on the rimmed tray. Roast for about 20–25 minutes, checking at 15, until nearly tender with some browning. If the knife still meets a hard center, continue before adding fish.

Prepare asparagus and butter: While potatoes roast, toss trimmed asparagus with the remaining olive oil, salt and pepper. Stir melted butter, lemon juice and garlic together. Season the salmon lightly with salt and pepper.

Arrange: Move potatoes to one side without piling them deeply. Put salmon in the center and asparagus alongside, using a second tray if needed to prevent overlap. Spoon garlic butter over salmon and asparagus. For very thin asparagus, add it about 5 minutes after the salmon instead.

Finish independently: Roast about 10–15 minutes, checking fish at 10 minutes. Measure the thickest center of each salmon portion from the side for 145°F / 63°C. Check that potatoes are fully tender and asparagus has the bite you like. Lift each finished component to a clean plate while the rest continues; do not leave fish baking solely for the potatoes.
Serve: Divide salmon, potatoes and asparagus among the plates. Spoon over pan butter and scatter with parsley. This includes its own starch and green vegetable; an additional salad is optional.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, date-night, light-and-fresh, bake, roast

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Shrimp
recipes.description: Shrimp in a garlic-butter pan sauce with white wine, lemon zest and parsley.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb raw large shrimp (20–24 per pound), peeled and deveined, tails removed
1/2 cup dry white wine or unsalted chicken stock
1/2 tsp kosher salt, divided to taste
Extra unsalted butter, optional, a small piece for finishing

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Zest the lemon before juicing it and measure the listed juice. Mince garlic and chop parsley. Pat shrimp dry, then season with half the salt and all the pepper. Keep the remaining salt for tasting the sauce.

Cook the shrimp: Melt half the butter over medium to medium-high heat, dividing this allocation between batches if needed. Add shrimp in a single layer without crowding. Cook about 1–2 minutes on the first side, turn, then cook another 1–2 minutes or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Move cooked shrimp to a clean plate; repeat with the remaining shrimp.

Cook the garlic: Reduce heat to medium-low and let the pan cool briefly if very hot. Add the remaining butter and garlic. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, then add pepper flakes for another 15 seconds. Do not let the garlic darken.
Reduce: Pour in wine or stock and scrape up the pale brown pan juices. Bring to a gentle simmer and reduce the liquid by roughly half, about 2–4 minutes, leaving the shrimp on their plate.

Finish: Turn off the heat and stir in lemon juice, parsley and zest. Add the shrimp and their juices and toss to coat; warm briefly over low heat only if needed. Taste and add remaining salt as needed. Swirl in a small piece of optional extra butter if you want a rounder finish.
Serve promptly: Divide shrimp and sauce evenly and serve with separately cooked noodles, rice or bread. Do not hold the finished shrimp in a simmering sauce.

recipes.recipeYield: 4 portions with a separately prepared starch or bread

recipes.name: Garlic Honey Lime Shrimp
recipes.description: Shrimp coated in a sweet honey-lime glaze with garlic, butter and a little cayenne.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
Cayenne pepper, a pinch or to taste
Fresh parsley or cilantro, chopped, for finishing

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Pat thawed shrimp dry. Mince garlic, chop the finishing herbs and measure honey and lime juice. Divide lime juice into two equal portions. Have separately prepared rice and vegetables ready for service.
Warm the garlic: Heat olive oil and butter in the skillet over medium heat. When the butter foams, add garlic and stir about 20–30 seconds until fragrant without browning it deeply.
Start the shrimp: Add shrimp in a single layer. Cook about 1–2 minutes until the underside changes color, then turn. Keep the garlic moving around the shrimp so it does not burn.

Glaze and finish cooking: Add honey, half the lime juice, salt and cayenne. Stir gently and cook about 1–3 minutes more, checking the thicker pieces early, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. If the sauce remains watery, transfer cooked shrimp to a clean plate and simmer the sauce briefly on its own. If too thick, loosen with a small splash of water.

Brighten and serve: Turn off the heat. Stir in the remaining lime juice and return any removed shrimp, tossing to coat. Scatter with parsley or cilantro and serve immediately. Divide the batch among rice-and-vegetable bowls for modest portions, or serve as two larger portions.

recipes.recipeYield: 4 modest portions with rice and vegetables, or 2 larger portions

recipes.name: Garlic Mashed "Mock" Potatoes
recipes.description: Drain the cooked cauliflower well and let surface steam escape before puréeing. Removing free water helps the mash hold its shape, while cream cheese, Parmesan and all the measured butter keep it rich.
recipeIngredient: 1 medium head Cauliflower, cut into small florets
1/2 tsp concentrated chicken or vegetable bouillon paste, using a paste labeled 1 tsp per cup of prepared broth
Salt, for boiling water and to taste; black pepper, to taste
Additional unsalted butter, a pat for serving, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Bring a pot of water to a boil and salt it with the listed allowance. Add small cauliflower florets and cook about 6–8 minutes, until very soft and easily crushed.

Drain and dry: Drain thoroughly in a colander and let surface steam escape briefly. Spread on a heatproof tray if needed. If free water remains, use tongs or a utensil to blot with clean absorbent towels once manageable; do not press scalding florets between paper towels with bare hands. Keep the cauliflower warm where the chosen equipment permits.

Purée: Use a food processor or immersion blender only as its actual manual permits for this food temperature and quantity. Never put hot cauliflower in a sealed personal cup. If cooling is required, allow it and rewarm after puréeing; it adds time. Combine cauliflower with all the cream cheese, Parmesan, minced garlic, specified concentrated bouillon paste and black pepper.

Check texture: Process until smooth, checking safely rather than assuming 1 minute works for every machine. Use batches if needed and recombine; do not add water to compensate for undercooked florets.
Finish: Stir in all the measured butter until melted. Taste after the cheese and bouillon are mixed through, and use any additional salt only if needed. Add the chopped chives.
Serve: Serve warm with the separate optional extra butter pat. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and reheat gently, stirring for even warmth.

recipes.name: Garlic Mashed Red Potatoes
recipes.description: Keep the red skins on and cook the potato quarters with whole garlic cloves until both crush easily. Drain well, then mash by hand with butter, warmed milk and Parmesan.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Scrub the potatoes and leave the skins on. Quarter them into similar-size pieces. Put potatoes and peeled whole garlic in a large pot, cover with cold water and add salt from the listed allowance.
Simmer: Bring to a boil, reduce heat and simmer about 15–20 minutes after boiling, until potato quarters and garlic crush easily. Larger quarters may need longer; check the thickest pieces.
Drain: Drain potatoes and garlic thoroughly. Return to the warm pot briefly, about 1 minute, letting surface steam escape without scorching the bottom.
Mash: Add all the butter and mash potatoes and garlic together by hand. Season with the listed salt and pepper to taste. Keep skin pieces and some rustic texture rather than beating vigorously.
Finish the mash: Gradually add all the warmed milk and Parmesan, mashing just enough to combine. Avoid a blender or food processor for the potatoes; stop at the desired rustic texture.
Serve: Serve promptly. Refrigerate leftovers in shallow containers and reheat gently to the measured leftover endpoint, stirring for even heating.

recipes.name: Chicken and Potatoes with Garlic Parmesan Cream
recipes.description: Seared chicken thighs finished in garlic-Parmesan cream with spinach, served with separately roasted potatoes.
recipeIngredient: cooking spray, as needed for the baking-dish variation, optional
olive oil, as needed to coat the potatoes for roasting
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the spinach
salt, to taste for roasted potatoes
4 tbsp unsalted butter, for the sauce
salt, to taste after the completed bake
black pepper, to taste after the completed bake

recipeInstructions.text: Start the potatoes: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Set out cooking spray (if using), olive oil, baby potatoes, and salt. Quarter the baby potatoes into similar pieces, toss with enough olive oil to coat and salt to taste, and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet pan. Roast about 20–25 minutes, checking for browned edges and a center that yields easily to a knife; continue as needed. Check that all the measured thighs fit without overlap in your oven-safe skillet; use a baking dish for the chicken finish if needed. Prepare the chicken and sauce while the potatoes roast. The optional cooking spray is for the baking-dish variation below, which uses a different oven temperature and omits the separate potato roast.

Brown the chicken: Use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, Italian seasoning, salt, black pepper, and unsalted butter: pat chicken dry with paper towels, then season with Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken skin-side down until deep golden, about 5–7 minutes, then brown the other side for about 2 minutes. Work in batches if needed, reducing heat if the butter or fond begins to burn. Transfer to a plate reserved for partly cooked chicken; continue directly with the recipe.

Wilt the spinach: Use unsalted butter and baby spinach: melt the butter for this step in the skillet, add spinach and stir until it begins to wilt, about 2 minutes. Transfer spinach to a bowl. Pour off excessive rendered chicken fat, keeping the browned fond and leaving no burned bits.

Make the roux: Use unsalted butter, garlic cloves, and all-purpose flour: melt the sauce butter over medium heat. Add garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1–2 minutes, without browning it. Whisk in flour and cook about 1 minute, stirring until smooth and lightly colored.

Finish the sauce: Use chicken broth, dried thyme, dried basil, heavy cream or half-and-half, and freshly grated Parmesan: gradually whisk broth into the roux with thyme and basil, loosening the browned fond. Simmer gently, whisking, until smooth and lightly thickened, about 1–2 minutes. Lower the heat and stir in cream and Parmesan, about 1–2 minutes, until the cheese melts. Do not boil hard after adding cheese. The sauce has contacted partly cooked chicken fond; wait until the final bake is complete before tasting it.

Finish the chicken in sauce: Stir the wilted spinach into the sauce and return the seared chicken skin-side up. Keep as much skin above the sauce as possible. If your oven-safe skillet cannot hold the thighs in one layer, transfer chicken, spinach and sauce to a baking dish large enough to fit them without overlap. Keep the roasted potatoes separate for crispness; adding them to the sauce will soften their surface.

Bake and measure: Transfer the skillet or chicken baking dish to the 425°F oven. Begin checking after about 10 minutes; the thickest part of every thigh, away from bone, and the sauce at the center must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue baking as needed; ten minutes is a first check, not a guarantee of completion. If the skin darkens early, shield it loosely with foil while the meat finishes. Check the separately roasted potatoes for tenderness as well. Rest safely cooked chicken 5 minutes before serving.

Serve: After the bake meets the temperature checks, taste the sauce with a clean spoon. Use salt, black pepper, and fresh parsley (if using): adjust salt and pepper, then add parsley if using. Serve one thigh per portion with potatoes, spinach and sauce.

recipes.name: Toum
recipes.description: This Lebanese garlic sauce requires patience - add oil in the thinnest possible stream, literally drop by drop for the first cup. This allows garlic's natural lecithin to bind oil and water into stable, fluffy foam.

recipeInstructions.text: The Puree: Place the garlic cloves and salt in a food processor. Pulse and scrape until the garlic is a completely smooth, uniform paste.
The First Emulsion: With the motor running, slowly drizzle in 1/2 cup of the oil, drop by drop. The mixture should begin to look like a thick paste.
The Stabilizer: Slowly drizzle in 1 tbsp of the lemon juice. The paste will turn noticeably whiter.
The Stream: Continue the process - alternating between 1/2 cup of oil and 1 tsp of lemon juice - until all the oil and lemon are used. The stream can be slightly thicker now, but never rushed.
The Texture: With the motor still running, slowly add the cold water. This will lighten the paste and give it its signature cloud-like fluffiness.
Set: Transfer to a glass jar and refrigerate for at least 4 hours before using. This allows the garlic vapors to mellow and the emulsion to set.

Store: Refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below and use within 4 days, or freeze small portions promptly. Thaw in the refrigerator; the emulsion may separate. Do not rely on lemon juice alone to establish a longer storage life.

recipes.keywords: Lebanese, Middle Eastern, acidic, rich, meal-prep, entertaining, grill, blend

recipes.name: Garlic Roasted Potatoes
recipes.description: Golden potatoes with tender centers, minced garlic and fresh parsley. Give each piece room on the pan so the cut faces roast instead of steaming.
recipeIngredient: 3 lb small red or Yukon Gold potatoes, scrubbed, dried and cut into roughly 1 1/2-inch pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Scrub and dry the potatoes, then halve or quarter them into roughly 1 1/2-inch pieces. Set out one or two rimmed half-sheet pans according to the space needed.

Coat and spread: Reserve one-quarter of the measured oil for the garlic. Toss potatoes with the remaining oil, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer with a cut face against the pan and a little space between pieces.

Roast until nearly ready: Roast for about 40–55 minutes, turning with a wide spatula after about 25 minutes and again if another face needs browning. Start checking at 40 minutes: a thin knife should slide into a thick center easily and the cut faces should have golden patches. If still firm, continue before adding garlic. Rotate pans and swap racks if using two.

Add garlic: Mix the garlic with the reserved oil. Once the potatoes are nearly tender, toss this mixture through them and return to the oven for about 5 minutes, watching for fragrant, pale-golden garlic. Extend briefly if needed for tenderness; stop before garlic turns dark. Total roasting is usually 45–60 minutes, but doneness governs.
Finish: Transfer to a serving bowl and toss with the parsley. Serve promptly, dividing into side portions. Avoid covering tightly during a short wait, which traps steam and softens the crust.

citation.name: Adapted from Ina Garten, Garlic Roasted Potatoes

recipes.name: Garlic Sauteed Green Beans
recipes.description: Green beans with browned patches, sliced garlic and a little lemon. A brief covered steam helps thicker beans become tender before the garlic goes in.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb fresh green beans, stem ends trimmed
2 tbsp olive oil, divided between the beans and garlic
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Water, a small splash only if needed to finish firm beans

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Trim, wash and thoroughly dry the beans. Slice garlic and measure lemon juice. Set aside one-quarter of the oil for garlic; the remainder is for cooking the beans.

Brown: Heat the bean oil in a broad skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add beans in a shallow layer with room to toss, splitting beans and this oil between rounds if crowded. Leave undisturbed about 2 minutes, then toss and cook another 3–5 minutes until browned in patches. Reduce heat if they scorch.

Check the center: Taste a cooled bean. If still firm, lower heat to medium, add a small splash of water carefully and cover for 2–4 minutes, then check again. Add another small splash only if the pan dries before the beans become tender. Uncover and let excess water evaporate. Skip steaming if already tender. If browning in rounds, finish their tenderness separately before combining.

Add garlic gently: Return all beans to the pan if using rounds. Reduce heat to medium-low and move the skillet off the burner briefly if still very hot. Push beans aside, add the reserved oil, garlic and optional pepper flakes. Stir for about 30–60 seconds until fragrant and lightly golden, then toss through the beans.
Season and serve: Remove from heat. Add salt, black pepper and the measured lemon juice. Toss and taste, then divide into side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, herbaceous, weeknight, light-and-fresh, saute, steam

recipes.name: Sigeumchi Namul (Sesame Spinach)
recipes.description: Briefly blanched spinach, cooled and gently squeezed, then loosened with garlic, sesame oil and toasted seeds.
recipeIngredient: 450 g fresh baby spinach, washed, tough stems removed
Cold water and ice, for cooling
1 tsp finely minced fresh garlic, added gradually to taste
1/4 tsp fine salt, added gradually to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Wash spinach and remove tough stems. Bring 2 liters water to a boil in a large pot. Fill a large bowl with cold water and ice and set a colander nearby.

Blanch in two batches: Submerge half the spinach, stir it under the water and cook about 30–60 seconds, until leaves wilt and stems bend. Lift directly into the cold water. Let the pot return to a boil and repeat with the remaining spinach.

Cool, drain and press: Once spinach is cool, drain. Take small handfuls and squeeze gently to remove excess water, stopping while the leaves remain moist. Do not twist into a hard, dry mass. Cut long strands into bite-sized lengths and loosen with your fingers in a bowl.
Season: Add sesame oil, seeds, half the garlic and half the salt. Toss gently, taste a small portion, then add remaining garlic and salt only as needed. Avoid crushing the greens into a paste.
Serve or chill: Divide into four small side portions. Serve promptly at cool room temperature or refrigerate until wanted. The spinach is blanched and dressed, not sautéed in garlic oil.

recipes.name: Garlicky Lemon Kale with Carrots
recipes.description: Thin carrot coins get a head start before the kale. Add the leaves in manageable handfuls, then use the measured water or broth for a short covered steam.
recipeIngredient: 1 large bunch Kale (stems removed; about 8 cups chopped for the original batch)
3 medium Carrots, sliced into thin coins
1/2 Lemon, juiced (about 2 tbsp juice for the original batch)
1/2 tsp Kosher Salt (plus more to taste)
1/4 tsp Red Pepper Flakes (optional, for heat)
1 tsp Sesame Oil (optional, for Asian-style preparation)

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Wash kale and carrots under running water. Remove the tough kale stems and chop leaves into roughly 2-inch pieces. Slice the carrots into thin coins. About 8 cups kale and about 2 tbsp juice from half a lemon describe the original batch, not exact scaled equivalents.

Cook carrots: Heat all the measured olive or vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add all carrots and sauté about 3–4 minutes, tossing until starting to soften with some color on the edges. Use enough vessels for the full batch, dividing all the cooking oil and later ingredients among them.
Add garlic: Add all minced garlic and cook about 30 seconds until fragrant, reducing heat if it browns quickly.
Wilt: Add kale in handfuls, tossing each until it settles enough for the next. Do not pile more than the vessel can toss and cover.

Steam: Add all the measured water or broth, cover and steam about 2–3 minutes, then check a leaf and carrot. Continue as needed until tender to your liking; a bright green color alone is not a tenderness test.

Finish: Uncover and toss about 30–60 seconds to evaporate excess liquid without drying the pan. Remove from heat. Add juice from all the listed lemon, all measured salt and black pepper, and optional red-pepper flakes. Add the optional measured sesame oil now if wanted. Toss through.
Serve: Taste and use the listed additional-salt allowance if needed. Additional lemon juice or pepper is optional seasoning beyond the measured base; serve warm.

recipes.keywords: American, Mediterranean, acidic, savory, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, saute, steam

recipes.name: Gefilte Fish Terrine
recipes.description: Eli and Max Sussman’s baked gefilte-fish terrine combines salmon with carp or pike and sets in a water bath. Coarsely ground fish gives a different texture from a smooth paste.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet, chopped
12 oz Boneless skinless salmon fillet, chopped
2 Lemons for zest, zest only; measured juice separate
2 cups Baby arugula, rinsed unless labeled prewashed or ready-to-eat; drained
1 tbsp Fresh horseradish, peeled and grated
Black pepper for salad, to taste
Boiling water for water bath, as needed to reach halfway up the loaf pan

recipeInstructions.text: Sweat onion: Rinse fresh produce under running water before peeling, cutting or zesting, including the lemons, dill, shallot and horseradish; follow any prewashed or ready-to-eat arugula label. Heat the assigned oil from 1/3 of the Olive oil and Medium onion in a skillet. Cook the onion about 8–10 minutes until soft and translucent without browning; transfer all the onion and cooking oil to a mixing bowl.

Grind fish: Keep Boneless skinless carp or pike fillet and Boneless skinless salmon fillet cold during preparation; check for bones. Pulse in a food processor until coarsely ground, then add to the onion bowl. Do not grind to a smooth paste.

Bind: Stir Heavy cream, Matzo meal, Large eggs, Carrot, Fresh dill, Lemons for zest, 1/9 of the Lemon juice, Cold water, Black pepper, and Kosher salt into the fish and onion until evenly combined. Add one ninth of the measured lemon juice here and reserve the remaining eight ninths for the salad. The original batch uses 1 tsp juice here; scale that share with the listed juice total. All the measured cream, matzo meal, eggs, carrot, dill, lemon zest, water, salt and pepper belong in this mixture.

Prepare pan: Preheat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, line the bottom and sides of a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan with nonstick baking parchment rated for at least 325°F, leaving overhang to fold over the surface. Spread all the mixture into the pan, fold the parchment over it and cover with foil. Keep the paper inside the covered pan; do not use wax paper or ordinary plastic wrap. Multiples need separate original-size loaves and baths; smaller amounts need appropriate smaller pans and earlier center checks. Keep comparable mixture depth and headroom rather than forcing every scale into this pan.

Water bath: Place the loaf pan in an original-batch 9-by-13-inch baking dish, or a suitable larger outer vessel, and carefully add Boiling water for water bath. Support the hot vessels securely and keep bath water out of the fish mixture.

Bake: Bake at 325°F, checking near the original 1 hour 15 minute planning time. Continue until a thin-tip thermometer in the center reaches 160°F /71°C and the center is firm. Check the center of every separately baked loaf; a firm surface or clean knife alone does not replace the measured endpoint.

Cool and chill: Remove the loaf pan carefully from the hot bath and cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate promptly at 40°F /4°C or below, within 2 hours of cooking (1 hour above 90°F /32°C). Chill at least 4 hours until cold throughout before inverting and peeling away the parchment. Making it the day before allows cooling and chilling without rushing.

Finish salad: Toss 2/3 of the Olive oil, 8/9 of the Lemon juice, Baby arugula, Radishes, Fresh horseradish, Shallot, Dill sprigs, Salt for salad, and Black pepper for salad together just before serving. Use all the remaining two thirds of the measured olive oil and eight ninths of the measured lemon juice, with the separate salad salt and pepper allowances. The original batch uses 2 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp plus 2 tsp juice here; scale those shares with the listed totals. Keep washed vegetables and raw-fish tools separate.

Serve: Slice the chilled terrine and serve with all the salad, Lemon wedges and Matzos. Ten portions are the planning yield for the original batch; slicing that original loaf into 8–10 portions is another serving option. Refrigerate unused terrine promptly, keeping the fresh salad separate.

recipes.name: General Tso's Cauliflower
recipes.description: This vegetarian General Tso adaptation brings a Chinese-American takeout sauce to cauliflower. The cauliflower gets an egg-and-starch coating and a separate soy, vinegar and mirin glaze.
recipeIngredient: 1 cauliflower head, washed, well drained and cut into bite-sized florets
water, as needed to thin overly stiff batter
1/2 cup peanut or vegetable oil, for shallow frying
6 scallions, washed; whites finely sliced and greens cut into 1-inch pieces, reserved
sesame seeds, for garnish, if wanted, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the batter: For the batter, use all-purpose flour, cornstarch, baking powder, salt, large eggs, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and water. Whisk the flour, coating cornstarch, baking powder and salt. Separately whisk the eggs, batter soy sauce and batter vinegar, then pour into the dry mixture while whisking. If too stiff to coat a floret, stir in a little of the thinning-water allowance until thick but dip-able. Do not taste raw egg/flour batter.

Fry the cauliflower: Use cauliflower head and peanut or vegetable oil for this stage. For the measured-oil route, heat the full listed frying oil in a skillet suitable for shallow frying. The separate oil-to-depth option uses a different, unmeasured frying supply. A small drop of batter should sizzle and float promptly without burning. Dip florets and fry in uncrowded rounds, turning until golden on all sides, starting checks around 4–5 minutes per original-size round. Cut a large sample: the coating should be set without wet batter and the center tender. Check 160°F in large coated pieces with a thin probe from the side; color alone is not an egg-batter endpoint. Lift onto absorbent paper towels; do not pour unused raw batter into the sauce.

Start the sauce: Have sesame oil, scallions, garlic cloves, fresh ginger, and small dried red chilies (if using) ready. Heat the sesame oil over medium heat in a saucepan with room for the finished dish. Stir scallion whites, garlic, ginger and optional chilies about 30 seconds until fragrant, lowering heat if garlic browns. Keep all the scallion greens aside for the thickened sauce.

Simmer the sauce liquids: Add vegetable broth, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and mirin, bring to a simmer and cook about 5 minutes over medium heat. The distinct batter and sauce soy/vinegar measures are both used.

Disperse the sauce starch: Whisk granulated sugar and cornstarch together in a small bowl. For the original batch, gradually whisk about 1/4 cup of hot sauce from the saucepan into this mixture until smooth; for a scaled batch take the corresponding proportional amount from that same sauce supply. Return all this mixture to the pot, bring to a simmer and add all the reserved scallion greens. This is recirculated sauce, not extra broth.

Finish thickening: Cook, stirring occasionally, about 7–9 minutes more, checking for a glossy sauce that clings to a spoon without scorching. Lower heat as needed; do not treat the clock as a requirement to boil a nearly dry pot.

Glaze the cauliflower: Add all the fried cauliflower and fold gently until coated and rewarmed, starting checks around 4–5 minutes for the original batch. Use enough uncrowded vessels for larger batches, dividing the entire batter, frying oil and sauce quantities proportionally. Serve promptly; extended holding softens the coating.
Serve: Garnish with sesame seeds (if using) and serve with separately prepared steamed rice.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, fry, saute, simmer, steam

recipes.name: General Tso's Tofu
recipes.description: This tofu adaptation brings a Chinese-American takeout sauce to plant-based protein. Coat the dry tofu gently with honey, thin red-pepper hot sauce, sesame seeds and cornstarch, then fry uncrowded pieces before making the glaze.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb extra-firm tofu, pressed dry and cut into 1-inch squares
2 tsp thin vinegar-based red-pepper hot sauce
1/3 cup peanut oil, for shallow frying; part is reused for aromatics

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the slurry: Mix cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl. Keep this separate from the tofu coating; re-stir just before adding it to the sauce.

Coat the tofu: For the coating, use extra-firm tofu, honey, thin vinegar-based red-pepper hot sauce, sesame seeds, and cornstarch. Wash and drain the vegetables before cutting. Mix the honey and hot sauce, gently toss in the dry tofu, then add all the sesame seeds and coating cornstarch. Lift and turn rather than crushing the pieces; aim for a light coating, not a pool of wet batter.

Fry in batches: Heat peanut oil in a shallow-frying skillet to about 350°F. Carefully add coated tofu in a single layer with space between pieces. Fry about 4–5 minutes per original-size round, turning once, until golden with a formed crust; lower heat if the coating darkens too quickly. Lift to a sheet pan with a slotted spoon. Repeat without crowding, allowing the oil to recover its heat.

Cook the aromatics: Have fresh ginger, garlic cloves, dried Chinese red chilies, red bell pepper, and Shaoxing wine (if using) ready. Transfer a portion of the used frying oil to a wok or saucepan: 3/16 of the listed frying-oil amount, which is 1 tbsp for the original batch. This comes from the frying supply, not an additional dose; do not add the remaining frying oil to the sauce. Heat over medium and stir the ginger, garlic and chilies about 30 seconds until fragrant, without scorching. Add all the bell pepper and optional wine.

Cook the broccoli: Use vegetable stock and broccoli florets in sequence: bring all the stock to a boil first, then add all the broccoli. Keep enough room to turn the vegetables; use additional vessels with the complete ingredients divided proportionally for larger batches.

Season and thicken: Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rice vinegar, salt, granulated sugar, and toasted sesame oil and return the sauce to a boil. Re-stir the separate slurry, then pour it in gradually while stirring. Simmer 30–60 seconds after each addition before deciding whether more is needed; stop when it coats a spoon and leave any unused slurry out of the dish. Continue until a broccoli stem yields with slight resistance.

Glaze and serve: Return all the fried tofu to the ready sauce and fold gently about 30 seconds to coat without breaking the pieces. Serve promptly over separately prepared rice. Holding glazed tofu softens its coating.

recipes.name: Glazed Carrots
recipes.description: Simmer the carrot sticks until tender, drain well and return them to the full butter-and-brown-sugar glaze. Keep the glaze salt separate from any optional salt in the boiling water.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs carrots, peeled and cut into matchsticks
Water, for a 1-inch depth in the saucepan
Salt as needed, optional for the boiling water

recipeInstructions.text: Wash and peel the carrots, then cut even matchsticks. Put them in a large saucepan and add water to a 1-inch depth. Use plain water, or add the separate optional boiling-salt allowance if you prefer salted water. The measured glaze salt stays reserved.

Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low and cover. Start checking around 8–10 minutes, sooner for very thin sticks. A fork should enter a center readily without raw hardness; stop before the sticks fall apart. Boiling and actual cut thickness determine the clock.

Drain and transfer the carrots to a bowl without rinsing. Melt all the butter in the same saucepan over low heat, then stir in all the brown sugar, glaze salt and white pepper until dissolved and glossy.

Return all the drained carrots and toss gently over medium-low heat until hot and coated. Start checking at 2–3 minutes; the carrots may need up to about 5 minutes to heat through and take on the glaze. Follow the clinging glaze rather than driving the sugar to a burnt crust.
Stir in all the optional listed thyme if using and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Glazed Chicken & Broccoli Sheet Pan Dinner
recipes.description: Chicken drumsticks with ginger-teriyaki glaze, fingerling potatoes and broccoli, roasted in stages.
recipeIngredient: black pepper, to taste for potatoes
1 broccoli head, cut into small florets
black pepper, to taste for broccoli
2 tbsp teriyaki glaze, thick purchased glaze or prepared homemade glaze

recipeInstructions.text: Start chicken and potatoes: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with foil, or parchment rated by its manufacturer for this temperature. Use skin-on chicken drumsticks, fingerling potatoes, 1/3 of the extra-virgin olive oil, salt, and black pepper: pat the drumsticks dry with paper towels and space them on one side. Put potatoes on the other side, leaving room in the center for broccoli. Toss potatoes with their one-third share of the oil, salt and pepper. Roast about 20 minutes, until potatoes begin to soften and chicken begins to brown.

Add broccoli: Use 2/3 of the extra-virgin olive oil, broccoli head, salt, and black pepper: add broccoli to the center space, tossing it with the remaining two-thirds of the oil, salt and pepper. Spread into one layer. If the vegetables crowd the chicken or pile up, use a second rimmed pan rather than compressing everything.

Brush on glaze: Mix teriyaki glaze and fresh ginger in a small bowl and brush a thin, even layer over the chicken. Keep this brush and bowl separate from serving utensils. Discard any glaze left in the bowl after the brush touches partly cooked chicken.

Finish roasting: Return to the 450°F oven and roast about 20–25 minutes more. The potatoes should be tender and the broccoli browned in spots; check the thickest part of every drumstick, away from bone, for 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking as needed. If the glaze darkens too quickly, loosely shield the chicken with foil while it reaches its endpoint. If vegetables sharing the chicken pan finish first, check that they have reached 165°F / 74°C after contact with chicken juices before transferring them with clean utensils to a clean dish. Vegetables cooked on a separate pan without chicken contact can be removed when tender. Continue cooking the chicken to its endpoint.

Rest and serve: Rest the safely cooked chicken for 5 minutes, then divide chicken and vegetables among the portions. Leave behind any scorched glaze on the pan rather than scraping it over the potatoes.

recipes.name: Gluten-Free Lemon Cupcakes
recipes.description: Beat oil and sugar for a full minute before adding eggs - this creates a stable fat-sugar network that traps moisture in gluten-free flour. Use both lemon juice and zest in the batter, then finish with sharp lemon buttercream for bright, fresh flavor.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/4 cups gluten-free measure-for-measure baking flour blend containing xanthan gum
2 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Finishing Touch)

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Whisk together GF flour, baking powder, and salt. Set aside.
The Emulsion: In a large bowl, beat the oil and sugar with an electric mixer for 1 minute. Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Stir in vanilla, lemon juice, and zest.
Combine: Gradually add the flour mixture and milk. Mix until just combined - GF flour doesn't develop gluten, but over-mixing can still lead to a gummy "Bounce."
Bake: Divide batter among 12 lined cups (about 2/3 full). Bake at 350°F for 18-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool completely before frosting. GF cakes are structurally fragile while warm.
The Frosting: Beat butter until creamy. Add lemon juice and 1 cup of sugar. Beat until smooth. Gradually add remaining sugar and milk until the frosting holds a stiff peak.
Finish: Frost generously. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

recipes.name: Gnocchi with Zucchini Ribbons & Brown Butter
recipes.description: Brown butter (beurre noisette in French, literally "hazelnut butter") is a classic Italian and French technique where you cook butter until milk solids turn golden and release nutty aroma. Use a vegetable peeler to shave zucchini into paper-thin ribbons so they wilt quickly.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Fresh or Frozen Potato Gnocchi
1 lb Zucchini (about 3 small), shaved into ribbons

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook gnocchi until they float (3-5 mins). Drain.
Brown: Meanwhile, in a large skillet, melt butter over medium-high heat. Cook for 2 minutes until it stops foaming and turns golden brown with a nutty aroma.
Aromatics: Add shallots and zucchini ribbons. Sauté for 2 minutes, tossing constantly until just wilted.
Emulsify: Add halved tomatoes, salt, nutmeg, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes until the tomatoes just begin to release their juices and form a light sauce.
Toss: Add the drained gnocchi, Parmesan, and parsley to the skillet.
Bind: Toss vigorously for 30 seconds until the cheese is melted and the gnocchi is glossy and coated. Serve immediately.

recipes.keywords: Italian, umami, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, light-and-fresh, saute, boil

recipes.name: Golden Veil
recipes.description: Slap the thyme sprig sharply in your palm before garnishing - this ruptures oil glands and releases the herb's essence without the bitterness of muddling. Add Prosecco only after shaking and straining the base so bubbles stay effervescent, cutting through smoky mezcal and rich cognac.
recipeIngredient: 2.5 oz Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
1 oz French honeyed herbal liqueur (40% ABV)

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Chill a large coupe or wine glass in the freezer for 10 minutes.
The Base: Combine gin, mezcal, cognac, lemon juice, French honeyed herbal liqueur, agave, and orange bitters in a shaker filled with large ice cubes.
Aeration: Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until the shaker is frosted and the mixture is perfectly emulsified.
Strain: Double strain into the chilled glass to ensure a silky mouthfeel.
The Crown: Top with the chilled Prosecco. Do not stir - let the bubbles naturally integrate the layers.
The Slap: Take the thyme sprig, slap it between your palms, and place it in the glass. Express the lemon peel over the rim and drop it in for the mandatory High Note.

recipes.name: Brined Roast Turkey, Inspired by Good Eats
recipes.description: An aromatic wet-brined whole turkey with salt measured by weight, a refrigerated preparation schedule and checks in breast, thigh and wing.
recipeIngredient: 1 whole young turkey, 14–16 lb (6.4–7.3 kg), fully refrigerator-thawed, not kosher, pre-brined or enhanced with a salt solution
225 g salt, weighed regardless of crystal size
3.8 L cold water, for the brine
2 tbsp canola or other neutral oil
150 g red apple, cored and sliced
1 cup (240 ml) water, for the roasting pan, plus up to 2 cups (480 ml) hot water if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Make and chill the brine concentrate: Put 1 L of the measured stock in a saucepan with all the weighed salt, sugar, peppercorns, allspice and ginger. Bring to a simmer and stir until dissolved, then remove from heat. Cool the saucepan in an ice-water bath, stirring the brine without getting bath water into it, then refrigerate until 40°F / 4°C or below. Keep the remaining 2.8 L stock and 3.8 L water cold. Budget up to two hours for cooling and use a thermometer rather than a clock to confirm readiness.

Brine for twelve hours: Remove packaging, neck and giblet bags from the fully thawed turkey. Reserve neck/giblets separately under appropriate refrigerated storage or discard. Combine the cold concentrate, remaining cold stock and measured water in a food-grade brining container. Submerge the turkey breast-side down, cover, and refrigerate for twelve hours at 40°F / 4°C or below. If necessary use a close-fitting food-grade brining bag supported in a deep leak-catching container; do not top up with plain water or leave the setup outside the refrigerator. The turkey’s original raw-storage limit still applies.

Drain and dry: Lift the bird carefully, letting cavity liquid drain into the container. Discard all used brine. Do not rinse the turkey in the sink. Pat dry with disposable towels, remove clinging spice pieces, and set on a rack over a rimmed tray, uncovered in the refrigerator, for four hours. Keep it below and separate from ready-to-eat foods. Clean raw-poultry contact surfaces.

Prepare for roasting: Heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C. Put the apple, onion, cinnamon, rosemary, sage and initial cup of pan water below a rack in a shallow roasting pan. Set turkey breast-side up on the rack, leaving its cavity empty; cook any dressing separately. Tuck wing tips underneath and brush the skin with the measured oil. Place a probe in the thickest breast meat without touching bone if using a leave-in thermometer.

Roast and check the whole bird: Roast for roughly 3 3/4–4 1/4 hours, beginning checks around three hours. Keep a shallow film of liquid in the pan, adding the listed hot water in small amounts if it dries; do not pour water over the skin. Shield areas that brown early loosely with foil. Before removing the bird, use an instant-read thermometer to verify at least 165°F / 74°C in both thick breast sections, the innermost part of each thigh and the innermost wing areas, away from bone. Continue cooking if any site is below that endpoint. The time is a planning range, not a finish guarantee.

Rest and carve: Transfer to a clean carving board, cover loosely and rest thirty minutes. Remove breast meat from the breastbone and slice across its grain; separate leg and thigh joints for serving. Offer about twelve portions with sides, distributing light and dark meat as desired. Pan aromatics are for flavoring drippings rather than a required side; discard them after straining drippings if used.
