recipes.name: Grandmommy’s Pecan Pie
recipes.description: Southern pecan pie is built on a simple syrup custard that's meant to barely set - you're aiming for that wobbling center that firms up completely as it cools. Karo syrup is traditional for a reason: it creates the right balance of sweetness and texture without crystallizing.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 350°F. Place the unbaked pie shells on a baking sheet.
The Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar, Karo syrup, and slightly beaten eggs until well combined.
The Emulsion: Slowly whisk in the melted butter, vanilla, and salt until the filling is glossy and uniform.
Layer: Divide the pecans evenly between the two pie shells. Pour the syrup mixture over the pecans - they will naturally float to the top to create the Crunch layer.
Bake: Bake for 40-45 minutes until the edges are set and the center has a slight, stable wobble (the Texture).
Cool: Let cool completely (at least 2 hours) before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

recipes.keywords: Southern, sweet, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Grandmommy’s Pound Cake
recipes.description: Grandmommy’s pound cake has a rich, buttery crumb. The key is baking at 275°F for a full 90 minutes; this ensures the cake rises evenly without a tough outer crust, resulting in a dense, velvety texture that defines a true pound cake.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 275°F. Generously grease and flour a large Bundt pan or three 9x5 loaf pans.
Cream: In a stand mixer, cream the butter and sugar on medium-high for 5-7 minutes until the mixture is pale, light, and doubled in volume.
Emulsify: Add the eggs one at a time, beating for 30 seconds after each addition to ensure a stable structure.
Incorporate: Reduce speed to low. Gradually add the pre-sifted flour in three parts, mixing until just combined.
Flavor: Fold in the lemon, almond, and vanilla extracts by hand.
Bake: Pour the thick batter into the prepared pan. Bake at 275°F for 1.5 hours (or at 300°F for 1 hour if using loaf pans) until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 20 minutes before inverting onto a rack.

recipes.keywords: Southern, sweet, acidic, rich, holiday, entertaining, weekend-project, comfort-food, bake

recipes.name: Grandmommy’s Turkey Dressing
recipes.description: A soft, spoonable family dressing made with crumbled unsweetened cornbread, white bread, onion, celery and poultry seasoning.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup self-rising cornmeal mix, spooned into the cup and leveled; use an unsweetened mix containing leavening and salt
8 tbsp (113 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled until just warm
180 g plain white sandwich bread, about 6–7 ordinary slices, weighed before drying
150 g celery, finely diced, about 3 medium stalks
200 g yellow onion, finely diced, about 1 large onion
4 1/2 cups (1080 ml) unsalted chicken or turkey stock, measured as a reserve; add only as needed, including the portion used for the vegetables
2–3 tsp salt-free poultry seasoning, to taste
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus up to 1/2 tsp more after tasting
2 tsp softened unsalted butter, divided, for greasing both pans

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cornbread: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Grease an 8-inch square metal pan with one teaspoon of the pan butter. Whisk the self-rising cornmeal mix and flour in one bowl. In another, whisk the milk, eggs and just-warm melted butter. Fold wet into dry only until no dry flour remains. Do not taste the raw batter. Spread in the pan and bake promptly.

Bake and cool: Bake about 30–40 minutes, checking at 30 minutes, until golden and a tester inserted in the center comes out with crumbs but no wet batter. Cool in the pan on a rack for 15 minutes, then turn out carefully and cool another 30–45 minutes, until no warmth remains in the middle. A compact crumb is acceptable for this dressing; a gummy, underbaked center is not.

Dry the white bread during cooling: Reduce the oven to 300°F / 150°C. Tear the white bread into small pieces and spread in one layer on a rimmed sheet. Dry about 15–25 minutes, turning once, until a cooled piece feels dry through the center, with little browning. Already dry bread may need less time. Cool on the sheet while the vegetables cook; this cooling overlaps the cornbread cooling period.

Tenderize the vegetables: Put onion, celery and half a cup of the measured stock in a covered skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook about 10–15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the celery is tender and the onion has no raw bite. If the pan dries before the vegetables soften, add a spoonful of stock from the measured supply. Keep any remaining pan liquid; it counts toward the dressing's total stock.

Crumble, season and hydrate: Heat the oven to 350°F / 177°C and grease a roughly 3-quart, 9-by-13-inch dish with the remaining teaspoon of butter. Crumble the entire cooled cornbread into coarse crumbs in a very large bowl; add the dried white bread, cooked vegetables and their liquid. Fold in two teaspoons of poultry seasoning, the pepper and half a teaspoon of salt. Fold in further stock in half-cup additions, allowing each addition to absorb before deciding on the next. Once evenly damp, wait five minutes, then add more stock a quarter-cup at a time only if dry centers remain. Stop when a spoonful forms a loose, moist mound without liquid collecting beneath it; the full reserve is not compulsory. Stock used for the vegetables comes from this same measured supply. Taste a cooled spoonful now that the eggs and flour are cooked; add the remaining seasoning or salt only if needed.

Bake immediately: Spread loosely in the prepared dish without pressing it dense. Bake uncovered about 50–60 minutes, until the center reaches at least 165°F / 74°C and the surface and edges are golden. Check around 40 minutes; if the top browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil and finish to the measured center temperature.
Rest and serve: Rest 10 minutes and spoon into twelve side portions. Serve with turkey and tart cranberry sauce; the cranberry supplies brightness without changing the family dressing's flavor.

recipes.keywords: Southern, American, savory, herbaceous, rich, holiday, entertaining, bake, simmer

recipes.name: Executive Granola
recipes.description: This is the go-to granola recipe for batch breakfast prep. The secret to getting those perfect clusters is creating a stable emulsion: whisk the oil and maple syrup together before pouring over the oats.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Mixed Nuts (Almonds, Walnuts, Pecans), chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Preheat oven to 350°F. In a large bowl, toss together oats, nuts, and seeds.
The Emulsion: In a separate jar or bowl, whisk together the oil, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt until smooth and uniform.
Combine: Pour the liquid emulsion over the dry mix. Toss with a spatula until the oats look dark and saturated.
The Roast: Spread the mixture in a thin, even layer on a large rimmed baking sheet.
Stir: Bake for 20-25 minutes. Stir the granola every 8 minutes to ensure the edges don't burn and the center gets crispy.
The Finish: Remove from the oven when deep golden brown. The granola will still feel soft; it will Crunch only after cooling.
Finish: Once stone-cold, stir in the dried fruit. Store in an airtight glass jar for up to 3 weeks.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, meal-prep, snack, bake, roast, blend

recipes.name: Grapefruit-Basil Gin Fizz
recipes.description: Muddling the basil before adding liquids releases its chlorophyll and essential oils, creating the botanical foundation of this cocktail. Fresh pink grapefruit provides bright acidity, amplified with aromatic bitters to bridge the gap between bitter tonic and sweet citrus.

recipeInstructions.text: Muddle: Place the chopped basil in the bottom of a tall Collins glass or highball glass. Use a muddler or the back of a spoon to press firmly for 10 seconds.
Thermal Prep: Fill the glass to the brim with large ice cubes.
Combine: Pour in the gin and the fresh grapefruit juice. Stir twice to integrate.
Effervescence: Top with the tonic water or seltzer. Do not stir again - let the bubbles carry the basil essence to the top.
The Finishing Touch: Add 3 dashes of bitters directly onto the surface.
The Slap: Take the basil sprig, slap it between your palms to release the scent, and tuck it into the ice as a garnish.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, herbaceous, entertaining, light-and-fresh, mix

recipes.name: Greek-Style Lamb Burgers with Mint Yogurt
recipes.description: Herbed lamb patties in warm pita with a cool, thick cucumber-mint yogurt sauce and measured optional toppings.
recipeIngredient: 680 g ground lamb, preferably about 80–85% lean
60 g yellow onion, very finely minced
1 clove garlic, finely grated, for the patties
3 tbsp finely chopped fresh mint, for the patties
1/2 tsp fine salt, for the patties
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, for the patties
2 tsp olive oil, for the skillet, divided
1 1/2 cups prepared [Mint Tzatziki with Honey](/mise/recipes/mint-tzatziki), approximately
4 pita breads, about 6–7 inches across; warm using [Warm, Soft Pita Bread](/recipes/warm-pita-bread)
40 g mixed greens, washed and dried, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Make the sauce and prepare toppings: Make one full batch of Mint Tzatziki with Honey, approximately 1 1/2 cups, or measure the same amount already prepared. This is the sauce counted in the ingredients; make it once. Refrigerate while preparing the meat. Slice any optional tomato and wash/dry greens before handling raw lamb. Heat the oven to 350°F / 175°C for the bread.

Mix and shape: Combine cold lamb with onion, patty garlic, the three tablespoons each of mint and parsley, patty salt and patty pepper. Fold gently just until evenly mixed and cohesive. Divide into four equal patties, each using about 170 g meat plus its share of aromatics. Shape into broad rounds or ovals about 3/4 inch thick. Keep the second pair refrigerated while the first cooks.

Cook the first pair: Heat a 12-inch heavy skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 tsp of the skillet oil and two patties with space between them. Cook about 4–5 minutes on the first side until well browned, then turn with a broad spatula. Reduce to medium as needed and cook another 4–5 minutes, then check from the side into each center. Continue cooking and turning as needed until each reaches 160°F / 71°C; allow roughly 10–14 minutes per batch. Do not press out the juices. Transfer to a clean plate and cover loosely.

Cook the second pair and warm bread: Carefully spoon excessive rendered fat into a heatproof container, leaving a thin film in the pan; add the remaining 1 tsp skillet oil. Cook the second pair with the same temperature check. During this batch, warm the four pitas as a foil-wrapped stack using the oven method, without the optional finishing oil or salt. Check the center bread and keep the stack wrapped. The first patties soften and cool slightly during this brief wait; a large griddle avoids the wait if available.

Balance and assemble: Stir and taste the chilled mint tzatziki. Start with 2–3 tbsp inside each pita and offer the remaining sauce alongside. Add one cooked patty to each and divide any optional feta, tomato and greens among them. Fold or serve open-faced if the bread is small. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Greek-inspired, acidic, rich, herbaceous, entertaining, pan-fry, no-cook

recipes.name: Greek-Style Turkey Meatball Pitas
recipes.description: Oregano and spinach turkey meatballs roasted in one batch, with a small cucumber-yogurt sauce and fresh vegetables.
recipeIngredient: 30 g baby spinach, washed, thoroughly dried and finely chopped
40 g red onion, very finely minced, for the meatballs
3/8 tsp fine salt, for the meatballs
1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for the meatballs
1 tbsp olive oil, for the tray and meatball surfaces, divided
3/4 cup (180 g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt
75 g English cucumber, coarsely grated then squeezed, for the sauce
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
1/8 tsp fine salt, for the sauce
4 pita breads, about 6–7 inches across; warm using [Warm, Soft Pita Bread](/recipes/warm-pita-bread)
100 g English cucumber, diced, for serving
30 g red onion, thinly sliced, for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Brush a rimmed half-sheet pan with 1 tsp of the oil. Wash, dry and cut the vegetables as listed, keeping the sauce cucumber separate from the serving cucumber. Reserve the remaining 2 tsp oil for the meatball surfaces.

Make the sauce: Squeeze the grated 75 g sauce cucumber in a clean towel until dripping slows, then stir into yogurt with the initial tablespoon of lemon juice, dill, garlic powder and sauce salt. Refrigerate. Keep the serving tomato, cucumber and sliced onion separate; do not stir them into the meat.

Mix and portion: Fold turkey with dried chopped spinach, the 40 g minced onion, fresh garlic, oregano, meatball salt and pepper. Mix just until evenly distributed and cohesive. Divide into twelve equal balls, roughly 45 g each and about 1 1/2 inches across. Set apart on the prepared tray and dab their surfaces with the remaining 2 tsp oil. Wash hands and raw-meat utensils before touching bread or sauce.

Roast and measure: Roast for about 15–20 minutes. Start checking at fifteen minutes by inserting a thermometer into the center of several of the largest balls; all checked centers must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking those that need it and check again. Do not wait for a dark crust if the centers are already done.

Warm the bread: During the roast, use a separate skillet and the pita warming method, omitting its optional oil and salt. Keep the four breads wrapped. Stir and taste the sauce, adding the reserved teaspoon of lemon only if needed.

Fill and serve: Divide sauce among the pitas, then put three cooked meatballs in each. Divide tomato, serving cucumber and sliced onion across the four. Fold loosely or serve open-faced. Serve promptly; the meatballs do not need a ten-minute rest before assembly.

recipes.keywords: Greek-inspired, acidic, rich, weeknight, quick-lunch, roast, no-cook

recipes.name: Greek Village Salad (Horiatiki)
recipes.description: Tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, olives, and feta with oregano and a light oil-and-vinegar dressing.
recipeIngredient: 600 g ripe tomatoes, cut into large bite-sized pieces
300 g English cucumber, cut into thick half-moons
120 g green bell pepper, seeded and sliced
1/3 cup (60 g) drained Kalamata olives, pitted
1 tbsp red wine vinegar, plus 1 tsp more only if needed
1/4 tsp fine salt, only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare vegetables: Wash and dry the produce, cut as listed, and place tomatoes, cucumber, pepper, and onion in a wide serving bowl. If the onion tastes particularly sharp, rinse its slices briefly, then drain and dry them first.
Dress lightly: Add olive oil, the initial tablespoon of vinegar, and oregano. Toss gently. Fold in olives and optional capers.

Add feta and taste: Lay feta slices on top. Taste a complete bite with a little cheese and olive. Add some of the measured salt only if needed, optional pepper, and the extra teaspoon of vinegar only if the vegetables need more brightness.
Serve: Divide among four plates, distributing vegetables, olives, and feta. Serve promptly. Keep any prepared-ahead components refrigerated and combine them shortly before eating.

recipes.keywords: Greek, Mediterranean, acidic, savory, briny, herbaceous, fresh, weeknight, light-and-fresh, no-cook

recipes.name: Greek Yogurt Bowl
recipes.description: Use the full-fat Greek yogurt as the thick base. Add washed fruit, then keep granola, nuts and the chosen seeds near the surface for texture.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Mixed Fresh Berries (blueberries, raspberries, strawberries)
1 tbsp Chia Seeds or Hemp Hearts
1 tbsp Sliced Almonds or Chopped Walnuts

recipeInstructions.text: Base: Spoon all the measured Greek yogurt into bowls for the listed portions.
Fruit: Wash and drain the berries; cut large strawberries into bite-sized pieces. Divide all the berries and optional sliced banana over the yogurt.
Crunch: Divide all the measured granola, chosen almonds or walnuts, and chosen chia seeds or hemp hearts over the fruit. Keep granola toward the surface.
Sweeten: Divide all the measured honey or maple syrup over the bowls.
Serve: Serve promptly for the contrast of creamy yogurt, fruit and crunchy toppings. Granola and chia change texture while standing.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, sweet, acidic, rich, weeknight, light-and-fresh, quick-lunch, no-cook

recipes.name: Green Beans with Shallots and Lemon
recipes.description: Green beans cooked until pleasantly tender, then warmed with softened shallots and finished with measured lemon. Honey is a small optional accent.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus up to 1 tsp more to taste
10 g salt, for the boiling water
1/8 tsp fine salt, for finishing, optional after tasting
2 tbsp water, for warming the beans if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the vegetables and water: Trim the beans, rinse and drain. Dice the shallots, zest the lemon and measure its juice. Bring two liters of water with ten grams salt to a boil in a 4-quart pot. Begin the shallots in step three while the water heats if you can watch both pans.

Cook to tenderness: Add beans and return to a gentle boil. Begin tasting after three minutes; many beans need four to six minutes, and very thick ones can need longer. A cooled piece should bite cleanly with a little resistance. Drain thoroughly. For immediate serving, keep them warm and move straight to the skillet finish; do not chill them first.

Soften shallots: Melt butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat. Add shallots and cook five to seven minutes, stirring, until softened and translucent. Lower heat if they begin browning sharply. Use a small splash from the listed finishing water if needed to help them soften.

Warm and coat: Add the drained beans and optional teaspoon of honey. Toss gently over medium heat for two to three minutes until hot and lightly coated. If the pan is dry, add a little of the remaining finishing water. For refrigerated prepared-ahead beans, allow about four to six minutes, cover briefly with the water as needed, and check they reach 165°F / 74°C before proceeding; then uncover so excess water evaporates.

Finish off heat: Remove from heat. Add lemon zest, the first tablespoon of juice and pepper. Toss, taste a bean and add the optional finishing salt or extra teaspoon of juice only if needed. Divide among four plates and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, fresh, bright, savory, holiday, entertaining, weeknight, light-and-fresh, boil, saute

recipes.name: Thai Green Curry with Chicken
recipes.description: Chicken, eggplant, pepper, and bamboo shoots in a fluid green-curry coconut sauce, finished with Thai basil.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
400 ml full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, divided
3 to 4 tbsp Thai green curry paste, according to its strength
1 tbsp neutral oil, only if needed when frying the paste
1 cup (240 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little hot water only if needed to loosen
250 g Japanese or Chinese eggplant, trimmed, halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2 inch thick
75 g canned bamboo shoots, drained and rinsed
4 makrut lime leaves, torn into large pieces
1 tbsp fish sauce, added gradually only as needed
1 tsp palm sugar or brown sugar, plus a little more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare ingredients: Cut vegetables and pick basil before handling raw chicken, then clean the board and tools. Measure 120 ml of the coconut milk for the paste; use the thick top portion if it has separated, or stir the can and measure if uniform. Reserve the rest.

Cook coconut and paste: In a wide saucepan, simmer the 120 ml coconut milk over medium heat about 3–5 minutes until thickened, stirring. Add green curry paste and cook about 2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant. If it sticks and has not released oil, add the measured tablespoon of neutral oil; a small splash of the reserved coconut milk can also loosen the pan. Do not require darkening or oil pooling before continuing.

Start chicken: Stir in chicken, remaining coconut milk, stock and torn lime leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer, separating the chicken pieces, and cook about 5 minutes. Do not taste the curry while chicken is still undercooked.

Cook vegetables and check: Add eggplant, pepper and bamboo shoots. Simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally so pieces are exposed to the hot liquid, until eggplant is tender and several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend as needed; if chicken finishes well before eggplant, follow troubleshooting.

Season and finish: Add the sugar and start with about 1 tsp fish sauce. Taste and add more fish sauce only as needed; some pastes need very little. If too thick, add a small splash of hot water. Remove the large lime-leaf pieces, turn off heat, and fold in basil. Serve four main portions with separately prepared plain rice.

recipes.keywords: Thai, spicy, savory, herbaceous, rich, weeknight, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Green Smoothie
recipes.description: Frozen mango and fresh avocado blend together into a thick, creamy smoothie that masks spinach's leafy texture. The avocado provides healthy fats and silkiness, while oats add complex carbohydrates for sustained energy.
recipeIngredient: 3/4 cup Almond Milk (or milk of choice)

recipeInstructions.text: The Stack: In a high-speed blender, add ingredients in this exact order: milk, oats, spinach, banana, avocado, and finally the frozen mango. Placing the greens at the bottom ensures they are completely pulverized first.
Process: Blend on low, then quickly increase to high speed. Process for 60 seconds until the mixture is a vibrant, uniform green with no visible leaf flecks.
Adjust: If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more milk. If you need more "High Note" sweetness, add 1 tsp of maple syrup and pulse again.
Serve: Serve immediately in a chilled glass with a wide straw.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, kid-friendly, snack, quick-lunch, blend

recipes.name: Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup
recipes.description: A quick creamy tomato soup with golden grilled-cheese sandwiches filled with avocado.
recipeIngredient: 1 (28 oz) can whole peeled San Marzano-style tomatoes, with their juices
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for the soup
4 slices sourdough or brioche, of similar size and moderate thickness
4 thin slices sharp Cheddar or Gruyère, sized to fit the bread
2 tbsp mayonnaise, for the outside of the bread
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Soften aromatics: Melt the measured butter in a saucepan over medium-low. Cook onion about 6–8 minutes until soft, then add garlic for 30–45 seconds until fragrant.

Simmer soup: Add all listed tomatoes and juices, broth and dried basil. Break up tomatoes with a spoon, bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 15 minutes, stirring, until soft. Prepare sandwich ingredients while it simmers.

Blend and add cream: Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup. Stir in cream and season with salt and pepper. Warm gently and keep hot at 140°F / 60°C or above for the brief sandwich cooking period, without a hard boil.

Assemble sandwiches: Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on one face of each bread slice, using only what is needed from the measured allowance. Place half the bread slices, mayonnaise-side down, in a cool skillet. Divide all the cheese and avocado evenly over these bases. Top with the remaining bread, mayonnaise-side up.

Toast gently: Set over medium-low to medium heat. Cook about 4–6 minutes per side, turning carefully, until golden and cheese has melted in the center. Lower heat if bread colors too quickly; cover briefly if the center needs help warming, then uncover. Use additional rounds if the skillet is crowded.
Serve together: Cut sandwiches as desired and divide the soup among the intended portions. Serve immediately for dipping; do not leave the sandwiches sitting in the soup.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, smoky, comfort-food, saute, simmer, blend, pan-fry

recipes.name: Chicken with Herbed Corn Salsa
recipes.description: This Mexican-inspired grilled chicken showcases summer corn charred directly on the grill until the kernels develop smoky, caramelized spots. The herb salsa combines fresh basil and mint with lemon and Parmesan, creating a bright, aromatic topping.

recipeInstructions.text: Grill chicken: Preheat the grill to medium-high. Season all the thighs with the listed salt and pepper allowance. Grill skin-side down first, turning as the surface browns; start checking at 15–20 minutes total and continue until the thickest part of each thigh reaches 165°F / 74°C, away from the bone. Move away from flare-ups or excessive direct heat. Transfer cooked chicken with clean utensils to a clean platter.
Grill corn: Grill all the shucked corn, rotating occasionally, for about 10 minutes, until the kernels are tender and charred in spots. Keep ready-to-eat corn away from raw chicken and its utensils.

Make herb sauce: While grilling, pulse all the basil, mint, Parmesan and garlic in a clean food processor until finely chopped. Add all the lemon juice and olive oil and pulse just to combine. Season with the listed salt allowance to taste.
Combine: When the corn is safe to handle, cut all its kernels off the cobs into a bowl and mix them with all the herb sauce.
Serve: Divide the chicken and complete corn-herb topping among the listed portions and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, sweet, acidic, umami, rich, herbaceous, entertaining, grill, blend

recipes.name: Grilled Corn Salad with Feta
recipes.description: Grill until the kernels are tender and charred in spots, then cool enough to handle before cutting them off. Choose either the large-ear or medium-ear count.
recipeIngredient: fresh mint, cilantro or parsley, as desired, washed, dried and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Choose and grill corn: Choose ONE of large ears of corn (if using) and medium ears of corn (if using): the large-ear count OR the medium-ear count, not both. Husk and remove silk. Heat the grill to medium-high following its instructions. Grill the chosen ears in one layer, turning often, starting checks around 10–12 minutes until tender with charred spots. Use batches if needed. Transfer to a clean board and cool until safe to handle.

Cut and toss: With the cooled ears held securely on a board or in a wide bowl, cut off all the kernels. Toss all the kernels with red onion, extra-virgin olive oil, and feta in a bowl large enough to lift and turn the full mixture.

Season and serve: Toss fresh mint, cilantro or parsley, kosher salt, and black pepper through all the corn mixture. Serve warm or cold; keep refrigerated if waiting for a cold service. For the source make-ahead route, grill corn one day before assembly, cool promptly in shallow portions and refrigerate covered; cut kernels and assemble on serving day.

recipes.keywords: American, grill, toss

recipes.name: Pork and Peaches
recipes.description: Butterflied pork shoulder is pounded to an even thickness so its centers cook more evenly. Cook it and the skin-on peach halves on a solid cast-iron pan or griddle over the grill, where the full butter and pan oil can stay with the food.
recipeIngredient: 2 lb Boneless pork butt or shoulder, butterflied and trimmed
Black pepper, to taste for pork
6 Fresh peaches, washed, skin on, halved and pitted

recipeInstructions.text: Pound and season: Prepare Boneless pork butt or shoulder, Salt, and Black pepper on a raw-meat board. Pound the butterflied pork with a meat mallet to an even approximately ¾ inch thickness and season with the salt and pepper allowances. Keep it refrigerated if waiting while preparing the grill.

Coat both sides: Mix Garlic cloves, Fresh rosemary, and 3/4 of the Extra-virgin olive oil into a paste in a small bowl and spread over both sides of the prepared pork, dividing evenly. This is three-quarters of the total olive oil; the remaining quarter is reserved for the cooking surface.

Heat solid cooking surface: Heat a large cast-iron pan or griddle over the grill. Once hot, reduce a gas grill to medium or move away from an intense fire as needed. Brush the solid surface with 1/4 of the Extra-virgin olive oil, shared across the chosen pan area. For two pans, divide this allocation across both. Use shimmering oil as the cue and manage heat rather than insisting on prolonged smoking.

Brown the pork: Place the coated pork on the hot solid surface. Leave it long enough to form a golden crust, beginning checks before the original approximately 8–10 minute first-side interval if the heat is strong. Lower or move away from intense heat if garlic is blackening before the pork center cooks. Turn with raw-pork tongs, then keep those tools separate from serving tools.

Cook buttered peaches: While the pork cooks, arrange Fresh peaches and Unsalted butter in a separate solid pan brushed with part of the reserved pan oil. The separate pan keeps ready fruit apart from raw pork juices. Put peaches cut-side down and dot with all the diced butter. Begin checking after about 5 minutes for softened fruit and browned faces; remove ready peaches with clean utensils to a clean platter. If the pan cannot hold a single layer, cook fruit in additional loads, sharing the full butter across them. Keep the fruit pan and its utensils separate from the raw-pork paste and cooking tools.

Finish and rest: Continue cooking pork on its second side, beginning checks during the original 5–7 minute interval and allowing longer if needed. Check several thick centers for at least 145°F /63°C before removal. Transfer with clean utensils to a clean board and rest 5 minutes, meeting the minimum 3-minute rest. Do not infer doneness from color or assume it finishes with the peaches.

Slice and serve: Slice the rested pork across the grain and serve with the buttered peaches. If serving pooled aqueous juices from the pork-cooking pan, bring those juices to a rapid boil before serving and use clean utensils. This means the watery juices, not the oil; do not add liquid to create a boil. Juices from the clean resting board may be served with the rested pork. Never add liquid from the raw-pork board or paste bowl.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, entertaining, date-night, grill

recipes.name: Banh Mi
recipes.description: Bánh mì sandwiches bring grilled pork, crisp bread, cool pickled vegetables, cilantro and creamy mayonnaise together. This lemongrass version uses the listed sugar and honey with fish sauce and garlic; a medium grill helps keep the sweet coating from blackening.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb pork tenderloin or pork butt, raw, fresh or fully thawed; thinly sliced
2 lemongrass stalks, tough outer layers removed; white parts finely minced
suitable grilling oil, as needed for the grates or grill basket
2 crusty baguettes, soft crumb and crisp crust; cut into serving lengths
[Pickled Carrots and Daikon](/mise/recipes/quick-pickled-carrots-and-daikon), as wanted for the sandwiches; prepared ahead, chilled and drained
fresh cilantro, as wanted for the sandwiches, washed
jalapeños, as wanted for heat, washed and sliced
cucumber spears, as wanted for the sandwiches, washed and cut
mayonnaise, a generous layer as wanted
liquid seasoning or soy sauce, a few drops as wanted per sandwich

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate the pork cold: Have pork tenderloin or pork butt, fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic cloves, and lemongrass stalks ready. Whisk the full fish sauce, sugar, honey, garlic and lemongrass supply together, then toss with all the thinly sliced pork. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 2 hours, or overnight. Keep the entire batch coated and use enough covered food-safe vessels for larger batches.

Prepare the pickles: If not prepared ahead, make the linked Pickled Carrots and Daikon while the pork marinates: allow about 20 minutes cutting and packing, then at least 1 hour in the refrigerator. Keep them refrigerated until assembly; choose the serving amount separately rather than assuming the full pickle recipe is used.

Grill the thin pork: Thread the pork onto suitable skewers or use a grill basket, following the equipment’s preparation instructions. Use suitable grilling oil as needed for the cooking surface. Lift the pork from the marinade and wipe away excess; discard the raw-contact marinade. Grill uncrowded slices over medium heat, starting checks around 3–4 minutes per side, until browned without blackening and at least 145°F in the thickest part, measured from the side with a thermometer suitable for thin food. Pork butt and tenderloin can differ in chewing texture; neither is guaranteed finished by the clock. Keep waiting raw pork refrigerated and add grill loads as needed.
Rest cooked pork: Transfer fully cooked pork to a clean platter and rest at least 3 minutes before assembly. Use clean utensils and remove any skewers before eating.

Assemble and serve: Use crusty baguettes, Pickled Carrots and Daikon, fresh cilantro, jalapeños, cucumber spears, mayonnaise, and liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Split the measured bread, spread generously with mayonnaise and add a few drops of liquid seasoning or soy sauce. Divide all the cooked pork among the serving lengths; layer cucumber, drained chilled pickles and cilantro, then jalapeños if wanted. Serve promptly. Four portions is the current original-batch plan, not a measured baguette-size yield.

recipes.keywords: Vietnamese, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, light-and-fresh, grill, no-cook

recipes.name: Grilled Zucchini with Mint and Lemon
recipes.description: Even zucchini planks cooked until tender with browned patches, then finished with measured lemon, mint and olive oil.
recipeIngredient: 680 g small-to-medium zucchini, trimmed and sliced lengthwise into 3/8-inch planks
2 tbsp olive oil, divided between cooking and finishing
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus 1 tsp more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and slice: Preheat a clean grill or grill pan over medium-high heat. Trim zucchini and slice into even 3/8-inch lengthwise planks. Pat the surfaces dry. For a stovetop pan, plan several uncrowded rounds.

Oil and season: Reserve 1/2 tbsp of the oil for finishing. Brush the remaining 1 1/2 tbsp over both sides of all the planks and distribute the measured salt and pepper. Oil coats the vegetables; do not add another unmeasured pour to the pan.

Cook in batches: Lay planks across the grill bars with space, using tongs. Cook about 3–4 minutes per side, turning once they release and have browned patches. Reduce heat if they blacken quickly. Check a thick center with a fork: it should be tender with light resistance, and the plank should lift intact. Transfer to a broad platter and repeat with remaining planks; do not pile and tightly cover the finished ones.

Dress and taste: Drizzle the cooked zucchini with the reserved 1/2 tbsp oil and initial tablespoon of lemon juice. Add mint and zest, then turn gently. Taste before adding any of the optional extra teaspoon of lemon.
Serve: Divide into four sides and serve warm, or after a brief hold while the main finishes. The planks will soften somewhat as they stand; this is not a promise that holding always improves them.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, smoky, herbaceous, acidic, fresh, weeknight, bbq, light-and-fresh, grill

recipes.name: Guacamole
recipes.description: Chunky avocado with tomato, red onion, garlic, cumin and a warm cayenne kick. Add lime and salt in stages, then taste with the food it will accompany.
recipeIngredient: 2 Roma tomatoes, cored, seeded and finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Rinse produce before cutting. Dice the onion and tomatoes, removing tomato cores and loose seed pulp; drain excess tomato juice. Mince jalapeño and garlic, chop cilantro, and juice the lime.

Mash: Halve and pit the avocados and scoop the flesh into a bowl. Toss with half the lime juice. Add half the measured salt, the cumin and cayenne, then mash with a fork or potato masher until creamy with small soft chunks.
Fold: Gently fold in the onion, tomatoes, jalapeño, garlic and cilantro until distributed. Keep the vegetables in distinct pieces rather than puréeing them into the mash.

Rest and season: Smooth the surface, press food wrap against it and refrigerate for about one hour. Stir gently and taste with a tortilla or other accompaniment. Add remaining lime and salt gradually only as needed. For immediate service, skip the rest and make the same seasoning check.
Serve: Share as four generous dip portions or use smaller spoonfuls as a taco or fajita topping. Finished volume varies with avocado size. Keep covered and refrigerated until needed.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, rich, tangy, spicy, fresh, entertaining, family-meal, game-day, no-cook

recipes.name: Gwock Family Macaroni and Cheese
recipes.description: The Gwock family recipe uses eggs and chunks of medium cheese rather than a flour-thickened sauce. Add milk until the macaroni is almost covered, as the original specifies; the exact milk volume and cheese type were not recorded.

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Boil macaroni in salted water for 10 minutes. Drain.
Prepare: Cut cheese and add to macaroni.
Continue: Add thin slices of margarine.
Continue: Add eggs.
Continue: Add milk untill almost completely covered.

Cook: Bake in 9x9 dish at 475 degrees for 20-25 minutes. Beat the eggs before folding them into the macaroni. Bake until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C; check before the end of the stated window and continue if needed. Stand five minutes before serving.

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Ham & Cheese Green Bean Casserole
recipes.description: Adapted from the Gwock Family recipe. Parboil the beans until they begin yielding, then drain before mixing so the condensed soup stays concentrated.
recipeIngredient: unsalted butter, as needed for greasing the dish
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or water
1 lb fresh green beans, washed, trimmed and cut into 2-inch lengths
2 cans (10 3/4 oz) condensed cream of mushroom soup
1/2 lb cooked ham, diced; ready-to-eat product
2 1/2 cups sharp cheddar cheese, freshly grated

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare dish: Heat oven to 350°F. For the original batch, use unsalted butter to butter a 9×13-inch oven-safe baking dish. Use enough dishes for similar filling depth with room below the rim when scaling.

Parboil beans: Set out low-sodium chicken broth or water and fresh green beans. Bring the blanching liquid to a boil in a saucepan, then add the beans. Begin checking around 5–6 minutes after adding beans: they should yield with slight resistance rather than remain hard or fall apart. Drain immediately without rinsing. Keep blanching liquid separate from casserole filling; discard it, or cool promptly and refrigerate separately if saving for another use.

Combine filling: Set out condensed cream of mushroom soup, half-and-half, garlic powder, kosher salt, black pepper, cooked ham, yellow onion, 4/5 of the sharp cheddar cheese, and 1/2 of the canned French fried onions. Whisk all the soup, half-and-half, garlic powder, salt and pepper together. Fold in all the drained beans, cooked ham, diced onion and the allocated cheese/fried onions. Four-fifths of the full cheddar and half the fried onions go inside; reserve the rest for the finishing stage. Do not dilute the condensed soup with the blanching broth.

Heat the full casserole: Transfer all filling to the buttered dishes. Bake at 350°F, starting checks around 30 minutes for the original pan, until bubbling toward the center. This begins the final check rather than certifying the center by color alone.

Add reserved topping: Scatter 1/5 of the sharp cheddar cheese and 1/2 of the canned French fried onions over the full filling, dividing the topping among dishes. Continue baking, starting checks around 10 minutes later, until the center reaches 165°F /74°C and the onions are golden. Check every dish; tent lightly if toppings brown before its center is ready.
Rest and serve: Rest 5 minutes before dividing the full casserole into the listed portions. The short rest thickens the hot sauce; keep leftovers chilled promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, rich, holiday, bake, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Ham & Cheese Quiche
recipes.description: Sauté the onion in butter before adding the cooked ham, then whisk parsley, pepper and nutmeg into the custard so they season every slice. This version uses a deep-dish shell and a relatively egg-heavy filling.
recipeIngredient: Butter or oil, as needed to grease a separate dish for excess filling

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the shell: Preheat the oven to 400 °F. Place the 9-inch deep-dish shell on a baking sheet. Follow its own instructions for partial baking, including any weights or docking they require. For a shell whose instructions permit this brief parbake, prick the bottom and bake 5–7 minutes to begin cooking it, then set aside. This short parbake is not a guarantee against sogginess; other shell instructions can take longer.

The Sauté: Melt the butter in a small skillet over medium heat. Sauté the minced onion for about 2–3 minutes, until softened and translucent, then add the cooked ham and optional cooked bacon. Cook about 2 minutes more, until warmed through and lightly browned in places. Set aside to cool slightly.
The Custard: Whisk the eggs and half-and-half with all the dried parsley, black pepper and pinch of nutmeg until smoothly blended. Do not whip to a thick foam.

Assemble: Scatter the ham-onion mixture, chopped spinach, cheddar and mozzarella into the partly baked shell. Slowly pour the custard over the fillings. Leave room below the rim; deep-dish shells vary. If it will not fit, bake the excess in a separate suitable greased oven-safe dish rather than overflowing the crust.

Bake: Reduce the oven to 375 °F. Bake for about 25–35 minutes as a first range, until the center is set with no liquid egg and measures 165 °F / 74 °C, checking without touching the crust or pan. The top may be golden; shield the crust edge with foil if it colors before the center is ready, and continue baking as needed.

Rest: Rest 10 minutes before slicing. The full original batch makes eight portions; apportion a different batch size accordingly. Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and use within 3 days. Reheat centers to 165 °F / 74 °C; cover the crust to limit further browning.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, acidic, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, bake, saute, no-cook

recipes.name: Hamantaschen
recipes.description: These triangular Jewish cookies for Purim require careful technique to prevent blowouts during baking. When folding the three sides, tuck one corner under the next flap to create a self-locking triangle.
recipeIngredient: Apricot Jam, Poppy Seed Paste, or chocolate-hazelnut spread

recipeInstructions.text: The Emulsion: In a stand mixer, cream butter and sugar until light and fluffy (3 mins). Add the egg, vanilla, and orange zest; beat until perfectly combined.
The Mix: Sift in the flour and salt. Mix on low speed until a crumbly dough forms. Stop immediately.
The Knead: Use your hands to gently knead the crumbles into a smooth, tacky ball. If too dry, add cold water 1 tsp at a time.
The Chill: Wrap in plastic and refrigerate for at least 3 hours (overnight is best).
Roll: On a floured surface, roll dough to a uniform 1/8-inch thickness.
Cut: Use a 3-inch round cutter to cut circles. Re-roll scraps once.

Fill & Fold: Place 1 tsp filling in the center. Fold the three sides up to form a triangle. The Pinwheel: Tuck the left corner of each flap under the adjacent side to lock it. Pinch the corners firmly.
Bake: Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake for 20-25 minutes until the edges are just barely golden.
Store: Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container to maintain the "Snap."

recipes.keywords: Jewish, sweet, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Har Gow (Shrimp Dumplings)
recipes.description: Har gow are Cantonese shrimp dumplings with translucent, pleated wrappers - a dim sum classic and a test of a chef's skill. The dough uses wheat starch (not wheat flour) mixed with boiling water, which gelatinizes the starch instantly and creates a flexible dough that steams into a glass-like wrapper.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb Raw Shrimp, peeled, deveined, and patted dry

recipeInstructions.text: The Filling: Finely chop the shrimp. In a large bowl, combine shrimp and all shrimp paste ingredients. Whip vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until the mixture is very sticky. Fold in bamboo shoots. Chill for 30 minutes.
The Dough: In a heatproof bowl, whisk wheat starch and cornstarch. Pour in the boiling water while stirring rapidly with chopsticks. Add lard/oil.
Knead: Once cool enough to touch, knead for 2 minutes until smooth. Roll into a cylinder and divide into 18 pieces. Keep covered with a damp towel.
Shape: Use a flat blade (lightly oiled) to flatten each dough ball into a thin 3-inch circle.
Assemble: Place 1 tbsp filling in the center. Fold and pleat carefully (aim for 7-10 pleats) to create the signature "bonnet" shape.
Steam: Place in a bamboo steamer on parchment. Steam over boiling water for exactly 6 minutes on high heat.
Serve: Serve immediately with chili oil and soy sauce for the mandatory High Note.

recipes.name: Harvest Sheet Pan Gnocchi with Kale
recipes.description: Sheet-pan gnocchi is a weeknight trick that turns frozen cauliflower gnocchi into something crispy and caramelized without a pot of boiling water. The key is a single layer - crowding the pan steams everything into mush instead of roasting it.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz Apple Chicken Sausage, sliced into rounds
2 cups Butternut Squash, diced into 1/2-inch cubes
1/3 cup Freshly Grated Parmesan or Nutritional Yeast

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 400°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Toss: In a massive bowl, combine gnocchi, sliced sausage, squash, and kale. Drizzle with 3 tbsp olive oil. Add rosemary, thyme, garlic powder, paprika, salt, and pepper. Toss until every leaf and cube is coated.
Spread: Spread the mixture in a single layer on the pan. (Crucial for the kale to crisp!)
Roast: Bake for 24-26 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the squash is tender and the gnocchi are golden.
The Crunch: The kale should be dark green and shatteringly crisp.
Finish: Sprinkle with Parmesan or nutritional yeast while still piping hot. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Apple Muffins
recipes.description: Combining applesauce and Greek yogurt creates incredibly moist muffins without excessive oil - a healthier approach that maintains dense, cake-like texture. Including both grated apple (for moisture) and cubed apple (for textural crunch) ensures every bite has distinct character.

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Preheat oven to 425°F. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt.
The Apples: Add the grated and cubed apples to the dry mix. Toss to coat - this prevents the fruit from sinking to the bottom.
Wet Mix: In a separate bowl, whisk oil, maple syrup, eggs, yogurt, applesauce, and vanilla until smooth and aerated.
Combine: Pour the wet into the dry. Stir with a spatula until just combined. A few streaks of flour are the mandatory guard against a tough muffin.
Bake: Divide into a lined 12-cup tin. Sprinkle the turbinado sugar over the tops. Bake at 425°F for 13-16 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes before removing.

recipes.name: Banana Bread
recipes.description: Whole-wheat flour, measured mashed banana and olive oil make a moist loaf sweetened with honey or maple syrup. Whisk the wet ingredients first, then fold the flour briefly and cool the loaf completely before slicing.
recipeIngredient: butter or neutral oil, for greasing the pan
1/2 cup dark chocolate chips or walnuts, chop walnuts if using, optional
ground cinnamon, a pinch for the top, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat and grease the pan: Preheat the oven to 325°F. Grease a 9-by-5-inch loaf pan for the original batch with butter or neutral oil. Measure the mashed banana before mixing.

Whisk the wet ingredients: In a large bowl whisk the extra-virgin olive oil, honey or maple syrup, large eggs, ripe banana, and milk of choice, combining the oil and honey or syrup first, beating in the eggs, then whisking in the banana and milk. Whisk until evenly combined; small banana lumps may remain.
Distribute the soda and seasonings: Whisk in the baking soda, vanilla extract, sea salt, and ground cinnamon until evenly distributed; break up any baking-soda lumps.
Fold in the flour: Switch to a large spoon or spatula and fold in the white whole-wheat flour until no dry pockets remain. Stop once combined; small banana lumps are fine.
Add the optional mix-ins: Gently fold in the dark chocolate chips or walnuts (if using).
Fill and finish the loaf: Scrape the batter into the prepared pan and level it gently. Sprinkle with ground cinnamon (if using); run a knife tip in a shallow zigzag to swirl the topping.

Bake and cool: Bake for about 55–60 minutes, checking the center at 55 minutes. A tester through the crumb should have no wet batter; try another spot if it hits melted chocolate. Continue baking if necessary and tent loosely with foil if the top darkens first. Cool in the pan on a rack for at least 10 minutes, loosen the edges and turn out carefully. Cool completely on the rack before slicing; allow about an hour, longer if still warm.

recipes.name: Carrot Cake Muffins
recipes.description: Using the finest holes on your grater for the carrots allows them to melt into the batter, providing moisture without large, distracting chunks. Applesauce reduces oil content while maintaining dense texture.

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup tin. In a medium bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.
Wet Mix: In a large bowl, whisk the shredded carrots, maple syrup, applesauce, egg, oil, and vanilla until smooth and emulsified.
Combine: Slowly stir the flour mixture and milk into the wet ingredients until just combined.
Bake: Divide batter into liners. Bake for 18-20 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool: Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before glazing.
The Glaze: Whisk softened cream cheese, powdered sugar, vanilla, and milk until smooth.
Finish: Dip each cooled muffin top into the glaze. Sprinkle with extra shredded coconut or walnuts for a textural "High Note."

recipes.name: Heirloom Tomato & Pesto Galette
recipes.description: Pesto and ricotta sit beneath the tomatoes, while the cheese and full measured olive oil finish the folded pastry. Pat the tomatoes dry before layering, but expect some juice as they bake.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup sharp cheddar or Gruyère, shredded; choose one
1/3 cup basil pesto, prepared homemade or store-bought
3 medium heirloom tomatoes, washed before slicing thinly
fresh chives and basil, chopped, for garnish
flaky sea salt and chile flakes, for finishing
extra-virgin olive oil, additional optional finishing drizzle, optional
whole-milk ricotta, additional optional finishing dollops, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Make and chill dough: Pulse all-purpose flour, cold butter, ice-cold water, granulated sugar, and sea salt as follows: combine flour, sugar and salt, then add all cold butter and pulse until crumbly with visible pieces. Add the listed ice water and pulse briefly until the dough holds when pressed. Form a disk, wrap tightly and chill for 30 minutes. Do not work the pastry until the butter disappears into a warm paste.

Heat oven and dry tomatoes: Heat the oven to 425°F. Slice medium heirloom tomatoes thinly, lay them on clean absorbent towels and pat the tops dry. Remove surface moisture without pressing the slices into pulp; the tomatoes will still release some juice during baking. Use a rimmed baking sheet and parchment rated for the oven temperature.

Roll and fill: Use all-purpose flour, whole-milk ricotta, and basil pesto for assembly. Before rolling or filling, decide the pan load and divide the full measured dough, pesto, ricotta and dried tomatoes proportionally among the galettes being made. For the original batch, roll one 12-inch circle with a 2-inch border; a circle up to 14 inches may have a border up to 3 inches. Leave enough pastry to fold and check that its allocated filling can fit before spreading pesto or ricotta. Transfer each circle to the lined sheet, spread its allocated pesto within the border, distribute its allocated ricotta and lay its allocated tomatoes on top. Keep every measured portion in the planned galettes; do not wait until all the dough is filled to decide on additional galettes.

Fold and finish crust: Fold the dough border over the tomato edges, pleating without stretching. Use sharp cheddar or Gruyère and extra-virgin olive oil to finish the border: brush all the measured oil onto the folded pastry, then sprinkle all the shredded chosen cheese over it. The optional serving drizzle is a separate allowance.

Bake: Bake at 425°F, beginning checks around 25–30 minutes for the original galette, until the pastry edges are golden and baked through and the tomatoes are hot and juicy. Lift an edge carefully to inspect the base; continue if pastry underneath is still pale and doughy, shielding an already-browned edge if needed. Keep additional galettes uncrowded and allow extra oven rounds as needed.

Serve: Serve warm with fresh chives and basil, flaky sea salt and chile flakes, extra-virgin olive oil (if using), and whole-milk ricotta (if using). Distribute the herbs and finishing seasoning; add the separate extra oil drizzle or ricotta dollops only if wanted. Keep the full measured oil and ricotta already used in the galette distinct from these optional extras.

recipes.name: Herb Pork Tenderloin
recipes.description: Lemon juice, zest, rosemary and thyme flavor the refrigerated marinade. Its olive oil is separate from the oil used for searing.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup Extra-virgin olive oil for marinade
3 Pork tenderloins, about 1 lb each in the original batch; keep individual diameter similar when scaling
3 tbsp Extra-virgin olive oil for searing
Kosher salt for meat seasoning, as needed before searing
Black pepper, to taste before searing

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the coating or marinade: Mix Fresh lemon juice, Lemon zest, Extra-virgin olive oil for marinade, Garlic, Fresh rosemary, Fresh thyme, Dijon mustard, and Kosher salt for marinade in a clean bowl or raw-meat container before adding the pork.

Coat and refrigerate: Add Pork tenderloins to the prepared lemon–herb marinade in a sealable raw-meat container or sturdy bag and turn to coat. Seal and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight. Keep the container separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.

Discard marinade and sear: Heat the oven to 400°F. Lift the tenderloins out, discard the raw-contact liquid and leave the herbs that cling to the meat. Have Extra-virgin olive oil for searing, Kosher salt for meat seasoning, and Black pepper ready. Season the pork with the separate salt and pepper allowances. Heat the measured pan oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering and sear the tenderloins on all sides until golden. Use manageable loads and divide that pan oil over the loads as needed; it is the whole batch amount, not 3 tbsp per skillet.

Roast and check every piece: Transfer the oven-safe skillet to the oven; if the batch needs more room, use an oven-safe roasting pan with space between the pieces. Begin checking after about 10 minutes and continue until the thickest center of every tenderloin reaches at least 145°F /63°C before removal. Do not assume that rest will supply a missing cooking temperature.

Rest on a clean platter: Transfer ready tenderloins to a clean platter, cover with foil. Rest for 10 minutes before carving each tenderloin. This exceeds the minimum 3-minute rest after the measured 145°F endpoint. Keep hot handles protected and avoid the raw marinade vessel.
Slice and serve: Carve across the grain into roughly ½-inch diagonal slices. Serve warm with the juices collected on the clean resting platter.

recipes.name: Herby Chicken Meatball Bowl
recipes.description: Whole-milk ricotta makes the chicken mixture soft, so mix gently and portion all of it into small logs or balls. Roast chickpeas and sweet potato on separate pans because they have different texture endpoints.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, fully cooked, drained and well dried
1 large sweet potato, washed and cut into bite-sized cubes
2 green onions, washed and finely chopped
1/2 cup fresh cilantro, washed and finely chopped
1/4 cup fresh dill, washed and finely chopped
1 lemon, washed; zest only for the meat mixture
black pepper, to taste in dressing
4 cups fresh kale, washed, tough stems removed and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Roast chickpeas: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Toss chickpeas, olive oil, salt, garlic powder, onion powder, Italian seasoning, and Parmesan on one sheet pan and spread in a workable layer. Start checking at 15 minutes for a crisp exterior; continue as needed, watching the cheese and spices for scorching. More cans need additional pan space, not more complete oil doses per pan.

Roast sweet potato: On another pan, toss large sweet potato, olive oil, salt, ground cinnamon, and ground cumin. Roast about 15–25 minutes, until tender inside and browned at the edges. Remove each roasting component when ready; chickpeas and potato do not share one universal clock.

Blend dressing: Blend Greek yogurt, fresh basil, fresh dill, jalapeño, honey, fresh lemon juice, olive oil, garlic cloves, salt, and black pepper smooth in a food processor or blender suited to cold mixtures. Make and taste this ready-to-eat dressing before handling raw chicken, or use separately cleaned tools. Keep it refrigerated while cooking.

Mix and shape: Gently combine ground chicken, whole-milk ricotta, large egg, panko breadcrumbs, shallot, green onions, fresh cilantro, fresh dill, lemon, salt, and black pepper, using all the zest from the listed lemon and keeping its flesh/juice out of the meat mixture. Kale stays for the serving bowls. Portion all mixture into small cylindrical logs using about 2 tbsp per log; total count varies with scoop size. You can also shape rounded meatballs; keep pieces similar in size and check their centers.

Cook chicken logs: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook logs in batches without crowding, starting with 3–4 minutes per side. Divide this oil allowance across all loads. Continue as needed until golden brown and the centers reach 165°F /74°C on a food thermometer; surface browning alone is not the endpoint. Transfer cooked pieces using clean tools.

Assemble: Divide fresh kale among the listed planning number of bowls, four at the original batch. Add all roasted chickpeas, sweet potato and cooked chicken, then distribute the dressing. The original four tablespoons pan oil belong 1 to chickpeas, 1 to potato and 2 to chicken; the separate dressing tablespoon brings total oil to 5 tbsp at original batch.

recipes.name: Homemade Chicken Stock
recipes.description: A great chicken stock is all about temperature control. Never let the stock boil violently after the initial heating step; high heat emulsifies the chicken fat into the water, resulting in a greasy, cloudy broth.
recipeIngredient: 4 lbs Chicken bones (backs, necks, wings, or carcasses)
1 large Yellow Onion, unpeeled, cut into quarters

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Place the chicken bones, onion quarters, carrots, celery, and halved garlic bulb in a large 8-to-12-quart stockpot.
Boil: Pour in the cold water. Bring the mixture to a boil over high heat, then immediately reduce the heat to low to maintain a gentle simmer.
Skim: Skim off any gray foam or impurities that rise to the surface during the first 30 minutes of cooking. This ensures a clean flavor.
Infuse: Add the parsley stems, thyme sprigs, bay leaf, and whole black peppercorns to the pot.
Simmer: Simmer gently, uncovered, for 4 hours. Keep the heat low so the liquid does not boil. If the water level drops too low and exposes the bones, add a cup or two of hot water.
Strain: Pour the stock through a colander lined with cheesecloth or a fine-mesh sieve into a large heatproof bowl. Discard the spent bones and vegetables.
Chill: Place the bowl of stock in an ice bath to cool it rapidly. Once cool, cover and refrigerate overnight.
De-fat: Scrape off the layer of solidified fat from the surface of the chilled stock before using or freezing.

recipes.name: Homemade Chili Oil
recipes.description: Chili oil is the secret weapon of Chinese cooking - a few spoonfuls transform dumplings, noodles, or rice into something extraordinary. The technique is simple: bloom aromatics in oil, then pour the hot oil over pepper flakes to release their color and flavor without burning.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Neutral Oil (vegetable, canola, or peanut)
1/2 cup Red Pepper Flakes (gochugaru or crushed red pepper)
1 tbsp Sichuan Peppercorns (optional, for numbing heat)

recipeInstructions.text: The Prep: Place red pepper flakes, sesame seeds, minced garlic, ginger, salt, and sugar in a large, dry stainless-steel bowl on a stable heatproof surface. Leave ample room for bubbling; do not pour hot oil into a storage jar. Wash and dry the fresh aromatics before mincing, and have a dry metal strainer ready.

The Infuse: In a small saucepan, combine oil, star anise, cinnamon stick, and Sichuan peppercorns if using. Heat gently, checking with a thermometer, until the spices are fragrant and the oil reaches about 275°F, roughly 8–10 minutes. Lower the heat if spices darken early; remove darkening spices rather than continuing to fry them. Turn off the heat.

The Pour: Remove the whole spices with the dry metal strainer. Test a small spoonful of oil on a few flakes in a separate dry heatproof dish: they should sizzle without blackening or smelling burnt. If they scorch, let the oil cool a little and test again. Carefully add the oil to the main mixture in small increments, stirring with a dry metal spoon and allowing bubbling to subside between additions. Keep your face and hands clear of the steam and splashes. Heating does not make this fresh-garlic-and-ginger oil shelf-stable.

The Store: Cool promptly in a heatproof container, then refrigerate at 40°F or below within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. Use within 4 days, or freeze small portions promptly. Stir before serving. Do not store this fresh-garlic-and-ginger oil at room temperature.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, Sichuan, spicy, savory, aromatic, umami, meal-prep, fry, infuse

recipes.name: Enchilada Sauce
recipes.description: This homemade enchilada sauce builds deeper flavor than store-bought versions by toasting chili powder and cumin directly in the hot oil-flour roux before adding liquid. This blooming technique releases the spices' fat-soluble aromatic oils.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp mild American-style chili powder blend (not pure cayenne)
1 tsp Apple Cider Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)

recipeInstructions.text: The Roux: Measure flour, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, salt and optional cinnamon together before starting. In a medium saucepan, heat oil over medium. When a small pinch sizzles in the oil, whisk in that mixture; reserve black pepper for the finish. Cook, whisking constantly, for 1 minute until fragrant and the color deepens.
Emulsify: Whisk in the tomato paste until smooth.
The Liquid: Slowly pour in the broth while whisking vigorously to remove all lumps.
Simmer: Increase heat to medium-high and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 5-7 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the back of a spoon.
Finish: Remove from heat. Whisk in the vinegar and black pepper. Taste and add more salt if needed.

Store: Use immediately, or transfer to shallow heatproof containers and refrigerate promptly, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below for 3–4 days, or freeze in small portions. Reheat leftovers to a rolling boil, stirring and adding a little broth or water if needed to restore a pourable consistency.

recipes.name: Homemade Pizza Night
recipes.description: Overnight no-knead dough, tomato sauce and a mozzarella-Parmesan topping bar, baked as four personal pizzas.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand with their juices
fresh basil, a few torn leaves, to taste, optional
12 oz fresh mozzarella, torn small, drained and blotted dry
flour, for lightly dusting the work surface during portioning
flour, for dusting the work surface and peel, as needed
olive oil, for lightly oiling the pans, if using the pan route, optional
prepared pizza toppings, a sparse single layer, as desired, optional
fresh basil, a few leaves, to taste, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the dough: Combine all-purpose flour, water, fine sea salt, and active-dry yeast until no dry flour remains. The dough will be sticky. Cover the bowl; no kneading is needed.

Ferment overnight: Let the covered dough rise around 72°F / 22°C until it is bubbly and more than doubled, approximately 18 hours. Check earlier in a warm room and allow longer in a cool one. When ready, portion it as below; do not extend the room-temperature rise blindly to two days.

Portion and relax: Lightly dust the work surface with flour. For four 10-inch pizzas, divide the dough into four equal portions, approximately 217 g each. For two 14-inch pizzas, divide into two approximately 434 g portions instead. Fold the edges underneath to make rounded balls without flattening out all the gas. Cover and rest about 1 hour until pliable. Alternatively, cover the risen, portioned dough individually and refrigerate up to 3 days; on baking day allow the covered balls about 2–3 hours at room temperature to relax instead of the one-hour rest. Prepare the oven and toppings during the last hour.

Set up the oven: Heat the oven to 500°F. For the pan route, use two room-temperature metal pans rated for that temperature, with enough flat area for the chosen diameter, and bake one at a time on the middle rack. A 14-inch round requires a suitably large round pan; do not assume it fits a standard baking sheet. For the stone route, put a suitably rated stone in the cold oven and preheat it for 1 hour; the stone and peel must fit the chosen diameter. Neither route uses parchment. Keep used pans aside to cool before reloading.

Cook the sauce batch: Have whole peeled tomatoes, olive oil, garlic cloves, fine salt, red pepper flakes (if using), and fresh basil (if using) ready. Warm the oil over medium-low heat, add the garlic and cook 30–45 seconds until fragrant but not browned. Stir in the tomatoes, salt and optional pepper flakes. Simmer 10–15 minutes, stirring, until spreadable without a puddle of loose liquid; add the optional basil at the end. Let cool enough to handle. Measure 3/4 cup for the full pizza batch and refrigerate the surplus promptly; the whole can is not meant to go onto the pizzas. If using prepared sauce instead, omit this entire sauce component and measure 3/4 cup thick pizza sauce.

Shape one pizza: Use flour and olive oil (if using) as needed. Stretch one ball to its chosen 10-inch or 14-inch diameter, leaving a thicker rim. Cover and wait another 10 minutes if it springs back. Move the untopped round onto a lightly oiled cool pan, or a lightly floured peel and confirm it slides. Keep unused dough covered and prepared perishable toppings chilled.

Allocate cheese and toppings: Divide fresh mozzarella, Parmesan, and prepared pizza toppings (if using) into four sets for small pizzas or two sets for large ones. Each 10-inch pizza gets 3 tbsp prepared sauce, 3 oz mozzarella and 1/4 oz Parmesan; each 14-inch pizza gets 6 tbsp sauce, 6 oz mozzarella and 1/2 oz Parmesan. Spread its sauce leaving a 1/2- to 3/4-inch rim. Add half of that pizza’s mozzarella, a sparse layer of the chosen toppings, then its remaining mozzarella and its full Parmesan portion. On a peel, check again that it slides and bake immediately. Use ready-to-eat pepperoni or fully cooked sausage, bacon or chicken; thinly slice quick-cooking vegetables, cook and cool mushrooms first, and drain wet toppings. Keep perishable toppings chilled until assembly.

Bake one at a time: Put the pan on the middle rack, or launch directly onto the stone. Start checking at 10 minutes; roughly 12–15 minutes is a guide, not a fixed endpoint for every size, cheese and baking surface. The underside should be browned, the center set and the rim golden, with melted cheese. Rotate safely with the pan or peel if browning is uneven, and allow longer if the bottom is pale. Keep the oven on between pizzas and give a stone about 5 minutes to recover.

Finish and serve in rounds: Add fresh basil (if using) after baking. Rest the pizza on a rack for 2–3 minutes, cut and serve. Shape, top and bake each remaining pizza separately, using its assigned sauce and cheese. Alternate pans and let them cool before reloading; never assemble on a hot pan. Four pizzas mean four oven rounds, not one 15-minute bake.

recipes.name: Rice & Orzo Pilaf
recipes.description: Long-grain rice and golden toasted orzo cooked in broth, then rested before fluffing. Optional lemon is added at the end.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (200 g) long-grain white rice, not parboiled or instant
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, optional finish
2 tbsp hot water, only if needed to finish firm grains

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse rice: Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water, then drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer. Measure the other ingredients.
Toast orzo: Melt butter in a 2–3 quart saucepan over medium heat. Add dry orzo and stir frequently for 3–4 minutes until golden brown. Add drained rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add seasonings and broth: Stir in garlic powder, onion powder, optional turmeric, salt, and pepper for about 15 seconds. Pour in broth carefully and bring to a gentle boil.

Simmer: Stir once, cover tightly, and reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook about 15–18 minutes. Check that the liquid is absorbed and taste a grain. If it remains hard and dry, add the measured hot water and cook covered a little longer.

Rest and finish: Once grains are nearly tender, turn off heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff gently and fold in dried parsley and optional lemon juice. Taste before adding any further seasoning.

recipes.name: Ketchup
recipes.description: Simmering tomato passata on lowest heat for 30 minutes slowly evaporates water and concentrates tomatoes' natural fructose, creating thick ketchup without added sugar. Red wine vinegar provides acidity that keeps the savory spices from tasting flat.
recipeIngredient: 14 oz (400g) Tomato Passata or Crushed Tomatoes
3 tbsp Red Wine Vinegar (The Finishing Touch)
Salt and Black Pepper to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: In a small non-reactive saucepan, whisk together the tomatoes, vinegar, smashed garlic, mustard, and all spices.
Reduce: Bring to a tiny simmer over low heat. Cook for 30 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent the bottom from scorching.
Refine: Once thickened and dark red, remove the garlic clove.
Emulsion: For the Kitchen Standard texture, use an immersion blender to puree the mixture until perfectly smooth and glossy.
Set: Let cool completely. Transfer to an airtight glass jar and refrigerate.
Store: Keeps in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.

recipes.name: Honey-Chipotle Chicken and Lime Rice Bowls
recipes.description: Smoky, gently sweet chicken cutlets with measured portions of lime rice, fresh greens, tomatoes and avocado, cooked in two home-skillet batches.
recipeIngredient: 900 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 6 cutlets of about 150 g each and even 1/2-inch thickness
2 tbsp chipotle peppers in adobo, finely chopped with their clinging sauce
2 tsp neutral oil, for the skillet, divided
120 g baby spinach or spring mix, washed and dried
300 g avocado flesh, diced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the marinade: Whisk chipotle, honey, lime juice, olive oil, Dijon, garlic and the measured salt in a bowl large enough for the chicken. Taste now if checking the heat; then put tasting utensils aside. Prepare the six evenly thick cutlets on a separate raw-meat board.

Marinate cold: Coat the cutlets, cover and refrigerate for thirty minutes, or up to two hours. Clean the raw-contact board, knife and work surface before preparing any bowl vegetables. There is no finishing sauce reserved from this raw-contact marinade.

Start rice and toppings: During marination, make two batches of Cilantro-Lime Rice together in a 3-quart saucepan: select 2× on that recipe for all amounts, starting with 360 g rice and 600 ml water. Follow its texture checks and ten-minute covered rest. Wash and dry the greens and dice the tomatoes. Leave avocado cutting until assembly. Preheat the skillet over medium heat near the end of marination.

Cook in two rounds: Add one teaspoon of the neutral oil. Lift three cutlets from their marinade, allowing excess to drip off; lay them in a single uncrowded layer. Cook about four minutes on the first side and three on the second, then turn and check every one to two minutes as needed. Allow roughly 10–12 minutes per round. Adjust heat down if honey or garlic begins to blacken. Insert a thin thermometer sideways into each cutlet's thickest center and cook each to at least 165°F / 74°C before removing. Transfer to a clean plate and tent loosely. Remove scorched loose coating carefully with a paper towel held in tongs, add the remaining teaspoon of oil, and repeat. Discard the used marinade; use clean utensils for cooked meat.

Rest and finish rice: Rest the final chicken batch five minutes; the first batch rests longer while the second cooks. Finish the rice with its oil, herbs and lime after its covered rest. Slice the chicken across the grain, retaining clean resting juices to spoon over its slices.

Build six bowls: Divide the cooked rice among six bowls, roughly 3/4–1 cup each depending on yield. Add the greens, tomatoes and freshly diced avocado equally, then the sliced chicken. Serve one lime wedge per bowl and squeeze only as much as needed after tasting.

recipes.name: Honey Garlic Butter Shrimp & Broccoli
recipes.description: Shrimp and broccoli in a generous honey-garlic butter glaze with ginger and red pepper flakes.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw shrimp (16–20 per pound), peeled and deveined, tails removed
2 cups fresh broccoli florets, cut into bite-size pieces with thin stems
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Water, a small splash only if needed to finish broccoli or loosen sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Pat shrimp dry and cut broccoli into small florets with thin stems. Whisk honey, soy sauce, garlic, ginger, pepper flakes and cornstarch in a bowl until no dry starch remains.

Cook shrimp: Melt half the butter over medium to medium-high without letting it darken. Add shrimp in a single layer; if necessary use batches sharing that butter allocation. Cook about 1–2 minutes on each side, continuing as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

Cook broccoli: Add the olive oil and broccoli. Sauté over medium heat about 5–7 minutes, turning, until a stem yields with slight resistance. If stems remain firm, add a small splash of water, cover briefly and check again; uncover to evaporate free water. Season lightly with pepper and only a little salt if needed, remembering the soy sauce. Transfer to a plate.

Thicken glaze: Lower heat to medium-low. Add remaining butter, stir the sauce bowl again and pour it in. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring, about 1–2 minutes until glossy and lightly thickened. Do not boil hard or reduce to a sticky candy. Loosen with a little water if necessary.

Combine: Return cooked shrimp, broccoli and plate juices. Turn gently for about 30 seconds just to warm and coat. Taste before adding more salt or pepper. Serve promptly over separately prepared rice.
