recipes.name: Honey-Glazed Carrots
recipes.description: Roast the carrots with oil first, then coat them with all the honey-butter-thyme glaze. The glaze can darken quickly at 425°F: check it before the end of the timer, and take the pan out once the carrots are tender and the coating bubbles without burning.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs carrots, peeled and cut into uniform 3-inch batons, or whole baby carrots
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, or 1/2 tsp dried thyme
Flaky sea salt, as desired for finishing
Extra fresh thyme leaves, optional for finishing

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven to 425°F. Wash and peel the carrots and cut uniform 3-inch batons, splitting especially thick pieces lengthwise for similar thickness, or use the listed whole baby-carrot option. Line enough rimmed sheets with parchment rated for 425°F or use bare oven-safe sheets.

Toss all the carrots with all the olive oil, kosher salt and black pepper. Divide among pans in a single layer, leaving room to turn. Roast about 20 minutes, then check a thick center for near-tenderness and turn as needed; thicker pieces may need longer before glazing.
Meanwhile stir all the melted butter, honey and measured fresh or dried thyme together. If using dried thyme, use half the listed fresh-thyme amount.

Remove the sheets and divide all the glaze among the carrots, tossing gently. Return to the oven, checking before 8–10 minutes and sooner if the honey darkens quickly. Finish when centers are tender and the glaze bubbles with golden edges; reduce heat or remove a finished pan rather than waiting for blackened honey.
Serve warm with the separate flaky-salt allowance and optional extra fresh thyme. The measured thyme has already gone into the glaze.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, comfort-food, entertaining, holiday, roast

recipes.name: Honey-Glazed Spareribs
recipes.description: Honey-glazed spareribs are a Chinese-American restaurant staple. This version uses a pressure cooker to achieve fall-off-the-bone tenderness in 20 minutes instead of hours of smoking or braising.
recipeIngredient: 2 racks Pork Spareribs (4 lbs total), cut into 3-rib sections

recipeInstructions.text: Puree: In a blender, combine hoisin, soy, molasses, ginger, garlic, and 1/2 cup of the honey. Blend until smooth.
Pressurize: Place the ribs in a pressure cooker. Pour the puree over the ribs. Add 1/4 cup water.
Cook: Seal and cook on HIGH PRESSURE for 20 minutes.

The Reduction: Allow pressure to release fully naturally, following the cooker instructions. Open only after its indicator confirms no remaining pressure and its instructions permit opening. Transfer the ribs to a foil-lined baking sheet, meaty side up. Pour the liquid from the cooker into a saucepan and boil over high heat for 10 minutes until reduced by half.
The Lacquer: Brush the ribs generously with the reduced sauce and the remaining 1/4 cup honey.
Char: Broil 6 inches from the heat for 3-5 minutes until the glaze is bubbling and charred at the edges.
Serve: Sliced into individual ribs with extra sauce on the side.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, sweet, savory, umami, smoky, entertaining, comfort-food, boil, blend

recipes.name: Honey-Lime Chicken Thighs for Tacos
recipes.description: Roasted thighs finished with a thin honey-soy glaze and fresh lime, with measured taco toppings for eight.
recipeIngredient: 1360 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, excess loose fat trimmed
16 small corn tortillas, about 6 inches across
300 g avocado flesh, sliced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Start onions and heat: Make the pickled onions if needed, then let them chill while you cook. Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Prepare two broiler-safe rimmed metal trays, bare or lined with suitable foil; do not use parchment.

Divide the glaze: Whisk honey, soy sauce, fish sauce, 2 tbsp of the lime juice, zest, cumin, paprika, garlic, oil and pepper. Reserve half in a clean bowl. Keep the remaining 2 tbsp lime juice separate for the final finish. Toss chicken with the other half of the glaze. No extra salt is needed by default.

Roast with space: Open thighs flat and distribute them between the trays with gaps. Roast about 25–35 minutes, rotating the pans and swapping rack positions after fifteen minutes. Start checking the thickest part of each thigh at twenty-five minutes. Continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C; remove finished pieces if others need longer.

Glaze and briefly broil: Brush cooked chicken with the clean reserved glaze using a clean brush; divide it between the trays. Place one tray at a time about 6–8 inches below the broiler, following the appliance guidance. Broil for roughly 1–3 minutes, watching constantly, until bubbling and browned in spots. Stop before blackening. A broiler is optional: the final glaze can set for a few minutes in the hot oven instead.

Rest, slice and warm: Rest cooked thighs five minutes, then slice across the meat and toss with the reserved fresh lime juice. Meanwhile warm tortillas in batches in a dry skillet over medium heat, about 20–30 seconds per side or until pliable, and keep wrapped in a clean towel. Drain one cup onions and slice the avocado.

Assemble: Divide chicken among sixteen tortillas, then distribute avocado, drained onions, cilantro and optional sesame seeds. Serve two tacos per person. Bread is already counted; rice would be a replacement starch for a different bowl, not another required taco ingredient.

recipes.keywords: Mexican-inspired, American, sweet, savory, acidic, smoky, umami, weeknight, entertaining, meal-prep, game-day, roast, broil

recipes.name: Honey Sesame Chicken
recipes.description: Pan-seared chicken in a light honey-soy glaze, finished with toasted sesame and scallions.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 tbsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
2 tbsp neutral oil, for cooking, divided
2 tbsp light soy sauce, for the sauce
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, plus a small splash if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Season chicken: Toss chicken with its 1 tbsp light soy sauce and cornstarch until lightly coated. Refrigerate while preparing sauce and garnishes. Do not wipe off the coating afterward.
Mix sauce: Stir honey, the sauce's 2 tbsp soy, rice vinegar, and measured water until combined. Prepare garlic, ginger, sesame seeds and sliced scallions.

Sear in two batches: Heat 2 tsp neutral oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add half the chicken without overlap. Leave 2–3 minutes until it releases more easily, turn, and continue cooking until several thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C, usually 6–8 minutes total. Transfer to a clean bowl. Repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the rest of the chicken.

Build the glaze: Reduce heat to medium-low. Add the final 2 tsp neutral oil and stir garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Pour in the mixed sauce, scraping up brown residue but leaving any blackened bits out. Bring to a gentle simmer. Return chicken and its juices and fold for about 1–2 minutes until hot and lightly coated. If the glaze becomes sticky or pasty, add a small splash of water.

Finish and serve: Turn off heat and fold in toasted sesame oil, sesame seeds and scallions. Taste before serving and divide into four main portions. Serve with separately prepared plain rice and a vegetable side.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, kid-friendly, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Honey Sriracha Salmon Bowls
recipes.description: Honey-sriracha salmon bites with jasmine rice, cucumber, avocado, edamame and spicy mayonnaise.
recipeIngredient: 240 ml water, for rice, plus water for rinsing
1 large avocado, sliced just before serving
680 g skinless, boneless salmon, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tbsp water, reserved only for loosening the finished sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Start the jasmine rice: Rinse the rice and drain well. Put it in a heavy 2-quart saucepan with the measured 240 ml water. Bring to a boil, cover and reduce to low; simmer about 15 minutes until absorbed. Move off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff. Follow the rice package if its method differs. This small batch gives roughly 2 cups cooked rice for four bowls.

Marinate the fish: While the rice heats, whisk reduced-sodium soy sauce, honey, sriracha, garlic and the separate 3 tbsp sauce water in a bowl. Check the salmon for pin bones, cut into even 1-inch cubes and gently turn in the marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Wash the raw-fish board, utensils and your hands before preparing ready-to-eat toppings.

Prepare toppings and edamame: During the marinade, slice cucumber and portion the mayonnaise. Bring the 750 ml water to a boil in a small saucepan, add the frozen shelled edamame and cook according to its package, usually 3–5 minutes, until steaming hot and tender. Drain. Slice avocado shortly before assembly. If using the cucumber salad variation, start its salting before the fish marinade, allow 5–10 extra minutes overall, and omit the plain sliced cucumber.

Drain and organize two batches: Lift fish from the marinade with a slotted spoon, letting excess drip back into its bowl; scrape off large garlic clumps into that liquid. Reserve all the drained marinade for the cooked sauce, keeping it separate from toppings and cooked fish. Divide the salmon into two equal batches. Have a clean plate ready for cooked fish.

Brown the salmon: Heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, then add 2 tsp oil. Add half the salmon in a single layer with space between pieces. Cook about 2–3 minutes on the first face until browned, then turn and cook another 3–5 minutes, turning onto another face as needed, until the thickest cubes reach 145°F / 63°C. Insert a fine-tip thermometer sideways into their centers. Remove pieces as they finish. Reduce heat if the honey starts darkening rapidly. Transfer to the clean plate, remove any blackened deposits from the pan, and repeat with the remaining 2 tsp oil and fish. Allow the pan to recover heat between batches.

Boil and reduce the sauce: Remove all cooked fish. If the pan has bitter black residue, clean it before proceeding. Carefully pour in the reserved raw-contact marinade and bring to a full bubbling boil throughout, stirring. Maintain that boil for 1 minute, then lower the heat and simmer about 1–3 minutes until glossy and lightly spoon-coating; stop before it turns sticky or stringy. Turn off the heat and fold in all the cooked fish and its juices just long enough to coat.

Assemble: Divide all the rice, salmon and sauce, cucumber, avocado and edamame among four bowls. Each gets approximately 1/2 cup rice, a quarter of the fish, a quarter of the vegetables and 2 tbsp sriracha mayonnaise. Add the optional sesame seeds. Serve promptly; the browned faces soften once coated, so these are glazed salmon bites rather than a lasting crisp crust.

citation.name: Adapted from Claire Cary at Eat With Clarity

recipes.name: Hot and Sour Soup
recipes.description: Hot and sour soup is a Sichuan/Hunan classic. The name is literal: "hot" from white pepper (not just chilies) and "sour" from rice vinegar.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 lb Chinese BBQ Pork (Char Siu), shredded
1 square Firm Tofu, cut into 1/4-inch strips
1 oz Dried Wood Ear Mushrooms, reconstituted and sliced
3 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured slurry water
1/4 cup water, for the cornstarch slurry
Sesame Oil and Scallions for garnish

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Use prepared stock and fully cooked char siu. The timing includes the 30-minute mushroom soak but excludes making stock or cooking the pork from scratch.

itemListElement.text: Prep: Soak dried mushrooms in boiling water for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse, and slice.
Infuse: In a large pot, heat the measured canola oil. Sauté ginger and chili paste for 1 minute. Add the BBQ pork, wood ears, and bamboo shoots.
Boil: Pour in the Chinese Chicken Stock. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season: Stir in the soy sauce, vinegar, and white pepper. Taste - it should be sharp and punchy.
Tofu: Add the tofu strips and simmer for 3 minutes.
Bind: Stir the cornstarch slurry and slowly pour into the soup. Simmer for 2 minutes until the soup is thick and clear.

The Current: Remove from heat. Stir the soup vigorously in one direction to create a current. Stop stirring and slowly stream in the beaten egg. Let the ribbons set, then gently return to a simmer if needed until the egg is fully set and the soup reaches at least 160°F / 71°C.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and garnish with sesame oil and fresh scallions for the final High Note.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, spicy, savory, acidic, umami, comfort-food, weekend-project, meal-prep, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Hot Mulled Apple Cider
recipes.description: Never let mulled cider reach a rolling boil once spices are added - high heat turns cinnamon bitter. A tiny pinch of sea salt amplifies the natural sweetness of apples.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: In a large heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine the apple cider, brown sugar, allspice, 1 tsp cloves, salt, nutmeg, and cinnamon sticks.
Heat: Bring the mixture just to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Infuse: Immediately reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Do not let it reach a rolling boil.
Strain: Pour the cider through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot or slow cooker to remove the whole spices.
Garnish: Stud each orange wedge with a whole clove.
Serve: Ladle into mugs and float a clove-studded orange wedge in each.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, holiday, simmer, boil, slow-cook

recipes.name: Frittata
recipes.description: Cook the vegetables until tender and let excess moisture evaporate before adding eggs; spinach and zucchini contribute different amounts of water. Whisk the eggs just until blended, then finish gently enough to keep the center tender.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Heavy Cream or Crème Fraîche (for richness)
1 cup (4 oz) Cheese, freshly grated (Gruyère or Sharp Cheddar)
3-5 cups Fresh Vegetables (Spinach, Zucchini, Peppers), chopped
Butter or oil, as needed to grease the casserole dish or muffin cups for baked variants

recipeInstructions.text: Choose the method and blend: Preheat to 425 °F for the stovetop-to-oven method, or 350 °F for a baked variant. Whisk eggs, dairy and measured salt just until yolks and whites blend. Fold in half the cheese, reserving half for topping. The original skillet batch uses a 12-inch oven-safe skillet; the pan and handle must tolerate the oven temperature.

Cook the vegetables: Heat the measured olive oil in the skillet over medium heat. Add dense vegetables such as peppers first, then zucchini and finally spinach. Cook until tender rather than merely tender-crisp, letting released water evaporate so there is no puddle before adding eggs. Use the listed raw vegetable amount; its cooked volume depends on the mix.

Set the skillet edges: For the stovetop method, pour the eggs over the cooked vegetables and stir briefly to distribute. Let the outside edge become pale and opaque, about 30 seconds to 1 minute. For a baked variant, skip to its method below after cooking the vegetables.

Finish the skillet: Sprinkle the reserved half of the cheese over the eggs and transfer carefully to the 425 °F oven. Bake about 7–14 minutes as a first range, until puffed and opaque, with a center that is gently set rather than liquid and reaches 160 °F / 71 °C. Check without touching the skillet. Remove as soon as the endpoint is reached; do not chase a deeply browned top.

Baked casserole variant: For the original batch, grease a 9-by 13-inch baking dish with the separate butter or oil allowance. Let the cooked vegetables cool briefly, stir them into the eggs, pour into the dish and add the reserved cheese. Bake at 350 °F for about 20–25 minutes as a first range, until the center is set and reaches 160 °F / 71 °C. Check earlier or continue as needed for the actual depth.

Baked mini variant: Instead of a casserole, grease standard muffin cups with the separate butter or oil allowance. Briefly cool the cooked vegetables and stir them into the eggs. The original batch fills about 18 cups with a scant 1/3 cup mixture each; scaled batches need more or fewer standard cups at the same depth. Add reserved cheese and bake at 350 °F for about 13–17 minutes as a first range, until centers are set and reach 160 °F / 71 °C. Check partially filled tins early and allow oven space or extra batches.

Finish: Let settle briefly, garnish with the fresh herbs and serve. The full original batch makes six portions; apportion a different batch size accordingly. The methods are alternatives using one batch of eggs, vegetables and cheese. Serve promptly; refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90 °F, and reheat centers to 165 °F / 74 °C.

recipes.keywords: Italian, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, entertaining, potluck, bake, saute, blend

recipes.name: In the Park
recipes.description: Gently muddle basil and lemon to release aroma without grinding the leaves. Double-strain the shaken cocktail to remove small pieces of leaf and citrus.

recipeInstructions.text: Continue: Layer 1st three ingredients in glass in the above order and muddle gently. Add Gin, juice, bitters and ice to the shaker, and shake vigorously.
Continue: Double strain over ice in a highball glass. Garnish with Freshly spanked basil leaf.

recipes.keywords: American, mix

recipes.name: Pressure-Cooker Baingan Bharta
recipes.description: Eggplant cooks with cumin, onion, tomato and warm spices, then reduces in the same pot to a glossy mash finished with cilantro and lemon.
recipeIngredient: 900 g globe eggplant, weighed after peeling and removing stems, cut into 1-inch cubes; buy approximately 1.1 kg whole
375 ml water, all for deglazing and pressure cooking
200 g yellow onion, peeled and finely chopped
1 tsp fine salt, plus up to 1/2 tsp more after reduction
300 g ripe Roma tomatoes, cores removed, finely chopped with their juices
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, reserved only for loosening the mash after pressure cooking if needed
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, divided and partly added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Peel and weigh the eggplant, then cut into even 1-inch cubes. Chop the onion and tomatoes, keeping all tomato juice. Measure the spices and the separate quantities of water. Keep the tomatoes aside for the top layer.

Sauté the onion: Heat all 4 tbsp oil using the cooker's moderate sauté setting. Add cumin and stir about 30 seconds until fragrant and a shade darker. Add onion and the initial 1 tsp salt. Cook about 8–12 minutes, stirring often, until softened with golden edges. Lower the heat if edges brown before the onion softens; do not add more oil.

Bloom spices and deglaze: Lower the sauté heat. Add garlic, ginger, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, turmeric, paprika and cayenne. Stir about 30 seconds, then cancel sauté and pour in all 375 ml pressure-cooking water. Scrape the entire base with a wooden spatula for 1–2 minutes, until it feels smooth with no stuck patches. The onion mixture should be loose and watery, not a paste.

Load the vegetables: Spread the eggplant over the deglazed base. Spoon all the tomatoes and their juices on top. Do not stir them down to the bottom. Check that everything is below the cooker's pressure maximum and clear of its lid fittings.

Pressure-cook and release naturally: Close and seal according to the cooker instructions. Cook on high pressure for 7 minutes; the countdown starts after the cooker reaches pressure. Turn Keep Warm off when cooking ends and leave the valve sealed until pressure has fallen completely on its own, usually 20–30 minutes or longer. Do not quick-release or force the lid open. Open only when the pressure indicator has dropped and the model's instructions confirm it is fully depressurized.

Check and mash: Test eggplant cubes from the middle and edge of the pot; they should collapse readily under a fork. If firm, simmer gently in the retained liquid until soft. Mash everything together with a potato masher, leaving a little texture. Keep all the liquid in the pot.

Reduce patiently: Select a sauté setting that maintains a steady uncovered simmer. Cook about 20–35 minutes, stirring and scraping the base often, until the mash is glossy and cohesive and a spoonful has no watery rim. It may need longer with especially juicy vegetables or a gentle cooker. Lower the heat and stir more frequently as it thickens; do not drain off the juices to hurry it. Taste only after reduction, then add some or all of the reserved 1/2 tsp salt if wanted.

Finish and serve: Cancel the heat and fold in cilantro and 2 tsp lemon juice. Taste before adding the remaining teaspoon lemon juice. Divide into four vegetable-main portions and serve with separately prepared basmati rice or naan and a little cucumber raita. Final volume varies with the vegetables and reduction; expect approximately 4–6 cups.

recipes.keywords: Indian, aromatic, spicy, savory, family-meal, meal-prep, pressure-cook, saute, simmer

citation.name: Adapted from Ashley Singh Thomas's Baingan Bharta at My Heart Beets

recipes.name: Pressure-Cooker Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.description: Sautéing bacon first, removing it for garnish, then cooking aromatics in the rendered fat infuses this soup with smoky umami backbone. Including a Granny Smith apple prevents the squash from becoming overly sweet - the apple's acidity balances the soup's natural sugars and provides brightness within the puree itself.
recipeIngredient: 1 Granny Smith Apple, cored and chopped (The Acid Note)
2 1/2 lbs Butternut Squash, peeled and cubed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Use an electric pressure cooker with a sauté setting. Follow the model’s minimum-liquid requirements and soup fill limit before sealing; do not exceed its marked limit. Use full natural pressure release for this soup. The 12-minute pressure timer excludes coming to pressure and releasing it; both vary with the cooker and load, so the listed 45 minutes is not a ready-to-serve deadline.

itemListElement.text: The Render: Set the electric pressure cooker to "Sauté" (High). Add diced bacon and cook until crispy (6-8 mins). Remove bacon to a plate, leaving the fat in the pot.
Aromatics: Add onion to the bacon fat. Sauté for 3 minutes until translucent. Stir in garlic, sage, and thyme; cook for 30-45 seconds until fragrant.
Pressure: Stir in the squash, carrots, celery, and chopped apple. Pour in the chicken stock and season with salt and pepper.
Cook: Secure the lid. Set to High Pressure for 12 minutes.

Release: Turn Keep Warm off and allow pressure to release fully naturally. Open only when the cooker indicates no pressure remains and its instructions permit opening. Remove and discard the thyme sprigs.

The Emulsion: Stir in the heavy cream. With the cooker off, use an immersion blender according to its hot-liquid instructions. Keep the blade guard submerged, start on low, and stop the motor before lifting it out. Puree until smooth.
Serve: Ladle into bowls. Garnish with the reserved crispy bacon and chives for the mandatory Textural Snap.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, rich, comfort-food, saute, blend

recipes.name: Pressure-Cooker Potato Leek Soup
recipes.description: Adapted from Sandy Clifton's potato-leek soup at Simply Happy Foodie, this version softens leeks in butter and oil before adding flour and broth. White pepper and nutmeg bridge the gap between earthy potatoes and rich cream, classic French seasonings for potato-leek soup.
recipeIngredient: 5 cups Leeks, cleaned and sliced (white and pale green parts only)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Use an electric pressure cooker with a sauté setting. Follow its minimum-liquid, maximum-fill and pressure-release instructions; these depend on the model.

itemListElement.text: The Sweat: Set electric pressure cooker to "Sauté." Add butter and olive oil. Once hot, add leeks and sauté for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until softened; reduce the heat if the leeks start to brown.
Aromatics: Add garlic and sauté for 30 seconds. Sprinkle the flour over the leeks and stir for 1 minute to cook out the raw starch taste.
Deglaze: Pour in the broth slowly, scraping the bottom of the pot to ensure no flour sticks.
Pressure: Add potatoes, bay leaf, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Secure the lid. Set to High Pressure for 7 minutes.
Release: Turn Keep Warm off and let pressure release fully naturally. Open only after the pressure indicator has dropped and the model’s instructions confirm it is safe.
The Emulsion: Remove the bay leaf. With the heat off, use an immersion blender with its head submerged to puree the soup. Stop once smooth; prolonged blending can make potato soup gluey.
Finish: Stir in the half-and-half. Taste and adjust salt if needed.
Serve: Garnish with a dollop of sour cream and fresh chives for Textural Balance.

recipes.keywords: French, sweet, rich, comfort-food, saute, steam, blend

recipes.name: Israeli-Style Hummus
recipes.description: A tahini-rich chickpea spread with strained garlic-lemon juice. Cook the chickpeas until their centers mash without grit, then adjust water until the hummus spreads easily.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (200 g) dried chickpeas, sorted and rinsed; weight is before soaking
2 tsp baking soda, divided between soaking and cooking
12 cups water, divided equally between soaking and cooking, plus more to keep chickpeas submerged
1 cup (240 g) tahini, thoroughly stirred in its jar
1/4 cup (60 ml) fresh lemon juice, plus up to 2 tbsp more to taste
4 medium garlic cloves, unpeeled and rinsed; remove loose dirty outer skin
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
1/2 cup (120 ml) cool water for blending, divided, plus more a tablespoon at a time as needed
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for serving the full batch

recipeInstructions.text: Soak overnight: Put the sorted, rinsed chickpeas in a large bowl with half the baking soda and half the soaking/cooking water. Stir, cover, and refrigerate for 12 hours. Leave plenty of room for expansion. Drain, discard the soaking water, and rinse well.

Cook to a creamy center: Put the chickpeas in a 4-quart pot with the remaining baking soda and fresh cooking water. Bring to a boil, allowing about 15 minutes, then reduce to a steady simmer. Skim foam as needed and leave the lid ajar. Keep the beans submerged, adding water if needed. Begin checking at 60 minutes; allow up to 2 hours of simmering or longer for older beans. Press several chickpeas with a fork: they must smear without a firm center. Some splitting is welcome. Keep them in the liquid until the tahini base is ready.

Infuse and strain garlic: While the chickpeas simmer, put the garlic, initial measured lemon juice and salt in a mini chopper or the processor's small insert. Pulse until the cloves are finely broken up in the juice, stopping to scrape. Leave for 10 minutes, then press through a fine-mesh strainer into a bowl. Discard solids and skins. Transfer the strained juice to the clean main processor bowl, checking that no skin fragments remain.

Make the sesame base: Add the stirred tahini to the garlic-lemon juice and process. Add half the measured blending water gradually, stopping to scrape, until the paste is uniform. It may become very thick before it smooths out.

Drain and puree: Drain the chickpeas thoroughly through a fine-mesh strainer, retaining any soft chickpea pieces but discarding the cooking water. Transfer to the processor while warm, following its temperature and fill limits, and add the cumin. Process for 4–5 minutes, pausing to scrape and following the machine's duty-cycle guidance. Add the remaining measured blending water a tablespoon at a time only as needed, then additional fresh water in small increments if the puree still holds a stiff mound. Aim for a smooth spread that holds a shallow spoon swirl; the hummus will firm as it cools.

Balance and serve: Taste a small spoonful at a comfortable eating temperature. Add some of the optional lemon juice if the hummus needs more acidity, and adjust salt in small pinches. Spread the amount being served in a shallow dish, make a well, and finish with the serving oil and optional paprika; use a proportional share of each garnish if serving only part of the batch. Offer warm pita and a crisp, tangy salad alongside. As a side to chicken, allow about 1/4 cup hummus per person; for five people that is 1 1/4 cups, leaving the rest to refrigerate. Pita, salad, and chicken are additional components.

recipes.keywords: Israeli, Middle Eastern, acidic, rich, nutty, meal-prep, entertaining, boil, simmer, blend

citation.name: Adapted from Michael Solomonov's Israeli-style hummus

recipes.name: Sausage, Kale and Ciabatta Stuffing
recipes.description: Milk-soaked ciabatta, browned sausage and tender kale baked in a shallow casserole, with a moist interior and a lightly crisp top.
recipeIngredient: 450 g raw mild Italian pork sausage, casings removed
300 g trimmed kale leaves, tough ribs removed, cut into thin ribbons
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, for wilting kale
1/4 tsp fine salt, optional after tasting
1 tsp olive oil, for greasing the baking dish, plus up to 1 tbsp if needed for the vegetables

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare bread and oven: Heat the oven to 350°F / 177°C. Grease a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with one teaspoon of the oil. Put the ciabatta pieces in a large bowl, pour over the milk and turn gently. Let them hydrate for about twenty to thirty minutes while cooking the sausage and vegetables, turning once more so exposed dry pieces get milk too.

Brown the sausage: In a large Dutch oven over medium heat, break the sausage into small bite-sized pieces and cook about eight to twelve minutes, stirring periodically, until browned and cooked through. Check the largest pieces reach 160°F / 71°C for pork. Transfer to a clean bowl with a slotted spoon. Pour off excess fat, leaving about one tablespoon in the pot. If there is less, add enough of the optional olive oil to reach that amount.

Soften aromatics: Cook onion and celery in that fat over medium heat for seven to ten minutes, until softened, stirring and scraping the base without burning it. Add garlic and stir for thirty seconds.

Tenderize kale: Add kale in handfuls and the measured water. Cover and cook five to eight minutes, turning once, until a tasted piece is tender rather than fibrous. Uncover and cook off any puddle for another two to three minutes. Remove from heat.

Combine and season: Fold the cooked sausage, kale mixture, parsley, Parmesan, basil, sage, rosemary and pepper into the hydrated bread with a large spoon. Keep some bread texture; do not knead it smooth or mix hot ingredients with bare hands. Taste a cooled spoonful now that the sausage is fully cooked. Add the optional quarter-teaspoon fine salt only if needed. Spread loosely and evenly in the prepared dish; do not compress it into a dense block.

Bake and check: Bake immediately, uncovered, for about thirty to forty minutes. The center must reach at least 165°F / 74°C and the top should be lightly browned. Cover loosely if the top colors before the center is ready.
Rest and serve: Rest ten minutes, then spoon into eight side portions. Expect a moist, rustic casserole, not slices of firm bread pudding.

recipes.name: Japanese Beef Rice Bowl (Gyudon)
recipes.description: Gyudon is Tokyo comfort food - beef and onions simmered in a slightly sweet, deeply savory broth served over rice. The dish came from the Meiji era when beef became part of Japanese home cooking, and it became an iconic fast-food staple.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Beef Sirloin or Ribeye (thinly sliced)
4 Eggs, fully cooked, or pasteurized shell eggs soft-boiled or poached (optional)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Egg Note: A soft yolk mixes into the broth and rice. For this option, use shell eggs labeled as pasteurized; otherwise cook both the yolk and white until firm. The egg is optional.

itemListElement.text: Make the Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, mirin, sake, garlic, ginger, and beef stock. Set aside.

Cook the Onions: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sliced onions with a pinch of salt. Sauté for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they soften and start to caramelize at the edges. They should be golden and fragrant.

Add the Beef: Increase heat to high. Add sliced beef to the pan in a single layer. Let it sit for 1 minute without stirring - this develops a slight crust. Toss and cook another 1 minute until the beef is mostly cooked through but still slightly pink inside (it will finish cooking in the broth).
Simmer: Pour the sauce over the beef and onions. Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 4-5 minutes. The sauce should reduce slightly and become glossy. Taste and adjust soy sauce or mirin if needed.

Assemble: Place warm rice in a bowl. Pour the beef and onion mixture with all its broth over the rice. If using an egg, top with a fully cooked egg or a soft-boiled or poached pasteurized shell egg. Warm rice is not a reliable way to cook an egg safely.
Garnish: Sprinkle with sliced green onions and a pinch of shichimi togarashi if desired.

recipes.name: Japanese Chicken Curry
recipes.description: Chicken thighs and vegetables in a gently thickened curry gravy with golden onions, apple, and a freshly made spiced roux.
recipeIngredient: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
300 g carrots, cut into pieces no thicker than 3/4 inch
400 g Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch pieces
4 cups (960 ml) unsalted chicken stock, plus a little water only if needed
1/2 tsp fine salt, plus more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Soften and brown onions: Heat oil in a heavy 5-quart pot over medium heat. Add onions and the measured salt. Cook about 15–20 minutes, stirring regularly, until soft and golden at the edges. Lower heat if they catch; a spoonful of the measured stock can loosen browned material.
Add aromatics and chicken: Stir in garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds. Add chicken and turn in the onions for 3–4 minutes. This starts cooking the surface; the chicken is not yet ready to eat.

Simmer vegetables: Add carrots, potatoes, remaining stock, apple, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, and soy sauce. Bring to a gentle simmer. Partly cover and cook about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes and carrots are nearly tender. Add a little water only if needed to keep most pieces in the liquid.

Make the roux: While the curry simmers, melt butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir in the 70 g flour and cook, stirring continuously, about 10–15 minutes until golden to light brown and smelling toasted. Use color and aroma rather than forcing it to a dark chocolate color. Turn the heat very low, stir in curry powder and garam masala for about 30 seconds, then remove from heat.

Incorporate smoothly: Ladle about a cup of liquid from the curry into a heatproof measuring jug. Gradually whisk it into the roux, beginning with small additions and smoothing each one before adding more. Scrape the loosened roux into the curry pot and stir thoroughly.

Finish gently: Simmer uncovered about 8–10 minutes, stirring the bottom often, until the gravy thickens and vegetables are fully tender. Check several large chicken pieces for at least 165°F / 74°C. Thin with a little water if the gravy stands in a mound; it should flow slowly. Taste and adjust salt only as needed. Divide into six curry portions and serve with separately prepared rice.

recipes.name: Japanese Cucumber Sunomono
recipes.description: Thin cucumber slices in a light sweet-sour rice-vinegar dressing, finished with toasted sesame.
recipeIngredient: 400 g Japanese, Persian, or English cucumber, washed and ends trimmed
1 tsp finely grated fresh ginger, optional
1/4 tsp shichimi togarashi, optional; check the label

recipeInstructions.text: Slice evenly: Cut cucumber into rounds about 1–2 mm thick with a sharp knife or a mandoline with its hand guard. Halve and remove large seed cores first if necessary. Aim for thin intact slices, not crushed fragments.

Salt and drain: Toss with the draining salt in a colander over a bowl. Leave for 10 minutes. Gently squeeze small handfuls to remove excess water without crushing, then transfer to a clean bowl. Discard the drained liquid.
Dissolve the dressing: While the cucumber rests, stir rice vinegar, sugar, and dressing salt until fully dissolved. Stir in optional grated ginger.
Dress briefly: Toss the drained cucumber with dressing and refrigerate for about 5 minutes. Taste a slice with some dressing; adjust with a little extra vinegar only if needed.

Finish: Divide among four small side bowls, including a little dressing. Sprinkle with toasted sesame and optional shichimi just before serving. For preparation a few hours ahead, refrigerate cucumber and dressing separately and combine near serving.

recipes.name: Japanese-Style Trout with Dashi
recipes.description: Reducing soy-mirin-vinegar until it becomes heavy syrup, then brushing it onto trout in multiple layers under the broiler creates a mahogany-colored, crispy glaze that contrasts delicate, flaky meat. Poaching julienned vegetables in dashi for exactly 1 minute keeps them crisp while infusing them with clean, oceanic flavor that balances the rich glaze.

recipeInstructions.text: The Glaze: In a small saucepan, bring soy sauce, mirin, sugar, and vinegar to a boil. Simmer for 10 minutes until reduced by half and thick enough to coat a spoon.
The Bath: In a separate pot, bring Dashi to a boil. Add carrots and leeks. Simmer for exactly 1 minute. Remove vegetables with a slotted spoon and set aside. Keep dashi warm.
Thermal Prep: Preheat the broiler. Arrange trout fillets, skin-side up, on a sturdy baking sheet.
The Lacquer: Broil for 2 minutes until the skin sizzles. Carefully peel off and discard the skin. Brush the meat with the glaze.
Stage 2: Broil for 3 minutes, brushing twice more with the lacquer, until the trout is cooked through and the surface is mirror-glossy.
Assemble: Mound rice in shallow bowls. Top with the glazed trout, nori, and the poached vegetables.
Serve: Carefully pour the hot dashi around the perimeter of the bowl. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Japchae (Korean Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
recipes.description: Japchae is Korean mixed stir-fry with sweet potato glass noodles - a dish that shows up at celebrations and fancy dinners because it's elegant and looks harder than it is. The glass noodles (also called dangmyeon) have a silky, slightly gelatinous texture that's completely different from wheat or rice noodles.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz Sweet Potato Glass Noodles (dangmyeon), also called Korean glass noodles
8 oz Beef Sirloin or Tenderloin, thinly sliced
2 Medium Carrots, cut into thin matchsticks
1 Medium Zucchini, cut into thin matchsticks
4 oz Mushrooms (shiitake or cremini), thinly sliced
1 cup Fresh Spinach (or 4 oz frozen spinach, thawed and squeezed dry)
2 tsp Gochugaru (Korean red chili flakes, optional)
1 tbsp Vegetable Oil, plus more as needed for the vegetables

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Glass Noodle Sourcing: Also labeled as "Korean sweet potato noodles" or "dangmyeon." They're available at any Asian market and increasingly at regular grocery stores. Do not confuse with rice noodles or tapioca noodles.

Vegetable Flexibility: This dish is forgiving. Use whatever vegetables need using: bell peppers, green beans, broccoli, shiitake mushrooms, cabbage. The principle is the same - cook each vegetable separately, then combine.

Beef Alternative: Shrimp can replace the beef; cook until the flesh is firm, pearly and opaque rather than following the beef time. Or skip the protein entirely for a vegetarian version - the noodles and vegetables are hearty enough.

Make-Ahead: Japchae tastes equally good warm or at room temperature and is perfect for meal prep. Refrigerate in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C), and keep for up to 3 days. Serve cold or reheat to 165°F / 74°C.

Timing: Allow about 40 minutes as a planning estimate, with the noodle cooking and beef marinade overlapping vegetable preparation. Sequential vegetable batches alone take about 10-14 minutes; more batches or slower knife work take longer. This estimate has not been kitchen-tested.

Texture Key: The reason to cook vegetables separately is texture. If you dump everything together and cook it, the vegetables become mushy. Separate cooking preserves the bite of each ingredient.

itemListElement.text: Cook the Noodles: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add the glass noodles and cook according to the package directions until translucent and tender with a slight chew. Drain in a colander, rinse under cool water, and set aside. If needed, use a little of the optional additional sesame oil to prevent sticking.

Marinate the Beef: While the noodles cook, combine the thinly sliced beef with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1/2 tsp minced garlic, 1/4 tsp black pepper, and 1 tsp cornstarch in a small bowl. This cornstarch coating (velveting) protects the meat from the high heat of the skillet. Refrigerate for 15 minutes while you prep vegetables.

Cook the Beef: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add the marinated beef in a single layer and let it sit for 1 minute without stirring to develop color. Stir and continue cooking until the thickest slices reach 145°F / 63°C; use a thin-tip thermometer inserted from the side. Transfer to a clean plate and rest at least 3 minutes while cooking the vegetables. Do not stop at partly cooked beef: the final toss is brief.

Cook the Vegetables (Separately): In the same skillet, add a little more oil if needed. Cook the harder vegetables first, one type at a time, for speed and texture control: - Carrots: 2-3 minutes, then transfer to a bowl - Zucchini: 2-3 minutes, then transfer to the bowl - Mushrooms: 2-3 minutes, then transfer to the bowl - Onion: 2-3 minutes until softened, then transfer to the bowl - Scallions: Cook about 1 minute until slightly softened, then transfer - Spinach: Cook until wilted (about 1 minute), drain excess liquid, then transfer. If using thawed, squeezed frozen spinach, warm it through instead.

Make the Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 2 tsp sesame oil, brown sugar, rice vinegar, and all the remaining minced garlic. Taste and adjust - it should be balanced between salty, sweet, and tangy.

Combine: Add the cooked glass noodles and all vegetables back to the large skillet. Return the cooked beef to the pan. Pour the sauce over everything and toss gently but thoroughly for 1-2 minutes until everything is coated and heated through. The heat should be low - you're just combining and warming, not cooking further.
Optional Heat: If you want spice, add 1-2 tsp gochugaru (Korean red chili flakes) when tossing with the sauce.
Serve: Transfer to a serving plate or individual bowls. Garnish generously with sesame seeds and a light drizzle of sesame oil. Serve at room temperature or warm.

recipes.name: Jeri's Lentil Soup
recipes.description: This traditional recipe was a wedding gift from Pat Miller and Sean Kilpatrick, passed down from Jeri, a Broadway dancer turned nutritionist. Adding sherry vinegar at the end brightens earthy lentils - the acidity wakes up the palate.
recipeIngredient: 16 oz Dry Green or Brown Lentils, rinsed
1 tbsp Sherry Vinegar or Fresh Lemon Juice
Salt and Black Pepper to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Plan on roughly 6 hours including preparation, the initial sauté, 5 hours on LOW, and the final 30-minute cook. Lentil age and slow-cooker behavior can extend this; tenderness, not the timer alone, determines when to finish.

itemListElement.text: Sauté: Heat oil in a large skillet. Sauté onions and carrots with the Italian seasoning for 5-8 minutes until translucent.
The Pot: Transfer the vegetables to a slow cooker. Add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, and broth.
Slow Cook: Cook on LOW for about 5 hours, until lentils are tender but not mushy. Test several lentils and extend the cooking if their centers are still hard.
Infuse: Stir in the white wine and parsley. Cook for another 30 minutes.

Texture (Optional): Turn the cooker off. Following the blender’s hot-liquid instructions, pulse briefly with the blade guard submerged and stop the motor before lifting it out. Leave some lentils and vegetables whole.
The Acid Balance: Stir in the sherry vinegar or lemon juice. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

recipes.name: Jerk Pork Shoulder
recipes.description: Jerk-seasoned pork shoulder with allspice, thyme, hot chile and citrus, braised until it shreds. A clean, separately refrigerated portion of marinade provides the fresh finish.
recipeIngredient: 6 scallions, roughly chopped, white and green parts
1–2 Scotch bonnet or habanero peppers, stemmed; remove seeds and membranes for less heat
2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves or 2 tsp dried thyme
Hot water, only if needed to prevent the braise drying out

recipeInstructions.text: Blend and reserve: Blend all marinade ingredients until mostly smooth. Before handling the pork, measure 1/4 cup into a clean covered container, label it for finishing and refrigerate at 40°F / 4°C or colder.
Marinate: Score the pork about 1/4 inch deep. Coat it with the remaining marinade, cover and refrigerate for 8–24 hours. Keep the clean finishing portion in its separate container.
Heat the oven: Heat to 325°F / 165°C. Keep the pork refrigerated until ready to sear; it does not need to reach room temperature.

Sear: Scrape excess marinade from the pork into a bowl reserved for the braise. Heat the Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear the pork, turning to brown its broad surfaces, about 3–4 minutes per side. Lower the heat if the sugary coating starts to blacken.

Braise: Add the scraped raw-contact marinade, stock and orange juice around the pork. Cover and cook in the oven about 3–3 1/2 hours, until a fork easily separates the meat. Check that liquid remains; add a little hot water if needed. The thickest part must reach at least 145°F / 63°C, but shreddable tenderness requires further cooking. Continue covered if still firm.

Rest and reduce: Move the pork to a board and rest for 20 minutes. During the rest, skim fat from the braising liquid and simmer it uncovered until glossy but still pourable, about 10 minutes. The rest also exceeds the 3-minute minimum after reaching the pork safety temperature.

Shred and finish: Shred the meat, discarding large pockets of fat. Toss with the reduced sauce and the clean 1/4 cup marinade reserved before raw contact. Do not use any unbraised scraped marinade here.

Serve or reheat: Serve in eight portions, or cool promptly for later meals. To reheat, spread pork and sauce in a covered baking dish at 325°F / 165°C until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C. Start checking after 20–25 minutes; a cold, deep dish takes longer.

recipes.name: Kachumber Salad
recipes.description: Small-diced cucumber, tomato, and onion with lemon, fresh herbs, and toasted cumin, dressed just before serving.
recipeIngredient: 300 g cucumber, washed and cut into 1/4-inch dice
250 g firm ripe tomatoes, cut into 1/4-inch dice
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, plus more only if needed
1/4 tsp chaat masala, optional; check ingredients for dietary needs

recipeInstructions.text: Toast and cool cumin: Shake cumin seeds in a small dry skillet over medium-low heat for about 1–2 minutes, until fragrant and a shade darker. Transfer to a plate, cool briefly, and crush with a mortar or the back of a spoon.

Cut vegetables: Dice cucumber and tomato into roughly 1/4-inch pieces and cut onion more finely. Remove tough cucumber skin or large watery seed cores as needed. Mince optional serrano; omit it for a milder salad. Combine vegetables with cilantro and mint.

Mix dressing: Stir lemon juice, cooled crushed cumin, measured salt, pepper, optional olive oil, and optional chaat masala together. If not serving yet, refrigerate vegetables and dressing separately.
Dress at serving: Toss gently with dressing. Taste a spoonful and add a little extra lemon only if the vegetables need more acidity. Divide into six small side portions and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Indian, bright, fresh, tangy, herbaceous, clean, weeknight, family-meal, quick-lunch, picnic, toast, toss, no-cook

recipes.name: Kalbi
recipes.description: Kalbi brings a soy, sake and sugar marinade to flanken-cut Korean barbecue ribs. Keep the 1/2-inch cut consistent and use both a direct-heat and a cooler grilling zone: the sweet coating can darken before the meat finishes.
recipeIngredient: 5 lb flanken-style beef short ribs, raw, fresh or fully thawed; cut across the bones about 1/2 inch thick
suitable grilling oil, as needed for the grill grates

recipeInstructions.text: Inspect and prepare: Inspect the cut ribs for loose bone fragments; remove visible fragments with a damp paper towel and pat dry, keeping raw juices away from ready-to-eat foods. Use covered food-safe vessels with room to turn the entire listed batch; divide all ingredients proportionally if more vessels are needed.

Apply the sake-sugar rub: Use flanken-style beef short ribs, sake, and granulated sugar. Stir the sake and granulated sugar together and rub the mixture onto both sides of the ribs. Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes while preparing the soy marinade.

Mix the soy marinade: Whisk soy sauce, dark brown sugar, toasted sesame oil, scallions, garlic cloves, black pepper, and vegetable oil until the brown sugar dissolves. This main marinade has no added water; the water-diluted alternative below is a separate choice.

Marinate cold: Pour the entire soy marinade over the ribs and turn to coat every slice. Cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 8 hours or overnight. Turn with clean utensils if needed for even contact; do not leave the ribs on the counter to warm through.

Set up the grill and sear: Set up a charcoal grill with medium-high direct heat and a cooler zone, following its operating instructions. Use suitable grilling oil as needed for the grates. Drain the ribs and wipe away excess marinade just before grilling; discard the raw-contact marinade. Grill uncrowded ribs over direct heat, starting checks around 2–3 minutes per side, until seared without blackening the sugar. Work in loads and keep waiting raw ribs refrigerated.

Finish on the cooler zone: Move the ribs to the cooler zone and begin checking after about 5 minutes, turning as needed. Continue until the meat is cooked through to at least 145°F in its thickest part away from bone, using a probe suitable for thin meat from the side. The fat and edges should be cooked to your liking; a clock or char alone does not establish the center temperature.

Rest and serve: Transfer to a clean platter and rest 5 minutes before cutting between the bones with clean kitchen shears and serving. For larger batches use enough grill space or more loads; keep the cut size, heat zones and endpoint the same.

recipes.name: Kale Caesar with Crispy Chickpeas
recipes.description: This Caesar replaces the traditional breadcrumbs and anchovies with crispy roasted chickpeas that add both crunch and plant-based protein. The massage is critical - working salt and a bit of oil into the shredded kale breaks down the tough fibers, transforming them into something tender and sweet.
recipeIngredient: 1 large bunch Lacinato (Dino) Kale, stems removed and shredded
1 can (15 oz) Chickpeas, drained and patted very dry
1 tsp White Miso or Soy Sauce
1/4 tsp Anchovy Paste (optional, for traditional Caesar depth)
1/3 cup Shaved or Grated Parmesan Cheese

recipeInstructions.text: Roast the Chickpeas: Preheat oven to 425°F. Pat the drained chickpeas very dry with a clean kitchen towel - any moisture will prevent them from crisping. Toss with 1 tbsp olive oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, and pepper on a sheet pan. Spread in a single layer and roast for 20-25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until golden and crispy. Set aside to cool - they will continue to crisp as they cool.

Massage the Kale: Place the shredded kale in a large bowl. Drizzle with 1 tsp olive oil and a pinch of salt. Using your hands, massage the leaves vigorously for 2 minutes until they turn dark green and soften significantly. This breaks down the cell walls and makes the kale tender.

Make the Dressing: In a blender or small food processor, combine the 1/4 cup olive oil, grated garlic, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, miso (or soy sauce), anchovy paste if using, water, salt, and pepper. Blend until completely smooth. The dressing should have the consistency of heavy cream. Adjust water if needed.
Toss: Pour the dressing over the massaged kale and toss well to ensure every leaf is evenly coated.
Assemble: Top with the crispy roasted chickpeas, shaved Parmesan, and a light dusting of lemon zest.
Rest: Let the salad sit for 5 minutes before serving. Unlike delicate greens, kale actually improves as it absorbs the dressing - it doesn't wilt.

Make-Ahead: The crispy chickpeas can be made up to 2 days ahead and stored in an airtight container. The dressing keeps refrigerated for up to 3 days. Massage the kale and dress it just before serving for the best texture.

recipes.name: Kale Salad with Mango, Avocado and Feta
recipes.description: Chopped kale with mango, avocado, feta and toasted seeds in an orange, honey and olive-oil dressing.
recipeIngredient: 1 bunch curly kale, tough ribs removed, leaves washed, dried and finely chopped
1 large ripe but firm mango, peeled, pitted and cubed
1 large ripe avocado, peeled, pitted and diced
1/2 cup toasted hulled pumpkin seeds or sunflower seeds
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for softening kale
3 tbsp + 1 tsp extra-virgin olive oil, for dressing
Salt and black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare kale: Remove tough ribs, wash leaves, dry thoroughly and chop finely. Put in a wide bowl and add the oil labeled for softening kale with a small pinch of salt. Rub gently for about 1–2 minutes until darker and more flexible, stopping before the leaves become wet and limp.

Prepare fruit and dressing: Peel, pit and cube mango. Finely dice onion and crumble feta. Zest and juice the orange; whisk its juice and zest with the oil labeled for dressing, garlic, Dijon and honey. Taste and add salt and pepper as needed.

Combine gradually: Toss kale with about half the dressing, then gently fold in mango, onion and feta. Taste a leaf with fruit and cheese. Add more dressing only if needed for a light coating and reserve the rest.
Finish: Dice avocado just before serving and fold it in gently. Scatter with toasted seeds, divide among side plates and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Katharine Hepburn’s Brownies
recipes.description: The small flour measure keeps these brownies dense and fudgy. Keep all the butter, sugar and nuts.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Walnuts or Pecans, coarsely chopped
Additional butter, as needed to grease the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 325°F. For the original batch, grease an 8×8-inch square pan with the separate additional butter. Melt all the measured butter over low heat in a saucepan and stir in all the cocoa until smooth. Remove from the heat and cool for about 5 minutes, until warm rather than hot; transfer to a bowl large enough for the complete mixture.
Add eggs: Whisk in all the eggs one at a time, then all the vanilla and the pinch of salt.
Fold: Combine all the sugar, flour and chopped walnuts or pecans in a separate bowl. Stir them into the cocoa mixture just until no dry flour remains.

Bake: Spread all the batter evenly in the prepared pan. Begin checking at 30 minutes; the original batch usually needs 30–35 minutes. The center should be set and fudgy, without a liquid wobble, and a toothpick should carry moist crumbs rather than wet batter. A chocolate smear can differ from raw batter; check another nearby spot if uncertain.
Cool: Cool completely in the pan before cutting into the listed portions. Chill after cooling if you prefer a firmer slice.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, rich, comfort-food, entertaining, kid-friendly, bake

recipes.name: Keto Egg Muffins
recipes.description: Use ready-to-eat air-dried Spanish chorizo or salami, not raw sausage. Finely diced meat and scallions distribute their flavor through the eggs, while pesto is whisked into the base.
recipeIngredient: 5 oz ready-to-eat air-dried Spanish chorizo or salami, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Grease standard muffin cups generously with the listed butter. The original batch uses about 12 cups; prepare more or fewer standard cups for different quantities, keeping the same fill depth. Use chorizo or salami labeled ready to eat, not a raw fresh sausage.
The Base: Divide the diced ready-to-eat chorizo or salami and scallions evenly among the prepared cups.
The Eggs: Whisk eggs with all the pesto and the salt and black pepper until blended without separate white streaks. No thick foam is needed.
Fold: Stir three-quarters of the shredded cheddar into the egg mixture; save one-quarter for topping.

Fill: Divide the egg mixture among the cups with about one-quarter headroom, stirring gently between pours to redistribute cheese. Sprinkle the reserved quarter of the cheese over the tops. Add extra cups if needed rather than overfilling.

Bake: Bake for about 15–20 minutes as a first range, until the centers are set with no liquid egg and reach 165 °F / 74 °C. Cup size and fill depth change the clock; check without touching the metal tin and continue baking if needed.
Serve: Let stand in the tin 5 minutes before loosening and removing. Refrigerate leftovers promptly, use within 3–4 days and reheat centers to 165 °F / 74 °C.

recipes.name: Key Lime Pie Ice Cream
recipes.description: This frozen dessert mimics the exact flavor profile of our Key Lime Pie. The secret to a smooth, professional churn is the condensed milk: the sugar and fats act as a powerful stabilizer, preventing the formation of large ice crystals and ensuring a silky texture.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (14 oz) Fat-free Sweetened Condensed Milk
1/2 cup Fresh Key Lime Juice (Nellie & Joe’s is the Kitchen Standard)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a large bowl, whisk together the condensed milk, key lime juice, 2% milk, cream, and salt until perfectly smooth.
The Churn: Pour the mixture into your ice cream maker. Churn according to the manufacturer's instructions (usually 20-25 minutes).
The Crunch: During the last 2 minutes of churning, add 1/3 cup of the coarsely crushed graham crackers.
The Finish: Transfer the soft-serve consistency ice cream to a chilled, freezer-safe container. Cover and freeze for at least 4 hours (ideally overnight) to firm up.
Serve: Scoop into bowls. Top with the remaining reserved graham cracker crumbs and a fresh lime wedge for the mandatory Acid Balance.

recipes.name: Key Lime Pie with Lime Zest
recipes.description: Lime zest gives this version a more aromatic filling. Bake the crumb crust before filling it, then check the custard with a thermometer; lime juice thickening alone does not cook the eggs.
recipeIngredient: 11 graham crackers or 1 1/4 cups crumbs (approximate volume)
5 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted and cooled

recipeInstructions.text: Mix filling: If using fresh limes, wash and dry them before zesting or squeezing, then measure the juice and zest. Whisk all condensed milk, lime juice, lime zest, egg yolks and filling salt together. Set aside while preparing the crust; refrigerate if preparation is delayed.

Make crust: Heat the oven to 350°F. Process the chosen graham-cracker supply to fine crumbs. Add all the crust sugar and crust salt, then pulse in all melted, cooled butter until the mixture resembles wet sand. The listed cracker count and crumb volume are alternatives, not two separate supplies.

Bake crust: Press all crumb mixture evenly into the bottom and sides of a 9-inch pie dish for the original batch. Bake about 10–12 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Cool briefly. Use separate original-size pies for multiples or appropriate smaller dishes for a reduced batch, with earlier checks; do not force extra filling into the same shell.

Bake filling: Give the entire filling a final whisk and pour it into the crust. Reduce the oven to 325°F and bake about 15–17 minutes for the original pie, until set around the edges with slight movement in the center. Check for 160°F /71°C in the filling and continue gently if needed. A colder filling or different dish can take longer.
Chill: Cool briefly on a rack, then refrigerate within 2 hours after baking, or 1 hour above 90°F /32°C. Chill at least 3 hours or overnight until fully cold and set through the center.
Finish: Just before serving, whip all the heavy cream with clean utensils to soft peaks and spread it over the chilled pie. Keep refrigerated until serving.

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Key Lime Pie
recipes.description: Whisk the yolks into condensed milk, then add lime juice for a smooth, tart filling. Lime juice thickens the mixture, but acidity does not replace cooking the eggs.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup + 2 tbsp Fresh Key Lime Juice

recipeInstructions.text: The Crust: Preheat oven to 350°F. Stir together crumbs, sugar, and melted butter until it looks like wet sand. Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 9-inch glass pie plate with about 4 cups capacity. Bake for 10 minutes. Let cool.
The Emulsion: In a large bowl, whisk the condensed milk and egg yolks until pale and thick.
The Bind: Slowly whisk in the key lime juice - the mixture will noticeably thicken.
Bake: Pour the filling into the cooled crust. Begin checking after 15 minutes and continue until the center reaches 160°F / 71°C, with set edges and a slight central wobble.
The Finish: Cool on a rack, then refrigerate promptly, within 2 hours of baking (1 hour above 90°F). Cover once cool and chill for at least 8 hours before slicing.
The Crown: Just before serving, whip the heavy cream and powdered sugar until stiff peaks form.
Serve: Mound the cream over the pie. Garnish with lime zest.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, holiday, bake

recipes.name: Kimchi Jjigae (Kimchi Stew)
recipes.description: Kimchi jjigae is Korean comfort food in its rawest form - kimchi is already fermented and pungent, so when you braise it with pork in stock, it becomes even more funky and complex. This is not a refined dish; it's what Korean mothers make on cold nights when they have leftover kimchi and want something warming and bold.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Kimchi, coarsely chopped (plus 2 tbsp kimchi juice)
8 oz Pork Belly or Shoulder, thinly sliced (or tofu for vegetarian)
4 oz Mushrooms, sliced (shiitake, oyster, or cremini)
2 tbsp Doenjang (Korean soybean paste, optional but recommended)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Kimchi Quality: Use kimchi that's at least a few days old - the older and funkier the better. Store-bought kimchi is fine; homemade is better.

Pork Options: Pork belly is traditional because it becomes tender and adds richness. But pork shoulder, beef, or tofu all work.

Heat Level: Gochugaru and gochujang can be intense. Start with the amounts listed and taste before adding more. You can always add heat; you can't take it out.

Doenjang Note: Doenjang (soybean paste) adds deep umami and is traditional but optional. If using, dissolve it in a bit of stock before adding to avoid lumps.

Make-Ahead: Kimchi jjigae tastes better the next day as flavors deepen. Store in the refrigerator for up to 4 days and reheat gently.

itemListElement.text: Prepare Ingredients: Chop the kimchi into roughly 1-inch pieces, reserving 2 tbsp of the brine. Slice the pork belly thinly (it will cook fast). Slice the onion and mushrooms. Mince the garlic.
Heat the Pan: Place a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add 1 tbsp vegetable oil and let it get hot.

Cook the Pork: Add the sliced pork and let it sit for 1-2 minutes without stirring to develop color. Stir and cook another 1-2 minutes until the pork is mostly opaque. Don't fully cook it - it will finish cooking in the braise.
Add Aromatics: Add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the sliced onion and mushrooms, cooking for 2 minutes until they begin to soften.

Build the Flavor Base: Add the gochugaru and gochujang, stirring quickly so they coat the vegetables and heat in the hot pan (about 30 seconds). This blooms the chili flavors. If using doenjang, add it now.
Add Kimchi: Add the chopped kimchi and stir everything together. Cook for 2 minutes so the kimchi heats through and releases its pungent aroma.

Braise: Add the stock and kimchi brine, stirring well. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Once simmering, reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 12-15 minutes so the flavors meld and the pork becomes tender. The liquid should reduce slightly and taste deeply savory and spicy.

Taste and Season: Taste carefully. Add fish sauce for more umami, sugar to balance heat and salt, or gochugaru if you want more spice. The balance should feel bold but balanced - no single flavor should overwhelm.
Finish: Drizzle with 1 tbsp sesame oil. Remove from heat.
Serve: Ladle into individual bowls over warm rice. Garnish with chopped green onions and sesame seeds. Serve with kimchi on the side and extra rice.

recipes.keywords: Korean, spicy, savory, umami, complex, weeknight, comfort-food, entertaining, simmer, braise

recipes.name: Gochujang-Glazed Oven Wings
recipes.description: Rack-roasted wings with a thin gochujang, honey and sesame glaze added just before serving.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) chicken wing drumettes and flats, fully thawed, tips excluded
1 tbsp aluminum-free baking powder, not baking soda
2 tsp neutral oil, for lightly greasing the racks

recipeInstructions.text: Dry and season: Pat fully thawed drumettes and flats dry. Lightly oil two oven-safe racks and set them over rimmed trays. Toss wings thoroughly with the baking powder and salt so there are no concentrated powder patches.

Refrigerate to dry: Arrange in a single spaced layer on the racks. Refrigerate uncovered for 8–24 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, on a low shelf with the trays containing drips. Include this time within the usual 1–2-day refrigerated raw-poultry storage window.

Roast and check: During the last 15 minutes of refrigerated drying, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Roast about 25 minutes, then turn wings and swap tray positions. Roast another 20–30 minutes, checking until skin is browned and several large pieces reach at least 165°F / 74°C away from bone. Around 175°F / 79°C is a useful tenderness target for wings. Remove smaller finished pieces earlier if necessary.

Make glaze: During roasting, combine gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar, water, garlic and ginger in a small saucepan. Simmer gently about 3–4 minutes, stirring, until garlic smells mellow and the glaze flows from a spoon. Turn off heat and stir in sesame oil. Keep warm; do not reduce to a stiff paste.

Coat at service: Put cooked wings in a clean bowl and toss with about two-thirds of the glaze. Add more only if needed for a thin coating; reserve the rest in a separate serving bowl. Do not broil the honey-coated wings or coat them repeatedly for a long hold.

Serve: Finish with scallions, sesame seeds and optional measured gochugaru. Divide into four main portions with separately prepared rice and cucumbers, or offer eight smaller appetizer portions. The 1.35 kg weight includes bones, not that much edible meat.

recipes.keywords: Korean-American, savory, sweet, spicy, umami, entertaining, game-day, roast, simmer

recipes.name: Sukju Namul
recipes.description: Sukju namul pairs tender mung bean sprouts with sesame oil, garlic and scallion. Drain gently rather than compressing the sprouts into a dry mass.
recipeIngredient: 350 g fresh mung bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
1 tsp fine sea salt, for cooking water
1/2 tsp fine sea salt, for seasoning, added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Bring the measured water and cooking salt to a boil. Set out a clean colander and prepare the scallion, garlic and sesame seasoning.

Cook thoroughly: Add the rinsed sprouts and let the water return to a boil. Start checking after 1–2 minutes, but continue until the sprouts are steaming hot throughout and above 165°F / 74°C, following any longer package instructions. Check the sprouts themselves with a food thermometer; boiling water alone is not the measurement. Do not stop merely to preserve a raw crunch. Use a larger pot or batches if the water stops boiling for a prolonged period.
Cool: Drain with clean equipment, then cool under cold running water or in a clean bowl of fresh cold water. Do not reuse the bowl that held unwashed sprouts without washing it.
Drain gently: Let water drain away, then lightly squeeze small handfuls to remove excess moisture without crushing the stems.
Season: Combine scallion, garlic, sesame oil and part of the seasoning salt. Gently toss with the sprouts and toasted sesame seeds. Taste before adding more of the remaining salt.

Serve or chill: Divide into four small sides or refrigerate promptly. People at higher risk of foodborne illness should avoid raw or lightly cooked sprouts; a short blanch alone does not meet that advice.

recipes.keywords: Korean, savory, weeknight, light-and-fresh, boil

citation.name: Adapted from Sue Pressey, My Korean Kitchen

recipes.name: Oi Muchim (Korean Cucumber Salad)
recipes.description: Sliced cucumbers tossed with gochugaru, garlic, sesame, and a sharp-sweet dressing. A brief salt-and-drain step limits dilution.
recipeIngredient: 600 g English or Persian cucumbers, ends trimmed
1 tbsp gochugaru (Korean red chile flakes), or less to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Slice: Wash cucumbers and cut into rounds about 1/4 inch thick. If an English cucumber is very wide, halve it lengthwise first and slice into half-moons.

Salt and drain: Toss with the measured salt in a colander over a bowl. Leave for 20 minutes, tossing once halfway through. Discard the drained liquid and gently blot the slices with a clean towel; do not wring them dry. Taste a slice: if unusually salty, rinse briefly, drain, and blot again.
Mix dressing: During the wait, combine gochugaru, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, and garlic in a serving bowl. Stir until the sugar dissolves.

Toss and serve: Add drained cucumbers, scallions, and sesame seeds. Toss gently and serve promptly. If using as a noodle-salad topping, lift portions out with a slotted spoon so excess dressing does not flood the noodles.

recipes.keywords: Korean, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, light-and-fresh, no-cook, toss

recipes.name: Korean Style Tacos
recipes.description: These Korean-Mexican tacos pair a gochujang sauce with cooked pulled pork or shredded chicken and tortillas. Roy Choi created the Kogi sauce for Steamy Kitchen’s smoky-pork taco adaptation; the chilled cucumber pickle supplies a cool, tangy contrast.
recipeIngredient: 1 large English cucumber, washed and sliced paper-thin
1/2 tsp fresh chili pepper, washed and finely minced
1 lb cooked [Pulled Pork](/mise/recipes/pulled-pork) or cooked shredded chicken, fully cooked before starting; chilled leftovers must be handled within their storage limit
scallions, as wanted for topping, washed and sliced

recipeInstructions.text: Start the cucumber pickle: Toss large English cucumber, rice vinegar, sugar, fresh chili pepper, and sea salt in a covered food-safe container. Refrigerate at 40°F or below for about 1 hour before assembly. Up to about 3 hours is the shorter texture plan; a longer refrigerated hold softens the cucumber rather than creating a precise safety deadline.

Mix the full sauce: Whisk gochujang, granulated sugar, soy sauce, rice vinegar, and toasted sesame oil until the sugar dissolves and the mixture is smooth. Keep this whole sauce supply separate from the cucumber’s vinegar, sugar and chili.

Heat the already cooked meat: Use cooked Pulled Pork or cooked shredded chicken. Reheat chilled meat in a skillet over heat adjusted to warm it evenly without burning, stirring and checking until it reaches 165°F throughout. Do not depend on a 3–4-minute clock or crispy edges to establish its temperature. Keep all the meat’s cooking juices and fat that came with the listed supply. Extra loads extend time; raw pork or chicken needs its separate complete cooking process before this recipe begins.

Coat with the sauce: Take the hot meat off direct high heat and toss it with the entire prepared Kogi sauce until evenly coated. The separate seared quarter-cup sauce variation below uses a different application sequence.

Warm the tortillas: Warm corn tortillas over a controlled open flame or in a dry pan, turning until hot and flexible with charred spots if wanted. Work in loads without multiplying heat or promising the same elapsed time.

Fill and finish: Divide all coated meat among the measured tortillas. Top with chilled cucumber pickle and scallions, then serve promptly. Lift the cucumber with a clean utensil, allowing excess pickle liquid to drain back into its container rather than soaking every tortilla.

recipes.keywords: Korean, Mexican, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, no-cook, saute, toast

recipes.name: Lamb Keema Matar
recipes.description: Keema matar pairs spiced ground lamb with sweet peas. Brown the lamb in its own rendered fat, soften the onion in that same pan and add the garam masala near the finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb ground lamb, raw, fresh or fully thawed
1 large yellow onion, peeled and finely diced
1/4 cup water, approximately, to keep the mixture saucy
fresh cilantro, as wanted for finishing, washed and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Brown the lamb: Heat a large skillet and use ground lamb, breaking it into small pieces as its fat renders. Cook until browned, adjusting heat to avoid blackened patches. Keep the full rendered fat in the pan. Use a vessel with room to stir the listed batch; for more meat use extra pans or loads and divide every ingredient proportionally.

Soften the onion: Have large yellow onion, fresh ginger, and fresh garlic ready. Add the diced onion to the lamb pan and cook about 5 minutes as a first check until it softens, stirring and lowering heat if it catches. Stir in all the ginger and garlic and sauté 30–45 seconds until fragrant without scorching.

Add spices and tomato paste: Stir in cumin seeds, turmeric, Kashmiri chili powder, and tomato paste and cook about 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant without burning. The garam masala remains for the finish.

Cook the peas and finish the lamb: Add frozen peas and water, cover and simmer gently, beginning checks around 5 minutes. Stir to distribute heat and continue until peas are hot and tender, following any package cooking directions, and the ground-lamb mixture reaches 160°F in several places with a food thermometer. A brown exterior and the covered clock do not establish the meat endpoint.
Finish the seasoning: Once the lamb is fully cooked, stir in garam masala, lemon, and fresh cilantro, using all the juice from the measured lemon, and taste.
Serve: Serve with separately prepared warm Naan or Basmati Rice. Those components have their own amounts and preparation clocks; four portions is the original planning yield.

recipes.keywords: Indian, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, rich, comfort-food, weeknight, sear, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Lavender London Fog Cocktail
recipes.description: A chilled Earl Grey and gin cocktail with oat milk, vanilla and a restrained hint of lavender, shaken and served in a coupe.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz (60 mL) Earl Grey concentrate, thoroughly chilled (from the batch below)
1/2 oz (15 mL) plain barista-style oat milk, chilled and shaken in its carton; preferably unsweetened
1/2 oz (15 mL) lavender–vanilla syrup, chilled (from the batch below)
Solid ice cubes, enough to fill the shaker
4 g loose Earl Grey black tea
120 mL water at 95°C / 203°F, plus enough to restore the strained tea to 120 mL

recipeInstructions.text: Brew the concentrate: Steep the 4 g Earl Grey tea in 120 mL water at 95°C / 203°F for 4 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, then add enough water to bring the strained tea back to 120 mL. This makes two 60 mL cocktail portions.

Make the syrup: Stir the 60 g sugar into 60 g hot water until dissolved. Off the heat, add the culinary lavender and steep for 3 minutes. Strain finely, then stir in the vanilla extract. Expect approximately 90–100 mL syrup, enough for about six cocktails after straining losses.
Chill: Transfer the tea and syrup to separate clean containers and refrigerate until thoroughly cold, allowing about 1 hour, or longer as needed. Chill a 7 oz coupe glass before mixing.

Measure one cocktail: Shake the oat milk carton. Add 1 1/2 oz (45 mL) gin, 2 oz (60 mL) cold tea concentrate, 1/2 oz (15 mL) oat milk and 1/2 oz (15 mL) cold syrup to the shaker. The remaining tea and syrup are for additional cocktails; do not add the whole batches.

Shake and strain: Fill the shaker with solid ice cubes and shake firmly for 10–12 seconds, until the shaker is very cold and often frosted. Strain through both the cocktail strainer and a fine-mesh strainer into the chilled coupe. Look for a lightly cloudy tea-beige drink with fine bubbles on the surface; the amount of foam depends on the oat milk.
Serve: Serve immediately, without ice or garnish. Taste before increasing lavender in a future syrup batch; the bergamot should remain clear.

recipes.keywords: aromatic, sweet, herbaceous, date-night, entertaining, infuse, mix
