recipes.name: Lemon Basil Shrimp Risotto
recipes.description: Add warm broth gradually and stir frequently, keeping the rice at a gentle simmer. Judge the finish by a tender center with a slight bite and a loose, creamy consistency.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb U10 shrimp (under 10 per pound), raw, peeled and deveined; thawed if frozen
5–6 cups chicken or vegetable broth, heated; add gradually only as needed
fresh basil, extra for serving, rinsed, optional
hot water, only if needed for grain hydration or loosening

recipeInstructions.text: Cook shrimp: Use U10 shrimp (under 10 per pound) and unsalted butter for this stage. Melt all the butter over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp in a single layer, sharing the butter between batches if needed, until the thickest flesh is firm, pearly and opaque through the center. Transfer to a clean plate; chop into bite-sized pieces on a clean board if desired.
Soften onion: In the same pan add large onion; cook around 2–3 minutes until translucent, adjusting heat rather than letting the remaining butter burn.
Add garlic: Add garlic cloves and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
Coat the rice: Add Arborio rice and stir for about 2 minutes, until grain edges look translucent, without browning them darkly.
Add wine: Pour in dry white wine and stir until mostly absorbed.

Hydrate gently: Use chicken or vegetable broth and hot water for this stage. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring frequently and adding another when the previous is mostly absorbed. Begin tasting around 18–22 minutes; keep cooking until the center is tender with a slight bite. Use only as much broth as needed; if it runs out while rice remains firm, continue with a little hot water. Leave room for finishing additions.

Finish the rice: Use lemon, heavy cream, freshly grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper for this stage. Stir in the full heavy cream and Parmesan, all the lemon zest, and the lemon juice to taste. Use the listed salt and pepper allowances. Loosen stiff rice with a little remaining hot broth or water as needed; keep any unused lemon juice in a clean container separately rather than assuming every lemon produces the same amount.

Return the shrimp: Use fresh basil leaves for this stage. Fold in all the cooked shrimp and basil; warm briefly, starting around 1 minute and checking that the shrimp are warm throughout. Do not extend the rice simmer with shrimp already in it.

Serve: Use fresh basil (if using) for this stage. Use the optional extra basil, divide among the listed portions and serve immediately. Rice that needs more liquid/time or extra shrimp batches extends the approximate 50-minute schedule.

recipes.name: Lemon Broccoli Tortellini
recipes.description: Cheese tortellini with roasted broccoli, wilted spinach and a lemon-butter finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb refrigerated or frozen cheese tortellini
1 1/2 lb fresh broccoli, cut into similar bite-sized florets, thick stems sliced thinner
4 cloves garlic, minced, divided equally between broccoli and sauce
1 large lemon, zested before juicing, juice divided between broccoli and finish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1/2 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Two Peas & Their Pod’s Lemon Broccoli Tortellini.

itemListElement.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Cut broccoli into similar bite-sized florets and slice thick stems thinner. Mince shallot and garlic, zest then juice the lemon, and set a large pot of water on to boil.

Roast broccoli: Toss broccoli with olive oil, half the garlic and half the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Spread on a rimmed half-sheet pan in one layer, using a second tray if crowded. Keep garlic among the florets rather than scattered on bare metal. Roast 20–25 minutes, turning once, until stems are tender and edges browned. Remove any pieces that finish early.

Start the sauce: Near the end of roasting, melt butter in a large deep skillet over medium-low. Soften shallot for about 3–5 minutes. Add the remaining garlic and pepper flakes for 30–45 seconds, then spinach. Turn gently for about 2 minutes until wilted. Lower heat or turn it off while waiting for pasta.

Cook tortellini: Time this stage by the package so it finishes near the vegetables. Season the boiling water moderately, add tortellini and cook as directed, avoiding a violent boil. Meet any specified filling temperature. Reserve the listed amount of cooking water before draining.

Combine gently: Add drained tortellini and broccoli to the spinach skillet. Add zest and about half the reserved water. Fold over low heat just until hot, then remove from the burner. Add Parmesan gradually and half of the remaining lemon juice. Fold gently, adding further water only until lightly coated. Taste before adding the rest of the lemon juice, salt or pepper. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Lemon Chicken Orzo Soup
recipes.description: Diced chicken and small pasta in a lightly thickened vegetable broth, finished with lemon zest, juice and parsley.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 3/4-inch pieces
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) additional chicken broth, only as needed to loosen
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
3 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste
Water, only for the optional separate-orzo make-ahead method, per pasta package

recipeInstructions.text: Soften vegetables: Heat butter and oil in a 5-quart pot over medium heat. Add onion, small carrot and celery pieces, and pepper. Cook about 7–9 minutes, stirring, until the vegetables soften; deep browning is not required.

Disperse flour: Add garlic and thyme and stir about 30 seconds. Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute. Add the initial 6 cups broth gradually, stirring to prevent flour clumps and loosen any brown residue.
Heat and add chicken: Bring to a steady simmer. Add diced chicken, stir to separate pieces, and return to a simmer. Keep the extra broth separate for later adjustment.

Cook orzo and check: Add orzo and simmer gently about 10–12 minutes, stirring across the bottom frequently. Check that pasta is just tender and several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Extend if needed, lifting cooked chicken out briefly if the pasta needs significantly longer.

Set consistency and season: Add additional broth in small amounts if needed for a spoonable soup and return to a gentle simmer. Taste and add salt gradually only if needed. Turn off heat, add parsley, lemon zest and half the juice, then taste before adding the remainder.
Serve: Divide among six bowls and serve promptly. For making ahead, cook the orzo separately in boiling water according to its package and add it to each serving; keep it separate from stored soup.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, savory, acidic, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Lemon-Garlic Broccolini
recipes.description: Check broccolini at the thicker stems, where tenderness takes longer than the leaves suggest. Keep sliced garlic from darkening while you toss the greens.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Wash and dry the broccolini and lemon. Trim dry stalk ends and split unusually thick stems lengthwise so the pieces cook more evenly. Zest all the listed lemon and reserve all the zest. Set aside half of the listed lemon amount for squeezing and cut the other half into serving wedges.

Heat: Heat all the measured olive oil in enough roomy skillets for uncrowded cooking over medium heat. Divide the same oil, garlic and flakes across vessels or rounds. Add sliced garlic and all red-pepper flakes and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant; do not let garlic blacken.

Cook broccolini: Add all broccolini and toss about 3–4 minutes as an initial check. Continue until thick stems yield to a fork but retain some bite, adjusting heat down if garlic darkens. Thick stems can take longer. Season with all the measured kosher salt and the listed unmeasured black pepper.

Finish with juice: Remove from heat and squeeze the reserved half of the listed lemon amount over the whole batch; toss. This is half the listed lemon amount, not an additional half beyond the serving wedges.
Serve: Transfer to a serving dish, add all reserved zest and serve promptly with the wedges from the other half.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, herbaceous, bright, weeknight, quick-lunch, saute

recipes.name: Lemon and Herb Instant Couscous
recipes.description: Fine instant couscous hydrated off heat and finished with lemon, olive oil, parsley and mint.
recipeIngredient: 250 g plain instant couscous; not pearl couscous
420 ml low-sodium vegetable or chicken broth, adjusted to the chosen package instructions
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, divided and partly added to taste
1/4 tsp fine salt, added only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and heat: Chop parsley and mint, grate lemon zest and measure the juice. Check the package’s liquid guidance for the measured couscous quantity; use the listed broth amount for the starting formula. Bring the broth to a full boil in a 2-quart saucepan.
Hydrate off heat: Remove from heat, stir in couscous, and cover immediately. Let stand about 5 minutes, or the package’s stated time. Keep the lid on during this initial rest.

Check and fluff: Uncover and taste a grain. It should be tender without a dry center and there should be no free liquid. If still dry, use the small hot-water correction in troubleshooting. Fluff with a fork, lifting rather than pressing.

Dress: Fold in olive oil, half the measured lemon juice, zest and pepper. Let excess steam escape for a minute, then fold in parsley and mint. Taste before adding the remaining lemon juice and measured salt; broth and optional feta may already supply enough salt.
Serve: Divide into four sides and add the optional feta. Pair with a main and vegetables; the couscous is the starch component of the plate.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean-inspired, herbaceous, acidic, savory, weeknight, meal-prep, entertaining, boil, steam

recipes.name: Lemon Herb Quinoa
recipes.description: Tender quinoa with lemon, olive oil, parsley, mint and dill. A covered rest separates cooking from dressing, so the grains stay light and the herbs taste fresh.
recipeIngredient: 2.5 cups water or low-sodium vegetable broth, plus hot water as needed if the grains remain firm

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse the dry quinoa in a fine-mesh strainer under cool running water for about 30 seconds, then shake and drain thoroughly. Follow any specific preparation directions on the package.

Toast, if wanted: Put the drained quinoa in a saucepan over medium heat. Stir until excess surface water has evaporated and the grains smell lightly nutty, about 2 minutes or a little longer if still wet. Skip this step for a milder flavor.

Simmer and check: Add the measured water or broth and salt. Bring to a boil, cover tightly and lower the heat to a gentle simmer. Cook about 15 minutes without repeatedly lifting the lid. Taste a grain and check for pooled liquid; the grain should be tender without a hard center. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered. If firm with liquid remaining, continue simmering without adding more.
Rest: When the grain is tender and free liquid has absorbed, remove from heat and leave covered for 5 minutes.

Dress: Fluff gently with a fork. Add olive oil and measured lemon juice, then fold in zest, parsley, mint, dill and black pepper. Taste before adding any more salt. Divide into four generous side portions; serve warm, or cool promptly for a chilled serving.

recipes.keywords: American, Mediterranean, acidic, herbaceous, fresh, savory, weeknight, meal-prep, light-and-fresh, boil, simmer

recipes.name: Lemon-Miso Tofu with Broccoli
recipes.description: Miso-glazed tofu is a Japanese izakaya staple adapted for weeknight cooking - the miso-lemon-maple glaze hits all five taste receptors at once (salt, sweet, acid, umami, and a touch of bitter from the char). The key is pressing the tofu bone-dry and dredging in cornstarch before frying - this creates the shatteringly crisp shell that holds the glaze without going soggy.
recipeIngredient: 14 oz Extra-firm Tofu, pressed dry and cubed
1 lb Fresh Broccoli, cut into small florets

recipeInstructions.text: The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk miso, lemon juice, maple syrup, 1 tbsp cornstarch, and hot water until smooth.
The Crunch: Toss dry tofu cubes in 1/3 cup cornstarch, salt, and pepper until "dusty."
Sear Tofu: Heat 3 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Fry tofu for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and very crisp. Remove to a plate.
Sear Veg: In the same pan, sauté broccoli for 6-7 minutes until tender and charred at the edges. Remove and set aside.
The Glaze: Wipe the pan. Add sesame oil, garlic, and ginger; sauté for 30 seconds. Pour in the miso-lemon mixture. Simmer for 3 minutes until thick and glossy.
Bind: Return tofu and broccoli to the pan. Toss vigorously for 30 seconds to coat.
Serve: Garnish with scallions and serve hot over rice.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, fry, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Lemon Pepper Oven Wings
recipes.description: Dry-roasted wings tossed lightly with lemon-zest butter, coarse pepper and a measured splash of juice.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg (3 lb) chicken wing drumettes and flats, fully thawed, tips excluded
1 tbsp aluminum-free baking powder, not baking soda
2 tsp neutral oil, for lightly greasing the racks
1 tbsp finely grated lemon zest, yellow part only
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Pat thawed wings dry. Lightly oil two oven-safe racks and place over rimmed trays. Toss wings evenly with baking powder and the wings' measured salt; avoid clumps. Spread them out with space between pieces.

Dry in the refrigerator: Refrigerate uncovered for 8–24 hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, on a low shelf with trays catching any drips. Count this within the 1–2-day raw-poultry refrigerated storage window.

Roast: During the last 15 minutes of refrigerated drying, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Roast about 25 minutes, turn wings and exchange tray positions, then roast another 20–30 minutes. Check several large pieces away from bone: all need at least 165°F / 74°C, with about 175°F / 79°C a useful tenderness target. Skin should be browned and rendered. Remove smaller done pieces if needed while larger ones finish.

Warm the butter: Near the end of roasting, melt butter gently in a small saucepan over low heat. Remove from heat and stir in zest, juice, pepper and garlic powder. Taste and add the butter's optional salt only if needed. Whisk before using; a little separation is normal.

Toss lightly: Transfer cooked wings to a clean bowl. Add about two-thirds of the warm butter mixture and toss. Add the rest only if needed for an even light coating, or serve it separately. Keep the wings uncovered and serve promptly rather than holding them in a pool of butter.

Finish: Scatter with the measured parsley and serve optional lemon wedges. Divide into four main portions with separately prepared sides, or eight smaller appetizer portions. Bones are included in the purchase weight.

recipes.name: Lemon Ricotta Pasta
recipes.description: A generous olive-oil and ricotta sauce with Pecorino, lemon and basil, tossed with hot pasta in a bowl.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 cup extra-virgin olive oil, including any finishing drizzle
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Delish’s Lemon Ricotta Pasta.

itemListElement.text: Start water and sauce: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and season moderately with salt; the Pecorino will also season the dish. Zest then juice the lemon. If you want a finishing drizzle, set aside a little of the measured oil first. In a large heatproof bowl, whisk ricotta, the remaining oil, Pecorino, zest, half the lemon juice and pepper flakes.

Cook to tenderness: Add pasta and stir as it softens. Follow package timing, tasting a strand near the end. Cook until tender with a little bite and no hard center. Before draining, scoop out the listed cooking-water reserve. Drain without rinsing.
Loosen the sauce: Whisk about one-quarter of the reserved water into the ricotta mixture. Add more a little at a time only if it is still too stiff to fold through the pasta.

Toss and finish: Add hot pasta to the bowl and toss thoroughly, adding further warm cooking water in small splashes until coated and slightly loose. Fold in basil and black pepper. Taste a complete bite, then add remaining lemon juice and salt only as needed. Use any oil deliberately reserved for finishing and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Lemony Broccoli Pasta
recipes.description: Spaghetti with broccoli and peas, coated in olive oil, Parmesan and fresh lemon.
recipeIngredient: 5 cups fresh broccoli florets, cut into small bite-sized pieces, thick stems sliced thinner
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from The Kitchn’s Lemony Broccoli Pasta.

itemListElement.text: Prepare: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cut broccoli into small bite-sized florets and slice thick stems thinner. Zest and juice the lemon, grate Parmesan and measure the oil. Season the boiling water moderately with salt.

Cook pasta and broccoli: Add spaghetti and stir as it softens. Follow package timing. Add broccoli when about 3–5 minutes remain, return to a gentle boil and check both for tenderness. If pasta is ready first, lift it out with tongs and let broccoli finish. Before draining, reserve the listed cooking water; drain without rinsing.

Cook peas and prepare the finish: While pasta cooks, cook peas according to package directions and drain. In a large heatproof serving bowl, combine olive oil, lemon zest and half the lemon juice. Have Parmesan and warm cooking water ready.

Toss away from heat: Add hot spaghetti, broccoli and cooked peas to the bowl. Sprinkle in Parmesan in several additions while tossing, adding about one-quarter of the reserved water initially and more in small splashes only as needed. Stop when everything is coated and moist, not swimming in water.
Season and serve: Add black pepper and taste a complete bite. Add the remaining lemon juice and salt only as needed, then divide into the intended portions and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Lime & Honey Glazed Salmon
recipes.description: Lime-honey salmon with warm black beans, charred corn and peppers over fresh spinach, finished with cilantro and toasted pepitas.
recipeIngredient: 2.25 lb (about 1,020 g) skinless, boneless salmon, cut into seven similar portions
1 1/2 tsp mild chili powder blend, without added salt
1 tsp fine salt, divided, plus up to 1/4 tsp more for the salad after tasting
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the glaze
1 tsp olive oil, for the foil
5 medium ears fresh sweet corn, husked and kernels cut off; about 600 g kernels
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the skillet
1 medium red bell pepper, cored, seeded and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, optional, for the salad
2 cans (15 oz each) black beans, rinsed and well drained; about 500 g drained
1 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the salad, plus up to 1 tbsp more after tasting
8 loosely packed cups baby spinach, washed and dried; about 240 g
1 avocado, diced just before serving, optional
1 lime, cut into eight wedges for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare everything and heat the oven: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a middle rack and a second rack positioned so the fish surface will sit 7–9 inches below the broiler. Cut corn from the cobs, chop onion, pepper, garlic and cilantro, and rinse and drain beans. Prepare the spinach and measure the pepitas. Line the metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit. Pat salmon dry, check for pin bones and divide into seven similar portions. Season with chili powder, smoked paprika, 1/2 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and all the black pepper. Keep chilled while charring corn. Whisk honey with the 2 tbsp glaze lime juice in a clean bowl; set aside the separate salad juice and serving wedges. Wash raw-fish tools and hands before returning to vegetables.

Char corn in two batches: Heat the deep, well-seasoned skillet over medium-high heat for about 2–3 minutes. Add half the dry corn without oil and spread into a shallow layer. Let it sit briefly, then stir occasionally for about 5–7 minutes, until juicy and tender with scattered browned patches. Lower heat if it starts blackening. Transfer to a large bowl. Let the pan recover its heat and repeat with the remaining corn; remove any burnt loose residue afterward.

Start baking the fish: Arrange salmon on the prepared pan with about an inch between portions. Bake on the middle rack while making the salad in the next two steps. Start checking the fish after 8 minutes; allow roughly 10–15 minutes for the specified thickness, aiming for about 135–140°F / 57–60°C before the glaze finish. This is an intermediate temperature, not the serving endpoint. If ready before the salad, remove the pan briefly to a heatproof surface.

Soften the aromatics: Reduce skillet heat to medium and add the tablespoon of olive oil, onion, bell pepper and remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook, stirring, about 6–8 minutes until the onion softens and pepper is tender with a little bite. Add garlic, the remaining 1 tsp cumin and optional red pepper flakes; stir 30–45 seconds until fragrant.

Warm and finish the salad: Fold the beans and all the corn into the skillet. Cook over medium heat for about 4–6 minutes, turning gently, until hot throughout. Remove from heat and fold in cilantro and the first tablespoon of salad lime juice. Taste and add some or all of the reserved lime and extra salt if wanted. Cover loosely and turn off the skillet before broiling.

Glaze and watch the broiler: Remove salmon from the oven if it is still inside and switch to high broil, allowing the element to heat according to the oven's instructions. Spread all the honey-lime mixture over the seven fillets in an even coating, without deliberately pooling it on the foil. Broil with the fish surface 7–9 inches below the heat for about 1–3 minutes, watching continuously; rotate the pan if needed. The glaze should bubble and develop golden patches without turning black. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and finish to 145°F / 63°C, with flesh that flakes under gentle pressure. If the glaze colors first, use the gentler oven finish in troubleshooting. Use clean utensils for serving and discard glaze left in the brushing bowl; it is not a cold sauce.

Serve seven complete portions: Divide all the spinach among seven wide bowls, then divide the warm bean-and-corn salad over it. Add one fillet per bowl. Dice the optional avocado and divide it among the bowls, then scatter the pepitas. Offer lime wedges for squeezing to taste. The spinach remains a fresh bed, lightly softened by the warm toppings.

recipes.name: Chicken Lo Mein with Shiitake and Bok Choy
recipes.description: Springy egg noodles with chicken, shiitake and bok choy, cooked in fragrant scallion-shallot oil in two manageable pan batches, with a separate shrimp variation.
recipeIngredient: 450 g (1 lb) fresh raw lo mein egg noodles, not dried noodles or pre-cooked noodles
450 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, sliced across the grain about 1/4 inch thick
1 tsp neutral oil, for the chicken
1 tsp light soy sauce, for the chicken
1/8 tsp ground white pepper, for the chicken
1/4 cup (60 ml) low-sodium chicken broth or water
3 tbsp (45 ml) prepared strained scallion-shallot oil, divided (preferred; or shallot oil or neutral oil)
4 scallions, whites thinly sliced and greens cut into 1-inch lengths
225 g fresh shiitake caps, tough stems removed, sliced 1/4 inch thick
340 g baby bok choy, washed and thoroughly dried, stems and leaves separated
150 g mung bean sprouts, rinsed and drained
2 tsp toasted sesame oil, divided between finishing batches
1 tsp Chinkiang black vinegar or unseasoned rice vinegar, optional, divided between finishing batches
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, only as needed to loosen noodles
15 g crisp fried shallots and scallions from the oil recipe, or prepared fried shallots, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Coat the chicken and prepare the sauce: Toss chicken with its cornstarch, 1 tsp oil, 1 tsp light soy and white pepper; refrigerate while preparing everything else. Whisk the six sauce ingredients together and divide into two equal portions.

Set up the vegetables: Keep mushroom slices, bok choy stems, leaves, sprouts and scallion greens separate. Cut stems into 1/2-inch pieces and large leaves into manageable pieces. Mix garlic, ginger and scallion whites. Divide every vegetable and aromatic group, the Shaoxing wine, sesame oil and optional vinegar into two portions for the final rounds.

Prepare noodles for this product: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to a full boil. Add fresh raw noodles, separate gently and cook according to their package range, tasting early until cooked through but springy. Rinse briefly with cold water, drain thoroughly and toss with 1 tsp of the measured pan oil. Divide into two loose piles and proceed promptly; start the pan work as soon as the noodles are ready.

Cook the chicken fully in two batches: Heat the wok or deep skillet over medium-high to high as appropriate for the pan, then add 2 tsp pan oil. Spread half the chicken in a layer. Leave about 1 minute for color, then turn and stir for another 2–3 minutes or until the thickest slices reach 165°F / 74°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat with another 2 tsp oil and the remaining chicken. Keep the cooked chicken divided for the two finishing rounds.

Cook the first vegetable portion: Add 2 tsp of the remaining oil. Cook half the mushrooms 3–4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until some surfaces brown. Add half the aromatics for 20–30 seconds, then half the wine and bok choy stems. Stir-fry about 2 minutes, adding a little measured hot water if needed for the stems to soften. Add half the leaves, sprouts and scallion greens and cook another 2–3 minutes, stirring, until thoroughly hot and cooked rather than raw-crisp.

Finish the first noodle batch: Add half the noodles and one portion of sauce. Fold from the bottom for about 1–2 minutes, using a little measured hot water only if needed to separate strands. Add half the cooked chicken and toss over the heat until everything is hot and evenly coated. Turn off the heat and fold in half the sesame oil and optional vinegar. Transfer to a warm serving platter and cover loosely for the short second round.

Repeat and serve: Use the last 2 tsp pan oil and the remaining vegetables, aromatics, wine, noodles, sauce and chicken to repeat steps 5–6. Finish with the remaining sesame oil and optional vinegar. Divide both batches among five bowls and add the optional 15 g crisp fried alliums from the oil recipe or prepared fried shallots. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Omelet Muffins
recipes.description: Use cooked bacon and thawed spinach squeezed free of excess water. Divide the finely diced vegetables among the cups, then add the eggs and cheese.
recipeIngredient: 3 tbsp Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed dry

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat the oven to 350 °F. Generously spray standard muffin cups, including the sides, and set the tin on a baking sheet. Start with cooked, chopped bacon. Prepare the frozen spinach according to its package if cooking is required, cool enough to handle, squeeze dry and measure the listed spinach amount after draining. These preparations add time if they are not already done.

The Base: Divide the cooked bacon, squeezed spinach, finely diced tomato, onion and pepper among the cups. The original batch uses about 12 standard cups; different quantities need more or fewer cups at the same size and fill depth.
The Eggs: Whisk the eggs, measured kosher salt and black pepper until the whites and yolks are blended. Do not whip to a thick foam.
Assemble: Divide the eggs evenly among the filled cups, leaving about one-quarter headroom. Sprinkle all the cheddar over the tops. Use additional cups if needed rather than pouring over the rim.

Bake: Bake for about 20–25 minutes, until the centers are set and opaque with no liquid egg, and reach 165 °F / 74 °C. Check a center without touching the metal tin; surface color does not replace the temperature check.

Cool and store: Let stand 5 minutes before loosening and removing. Refrigerate promptly in shallow containers and use within 3–4 days, or freeze individually for up to 3 months for quality. Reheat the center to 165 °F / 74 °C; a fixed 45-second microwave time cannot cover chilled and frozen portions.

recipes.name: Made-In-The-Pan Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This cake is pure American efficiency - everything mixes right in the pan, no bowls to clean. The trick is understanding what each ingredient does: vinegar reacts with baking soda to create lift and crumb structure, cocoa powder needs cold water to bloom properly, and the whole formula relies on mixing order so ingredients emulsify correctly into a smooth, lump-free batter.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Apple Cider Vinegar for richness

recipeInstructions.text: The Dry Mix: Preheat oven to 325°F. In an 8x8-inch square baking dish, whisk the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking soda, and salt until uniform. Use your fingers to crush any cocoa lumps.
The Wells: Make three wells in the dry mix. Pour the oil into one, the vanilla into the second, and the vinegar into the third.
Combine: Pour the cold water over everything. Using a fork or small whisk, stir in circular motions until a smooth batter forms. Scrape the corners of the pan carefully.
Bake: Sprinkle the chocolate chips over the top. Wipe the edges of the dish with a damp towel for a clean "Kitchen Standard" look.
Cook: Bake for 28-33 minutes until a toothpick comes out with just a few moist crumbs.
Finish: Dust with confectioners' sugar once cool for the mandatory High Note visual.

recipes.name: Mandarin/Pineapple Orange Salad
recipes.description: Citrus salads are a Southern and Caribbean tradition - canned or fresh fruit with a bright dressing and sometimes nuts for crunch. The trick is draining fruit well so the salad doesn't turn watery.

recipeInstructions.text: Dissolve: In a large bowl, whisk the Orange Jello and sugar into the boiling water until no crystals remain.
Emulsify: Add the sour cream to the hot liquid. Whisk vigorously until the mixture is completely smooth and pale orange.
Texture: Fold in the crushed pineapple (with its juice) and the drained mandarin oranges.
The Finish: Pour the mixture into a glass bowl or a decorative mold.
Chill: Refrigerate for at least 4 hours (ideally overnight) until perfectly congealed and firm.
Serve: Serve chilled as a bright side dish or a light dessert.

recipes.name: Mango Cabbage Slaw
recipes.description: Thin cabbage shreds, ripe mango, bell pepper and herbs in a lime-honey dressing with a pinch of allspice. A short chilled rest softens the cabbage just enough to bend while keeping its crunch.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups green cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
2 cups red cabbage, cored and very thinly shredded
1 large ripe but firm mango, peeled and cut into matchsticks
1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and thinly sliced
3 tbsp fresh lime juice, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Core and thinly shred the cabbages, then measure them into a large bowl. Peel the mango and cut the flesh away from the pit into thin matchsticks. Prepare the bell pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions.
Whisk the dressing: Whisk the measured lime juice, oil, honey or agave, mustard, measured salt, pepper and allspice in a small bowl until well combined. Whisk again if it separates before use.
Toss gently: Add the mango, pepper, onion, cilantro and scallions to the cabbage. Pour over the dressing and lift gently from the bottom to coat everything without crushing the mango.

Rest and taste: Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes, or up to 30 minutes for softer cabbage. Toss gently and taste a forkful, adding a little extra lime or salt only if needed. Serve as six generous side portions, lifting out of any pooled liquid.

recipes.name: Mango-Rita Green Smoothie
recipes.description: A green smoothie with mango and lime is tropical and tart - the acid cuts through the sweet fruit and mild greens. The trick is using ripe mango (it should yield slightly to pressure) so the smoothie is thick and creamy without needing yogurt or ice cream.
recipeIngredient: Tiny pinch of Sea Salt (The "Trust Me" Note)

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a high-powered blender, combine the spinach, coconut water, and orange. Blend on high for 30 seconds until the greens are completely pulverized.
The Bulk: Add the frozen mango, frozen pineapple, lime juice, and the pinch of sea salt.
Process: Blend on high for 60 seconds until perfectly velvety.
Adjust: If the smoothie is too thick, add a splash more coconut water. If you want more "Snap," add extra lime juice.
Serve: Pour into two chilled glasses. Garnish with a lime slice and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Maple-Roasted Sweet Potato Wedges
recipes.description: Brown the sweet potato wedges on their cut faces before brushing on the maple syrup. The late glaze gives a sticky, sweet finish with less time to scorch; it still needs close attention during the final 8–10 minutes.
recipeIngredient: 2 lb sweet potatoes, scrubbed, skin left on and cut lengthwise into wedges about ½ inch thick
flaky sea salt, a pinch, to taste at serving

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and cut: Heat the oven to 425°F. Use a large rimmed baking sheet or enough sheets for the measured wedges; if lining, use parchment rated for this heat or suitable foil. Scrub the sweet potatoes under running water, leave the skins on and cut lengthwise into wedges about ½ inch thick, with a skin edge and flat cut faces. Dry the cut surfaces. Make wedges rather than parallel planks.

Coat and arrange: Toss sweet potatoes, olive oil, kosher salt, and black pepper in a large bowl until the wedges are evenly coated. Arrange in one layer on a flat cut face, with space between wedges. The measured oil and seasonings coat the full batch, not each sheet.

Brown the first face: Roast for 18–20 minutes. Lift a wedge to check the underside for golden browning; test a thick center for softening. If still hard, continue the unglazed roast before adding maple. The final stage should finish nearly tender wedges, rather than leave syrup to scorch while a raw center cooks.

Turn and brush: Turn the wedges onto another cut face and set out pure maple syrup and smoked paprika (if using). Brush the syrup across all the wedges, using the whole measured maple amount for the full batch. Sprinkle the optional paprika over them if using. Keep the thin glaze on the wedges rather than pouring a pool onto the empty pan.

Finish and watch the maple: Return to the oven for 8–10 minutes, checking the maple closely. Centers should be easily pierced and the glaze bubbling and browned, without blackened sugar. Remove ready wedges sooner if they darken quickly. The two stages normally total 26–30 minutes, but thicker pieces or extra sheets may need longer before glazing.
Taste and serve: Transfer to a serving dish and use flaky sea salt if needed after tasting. Serve warm; expect tender centers and browned, sticky edges rather than guaranteed fry-like crispness.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, caramelized, weeknight, comfort-food, entertaining, roast

recipes.name: Mapo Tofu
recipes.description: Sichuan peppercorns and doubanjiang give mapo tofu its numbing, spicy character. This version uses medium-firm tofu, briefly warmed in salted water and then handled gently in the pork sauce.
recipeIngredient: 1 block (14 oz) Medium-Firm Tofu, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1 tbsp Fermented Black Beans, rinsed and roughly chopped
1 tbsp Sichuan Peppercorns, toasted and ground
2 Green Onions, white and green parts separated, thinly sliced
1 tbsp cornstarch, mixed with the separately measured slurry water
2 tbsp water, for the cornstarch slurry
Water, enough for the tofu bath; drained and discarded
Salt, to taste, for the tofu bath; drained and discarded

recipeInstructions.text: Parcook the tofu: Wash the scallions before slicing. Mix the separately measured slurry cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl and set aside. Bring enough tofu-bath water to cover the cubes to a gentle boil and season it with the bath salt allowance to taste. Slide in all the tofu and simmer 2–3 minutes, then lift and drain gently; discard this bath water.

Cook the pork: Heat all the neutral oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat. Add all ground pork and break into small crumbles, beginning checks around 3–4 minutes. Retain all rendered fat. Brown color is a cooking cue, not proof of 160°F; continue cooking the pork with the sauce.

Fry the bean paste: Push pork aside and add all doubanjiang and rinsed, chopped fermented black beans to the existing oil and fat. Stir 1–2 minutes until fragrant and the oil takes on red color, reducing heat before the paste scorches.
Build the sauce: Stir in all garlic, ginger and scallion whites about 30 seconds, then add all measured broth, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a simmer.

Warm the tofu: Gently slide in all drained tofu. Spoon sauce over the cubes or nudge with the back of a ladle rather than stirring hard. Simmer about 5 minutes; check representative pork-containing sauce areas for at least 160°F before tasting or finishing. Use enough vessels for the complete scaled formula, divided proportionally, without crowding the cubes.

Thicken: Re-stir the entire separate slurry and drizzle it in two additions, gently swirling between them. Let the sauce simmer after each addition until thickening is visible; use the full listed mixture for this route and cook until the sauce clings without raw-starch taste.
Finish: Add all measured sesame oil and chili oil, then all the toasted, ground Sichuan peppercorns and scallion greens. Fold gently and serve promptly over separately prepared white rice.

recipes.name: Marinated Flank Steak Salad
recipes.description: Flank steak’s long grain makes the direction of slicing especially important. This soy-Dijon and lemon version keeps a rich vinaigrette, pepitas and crisp shallots around the sliced beef.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, for the marinade
3 tbsp soy sauce, or gluten-free tamari
1 tbsp neutral cooking oil, or shallot oil, for searing
1 large head romaine lettuce, washed and torn
1 head butter lettuce, washed and torn
1 avocado, washed before cutting, then diced

recipeInstructions.text: Score the Steak: Lightly score both sides of flank steak in a shallow diagonal diamond pattern, about 1/8 inch deep. Keep the cuts superficial; do not cut through the steak. Use separate equipment for the raw meat and ready-to-eat salad.

Marinate: Whisk extra-virgin olive oil, soy sauce, Dijon mustard, garlic cloves, and fresh lemon juice in a nonreactive dish or food-storage bag and add the steak. Seal and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or up to 12 hours.
Dry the Surface: Take the steak from the refrigerator when ready to cook. Lift it from the marinade and pat the surface dry. Discard the used marinade; keep it away from the dressing and salad.

Make the Vinaigrette: Shake or whisk extra-virgin olive oil, fresh lemon juice, Dijon mustard, small shallot, kosher salt, and freshly ground black pepper together. Keep the washed salad and toppings cold while the meat cooks.

Sear the Steak: Use flank steak and neutral cooking oil: heat the oil in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high to high heat until shimmering. Lay the steak flat without crowding. Begin checking around 4–5 minutes per side for the original cut, adjusting heat if the surface is burning; continue until the thickest part reaches at least 145°F before removing it. For more steaks, use additional suitable pans or complete cooking batches, dividing all the measured searing oil among them. Cut thickness and starting temperature change the clock.

Rest: Transfer to a clean cutting board and let the steak rest for 10 minutes, exceeding the minimum 3-minute rest after the 145°F endpoint. Keep the meat and cooked juices separate from the raw-meat equipment.
Slice: Slice as thinly as possible across the grain with the carving knife angled about 45 degrees. Keep the salad cold until assembly.

Assemble: Bring large head romaine lettuce, head butter lettuce, English cucumber, avocado, and radishes to the serving bowl. Toss both lettuces with half of the prepared vinaigrette. Arrange the cucumber, avocado and radishes over the greens, add all the sliced steak, and drizzle with all the remaining vinaigrette.
Finish: Scatter toasted pepitas and Crispy Shallots over the top just before serving so the toppings stay crisp.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, bright, savory, clean, crispy, umami, weeknight, everyday, kid-friendly, marinate, sear, toss

recipes.name: Bulgogi
recipes.description: Bulgogi uses very thin slices so the beef can cook quickly in uncrowded pan loads. This marinade keeps its soy, sesame oil, brown sugar and grated pear; the pear contributes fruit and sweetness without a promise of enzyme-driven tenderness.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb ribeye beef, raw, fresh or fully thawed; very thinly sliced, unseasoned for the homemade marinade
1/2 Bosc or Asian pear, washed, cored and grated
suitable high-heat cooking oil, a small splash as needed for the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare thin slices: Keep the beef cold. If starting with a whole ribeye, use about 45 minutes in the freezer as a first check until firm enough to slice thinly, still yielding to the knife; this adds preparation time. Pat unseasoned sliced beef dry with paper towels before marinating.

Mix and marinate: For the homemade route, use ribeye beef, soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, brown sugar, Bosc or Asian pear, garlic cloves, fresh ginger, green onions, and black pepper. Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, grated pear, garlic, ginger, green onions and pepper together. Toss with all the sliced beef, cover and refrigerate at 40°F or below for at least 30 minutes or overnight. The pre-marinated option below replaces the complete homemade marinade.

Cook in uncrowded loads: Heat a heavy skillet or wok over high heat until hot, adjusting if the coating scorches rather than browns. Use suitable high-heat cooking oil as needed. Lift the marinated beef from excess pooled marinade, leaving a coating on the slices, and spread one uncrowded layer in the pan. Begin checking after 1–2 minutes for browned edges, then flip and begin checking after about 30 seconds. Continue until the pieces reach at least 145°F in the center with a thermometer suitable for thin food, inserted from the side; follow any higher endpoint on a product label. These are first checks, not guaranteed finishing times.

Rest and serve: Move fully cooked beef to a clean serving dish and rest at least 3 minutes before eating. Continue with the remaining pan loads, keeping waiting raw beef cold and using separate clean utensils for cooked beef. Discard pooled raw-contact marinade; do not add it at the end. More loads extend elapsed time.

recipes.keywords: Korean, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, marinate, sear

recipes.name: Massaman Curry
recipes.description: Tender beef, potatoes and onion in a rich coconut curry with whole peanuts, warming spices and a sweet-tart tamarind finish.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes; trim tough outer silverskin but retain marbled fat
2 tbsp neutral cooking oil, divided between browning and the curry paste
3 tbsp prepared massaman curry paste; start with less if particularly hot or salty
1 tsp whole green cardamom pods, measured before lightly cracking, optional
3–4 whole dried red chiles, optional for extra heat
1 (14 oz) can full-fat unsweetened coconut milk, stirred together
Hot water, only as needed to maintain the braising liquid
2 medium waxy or all-purpose potatoes, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch / 2 cm cubes
1 large yellow onion, peeled and cut into 1-inch / 2.5 cm chunks
1/2 cup unsalted or lightly salted roasted peanuts
2 tbsp fish sauce, divided and added to taste
1 tbsp finely chopped palm sugar or packed brown sugar
1 tbsp unsweetened Thai-style tamarind purée made from pulp and water, plus more only if needed after tasting
Additional palm or brown sugar, only if needed after tasting

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the beef and aromatics: Cut the trimmed chuck into 1-inch / 2.5 cm cubes and pat dry. Chop garlic and ginger and measure the paste, milk and stock. Reserve one-third of the oil for the paste; use the remaining two-thirds for browning. Keep raw-meat tools separate from serving utensils and wash them after preparing the beef.

Brown in batches: Heat the browning oil in portions over medium-high in the heavy pot. Brown the beef in an uncrowded layer, about two batches for the full recipe, using an equal share of that oil for each batch. Leave two broad faces against the pot for about 2–3 minutes per face, turning once browned. Transfer to a plate; it is still raw inside. Allow the pot to regain heat between batches and lower the heat if the coating starts to blacken.

Build the curry: Lower to medium-low. Add the reserved oil, optional cracked cardamom pods and whole dried chiles; stir for about 20 seconds. Add massaman paste and cook 1–2 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not scorched. Stir in garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds. Gradually stir in the coconut milk, then stock and half the fish sauce, scraping up brown residue. There is no need to wait for coconut oil to separate. Return the beef and all its plate juices to the pot.

Braise the beef: Bring to a gentle simmer. Liquid should come just about to the top of the beef in the pot; add a little hot water if needed. Cover, lower the heat and braise gently for about 1 1/2–2 1/2 hours, beginning tenderness checks after 75 minutes. Every 20–30 minutes, stir along the bottom and check the liquid, adding hot water as needed to keep the beef mostly surrounded by sauce. A fork should enter the meat with only slight resistance before you continue. Toward the end of this stage, peel and cut the potatoes and onion.

Add potatoes and onion: Stir in the vegetables, cover and simmer about 20–30 minutes, stirring gently once or twice. The potatoes should be tender through the center and the beef should yield easily to a fork. Check a thick beef cube reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; tenderness usually requires cooking beyond that minimum. The off-heat rest comes before serving. If either needs longer, keep cooking gently and maintain enough liquid to prevent sticking. Lift out any potatoes that finish before the beef and return them at the finish.

Finish the sauce: Stir in peanuts, the starting amount of sugar and the starting amount of tamarind purée. Simmer 3–5 minutes. If the sauce is watery, simmer uncovered for another 5–10 minutes before final seasoning; it should coat a spoon but still flow around the meat. Taste with a piece of potato, then add the remaining fish sauce and optional extra sugar or tamarind in small amounts as needed. If using lime instead of tamarind, add it only after turning off the heat. Remove the cardamom pods and whole chiles before serving.

Rest and serve: Rest off heat for 5 minutes. Serve with a modest portion of separately prepared Basmati Rice. The potatoes already supply some starch. Coconut Jasmine Rice is a richer accompaniment. Add cilantro and lime wedges at the table.

recipes.name: Sushi Rice (Shari)
recipes.description: Vinegar-seasoned short-grain rice with tender, distinct grains that cling together lightly. Includes soaking, resting, seasoning and short cooling time.
recipeIngredient: 400 g Japanese short-grain white rice, not glutinous rice
480 ml cold water, plus water for rinsing
1 piece dried kombu, about 5 cm square

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and soak: Rinse the rice several times, gently swishing and draining until the water is less cloudy. Drain well, transfer to a heavy 3-quart saucepan and add the measured cooking water. Wipe away visible grit from the kombu with a barely damp cloth and add it. Soak for 30 minutes.
Heat and cook: Bring toward a boil over medium heat with the lid slightly ajar. Remove the kombu when the water starts bubbling. Close the lid, reduce to low and simmer gently for 12–15 minutes.

Rest and check: Move off the heat and leave covered for 10 minutes. Check a grain for a tender center. If grains are still firm and water remains, cover and cook on low for 3–5 minutes, then rest off heat for 5 minutes and check again. If the pot is dry but the center is hard, use the measured-water correction in troubleshooting. Already mushy rice will not become firm through extra stirring or cooking.

Mix the seasoning: While the rice cooks, stir four fifths of the measured vinegar, the sugar and two thirds of the measured salt in a small bowl. Warm briefly if needed to dissolve, without boiling. Reserve the remaining vinegar and salt.

Season and cool briefly: Transfer hot rice to a wide nonreactive bowl. Distribute the seasoning over it and gently lift and fold with a rice paddle. Fan as steam escapes, about 5–10 minutes; judge by the rice rather than expecting a fixed temperature after two minutes. Taste, dissolve any reserved salt needed in the reserved vinegar, then fold in that vinegar whether or not extra salt is used. For poke, let the portion being used become only barely warm before topping with cold fish and serving immediately.

Use or refrigerate: Cover loosely with a clean damp towel only during brief assembly. Measure the amount required by the main recipe; this batch makes approximately 5 1/2–6 cups. Refrigerate extra rice promptly rather than leaving the whole batch out while eating.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Chicken Bowls
recipes.description: This modular grain bowl treats each component as an independent element. Marinating chicken thighs in oregano and lemon, then searing over high heat develops a charred, crispy crust characteristic of Greek souvlaki.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs Chicken Thighs, boneless and skinless
2 cups Cooked Yellow Rice or Quinoa

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: In a large bowl, toss chicken thighs with olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, and garlic. Let sit for at least 15 minutes (ideally 2 hours).
The Sear: Heat a large skillet or grill to medium-high. Cook chicken for 5-6 minutes per side until deeply charred and the internal temp is 165°F.
Rest: Transfer to a board and let rest for 5 minutes. Slice into thin strips.
Assemble: In four deep bowls, spread a generous base of hummus. Top with a scoop of warm rice or quinoa.
Layer: Arrange the sliced chicken, cucumbers, and tomatoes in distinct "stacks" around the bowl.
Finish: Top with crumbled feta and a massive pile of Pickled Red Onions. Serve with a lemon wedge for the final High Note.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, acidic, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, grill, no-cook

recipes.name: Lemon-Oregano Chicken with Roasted Peppers
recipes.description: Boneless thighs in a measured lemon, garlic and oregano marinade, with peppers and onions roasted on a separate tray.
recipeIngredient: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, excess loose fat trimmed
3 tbsp olive oil, for the marinade
3/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken
1/2 tsp ground black pepper, for the chicken
400 g bell peppers, cored and cut into 3/4-inch strips
200 g red onion, peeled and cut into 3/4-inch wedges
1 tbsp olive oil, for the vegetables
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the vegetables
1/4 tsp ground black pepper, for the vegetables
1 tbsp chopped parsley, optional finishing herb

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate cold: Whisk marinade oil, lemon juice, garlic, oregano, chicken salt and chicken pepper. Toss with chicken, cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours for a longer preparation window. Keep the chicken’s original storage/use-by limit in mind; marinating does not reset it.

Prepare trays and vegetables: During the marinade, heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss peppers and onion with their separate oil, salt and pepper and spread on one rimmed half-sheet pan. Lift the thighs from the marinade, allow excess to drip off, open them flat and space them on a second pan. Discard the raw-contact marinade; do not use it as a serving sauce. Wash raw-meat utensils and hands.

Roast and check separately: Put chicken below the vegetable tray. Roast for about 25–35 minutes, turning the vegetable pieces and rotating each tray front to back after fifteen minutes. Start checking chicken at twenty-five minutes: insert a thermometer into the thickest part of every thigh and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Remove finished pieces to a clean board. Vegetables should be soft through the thick onion wedges with browned edges; let them continue separately if needed.

Rest and portion: Rest the cooked chicken for five minutes, then slice across the meat. Divide the full chicken and vegetable batches among four plates. Scatter the optional measured parsley over the vegetables. This recipe supplies the protein and roasted vegetables; bread, grains and sauces are additional components.

recipes.keywords: Greek-inspired, Mediterranean-inspired, savory, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, entertaining, meal-prep, roast

recipes.name: Mediterranean Grain Salad
recipes.description: Chewy farro carries the full olive-oil dressing, olives and feta, while diced vegetables and fresh herbs keep the salad varied. Pearled farro and whole wheat berries do not share a guaranteed cooking clock.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 tsp Kosher Salt, for cooking the grain
1 cup Kalamata Olives, pitted and halved
Additional kosher salt, to taste after mixing
Additional fresh lemon juice, to taste after mixing

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the farro: Rinse all the dry pearled farro. Bring all the listed broth and measured kosher salt to a boil in a pot with room for the grain to expand. Add the farro, reduce to a gentle simmer and cover. Begin checking around 25–30 minutes, following the actual product instructions if they differ; the center should be tender with a pleasant chew, without a hard core. Drain excess cooking liquid.

Cool and prepare: Spread the drained grain in a shallow layer and refrigerate promptly to cool; do not leave a large warm batch on the counter waiting for room temperature. While it cools, wash the cucumber, tomatoes, pepper, onion and herbs under running water, then prepare as listed. Put all diced vegetables and halved olives in a large clean bowl.

Make the dressing: Whisk all the measured olive oil, lemon juice, oregano, grated garlic and black pepper together. These full quantities belong to the dressing; keep any additional salt and lemon juice separate for the finished salad.

Combine: Add the cooled grain to the vegetables and olives. Fold in all the dressing until the full salad is coated. Use enough bowl space, or divide all components proportionally among more bowls, rather than crowding and crushing the grains.

Finish: Just before serving, fold in all the feta, parsley, mint and dill. Taste and use the separate additional salt or lemon juice allowances only if wanted. Serve chilled, or briefly out of refrigeration for immediate service.

Make ahead: Refrigerate the grain, dressed vegetables and herbs/feta separately if preparing ahead. Combine and add the full herb/feta supplies close to serving. Keep at 40°F or below; count storage from the oldest prepared component.

recipes.keywords: Greek, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern, acidic, herbaceous, savory, fresh, weeknight, meal-prep, light-and-fresh, entertaining, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Mediterranean Pinwheels
recipes.description: These quick appetizers or lunch components require proper technique to avoid falling apart. Blending cream cheese with flavored oil from sun-dried tomatoes creates a tacky, flavor-rich spread that binds the fillings to the tortilla.
recipeIngredient: 6 large Spinach or Sun-dried Tomato Tortillas
2 tbsp Oil (reserved from sun-dried tomato jar)
6 oz Sun-dried Tomatoes in oil, chopped
10 oz Frozen Spinach, thawed and squeezed bone-dry

recipeInstructions.text: The Bind: In a food processor, blend cream cheese, garlic, a few sun-dried tomatoes, and 2 tbsp of the tomato oil until completely smooth.
Prep: Lay out the 6 tortillas. Spread a thick, even layer of the cream cheese mixture over each, leaving a 1/2-inch border at the top.
Layer: Scatter the chopped spinach, remaining sun-dried tomatoes, Parmesan, and feta over the cream cheese. Place a single line of fresh basil leaves across the center of each tortilla.
The Roll: Starting from the edge parallel to the basil, roll the tortilla very tightly, squeezing gently as you go to ensure the "Emulsion" binds the layers.
The Finish: Wrap each log tightly in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (mandatory for clean slicing).
Cut: Using a sharp serrated knife, slice into 1-inch pinwheels.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Salmon with Lemon-Herb Emulsion
recipes.description: Crisp-skinned salmon over herbed orzo, chickpeas, tomatoes and feta, with a shaken lemon, olive oil and oregano dressing.
recipeIngredient: 4 skin-on salmon fillets, 6–8 oz each, of similar thickness
2 tbsp olive oil, for searing salmon
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the dressing
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for the orzo
1 tsp smoked paprika, divided equally between salmon and chickpeas
1 cup canned chickpeas, measured after draining and rinsing, then thoroughly dried
Fresh parsley and mint, chopped, to taste
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C. Drain, rinse and thoroughly dry the chickpeas. Zest the lemon, then juice it. Halve tomatoes, chop herbs and measure the separate oil amounts. Pat salmon skin dry, remove pin bones and refrigerate while starting the sides.

Roast chickpeas: Toss chickpeas with their allotted oil, half the smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Spread in one layer on a rimmed tray. Roast about 25–35 minutes, shaking at about 15 minutes, until lightly crisp and beginning to brown. Begin checking at 20 minutes; do not insist that the centers turn hard.

Mix dressing and cook orzo: Shake the dressing oil, garlic, honey, oregano and half the lemon juice in a closed jar. Taste, then add more of the remaining lemon juice, salt and pepper as needed. Meanwhile cook orzo in boiling salted water according to its package until tender with a little bite. Drain, then toss with the orzo oil, tomatoes, feta, parsley and mint. Cover briefly to keep warm while the fish cooks.

Heat the skillet: When chickpeas are about 10 minutes from ready, season salmon with lemon zest, the remaining smoked paprika, salt and pepper. Heat the salmon oil in a broad skillet over medium-high until shimmering, not smoking heavily. If portions cannot fit with space between them, use two skillets with the oil divided between them, or cook in batches, reserving a proportional share of the searing oil for each batch.

Sear and finish: Lay salmon skin-side down, away from you. Press gently with a spatula for the first few seconds to keep skin in contact. Cook about 4–6 minutes until the skin browns and releases; reduce heat if spices darken rapidly. Turn carefully and cook about 2–6 minutes more, depending on thickness. Check the thickest center from the side for 145°F / 63°C. If the outside is done before the center, lower the heat and continue gently. Remove each portion when ready.

Assemble: Divide the herbed orzo among plates, scatter over roasted chickpeas and add salmon with its skin facing up. Shake the dressing again and spoon around the fish and over the orzo, keeping the skin exposed. Serve immediately. The pasta, legumes and tomatoes are already part of this dish; a separate grain is unnecessary.

recipes.name: Melon Daiquiri
recipes.description: The daiquiri is a Cuban drink named after a beach near Santiago - born from American occupation and the sugar trade. A good daiquiri is balanced: rum, lime juice, and sugar in equal parts, with the lime juice providing the backbone.
recipeIngredient: 6 cups Honeydew Melon, peeled, deseeded and cubed
1/2 cup Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Thermal Prep: Freeze your melon cubes for 30 minutes prior to starting for the best texture.
Blend: Combine the honeydew, light rum, lime juice, and melon liqueur in a high-powered blender.
Process: Pulse on low, then increase to high until perfectly smooth. Add a handful of ice only if needed to reach a "thick-shake" consistency.
Skew: Thread 3 cantaloupe cubes onto each sugar cane skewer.
Serve: Pour into chilled coupes or martini glasses. Garnish with the skewers and serve immediately for the maximum "Bounce."

recipes.keywords: Caribbean, sweet, acidic, entertaining, blend

recipes.name: Arroz Rojo
recipes.description: Long-grain rice toasted in oil, then simmered with tomato, onion, garlic and broth. A covered rest helps the grains settle before fluffing.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup plain tomato puree, or 1 cup freshly blended Roma tomatoes
1 cup chicken broth, plus hot water as needed if the rice remains firm

recipeInstructions.text: Rinse and drain: Rinse the dry rice in several changes of cool water until less cloudy. Drain thoroughly in a fine-mesh strainer, shaking out excess water while you dice the onion and mince the garlic.

Toast: Warm the oil in a heavy saucepan over medium heat. Carefully add the drained rice; residual water can spatter. Stir constantly for about 3–5 minutes, until the grains look opaque and lightly golden and smell nutty. Lower the heat if individual grains darken quickly.
Add aromatics: Stir in the onion and garlic. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring, until fragrant without browning the garlic.
Add liquid: Carefully stir in the measured tomato puree, broth and salt. Bring to a gentle boil, stirring once to distribute the rice and release any grains stuck to the base.

Simmer and check: Place the cilantro sprig on top. Cover tightly and reduce to a low simmer. Cook about 15–18 minutes without repeatedly opening the lid. Taste a grain: it should have no hard center, and free liquid should be absorbed. If firm and dry, add a little hot water and continue covered; if firm with liquid remaining, continue gently without adding more.
Rest: Remove from heat once tender and leave covered for 10 minutes.
Finish: Remove the cilantro sprig. Fluff gently with a fork and divide into four side portions.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, weeknight, meal-prep, fry, simmer, boil, blend

recipes.name: Skillet Esquites (Mexican Corn Salad)
recipes.description: Sweet corn with browned edges, lime, chile, and cotija in a light creamy dressing. Learn to manage pan moisture before adding the delicate finishing ingredients.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups (600 g) fresh sweet-corn kernels or thawed frozen corn, thoroughly drained
2 tbsp Mexican crema or sour cream
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, divided, plus more to taste
1/2 tsp pure ground ancho chile (not a salted seasoning blend)
Fine salt, to taste after adding the cotija

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and mix the dressing: Drain corn thoroughly and blot away surface water. Whisk mayonnaise, crema, 1 tbsp lime juice, ground ancho chile, and garlic in a large bowl. Set aside the remaining lime, cheese, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.

Brown the first batch: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high until shimmering. Add half the corn and spread it out. Leave for about 2 minutes, then stir and continue cooking for 3–5 minutes, until tender with golden-brown patches. Reduce heat if it spits violently or scorches. Transfer to a wide plate.
Repeat: Add the remaining oil and corn. Cook the second batch in the same way, adjusting the heat as needed. If dark residue is burning, remove it carefully before adding the second batch.
Dress while warm: Let the corn stop steaming vigorously for 2–3 minutes. Add both batches to the dressing and toss. Fold in cotija, scallions, cilantro, and optional jalapeño.

Balance and serve: Taste, add the remaining lime by the teaspoon as needed, and add salt only if the cheese has not supplied enough. Divide into six side portions and serve warm or cool. Chill promptly if making ahead.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, sweet, acidic, rich, weeknight, entertaining, light-and-fresh, saute, toss

recipes.name: Yogurt-Marinated Chicken and Onion Kabobs
recipes.description: Skinless chicken and thin onion layers in a garlic, lemon and yogurt marinade, grilled with warm spices and a measured center-temperature check. Plan the overnight soak and grill capacity.
recipeIngredient: 2 1/2 lbs (1130 g) boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed and cut into about thirty-six 1 1/2-inch pieces
250 g peeled red onion, cut into 1-inch squares and separated into single or thin paired layers
1 cup (240 g) plain whole-milk Greek yogurt
1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, plus up to 1/2 tsp more for extra heat
1 tsp neutral oil, for grill grates (or 1 tbsp for the three-batch skillet option)

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and coat: Cut the peeled onion into one-inch squares and separate into single or thin paired layers. Cut chicken into about thirty-six pieces roughly 1 1/2 inches across, keeping thickness similar. In a bowl large enough to hold everything, whisk yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice and zest, garlic, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, the desired red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper. Add chicken and onion and turn to coat evenly. Cover and refrigerate for eight to twenty-four hours.

Prepare the grill: Near the end of marinating, heat a gas grill with the lid closed, then keep a medium-high cooking zone and a low or unlit zone. For charcoal, allow coals to establish and arrange them on one side, leaving the other side cooler. Follow the grill's lighting instructions. Set out a clean serving platter and utensils; the raw-marinated tray is not the serving platter.

Thread and drain: Divide chicken among twelve 10–12-inch skewers, about three pieces each. Distribute onion in thin layers between the chicken and at both ends, keeping the whole food-bearing length over the cooking zone. Do not thicken the onion stacks to use it up; use an additional onion-only skewer if needed and count it in the grill capacity. All this onion has contacted raw chicken and must be cooked; it cannot become a raw garnish. Thread without tightly compressing or wrapping pieces into thick bundles. Let excess marinade drain back into its bowl so a thin film remains, then discard the residue. Keep six skewers refrigerated while the first six cook, unless the grill is large enough for the whole batch with a clear cooler zone. Lightly oil clean grates with the measured teaspoon neutral oil using a folded paper towel held in long tongs.

Grill the first round: Lay six skewers over the cooking zone without touching. Close the lid between turns and turn about every three minutes once the first surface releases, using a broad spatula to help if needed. Cook for about twelve to fifteen minutes, moving skewers to the cooler zone if the coating browns too quickly. Cook any extra onion skewer alongside until the layers soften and reach 165°F / 74°C because of their raw-chicken contact. Onion edges should soften with some browned spots; the chicken coating need not become uniformly crisp.

Check and repeat: Begin checking around twelve minutes. Probe the largest pieces on each skewer from the side, avoiding the hot metal, and continue until each reaches at least 165°F / 74°C. Check any unusually thick pieces separately. Transfer fully cooked skewers to the clean platter and cover loosely during the short second round. Cook the remaining six the same way, keeping the same thermometer endpoint. A tight cover softens the coating, and the first round will not retain the same surface texture as chicken served straight from the grill.

Rest and finish: Rest the final round for five minutes, then serve two skewers per person with the chopped parsley and lemon wedges. For six plates, add one-and-a-half four-side batches of Lemon and Herb Instant Couscous, starting with 375 g dry couscous, plus vegetables or salad. Alternatively, warm six pita breads and add a vegetable side. These are extra components and preparation time. The onion in each portion is a seasoning vegetable, about 40 g raw weight, not a full vegetable side.

recipes.name: Mini-Shell Pasta with Bacon and Peas
recipes.description: Small pasta shells with smoked bacon, sweet peas, mint and a rich Parmesan finish, loosened with pasta water.
recipeIngredient: 10 slices smoked bacon, cut crosswise into thin slivers
2 tbsp crème fraîche or heavy cream
1 lemon, juiced, added gradually to taste
2 tbsp fresh mint, finely chopped, divided between sauce and garnish
1 cup hot pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; use only as needed
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from The New York Times’ Mini-Shell Pasta with Creamy Smoked Bacon and Peas.

itemListElement.text: Start water and prepare: Bring pasta water to a boil. Cut bacon into thin slivers, finely grate Parmesan, chop mint and juice the lemon. Season the water moderately; bacon and cheese bring much of the salt.

Cook bacon: Melt butter in a large deep skillet over medium-low to medium. Add bacon and cook, stirring, about 10–15 minutes or as its package directs, until cooked through and golden with crisp edges. Lower heat if butter darkens quickly. Keep the rendered fat for the sauce; do not add more oil.

Cook pasta and peas: Meanwhile cook pasta according to package directions until tender with a little bite. Cook peas fully according to their package in a separate saucepan or microwave-safe bowl and drain. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining pasta without rinsing.

Combine: Stir cooked peas, crème fraîche or cream and half the mint into the bacon pan over low heat. Add hot pasta and about one-quarter of the reserved water. Toss gently until hot and coated, using the pasta pot instead if the skillet is too full.

Add cheese off heat: Remove from the burner and wait until bubbling subsides. Fold in Parmesan a handful at a time, adding warm water in small amounts as needed for a creamy coating. Add half the lemon juice, taste, then add more of the remaining juice only as needed. The sauce should remain slightly loose for plating.
Serve: Add black pepper and taste before salt. Divide into the intended portions and scatter the remaining measured mint over the top. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Mint Tzatziki with Honey
recipes.description: Thick Greek yogurt with crisp diced cucumber, fresh mint, olive oil, garlic and a little honey. Spoon it into lamb pitas or serve alongside grilled meat and vegetables.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (240 g) plain full-fat Greek yogurt
100 g English cucumber, ends trimmed, finely diced

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the cucumber and herbs: Wash and dry the cucumber and mint. Cut the cucumber into fine dice, about 3 mm across, then pat with a clean kitchen towel. Finely chop the mint and mince the small garlic clove.
Mix: Stir the yogurt, olive oil and honey together until evenly blended. Fold in the cucumber, mint, garlic and half the measured salt.

Taste and serve: Taste, then add the reserved salt only if needed. Serve now, or cover and refrigerate while preparing the meal; stir and taste again before serving. For four lamb pitas, start with 2–3 tablespoons in each and offer the rest alongside. The full batch makes approximately 1 1/2 cups, depending on the yogurt and cucumber.

recipes.name: Miriam’s Melt-In-Your-Mouth Rosh Hashanah Brisket
recipes.description: Miriam Szokovski’s honey-and-balsamic brisket is a Rosh Hashanah centerpiece with onions cooked underneath the meat. Its uncovered 400°F start is followed by a tightly covered 250°F braise; check for tenderness with a fork rather than treating four hours as a guarantee.
recipeIngredient: 2 large Spanish onions, sliced into thick rounds

recipeInstructions.text: Foundation: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Lay large Spanish onions across the bottom of a heavy baking dish or Dutch oven. Choose a vessel in which the meat can lie without folding or crowding, with room for its juices and a tight lid or foil cover. For a larger batch, use enough vessels and divide all the onions, rub and liquids in proportion to the meat in each; a smaller batch needs an appropriately smaller vessel.
Rub: Mix paprika, garlic powder, kosher salt, and dried chives (if using) in a small bowl, omitting the chives if not using them. Pat the full measured rub over both sides of first-cut brisket.

Uncovered Roast: Place first-cut brisket on the onions. Roast uncovered for 1 hour for the original 3 lb batch. Watch for browning rather than blackened spices or onions; smaller or thinner cuts need earlier browning checks, and pan shape affects the result.

Cover: Remove the dish from the oven. Pour balsamic vinegar and honey over the meat, retaining all its juices. Cover tightly with a heavy lid or double layer of foil, and reduce the oven to 250°F. The onions and meat release liquid during the covered cook.

Low and Slow: Return the covered dish to the oven and begin checking around 4 more hours for the original batch. Turn the meat about once an hour, or at least once halfway through, spooning the liquid back over it and promptly replacing the cover. Begin checking tenderness earlier for smaller or thinner cuts, and allow longer for thicker cuts. Continue until a fork enters with almost no resistance; size, thickness, pan and oven can change the clock. Check that the center has reached at least 145°F, then let it rest at least 3 minutes before handling.

Chill for Slicing: Divide the cooked brisket into smaller sections that can lie in shallow containers, and divide all the onions, juices and rendered fat among them. Refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below, within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour above 90°F. Do not leave a deep pan on the counter until completely cold. Chill until the meat is cold throughout, preferably overnight.

Slice and Reheat: Remove the cold meat and slice thinly against the grain. Reheat the full onions, sauce and fat in a saucepan, stirring to bring the sauce to a rolling boil briefly. Return all of it to the sliced meat and reheat covered in the oven or on the stovetop until the meat and sauce reach 165°F throughout, checking several places. Serve with all the onions and sauce; prolonged boiling will concentrate the sweet sauce, so avoid unnecessary continued reduction.

recipes.keywords: Jewish, sweet, acidic, holiday, bake, roast, braise

recipes.name: Misir Wot (Ethiopian Red Lentil Stew)
recipes.description: Berbere and niter kibbeh give this Ethiopian lentil stew its spiced, buttery character; the same-volume olive-oil option gives a different, dairy-free base. Start the finely diced onions without fat until softened and concentrated, then add the full listed fat before the aromatics.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 cups Red Lentils, rinsed until water runs clear
3 tbsp Niter Kibbeh (Ethiopian spiced butter) or Extra-Virgin Olive Oil for vegan
2 large Red Onions, finely diced (about 3 cups for the original batch)
1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice, for finishing
Additional water, as needed to adjust the stew consistency
Additional kosher salt, to taste after cooking
Additional berbere, to taste after cooking

recipeInstructions.text: Soften the onions: Put all diced onions in a heavy pot over medium heat without oil. Stir frequently for 8–10 minutes as a first check, until their released moisture has reduced and the onions soften. Lower heat if they catch; stop at softened onions with reduced moisture rather than waiting for deep caramelization.

Add fat and spices: Add all the listed niter kibbeh or olive oil and cook 3–4 minutes until onions begin to turn golden. Add all garlic and grated ginger and stir 30–45 seconds. Add all the measured berbere, tomato paste, cardamom and fenugreek and stir 2 minutes without scorching.

Cook the lentils: Add all rinsed red lentils, all the listed cooking water and measured kosher salt. Bring to a boil, lower to a gentle simmer and cover. Cook 25–30 minutes as a first check, stirring every 5–7 minutes and reaching the bottom to prevent sticking, until the lentils have broken down with no firm centers. For scaled batches follow the listed water and salt amounts.

Adjust consistency: If too thick before the lentils are tender, use the separate water allowance a few tablespoons at a time and continue the gentle simmer. If tender but too thin, simmer uncovered briefly until thick and scoopable. Use a vessel with room to stir the full batch; divide the complete formula proportionally among more pots if needed.

Finish: Stir in all the measured lemon juice. Taste the fully cooked stew and use the separate additional salt and berbere allowances only if wanted; simmer briefly after an extra spice addition to incorporate it. Keep the full listed berbere and fat in the main formula.
Serve: Serve thick and scoopable with injera, or over separately prepared basmati rice. The starch accompaniment has its own preparation and clock.
