recipes.name: Miso-Glazed Roasted Cauliflower
recipes.description: White miso, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil and rice vinegar make a concentrated glaze for the cauliflower. This sauce coats the florets before roasting, so check it when turning: miso and sweeteners can darken before a thick center is tender.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb fresh cauliflower florets, similar-sized; washed and dried, very large florets split
scallions, for garnishing, washed and thinly sliced

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set out a large rimmed sheet or enough sheets for one layer of the measured florets. If lining, use parchment rated for this heat or suitable foil. Wash the cauliflower under running water, divide into similar-sized florets, split very large ones and dry them.

Choose one glaze route: Set out white miso paste, mirin, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, fresh ginger, honey (if using), and additional soy sauce (if using) and choose one sweetening route before combining. For the mirin version, use the mirin and omit the optional honey and additional soy sauce. For the honey variation, omit mirin and use the measured honey plus additional soy sauce, while retaining the separately listed soy sauce. Do not combine both routes. Whisk the chosen ingredients until the miso is evenly dispersed; taste a small sample to understand the salty, sweet and acidic balance.

Coat and spread: Toss fresh cauliflower florets with all the chosen glaze in the large bowl. Spread in a single layer, with flat cut faces against the sheet where possible. Keep room between pieces; if the scaled batch piles up, use additional sheets or batches rather than a deeper layer.

Watch the coating and centers: Roast for 25–30 minutes, gently turning around halfway through and checking the coating then. Test a thick floret with a knife: its center should be tender and the coating browned without blackened bitterness. If the glaze darkens before the centers soften, move pieces away from hot spots, turn the dark faces upward and finish under loose foil while checking the centers; covered pieces will have softer edges. Remove ready pieces promptly rather than requiring every edge to char. More sheet area or larger florets may change the time.

Garnish and serve: Scatter sesame seeds and scallions over the hot cauliflower and serve. The sesame seeds and scallions are both included finishes; wash the scallions before slicing and keep them away from raw-meat tools.

recipes.name: Miso-Mashed Potatoes
recipes.description: Yukon Gold potatoes gently mashed with white miso, butter, warm milk and a little garlic, finished with optional scallions.
recipeIngredient: 900 g peeled and trimmed Yukon Gold potatoes, cut into even 1-inch pieces
2 L cold water, or enough to cover the potatoes by about 1 inch
8 g salt, for the cooking water
4 tbsp (57 g) unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
2 tbsp (36 g) plain white rice miso, without added dashi; choose certified gluten-free miso if needed
1/2 cup (120 ml) whole milk, plus up to 1/4 cup (60 ml) more if needed
1/8 tsp fine salt, optional after tasting
2 tbsp thinly sliced washed scallion greens, optional garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Cut and cover: Peel and trim the potatoes to the listed net weight, then cut into even one-inch pieces. Rinse briefly, put in a 5-quart pot and cover with about two liters cold water, adding enough to sit an inch above the potatoes. Add the eight grams of cooking-water salt.

Simmer to tenderness: Bring to a boil, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook about 18–22 minutes after the water begins simmering, until several tested pieces yield easily to a knife and a cooled bite is completely soft in the center. Keep cooking if needed; larger pieces take longer.

Warm the miso dairy during cooking: In a small saucepan over low heat, whisk the initial half-cup milk with the miso and garlic powder until the miso has no large clumps. Add the butter and warm gently until melted. Do not boil or reduce the mixture. Wash and slice the optional scallions while the potatoes finish.

Drain and briefly dry: Drain well in a colander. Return potatoes to the pot over low heat for one to two minutes, shaking gently, until surface water evaporates and the pieces look matte. Remove from heat before they stick or brown.

Mash and fold: Pass the hot potatoes through a ricer or mash gently by hand. Fold in the warm miso dairy in two additions with a spatula, stopping as soon as it is incorporated. If stiff, warm and add the reserved milk one tablespoon at a time until the mash forms a soft mound. Do not beat it smooth in a blender.

Taste and serve: Taste before adding the optional one-eighth teaspoon of salt; the miso may supply all the finishing seasoning needed. Scatter with the optional scallions and divide into four generous side portions, or six smaller portions on a plate with another starch. Pair with a simply seasoned roast and a crisp or lemony vegetable.

recipes.name: Miso Salmon with Bok Choy
recipes.description: Citrus-miso salmon with garlic, scallions and oyster-seasoned bok choy over jasmine rice.
recipeIngredient: 540 ml water, for rice, plus water for rinsing
900 g skinless, boneless salmon, divided into four similar fillets
1/4 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 tsp neutral oil, for the foil
600 g trimmed baby bok choy, washed and dried
4 tsp neutral oil, for the skillet, divided
2 tbsp water, for the bok choy, divided

recipeInstructions.text: Start rice and heat the oven: Heat the oven to 400°F / 205°C with a rack in the middle and another positioned for the later broil. Rinse the jasmine rice and drain well. Put it in a heavy 2-quart saucepan with 540 ml water, bring to a boil, cover and reduce to low. Simmer about 15 minutes until water is absorbed, then move off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Fluff before serving. This is a starting method for regular jasmine white rice; follow the package if its ratio differs.

Mix and divide the marinade: While the rice cooks, whisk miso, honey, soy sauce, mirin, lemon juice, rice vinegar, half the minced garlic, half the scallions and half the pepper. Reserve 2 tbsp in a clean bowl for finishing. Check fish for pin bones and pat dry; place it in a shallow dish with the remaining marinade, turn to coat, cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Do not leave this acidic marinade on overnight.

Prepare the vegetables and pans: During the marinade, split small bok choy heads lengthwise; quarter larger heads so thick stem sections are about 1 inch across. Wash between the stalks, drain and dry thoroughly, then divide into two equal batches. Divide the remaining garlic, scallions and pepper between those batches. Line a metal half-sheet pan with foil and spread its teaspoon of oil where the fish will sit.

Roast the salmon: Lift fish from the marinade, letting excess drip off. Gently scrape off thick clumps, leaving a thin coating. Arrange on the prepared pan with space between portions and discard the raw-contact marinade. Roast about 12–16 minutes, until the fish is nearly cooked; check its center toward the end. If it reaches 145°F / 63°C before the final broil, it is already cooked and needs at most a very brief coloring step.

Cook bok choy in two batches: While fish roasts, heat a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat with 2 tsp neutral oil. Add half the bok choy cut-side down and cook 2–3 minutes until lightly browned. Turn, add half the reserved vegetable garlic and scallions, and stir 30 seconds until fragrant. Add 1 tbsp water, cover and steam 1–2 minutes until stems are crisp-tender. Uncover, evaporate any pooled water, then toss with 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and half the remaining pepper. Transfer to a serving dish and loosely cover. Repeat with the second batch and the remaining vegetable ingredients. Turn off the skillet before broiling; if the fish is waiting for its finish, set its pan briefly on a heatproof surface.

Glaze and briefly broil: Spread the clean reserved 2 tbsp marinade over the four fillets, using a clean utensil. Switch to high broil and place the fish surface 7–9 inches below the element. Watch continuously for 1–3 minutes, until the coating bubbles and browns. Check each fillet sideways in its thickest center and cook to 145°F / 63°C. If color arrives first, finish gently in the oven as described above. Let the fish stand briefly while fluffing and serving the rice.

Serve the complete dinner: Divide all the rice and bok choy among four bowls or plates and add one fillet to each. The original batch supplies about 225 g raw salmon and 150 g trimmed bok choy per diner, with roughly a cup of cooked rice. A small cucumber salad is an optional cool contrast, rather than a second required vegetable batch.

recipes.name: Miso Sesame Dense Bean Salad
recipes.description: Cook and cool edamame as its package directs before it joins the chickpeas and crunchy vegetables. Whisk the thick miso with tamari and the measured acids until smooth, then toss thoroughly so the seasoning does not remain in isolated clumps.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup snap peas, optional, when in season
Roasted peanuts or almonds, chopped, optional
1 teaspoon sweetener, like honey, maple syrup, or coconut sugar
1 teaspoon chili crisp or chili flakes, add more or less to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Prepare shelled edamame according to its package cooking instructions when required; do not merely thaw a product labeled for cooking. Drain and cool promptly before mixing. Drain/rinse chickpeas and drain well. Wash and dry vegetables, then combine chickpeas, cooled edamame, optional snap peas, cabbage, carrots and sliced green onions in a large bowl.
Mix dressing: Whisk miso with tamari, rice vinegar, sesame seeds, lime juice, sesame oil, sweetener and chili crisp or chili flakes until the miso lumps break up and the dressing is evenly mixed.

Toss and serve: Fold dressing through the beans and vegetables until evenly coated. Top with optional chopped roasted nuts just before serving. Serve immediately or cover and refrigerate 30 minutes. Keep unused salad refrigerated in a covered container for up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Miso Soup
recipes.description: Whisk miso smooth with some of the prepared dashi before returning it to the pot off the heat. This disperses the paste through the broth without crushing the silken tofu.
recipeIngredient: 4 cups prepared dashi, homemade or made with instant dashi granules according to package instructions
4 oz Silken Tofu, cut into small cubes

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare wakame: Follow the dried wakame package's preparation instructions, using all the listed wakame. If it requires a separate soak and drain, complete that before adding it to the soup; use enough soaking water as instructed and discard it. Wash and thinly slice the green onions.

Heat dashi: Measure all the prepared dashi into a saucepan with room for tofu and seaweed. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat to low. Homemade Dashi is a separately prepared component; measure its strained output for this soup. Instant granules must be prepared according to their package.

Warm tofu and seaweed: Gently add all the tofu cubes and prepared wakame. Simmer gently, starting with about 2 minutes, until tofu is heated through and the seaweed is tender; product preparation and starting temperature affect the clock. Avoid rough stirring that breaks the tofu.

Disperse miso: Put all the miso in a small bowl. Ladle enough broth from this same pot to whisk it smooth, about 1/2 cup at the original batch. This is part of the measured dashi, not additional water or stock.
Finish: Turn off the heat. Gently stir all the miso mixture back into the pot. Add all the green onions and serve promptly in the listed planning number of small bowls.

recipes.name: Candy-Coated Chocolate Cookies
recipes.description: Folding only 3/4 of the candies into the dough, then pressing the remaining candies into the tops of the dough balls after scooping ensures vibrant colors stay visible on the finished cookies instead of bleeding into the batter during baking. Using a high ratio of brown sugar to white sugar creates chewy cookies that contrast the crisp candy shell.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Baking Soda + 1 tsp Sea Salt

recipeInstructions.text: Cream: In a large bowl, beat the shortening (or butter) with both sugars until light and fluffy (2 mins). Add eggs and vanilla; beat until emulsified.
Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt. Gradually add to the wet mix until just combined.
Inclusions: Fold in 1 cup of the candies.
Shape: Preheat oven to 350°F. Drop teaspoon-sized balls of dough onto ungreased sheets.
Press: Press 3-4 of the remaining candies into the top of each ball.
Bake: Bake for 9-11 minutes until the edges are just golden. Do not over-bake; they will set on the pan.
Cool: Let rest on the pan for 5 minutes to ensure proper texture.

recipes.name: Momma’s Turkey and Vegetable Meatloaf
recipes.description: A family-style turkey loaf with softened vegetables, a measured breadcrumb panade and a thin ketchup finish.
recipeIngredient: 40 g fine dry unseasoned whole-wheat breadcrumbs
100 g green bell pepper, cut into small dice
150 g zucchini, coarsely grated, then gently squeezed to about two thirds of its starting weight

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment. Mix breadcrumbs and milk and let hydrate at least 5 minutes. Grate and gently squeeze the zucchini to about two-thirds of its starting weight; prepare the other small-cut vegetables.

Soften and cool vegetables: Heat oil in a skillet over medium heat. Cook onion and pepper about 5 minutes, stirring. Add carrot and zucchini and cook another 4–5 minutes until softened and no liquid pools in the pan. Spread on a plate to cool about 5–10 minutes while preparing the remaining ingredients; they should no longer feel hot.
Mix: Beat egg into the hydrated crumbs with garlic powder, salt and pepper. Stir in cooled vegetables. Add cold turkey and fold gently until evenly combined, without prolonged kneading.
Shape and begin baking: Shape a free-form loaf roughly 9 by 4 inches and 2–2 1/2 inches high on the prepared tray, smoothing large cracks without packing hard. Bake about 35 minutes.

Glaze and check: Spread all the ketchup over the top in a thin layer. Continue baking about 15–25 minutes, checking until the center reaches 165°F / 74°C in several positions. Extend as needed. If the top darkens early, tent loosely with foil; a browned glaze is not the doneness test.

Rest and portion: Let rest for 10 minutes before cutting six portions. Each can be one thick slice or two thinner slices. Serve with separately prepared sides; the base recipe includes the loaf and its ketchup finish only.

recipes.name: Chocolate Cake
recipes.description: This family chocolate cake uses butter and boiling water to bring the cocoa into a smooth batter. The entire batter mixes in the saucepan used to melt the butter, minimizing cleanup.

recipeInstructions.text: Melt & Bloom: In a large saucepan over medium heat, bring the butter, cocoa powder, and water to a gentle boil. Remove from heat immediately.
The Batter: Into the hot saucepan, whisk in the sugar, buttermilk, baking soda, salt, and eggs until smooth. Gradually fold in the flour and vanilla.
Bake: Pour the batter into a greased 9x13 rectangular pan (or two 8-inch squares). Bake at 350°F for 25-30 minutes until a tester comes out clean.
The Frosting: While the cake bakes, melt the 1 stick of butter in a clean saucepan. Whisk in the cocoa and milk. Remove from heat and stir in the powdered sugar until silky.
Seal: Pour the warm frosting over the hot cake immediately after removing it from the oven. Let cool completely (if you can wait!) before slicing.

recipes.name: Mongolian Beef with Ginger and Scallions
recipes.description: Thinly sliced beef browned in batches and briefly coated in a ginger-scallion soy glaze.
recipeIngredient: 680 g flank steak, sliced across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick strips about 2 inches long
3 tbsp (24 g) cornstarch, for the beef coating
3 tbsp neutral oil, for three beef batches
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus 1 tbsp for the slurry
3 tbsp (40 g) packed light brown sugar
80 g scallions, cut into 2-inch lengths, white and green parts separated
2 small dried red chilies, optional, left whole for mild heat or broken for more

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the beef: Pat the steak dry and slice across the grain into 1/4-inch-thick, roughly 2-inch-long strips. Toss with the 3 tbsp coating cornstarch, separating slices and shaking off loose excess. Divide into three roughly equal batches.

Mix the sauce and slurry: Stir soy sauce, 120 ml water and brown sugar together until the sugar mostly dissolves. In a separate cup, mix the 1 tsp slurry cornstarch with 1 tbsp cold water. Keep ginger, garlic, chilies and the two scallion portions beside the stove.

Sear three batches: Heat a heavy skillet over medium-high. Add 1 tbsp frying oil; it should shimmer without smoking heavily. Add one batch in a single layer and sear about 1–2 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through. Probe thicker strips from the edge to check at least 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Repeat twice with 1 tbsp oil for each batch, letting the pan regain heat. Reduce heat if the coating burns before the meat cooks.

Cook aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Carefully discard excess oil and any blackened starch, leaving browned but unburned bits. Add the separate teaspoon oil, ginger and optional chilies; stir about 20 seconds. Add garlic and scallion whites and stir another 20–30 seconds without browning the garlic deeply.

Thicken gently: Pour in the mixed sauce and simmer about 1 minute. Stir the slurry again, add half, and simmer 20–30 seconds. Add the rest only if needed for a light spoon-coating consistency; discard unused slurry. Loosen with a tablespoon of water if it becomes sticky or pasty.

Coat and check: Return beef and its juices with the scallion greens. Toss over medium heat about 30–60 seconds, just until evenly coated and greens wilt. Verify sliced beef reaches at least 145°F / 63°C; give it at least 3 minutes before serving. Transfer off the hot pan for this wait. For the chicken variation, verify 165°F / 74°C in several thick strips instead.

Serve: Remove whole chilies or tell diners they are present. Divide among four portions with plain rice and vegetables prepared separately. Serve promptly; the coating will continue softening in the glaze.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, fry, simmer

recipes.name: Mongolian Chicken
recipes.description: This Chinese American takeout-style chicken uses a light cornstarch coat and a sweet soy glaze. Fry the thin pieces until cooked, then add slurry gradually so the sauce clings without becoming a heavy gel.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, raw, fully thawed if frozen; pat dry and slice ¼ inch / 6 mm thick
1 tbsp vegetable oil for coating the chicken
1/4 cup cornstarch for dredging, use this supply for any second dredge; discard the unused raw-contact starch
1/3 cup (80 ml) vegetable oil for frying, retain part for aromatics after frying; drain the excess
3 scallions, cut diagonally into 1–2-inch lengths (about 5 cm at the long end); keep white and green parts separate
1/4 cup hot water or low-sodium chicken stock
2 tbsp cornstarch for the slurry, prepare the full slurry; use only as much as the sauce needs

recipeInstructions.text: Separate the scallions: Prepare scallions, keeping all white parts in one bowl and all green parts in another. Both portions will be used; their natural size varies.
Prepare the slurry: Mix cornstarch for the slurry and water for the slurry in a bowl and set beside the stove. Stir again immediately before using it; settled starch will otherwise thicken unevenly.

Lightly coat the chicken: Have boneless skinless chicken breast or thighs, vegetable oil for coating the chicken, and cornstarch for dredging ready. Mix the chicken with the coating oil, then dredge in the listed cornstarch, shaking off excess so each piece is lightly coated. If the coating becomes damp before frying, use the same measured dredging supply for a second light coating. Discard unused dredging starch after the chicken has gone into the pan; it has touched raw chicken.

Fry in manageable loads: Heat vegetable oil for frying in a wok over high heat until hot, without letting it smoke. Add the coated chicken in a single layer; fry in loads if necessary. Start checking the first side at about 1 minute and the second at about 30 seconds, turning as needed until the coating is browned and crisp and the thickest pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Use a thin-tip thermometer from the side. Transfer fully cooked chicken to a clean paper-towel-lined plate. Reuse the frying oil for subsequent loads; the times are first checks, not doneness guarantees.

Use the retained frying oil: Drain excess frying oil, retaining the corresponding scaled share for the aromatics: the original batch leaves 1 tablespoon from its measured ⅓ cup. This is retained frying oil, not another oil addition. Set the wok over medium-high heat, add ginger and stir about 20 seconds until fragrant.
Add garlic, chilies and scallion whites: Add dried red chili peppers (if using) and garlic cloves and all the reserved scallion whites. Stir-fry for about 15 seconds, keeping the garlic moving.

Dissolve the sugar: Add soy sauce, brown sugar, and hot water or low-sodium chicken stock, bring to a simmer and stir until the sugar dissolves. Simmer for about 2 minutes, watching that the small amount of liquid does not reduce to a scorched film.

Thicken and coat: Stir the prepared slurry again and add it slowly, letting each addition thicken before adding more. Stop when the sauce coats the back of a spoon; the full prepared slurry may not be needed. Add all the cooked chicken and reserved scallion greens, then toss for about 10 seconds until the sauce clings. If there is still excess thin sauce, add a little more of the remaining prepared slurry and stir until thickened. Check chicken for 165°F / 74°C before serving. Discard unused slurry and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Moroccan-Inspired Carrot Salad with Orange and Mint
recipes.description: Coarsely grated carrots with a light citrus dressing, mint and a restrained optional orange-blossom aroma.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp sugar, optional and only if needed
1/4 tsp orange blossom water, optional, plus up to 1/4 tsp more to taste
1/2 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1/4 cup fresh mint, thinly sliced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Grate carrots: Use the coarse holes of a box grater or a food-processor shredding disc. Transfer to a bowl. If loose liquid has already collected, pour it away without squeezing the shreds dry.

Mix and taste the dressing: Whisk orange juice, lemon juice, olive oil, cumin, paprika, cinnamon, optional cayenne and half the salt. Add the optional quarter-teaspoon orange-blossom water and taste a small amount with a carrot shred. Add sugar or more blossom water only if the balance needs it.

Dress and chill: Toss dressing through carrots, adding the optional raisins if chosen. Cover and refrigerate for about 20 minutes to let the shreds soften lightly. There is no need for a long warm countertop rest.

Finish freshly: Slice mint and chop parsley just before serving, fold them through and taste. Add remaining salt only if needed. Toss up any dressing from the bottom and divide into six side portions. If excess water has accumulated, drain a little before the final seasoning check.

recipes.keywords: Moroccan-inspired, North African, bright, sweet, tangy, warm, fresh, weeknight, family-meal, picnic, make-ahead, no-cook, toss

recipes.name: Moroccan-Inspired Chicken with Apricots, Chickpeas and Almonds
recipes.description: Bone-in chicken gently braised with onion, apricots and chickpeas, balanced with a measured preserved-lemon finish and toasted almonds.
recipeIngredient: 6 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1.5 kg total, fully thawed
1 tsp fine salt, divided and partly added to taste
1 small pinch saffron threads, about 0.05 g, optional, steeped in 2 tbsp warm water
1 1/2 cups (360 ml) low-sodium chicken stock, plus up to 1/2 cup (120 ml) only if needed
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) chickpeas, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
20 g preserved-lemon rind, pulp removed, rinsed if very salty and finely chopped
1 tsp honey, optional and only if needed after tasting
1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and season: Pat thighs dry. Season with half the salt and all the pepper. Measure ground spices together, slice onions, chop garlic and preserved rind, and halve apricots. If using saffron, steep it in the listed warm water while preparing the pan.

Sear in two batches: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wide Dutch oven over medium-high. Sear three thighs skin-side down about 6–8 minutes until golden, then turn for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate. Add the second tablespoon oil if the pan needs it and repeat with the remaining thighs, lowering heat if drippings scorch. If enough chicken fat rendered, reserve unused oil rather than forcing it into the pan.

Build the onion base: Pour off excess fat, leaving about 1 tbsp. Cook onions over medium 10–12 minutes until soft and lightly golden, stirring. Add garlic for 30 seconds, ground spices for another 20–30 seconds and tomato paste for 1 minute. Add stock and scrape up the browned residue.

Begin the covered braise: Add apricots, cinnamon stick and optional saffron water. Return chicken skin-side up with any collected juices. The liquid should reach partway up the meat; add a little of the extra stock only if the base is too dry. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and reduce heat to maintain quiet bubbling.

Finish meat and beans: After about 30 minutes, add chickpeas and preserved-lemon rind around the chicken. Cover and continue another 10–25 minutes, checking the thickest thighs clear of bone reach 165°F / 74°C and the meat yields readily to a fork. Add a little stock if the pan is drying. Remove the cinnamon stick.

Toast almonds: During the braise, toast almonds in a dry skillet over medium-low about 3–5 minutes, stirring, until golden and fragrant. Transfer promptly to a cool plate rather than leaving them in the hot pan.

Set sauce and seasoning: If sauce is thin, lift chicken to a clean plate and simmer the sauce uncovered briefly until spoonable. Taste before adding the remaining salt, optional honey and fresh lemon juice in small amounts. Return chicken, fold half the herbs into the sauce and let stand off heat about 5 minutes.

Serve: Give each diner one thigh with sauce, chickpeas and apricots. Scatter almonds and remaining herbs at the table. A small portion of Garlic Butter Pearl Couscous is one possible accompaniment; it has its own cooking method and portion size.

recipes.name: Challah
recipes.description: Challah is traditional Jewish bread for Shabbat and holidays. Using five eggs creates rich, brioche-like crumb.

recipeInstructions.text: Activate: In a massive bowl, whisk yeast and 1 tbsp sugar into 1 3/4 cups lukewarm water. Let stand for 10 minutes until foamy.
The Emulsion: Whisk in the oil, 4 eggs, and the remaining sugar and salt.
Incorporate: Gradually add the flour, 1 cup at a time, until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Transfer to a floured surface. Knead by hand for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic (or use a stand mixer with a dough hook).
First Rise: Place in a greased bowl, cover with plastic, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour until doubled.
Shape: Punch down the dough. Divide into two halves. Divide each half into 6 balls. Roll each ball into a 12-inch strand.
The Braid: Braid into two 6-strand loaves (see notes for braiding pattern). Place on a greased sheet.
Second Rise: Brush with beaten egg. Let rise for another 45-60 minutes.
Bake: Preheat oven to 375°F. Brush once more with egg and sprinkle with seeds. Bake for 35-40 minutes until deep mahogany brown.
Cool: Let cool completely on a rack before slicing.

recipes.keywords: Israeli, sweet, rich, weekend-project, entertaining, bake

recipes.name: Meera Sodha's Naan
recipes.description: Soft skillet naan with a little yogurt tang, browned bubbles and a tender center. Serve plain or brush the warm breads with garlic butter.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, reserved for kneading and rolling; use only as needed
2 tbsp neutral oil, for the dough
1 tsp neutral oil, for coating the dough
1 cup (240 ml) whole milk, warmed to 110–115°F / 43–46°C
2 tbsp (30 ml) whole milk, reserved only if the dough feels dry

recipeInstructions.text: Hydrate the yeast: Warm the measured cup of milk to 110–115°F / 43–46°C. Stir in the sugar and active dry yeast and leave for 5–10 minutes, until the granules have hydrated and activity appears at the surface. Do not use hot milk. Meanwhile, whisk the 500 g flour, fine salt and baking powder together in a large bowl.

Mix and knead: Add the yogurt, 2 tbsp oil and all the yeast-milk mixture to the flour. Mix until no loose pockets of flour remain, then knead on the work surface for about 5–8 minutes until smoother and elastic. Use the dusting flour sparingly. If the dough is stiff or cracks, knead in the correction milk a teaspoon at a time, only as needed for a soft, slightly tacky dough.

Let rise: Coat the dough with the separate teaspoon of oil and put it in a bowl with room to double. Cover and leave in a comfortably warm place for 60–90 minutes, until roughly doubled. Allow longer in a cool room; do not speed it up in a hot oven.

Divide and relax: Gently deflate and divide into 12 equal pieces, about 70 g each before any correction milk or dusting flour. Round into balls, cover and rest for 10 minutes. During this rest, melt the optional butter with the minced garlic in a small saucepan over low heat. Stir for about 1 minute after melting, until fragrant but not browned, then take off heat. Set out the towel-lined platter. During the final 5 minutes of the dough rest, begin heating the dry skillet over medium-high.

Heat the pan and roll: After the dry 12-inch cast-iron skillet has heated for about 5 minutes, roll two balls on a lightly dusted surface into ovals about 5 by 8 inches and roughly 1/8 inch / 3 mm thick. Keep the remaining balls covered. If a piece springs back, cover it for another 5–10 minutes and work on another. Do not stack uncooked ovals directly together.

Cook one bread: Brush loose flour off the oval and lay it flat in the hot pan. Cook about 30–45 seconds, until bubbles form and the underside has brown patches. Flip and cook about 30–45 seconds more. Flip again for about 10–20 seconds, pressing an undercooked edge lightly against the pan if needed. Check the first bread by tearing through a thick section near its center: there should be no sticky, raw dough inside. Adjust heat and time for the next round; a few dark freckles are enough, and blackening the whole surface is not the aim. Do not taste raw dough.

Wrap and repeat: Brush the hot bread with a little of the optional garlic butter, sharing the full amount across twelve, then enclose in the towel. Cook the second rolled bread. Between rounds, take the pan briefly off the burner while rolling the next pair; return it to the heat and let it recover before cooking. Wipe away scorched flour with a dry folded paper towel held in tongs. Allow about 30–40 minutes for rolling, pan adjustments and all twelve cooking rounds.

Serve: Bring the wrapped stack to the table promptly. Twelve breads make six portions of two, or twelve smaller one-bread accompaniments. If serving rice as well, start with one naan per person and offer the rest as wanted.

recipes.name: Nana Ruth’s Applesauce
recipes.description: This traditional applesauce appears on Jewish holiday tables for Rosh Hashanah, Thanksgiving, and Hanukkah. McIntosh apples have thin skin and high water content, allowing them to break down into naturally velvety texture without needing a blender.

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Core and peel the apples. Cut into large chunks.
The Rinse: Place apple chunks in a heavy nonstick pot. Fill with water, rinse, and repeat, leaving about 1/4 inch of water at the bottom of the pot.
Season: Squeeze the lemon over the apples. Add the honey, sugar, cinnamon, and nutmeg.
Boil: Bring to a boil over high heat. Immediately cover and reduce heat to very low.
Simmer: Cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The apples should be very soft and falling apart.
The Crush: Use a potato masher or the side of a heavy spoon to crush the apples against the side of the pot into a chunky, uniform sauce.
Serve: Best served warm with a dusting of extra cinnamon.

recipes.name: Nana’s Biscuits
recipes.description: Nana’s biscuits are mixed by hand, rolled into small balls and flattened with the palm. Keep the butter version’s fat cold and handle the dough gently.
recipeIngredient: 1/4 cup Unsalted Butter, cold and cubed
Butter, for greasing the baking sheet
Self-rising flour, for dusting as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Lightly grease a metal baking sheet with butter. If you plan to broil the tops, use a broiler-rated pan without parchment and follow your oven’s rack-clearance instructions.
Cut the fat: Put the sifted self-rising flour in a large bowl. Rub in all the cold cubed butter with your fingertips until coarse crumbs and some pea-sized butter pieces remain.

Mix gently: Add the listed buttermilk and pinch of baking soda. Mix gently by hand just until the dough comes together. If dry flour remains, add extra buttermilk a little at a time; if too sticky to handle, use a light dusting of self-rising flour.

Shape: Roll into similarly sized small balls and flatten slightly with your palm on the greased sheet. The original-size butter batch plans about 12; follow the listed scaled count without enlarging the biscuits or crowding the sheet.

Bake and serve: Bake for about 10–12 minutes until the centers have set. If baked through but still pale on top, broil briefly, watching continuously and removing the pan as soon as the color develops, about 1 minute. Broiling colors the top; it does not replace baking the middle. Let the biscuits stand briefly before serving.

recipes.name: New York Crunch Roll
recipes.description: Tuna, avocado and cucumber rolled with a small layer of crisp tempura flakes. Add the crunch just before rolling and eat promptly while it still has texture.
recipeIngredient: 230 g trimmed boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna, weighed after removing tough connective tissue; see raw-service sourcing note
150 g ripe avocado flesh, from about 1 medium avocado
100 g English cucumber, weighed after removing the watery seed core
1/3 cup ready-to-eat tempura flakes (tenkasu or agedama), not uncooked batter mix
4 full sheets unseasoned roasted nori, about 19 x 20 cm each; trim as directed
120 ml water, for dampening hands and the knife
1 tsp unseasoned rice vinegar, for the hand-dipping water

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare rice and equipment: Make Sushi Rice (Shari), weigh out 320 g and refrigerate surplus rice promptly. Let the rolling portion become barely warm during final preparation. Wrap a clean mat in food-safe film. Mix water and vinegar for lightly dampening fingers and the knife; it is not a sanitizer. Do not dip a raw-filling-coated hand or blade into this clean water. Wash hands and clean the blade before returning to it, use a separate damp cloth for wiping the cutting blade, and replace the water if contaminated.

Prepare vegetables: Wash the cucumber, remove the watery core and weigh 100 g; cut into slender matchsticks and pat dry. Near rolling time, halve the avocado, lift its pit out with a spoon, scoop out the flesh and weigh 150 g. Slice about 5–6 mm thick. Divide cucumber into four 25 g portions and avocado into four equal portions, about 38 g each. Refrigerate briefly until needed. Keep tempura flakes sealed and dry.

Cut tuna and portion rice: With separate clean equipment, remove tough visible connective tissue, weigh the listed usable amount of cold tuna and cut across its muscle grain where visible into strips about 6–10 mm thick. Short strips can be laid end to end. Divide into four equal portions of about 58 g and refrigerate. Clean the work area and hands. Divide rice into four 80 g portions using a clean utensil.

Lay out the first roll: Trim the first full nori sheet to about 19 x 15 cm and save its dry offcut airtight for another use. Leave the other sheets untrimmed until the first closure check. Place one rectangle shiny side down with its 19 cm edge nearest you. Lightly dampen fingers and shake off extra water, then spread one rice portion evenly, leaving a 1 cm bare strip along the far edge. Take out one portion each of tuna, avocado and cucumber and arrange in a compact horizontal line about 4 cm from the near edge.

Add crunch and roll: Sprinkle one quarter of the tempura flakes, about 1 tbsp plus 1 tsp, along the filling immediately before rolling. Lift the mat's near edge and tuck nori and rice over the filling. Lift the mat clear as you continue forward so it stays outside the roll. Seal on the bare nori edge, barely moistening it if necessary, then press gently through the mat without crushing the avocado. Check the first roll's closure, then cut and serve it following the next step. Trim the remaining sheets to match and continue one roll at a time, cutting and serving each as it is completed for the clearest crunch. Do not build a rice ridge.

Cut and serve: Set seam-side down briefly while preparing a sharp knife. Wipe and lightly dampen the blade, cut each roll in half, then halve each section twice for eight pieces per roll. Wipe and dampen between cuts as needed. Serve promptly as 32 pieces, about two main portions or four appetizer portions. Keep unused fish portions cold while working.

recipes.name: No-Cook Playdough
recipes.description: While not edible, this no-cook playdough stays soft and pliable for months. Cream of tartar acts as preservative and stiffener, preventing stickiness.
recipeIngredient: Liquid Watercolors or Wilton Icing Colors

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, salt, and cream of tartar until perfectly combined.
The Emulsion: In a separate heatproof jug, mix the boiling water and vegetable oil. If using one color for the whole batch, add the coloring to the liquid now.
Combine: Slowly pour the liquid into the dry ingredients. Stir with a large spoon until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead: Once cool enough to handle, dump the dough onto a clean surface. Knead vigorously for 2-3 minutes until it becomes completely smooth, elastic, and non-sticky.
Finish: If you want multiple colors, divide the white dough and knead the colors into each portion separately.
Store: Keep in an airtight container or a zip-top bag to maintain the "Bounce."

recipes.name: Noodle Pudding
recipes.description: Adapted from Mary Later’s recipe. Coarsely crushed corn flakes hold more texture than powder on the rich noodle custard.
recipeIngredient: unsalted butter, as needed for greasing dishes
water, enough to boil the noodles
salt, as desired for the noodle water
8 oz unsalted butter, melted and cooled until lukewarm
2 cups corn flakes, coarsely crushed; measure after crushing
1/4 cup golden raisins, for half the pudding only, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare dishes: Heat the oven to 325°F with a rack in the center. For the original batch, use unsalted butter to grease a room-temperature 9×13-inch glass dish, preferably the existing deep 4-quart plan, and have a smaller greased oven-safe overflow dish ready. Follow the actual dish’s temperature and thermal-shock instructions.

Cook noodles: Set out medium-width egg noodles, water, and salt. Bring the salted water to a boil, then add the full dry noodle amount and cook just to al dente, following its package as a guide. Drain well and let the noodles cool until warm, not steaming hot, before adding to the custard.

Mix custard: Set out sour cream, large-curd cottage cheese, block-style cream cheese, 3/4 of the unsalted butter, large eggs, granulated sugar, and ground cinnamon. Beat the softened cream cheese with a little sour cream until smooth, then mix in the remaining sour cream and all the cottage cheese, eggs, granulated sugar, cinnamon and allocated butter, keeping the cottage-cheese curds if desired. The butter allocation here is three-quarters of the full butter amount; reserve the other quarter for the topping. Use lukewarm butter and warm noodles so they do not cook the eggs on contact.

Combine and divide: Fold all the warm noodles into all the custard. Set out golden raisins (if using). For a half-raisin pudding, divide the noodle mixture in half and add all the optional raisins to only one half. Spoon the two mixtures into opposite sides of the greased dish; omit raisins for an entirely plain pudding. Leave at least 1/2 inch below the rim for topping and slight puffing. Put excess mixture in the overflow dish rather than filling to the brim.

Coat topping: Toss 1/4 of the unsalted butter, corn flakes, and light brown sugar until all the coarse corn flakes are coated with the remaining one-quarter butter and packed brown sugar. Scatter across the full noodle mixture without pressing down. With an overflow dish, divide topping in proportion to surface area.

Bake and check the center: Bake at 325°F, beginning checks around 60 minutes for the original deep dish; 65–80 minutes is the existing planning range. The edges should be set, the center should have only a slight wobble with no liquid custard, and its center must reach 165°F /74°C. Check every dish; smaller overflow portions may finish earlier. Loosely tent if the topping colors before the center is ready.
Rest and serve: Set hot glass on a dry trivet following the vessel’s instructions. Rest 15 minutes before dividing into the listed portions. Keep the raisin and plain halves distinct when serving.

recipes.name: Oatmeal Risotto
recipes.description: Oatmeal risotto treats steel-cut oats with the same respect Italians give Arborio rice - an overnight soak followed by a slow simmer until each grain is creamy outside and slightly chewy at the center. The mashed banana folded in at the end acts like the butter-and-cheese mantecatura in real risotto, creating body without dairy.
recipeIngredient: 3 cups Chicken Broth or Filtered Water

recipeInstructions.text: The Hydration: In a medium bowl, combine the oats and water/broth. Cover and refrigerate overnight at 40°F or below. Keep the oats and all soaking liquid cold until ready to cook.
The Acid Balance: In a small bowl, pour the sherry vinegar over the golden raisins. Let soak while the oats cook.
Simmer: Pour the oats and their soaking liquid into a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer. Add brown sugar and salt.
Cook: Cook for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are "squeaky" to the bite (al dente).
The Emulsion: Fold in the mashed banana. Cook for 2 more minutes until the banana has melted into the oats, creating a creamy "Bounce."
Serve: Divide into bowls. Top with the vinegar-soaked raisins and a few generous shavings of Parmesan cheese for the final savory High Note.

recipes.name: Soft Pumpkin Cookies
recipes.description: These autumn cookies achieve incredible softness by whisking pumpkin puree directly into creamed butter and sugar, ensuring moisture is fully emulsified before flour is added. The butter-sugar glaze adds sweetness that balances earthy spices.

recipeInstructions.text: Dry Mix: Whisk together flour, baking soda, baking powder, and spices.
Cream: In a large bowl, beat softened butter and sugar until fluffy. Add the pumpkin, egg, and vanilla; beat until smooth.
Combine: Gradually add the dry mix until just combined. The batter will be very soft and scoopable.
Shape: Drop by rounded tablespoons onto greased sheets.
Bake: Bake at 350°F for 15-18 minutes until the edges are firm and the tops are slightly golden.
Glaze: Whisk glaze ingredients until smooth. Drizzle over warm cookies.
Serve: Let cool for 10 minutes to allow the glaze to set into a "Snap."

recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Strawberry Ice Cream
recipes.description: Sliced strawberries macerated in lemon juice and sugar for several hours draw out natural syrup and soften the fruit, preventing them from freezing into icy chunks. Tempering yolks with hot milk and vanilla bean ensures dense, custardy texture that showcases bright strawberries perfectly.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Macerate: Toss strawberries with lemon juice and 1/4 cup sugar. Refrigerate for at least 3 hours until syrupy.
Custard Base: In a saucepan, heat milk, cream, and vanilla bean seeds until simmering.
Emulsify: In a large bowl, whisk yolks, salt, and remaining sugars until pale. Slowly whisk in the hot cream to temper.
Thicken: Return mixture to the pan. Cook over medium-low, stirring constantly, until the custard coats a spoon. Do not boil.
Chill: Remove vanilla pod. Let cool for 30 minutes, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours until ice-cold.
Churn: Stir the macerated strawberries (including all juice) into the custard. Pour into ice cream maker and process for 25-35 minutes.
Set: Freeze for 2 hours to harden into the Kitchen Standard texture.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, acidic, rich, herbaceous, entertaining, comfort-food, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Old-Fashioned Vanilla Ice Cream
recipes.description: Gradually whisk hot milk into yolks and sugar, then stir the custard over gentle heat to 165°F. Stop before it boils.

recipeInstructions.text: The Base: In a small saucepan, heat milk and the pinch of salt over medium-low until just simmering.
Emulsify: In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolks and sugar until pale yellow. Slowly stream in the hot milk while whisking constantly.
Thicken: Return the mixture to the pan. Stir constantly over gentle heat until it reaches 165°F and coats the back of a spoon. Remove from the heat immediately. Do not boil.

The Chill: Transfer to a shallow container and refrigerate promptly for at least 4 hours, until thoroughly cold, at 40°F / 4°C or below. Prepare the ice cream maker, including freezing its bowl if required, according to its instructions.

Churn: Stir in the chilled heavy cream and vanilla bean paste. Pour into your prepared ice cream maker, respecting its liquid-fill limit. Churn in batches if needed and keep waiting base refrigerated.
Set: Churn according to instructions (usually 20 mins). Transfer to a freezer-safe container and freeze for 2 hours before serving.

recipes.name: Old Fashioned
recipes.description: The Old Fashioned dates to the 1880s, when bartenders started getting fancy with cocktails, adding fruit and elaborate garnishes. Patrons who wanted their drinks made the 'old fashioned way' - just whiskey, sugar, water, and bitters - gave the drink its name.

recipeInstructions.text: Place the sugar cube: in an Old Fashioned glass and saturate with bitters. Add a splash of water.
Muddle the sugar until: dissolved (or simply add simple syrup instead).
Add the whiskey and: fill the glass with one large ice cube.
Stir gently for 10-15: seconds.
Express an orange peel: over the drink by holding it over the glass and giving it a good twist to release the oils. Rub the peel around the rim of the glass and drop it in.
Optionally add a maraschino: cherry. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Orange-Rosemary Chicken with Beets and Fennel
recipes.description: Skin-on chicken thighs with roasted beets, carrots and fennel, finished with orange, garlic and a little butter.
recipeIngredient: 4 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, about 1 kg total, fully thawed
600 g peeled beets, cut into 1/4-inch-thick half-moons
300 g peeled carrots, cut into pieces no thicker than 1/2 inch
300 g trimmed fennel bulb, cut into 1/2-inch wedges with a little core holding each together
2 tsp finely chopped fresh rosemary leaves

recipeInstructions.text: Heat and prepare: Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Cut vegetables evenly and pat chicken skin dry. Mix orange juice, zest, melted butter, rosemary and all the garlic in a small bowl; keep aside for the final stage.

Start roots first: Toss beets and carrots with 2 tbsp oil, half the salt and half the pepper on one rimmed sheet. Spread into one layer and roast for 15 minutes. If your sheet cannot hold that layer, use a larger pan or accept an additional cooking batch rather than piling the roots.

Add the chicken tray: On the second sheet, toss fennel with the remaining tablespoon oil and arrange it around the thighs, keeping the skin exposed. Divide remaining salt and pepper over chicken and fennel; sprinkle chili powder over the chicken. Put this tray in the oven, leaving the root tray cooking too.

Roast to separate endpoints: Roast another 40–50 minutes, swapping the trays' rack positions halfway through and turning vegetables. Begin checking thighs around 35 minutes after they enter: the thickest meat, clear of bone, must reach 165°F / 74°C, and the joint should move easily. Check roots with a fork. Remove any component that finishes early instead of letting it overcook.

Finish the vegetables: During the final 8–10 minutes of vegetable cooking, spoon the orange-garlic mixture over the roots and fennel, keeping it off chicken skin. Stir the vegetables and return them to the oven so the garlic cooks and the juice reduces a little. If chicken finishes first, transfer it to a clean plate and continue finishing vegetables separately.

Rest briefly and serve: Let cooked thighs rest about 5 minutes. Divide vegetables among four plates and serve one thigh with each. Spoon a little vegetable-pan liquid around the meat rather than over the skin. Add no extra orange until you taste the finish.

recipes.keywords: American, spicy, sweet, acidic, rich, weekend-dinner, date-night, entertaining, bake, roast

recipes.name: One-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken Thighs
recipes.description: Lemon, oregano and thyme give this skillet chicken its Mediterranean-style flavor. Brown the skin first, keep it above the sauce while roasting where possible, and judge thigh temperature and optional vegetable tenderness separately.
recipeIngredient: 8 bone-in skin-on chicken thighs, raw, fresh or fully thawed; original eight-thigh batch is about 2.5–3 lb total
2 lemons, washed, zested and juiced; reserve all juice and zest from these same lemons
1 lb potatoes or root vegetables, washed, peeled if wanted and cut into 1-inch pieces, optional
fresh parsley, as wanted for garnish, washed and chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat and season: Preheat the oven to 425°F. Use an oven-safe skillet with room for all the measured thighs in one layer and, if using them, the vegetables; use additional oven-safe vessels if necessary. Pat all the measured thighs dry and season both sides with all kosher salt and black pepper. Divide every measured ingredient proportionally among any extra vessels; do not add extra oil or stock.

Sear the chicken: Heat the assigned two-thirds of olive oil over medium-high heat and use bone-in skin-on chicken thighs and 2/3 of the olive oil for searing. Put chicken skin-side down without crowding; work in loads if needed, using this same measured oil supply across the loads. Cook about 5–6 minutes until deeply golden and releasing from the pan, then turn and cook about 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate; keep all rendered fat in the cooking pan.

Cook aromatics: Use 1/3 of the olive oil, garlic cloves, fresh oregano, and fresh thyme for this stage. Reduce heat to medium, add the remaining one-third of the measured oil and all the garlic, and sauté for 30–45 seconds until fragrant. Then stir in all the oregano and thyme for about 15 seconds; do not let the garlic blacken.

Add lemon and stock: Use lemons and chicken stock or water to deglaze: pour in all the juice from the measured lemons and the stock or water, scrape the browned bits, then stir in all the reserved zest. Keep the whole sauce and rendered fat.

Return chicken and optional vegetables: Return all the partly cooked chicken and its plate juices to the pan, skin-side up, keeping skin above the liquid where possible. Nestle potatoes or root vegetables (if using) around the thighs. Transfer the oven-safe vessel or vessels to the preheated oven; do not crowd or stack the thighs.

Finish to temperature and tenderness: Start checking after 12–15 minutes without vegetables, or 15–18 minutes with them. These are first checks, not guaranteed finishing times. Every thigh must reach 165°F / 74°C in its thickest part away from the bone. Vegetables must be fork-tender; if chicken finishes first, remove it with clean utensils to a clean platter and continue cooking the vegetables and full sauce. Check raw-contact sauce and vegetables reach 165°F / 74°C before tasting or serving them, stirring liquid for a representative reading. Larger loads or different roots can need longer.

Rest and garnish: Rest cooked chicken for 5 minutes. Once chicken and the raw-contact sauce/vegetables have reached their endpoints, taste the sauce and scatter fresh parsley over the finished dish. Serve all the sauce and rendered fat with the chicken.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, Italian, bright, savory, herbaceous, weeknight, meal-prep, roast, sear

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken Meatballs with Greens
recipes.description: Yogurt and panko bind these Italian-American-style garlic-and-oregano chicken meatballs. Brown them gently, then cover them with chard and lemon slices to finish cooking in the greens’ moisture.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb ground chicken, raw; fresh or fully thawed
olive oil, as needed to coat palms
additional olive oil, as needed if the pan dries during browning
1 lb Swiss chard, washed; tender stalks sliced and leaves cut into 1-inch ribbons
1 lemon, washed; half thinly sliced and half reserved for finishing juice
salt, to taste for the greens

recipeInstructions.text: Mix gently: Combine all ground chicken, plain Greek yogurt, panko breadcrumbs, garlic cloves, scallions, dried oregano, red pepper flakes, and salt in a bowl, mixing just until evenly combined. The oregano and red pepper belong to this mixture; reserve cumin for the greens. Keep the raw chicken mixture cold if preparation pauses and do not taste it raw.

Shape meatballs: Use olive oil to lightly coat your palms, refreshing the coating as needed, and form all the mixture into uniform balls about 2 inches across. The original batch plans about 14 meatballs; at other batch sizes keep the size similar and use the entire mixture rather than holding the count fixed.

Brown meatballs: Use a heavy pot with a tight lid and a broad base; the original route uses a 12-inch Dutch oven. Heat over medium, then use additional olive oil and 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, starting with half of the measured oil supply and adding the separate unmeasured browning allowance only if needed. Add the meatballs without crowding and turn gently when they release, about 7 minutes for initial browning. This is not their final temperature check. Use additional cooking vessels when the complete batch and greens cannot fit; divide the whole measured formula proportionally.

Dress greens: Meanwhile, in a clean bowl toss all Swiss chard, 1/2 of the lemon, 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, ground cumin, and salt, using the remaining half of the measured oil and half the measured lemons as thin slices. Scrunch the leaves to coat; reserve the other lemon half for serving.

Cover with greens: Pile all the dressed greens and lemon slices directly over all the browned meatballs. Cover tightly and cook over medium for about 12–15 minutes as an initial estimate. The covered greens release moisture to finish cooking the meatballs.

Check centers: Continue covered cooking until meatball centers reach 165°F / 74°C and the greens and tender stalks have softened. Check large meatballs and different pot positions with a thermometer; browning alone does not establish the endpoint. Extra loads or a deeper mound of greens can take longer.

Scoop and finish: Scoop the meatballs and greens onto plates, spooning all the cooking juices over them. Use all 1/2 of the lemon for the finish: squeeze the reserved lemon juice over the portions. Use clean serving utensils.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, saute, simmer, steam, braise

recipes.name: One-Pot Chicken, Quinoa & Mushrooms
recipes.description: Chicken thighs and quinoa finish together after mushrooms are browned, with spinach and lemon added at the end.
recipeIngredient: 6 boneless skinless chicken thighs, about 150 g each
255 g dry white quinoa, rinsed and well drained
2 1/2 cups (600 ml) low-sodium chicken broth, plus a little hot water if needed
150 g fresh spinach, washed and roughly chopped
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Sear in batches: Pat chicken dry and season with half the salt, pepper, rosemary, and paprika. Heat two teaspoons oil in a wide deep sauté pan over medium-high heat. Sear three thighs at a time for about 2–3 minutes per side, lowering heat if spices darken too quickly. Transfer to a plate; the centers are not yet cooked.

Brown mushrooms: Add remaining oil, mushrooms, onion, and remaining salt. Cook about 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushroom liquid has mostly evaporated and golden patches appear. Scrape up browned material without burning it.
Add grains and broth: Stir in drained quinoa and broth. Bring to a gentle simmer, then nestle chicken and its juices into the quinoa in one layer. Cover tightly and reduce to a gentle simmer.

Check both components: Cook about 18–22 minutes. Probe each thigh for 165°F / 74°C and check quinoa in several places for the same temperature before tasting it. The seeds should be tender with a little bite and most free liquid absorbed. Extend gently if needed, using the component-specific fixes in troubleshooting rather than overcooking everything together.
Wilt and rest: When chicken and quinoa meet their checks, scatter spinach over the pan. Cover and heat gently for about 2 minutes until wilted. Remove from heat and rest covered for 5 minutes.

Finish with lemon: Lift chicken briefly to a clean plate, fold spinach through quinoa, and stir in half the lemon juice. Taste and add the remainder as needed. Divide quinoa and vegetables into six portions and add one thigh to each.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, smoky, weeknight, meal-prep, comfort-food, sear, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Spicy Thai Noodles
recipes.description: This Thai-inspired pasta uses the same pot for boiling noodles, scrambling eggs, and sautéing vegetables. Divide the oil between the eggs and vegetables, then toss everything with the soy-ginger sauce.
recipeIngredient: Red pepper flakes, a pinch, optional
Fully cooked chicken or shrimp, optional addition, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Cook pasta in a large pot of salted water according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, brown sugar, Sriracha, and grated ginger until smooth.
The Eggs: In the same large pot, heat 1 tbsp oil. Scramble the eggs with the optional red pepper flakes until fully set, with no liquid egg remaining. Remove and set aside with the pasta.
The Veg: Add the remaining half of the oil to the pot. Sauté zucchini, mushrooms, and carrots for 5 minutes over high heat until tender-crisp.
Bind: Turn heat to low. Return the pasta and eggs to the pot, along with any optional fully cooked chicken or shrimp. Pour the sauce over everything.
Toss: Toss until the pasta is evenly coated and everything is hot, about 1–2 minutes. If using refrigerated leftover protein, heat it to 165°F / 74°C throughout; the final toss may take longer.
Serve: Remove from heat. Stir in the green onions, cilantro, and crushed peanuts. Serve immediately, or refrigerate promptly for chilled servings.

recipes.keywords: Thai, spicy, sweet, savory, umami, weeknight, quick-lunch, saute, boil

recipes.name: Onigiri (Japanese Rice Balls)
recipes.description: Onigiri are Japanese rice balls - simple, transportable, and a staple of bentos and home cooking for centuries. What makes them special is the ritual: the rice is still warm when shaped, and the small amount of salt on your hands seasons the outside just enough.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Cooked Japanese Short-Grain Rice (warm or room temperature)
Filling A: 4 oz Canned Tuna, drained and mixed with 1 tbsp Mayo + 1 tsp Soy Sauce
Filling C: 1/4 cup Salmon Flakes (fresh cooked or canned) mixed with 1/2 tsp Soy Sauce
Filling D: 2 tbsp Sesame Seeds mixed with 1/2 tsp Sea Salt
Water in a small bowl (for wet hands)

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description:
Filling Ideas: Keep fillings minimal - a single flavor is more traditional. Tuna mayo, umeboshi (pickled plum), grilled salmon, kombu (kelp), or just sesame salt all work beautifully.

Hand Temperature: Warm hands make shaping easier and prevent the rice from cooling too much. If your hands get cold, re-wet with warm water and re-salt.

Nori Texture: For maximum crispness, wrap nori just before serving. For softer nori, wrap 30 minutes ahead and let the moisture from the rice soften it slightly.

itemListElement.text: Cook the Rice: If starting from scratch, prepare 1 cup Japanese short-grain rice according to package directions (usually 1:1 ratio with water). Let rest for 10 minutes after cooking. Use warm rice for the best texture when shaping.

Prepare the Work Surface: Have a small bowl of water nearby. Wet your hands slightly and sprinkle a pinch of salt into your palm. This is crucial - it prevents sticking and adds a subtle salty flavor to the outer rice.

Form the Triangle (Basic Shape): Take about 1/2 cup cooked rice in your palm. Make a small indent in the center with your thumb, creating a pocket about the size of a marble. Place 1 tbsp of your chosen filling into the pocket.

Encase the Filling: Cup your hand to gently bring rice up and around the filling, enclosing it completely. You should have a ball of rice with filling inside. Squeeze gently but firmly - you want it compact enough to hold together but not so tight that it becomes dense.

Shape into Triangle: Place the rice ball on your work surface. Using both hands (re-wet and re-salt if needed), gently shape it into a triangle by applying even pressure on three sides. The shape comes from your hands, not from pressing into a mold. A triangular onigiri is iconic and practical - it sits flat and is easy to wrap.

Wrap with Nori: Cut nori into strips about 1 inch wide and 3-4 inches long. Wrap one strip around the middle of the onigiri, like a belt. The nori will stick to the rice from its slight moisture. If wrapping right before serving, the nori stays crispy; if you wrap earlier, it softens slightly from the rice moisture.

Garnish and Store: Sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired. Serve warm or at room temperature. For make-ahead service, refrigerate promptly at 40°F or below and transport with an ice pack. Count preparation and service together: discard perishable onigiri left out over 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. If frozen, thaw in the refrigerator rather than on the counter. Keep nori separate until serving for crispness.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, savory, umami, weeknight, meal-prep, entertaining, lunch, shape

recipes.name: Orange and Paprika Pulled Pork
recipes.description: Orange and paprika season this shoulder, distinct from the smoked-salt pulled pork. Cook until it pulls apart with little resistance, then spoon back cooking juices as needed.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Start with fully thawed pork kept refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual cooker’s load and whole-roast size requirements. Place the diced onion, chopped garlic and all the orange juice in the cooker.

Season: Mix all the paprika, oregano, salt, pepper and cumin. Trim excess external fat, keeping the shoulder’s internal marbling; rub all the measured spice mixture over the shoulder and put it in the cooker.

Cook: Cover and cook on LOW for about 8 hours. Start with fully thawed pork. The shoulder should be fork-tender, commonly around 195–205°F; the food-safety minimum is 145°F / 63°C with three minutes rest. Continue cooking if it does not pull apart easily. Keep the cooker covered except for necessary checks.

Shred: Move the fully cooked shoulder to a clean board or plate and pull apart with two forks. If it resists, return it to covered cooking rather than force it into dry chunks. Remove any bone when present.

Moisten and serve: Spoon some of the hot cooking juices over the shredded pork until it is moist without flooding it; retain the rest for serving if wanted. Divide among the listed portions and serve.

recipes.keywords: American, slow-cook

recipes.name: Chocolate Sandwich Cookie Cheesecake
recipes.description: A dense chocolate cheesecake with a thin chocolate-cookie base, chocolate-creme cookie pieces through the filling and more cookies baked on top.
recipeIngredient: 32 regular-size chocolate sandwich cookies with chocolate-flavored creme, about 14–15 g each, divided; keep the creme filling
32 oz (907 g) full-fat block cream cheese, softened as directed
8 oz (227 g) semisweet baking chocolate, chopped
1 tsp neutral oil, for greasing the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the pan and cookies: Once the cheese is softened as described above, heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C with a rack in the middle. Grease the bottom and sides of the springform pan with the measured oil. Finely crush twelve whole cookies, creme included. Quarter the other twenty cookies and keep all their crumbs. Measure a level 1 1/2 cups of these pieces and crumbs without packing for the filling; set all the remaining pieces aside for the top.

Bake the crust and melt the chocolate: Press the fine crumbs evenly and firmly across the bottom of the pan, with no bare patches. Set the pan on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 10 minutes. Cool on a rack while mixing the filling. Put the chopped chocolate in a dry microwave-safe bowl and heat at half power in 20–30-second bursts, stirring between each, until just melted. Let it become lukewarm but still fluid; avoid getting water in it.

Smooth the cheese: Beat the softened cream cheese, sugar and vanilla at low to medium-low speed until smooth, about 2–3 minutes, stopping to scrape the bottom and sides of the bowl. Mix in the lukewarm chocolate until the color is even. Scrape again; avoid whipping the mixture fluffy.

Add eggs and cookies: Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing only until each disappears. Scrape the bowl and fold in the measured 1 1/2 cups of cookie pieces with a spatula. Do not taste the raw batter. Spread gently over the cooled crust and scatter all the remaining quartered cookies and crumbs over the top.

Bake to a set center: Bake on the rimmed sheet for about 50–70 minutes, checking at 50 minutes. The edges should be set and the central few inches should tremble together when the pan is nudged, without a liquid wave. Check the filling in the center with an instant-read thermometer, avoiding cookie pieces and the pan base; it must reach at least 160°F / 71°C. Continue in 5-minute intervals if needed, then remove to a rack.

Cool and chill: After about 10 minutes, carefully run a thin knife between the cake and the pan wall without opening the clasp. Cool on the rack for about 1 hour total, then refrigerate in the pan, loosely covered and with space around it. Refrigerate within 2 hours of leaving the oven, or within 1 hour if the kitchen is above 90°F / 32°C. Once cold, cover well. Chill for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until cold and firm through the center.

Unmold and slice: Release the clasp and lift off the ring; leave the cake on its base for support. Cut into sixteen slices with a sharp knife, wiping it clean between cuts. Serve chilled, with coffee or unsweetened tea if desired.
