recipes.name: Saffron Cardamom Rice
recipes.description: Buttery basmati with saffron milk, green cardamom and golden onion, gently simmered and rested before fluffing.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 cups (about 300 g) aged white basmati rice, not parboiled or quick-cooking
2 1/2 cups (600 ml) water, for cooking, plus water for rinsing
6 green cardamom pods, lightly cracked but kept together
1 black cardamom pod, optional, lightly cracked
1 small cinnamon stick, about 1 1/2 inches long
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only for correcting firm grains
2 tbsp toasted unsalted sliced almonds or chopped pistachios, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Steep the saffron: Warm the milk until steaming but not boiling, in a small saucepan or in brief microwave bursts in a heatproof bowl. Lightly crumble the measured saffron threads into it and steep for at least 15 minutes while continuing with the rice and onion. Keep all the threads and liquid.

Rinse and prepare: Rinse basmati gently in several changes of cool water until much of the loose starch washes away. Drain thoroughly without soaking. Slice the onion thinly and lightly crack the cardamom pods. Measure the remaining spices, water and salt before heating the ghee.

Cook spices and onion: Heat ghee in the heavy saucepan over medium heat. Add green cardamom, optional black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf; stir 20–30 seconds until fragrant. Add onion and cook for about 10–15 minutes, stirring often, until soft and lightly golden with a few browned edges. Lower the heat if the spices darken rapidly. This is a golden onion base, not a dark caramelized one.

Coat rice and add all liquid: Fold in drained rice and stir gently for about 1 minute to coat it with ghee. Add the measured cooking water, all the saffron milk and threads, and the salt. Stir once and bring to a gentle boil, allowing about 5 minutes to heat. Cover snugly and lower the heat to maintain a very gentle simmer.

Simmer and check: Cook for about 15–20 minutes. Near the end, briefly part the rice at the edge and taste a grain: the liquid should be absorbed and the center tender. If firm and dry, use the measured hot-water reserve as described in troubleshooting. If firm with liquid remaining, re-cover and cook a little longer. Do not force the rice dry over high heat.

Rest, fluff and finish: Once the grains are tender and free liquid is absorbed, turn off the heat and rest covered for 10 minutes. Remove visible cardamom pods, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf; let diners know that small pieces may remain. Lift and fluff gently with a fork or rice paddle, folding in cilantro. Add the optional toasted nuts at serving. Expect roughly 4 1/2–5 cups, enough for four generous rice sides or smaller portions beside dal and potatoes.

recipes.keywords: Indian, aromatic, warm, floral, buttery, entertaining, special-occasion, family-meal, saute, simmer, steam

recipes.name: Sage Brown Butter Ravioli
recipes.description: Brown butter and sage is a classic Northern Italian sauce, especially popular with filled pasta like ravioli or tortellini. The French call it beurre noisette ("hazelnut butter") for its nutty aroma.
recipeIngredient: 16 oz Butternut Squash Ravioli (fresh or frozen)
1/2 tsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)
Coarse Sea Salt and Black Pepper

recipeInstructions.text: Boil: Cook ravioli in salted water according to package directions. Drain.
Brown Butter: In a large light-colored skillet (mandatory to see color), melt butter over medium. Whisk constantly for 5 minutes until it smells like nuts and golden flecks appear.
Crisp Sage: Add the sage. Fry for 1 minute until the leaves are crispy and fragrant.
Emulsify: Carefully pour in the broth and cream (it will splatter). Whisk vigorously until a smooth, thick emulsion forms.
Bind: Stir in the Parmesan and lemon juice.
Toss: Add the cooked ravioli to the pan. Toss for 1 minute until every pillow is coated in the brown butter silk.
Serve: Garnish with extra Parmesan and a crack of black pepper.

recipes.keywords: Italian, acidic, umami, rich, weeknight, date-night, entertaining, fry, boil

recipes.name: Salsa Verde Chicken Casserole
recipes.description: This Tex-Mex casserole is a quick weeknight meal that layers chicken, tortillas, and cheese like lasagna. Whisking salsa verde into sour cream creates a tangy, creamy sauce that keeps the chicken moist during baking.

recipeInstructions.text: The Bind: In a medium bowl, whisk together the sour cream and 1 cup of the salsa verde.
Combine: Fold the shredded chicken and cilantro into the sauce.
Layer: Grease an 8x8 baking dish. Spread a thin layer of the remaining salsa on the bottom. Top with 4 halved tortillas.
Stack: Spread half the chicken mixture over the tortillas and top with 1 cup of cheese. Repeat with remaining tortillas, chicken, and cheese.
Bake: Preheat oven to 375°F. Bake for 25-30 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges are golden brown.
Finish: Remove from heat. Top with the chopped tomatoes and sliced avocado for the final High Note.
Serve: Serve hot with a side of Cilantro Lime Rice.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, acidic, rich, comfort-food, meal-prep, bake

recipes.name: San Marzano Tomato Sauce
recipes.description: This quick Italian-American tomato sauce works with stuffed shells, baked ziti, and eggplant Parmesan. Allow about twenty-five minutes for preparation, warming the pan and tomatoes, and the short simmer.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (28 oz) Crushed San Marzano Tomatoes (look for DOP certification; ingredient list should be just tomatoes and salt)
3 cloves Garlic (smashed whole for subtle infusion, or sliced for bolder flavor)
1 sprig Fresh Basil (or 1/2 tsp dried oregano)

recipeInstructions.text: The Garlic: Warm olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the smashed or sliced garlic and let it sizzle gently until fragrant and still pale, about 1–2 minutes; thin slices may finish sooner. Lower the heat if the edges begin to color.
The Tomatoes: Pour in the crushed San Marzano tomatoes. Add the whole basil sprig or the measured dried oregano. Season with a pinch of salt.
The Simmer: Let the sauce bubble gently for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce will darken slightly and thicken just enough to coat the back of a spoon.

Finish: Remove the whole basil sprig if used. Remove smashed garlic cloves if you want a subtler sauce; leave sliced garlic and dried oregano in the sauce. Taste and adjust salt. Use immediately, or refrigerate promptly in shallow containers within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F / 32°C). Keep at 40°F / 4°C or below for 3–4 days, or freeze; when reheating, bring the sauce to a rolling boil while stirring. This is a cooked refrigerator sauce, not a canning formula.

recipes.keywords: Italian, savory, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, meal-prep, simmer

recipes.name: Sausage and White Bean Skillet
recipes.description: Sausage and white beans is Italian comfort food - sausage brings the fat and seasoning, while white beans add body and earthiness. This is the kind of dish Italian grandmothers have been making for decades with whatever they had on hand.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Italian Sausage (sweet or spicy, either form - links or bulk)
2 cans Cannellini or Great Northern Beans (15 oz each), drained and rinsed

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Leftover Magic: This tastes even better the next day. Store in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat gently over medium heat, adding a splash of water or stock if it tightens.

itemListElement.text: Cook the Sausage: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. If using sausage links, slice them into 1-inch rounds. Add sausage to the dry pan and let it brown without stirring for 2 minutes. Break it apart if using bulk sausage, or stir links to brown on all sides (about 5 minutes total). Transfer to a plate.

Aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. In the same pan (don't clean it - those brown bits are flavor), add diced onion. Sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 30-45 seconds until fragrant.
Tomato Paste: Add tomato paste, oregano, thyme, and red pepper flakes. Stir constantly for 1 minute. This blooms the spices and tomato and prevents them from being raw and bitter.
Beans and Stock: Add beans and chicken stock. Stir to combine. Return sausage to the pan.
Simmer: Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 8-10 minutes until the broth reduces slightly and the flavors meld. The mixture should be thickened but still saucy.
Brighten: Remove from heat. Taste for salt and pepper. Add lemon juice and stir. The lemon should pop the dish to life - it's no longer heavy, it's bright.
Serve: Spoon into bowls. Garnish with fresh parsley and grated Parmesan. Serve with crusty bread for soaking up the broth.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, savory, herbaceous, rich, weeknight, meal-prep, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Sausage Breakfast Casserole
recipes.description: This breakfast casserole is ideal for holiday mornings because it feeds a crowd and can be assembled the night before. Baking covered first sets the egg custard without drying it out, then uncovering and increasing heat to 400°F for the final 15 minutes crisps the hash brown crust on top.
recipeIngredient: 30 oz Frozen Shredded Hash Browns, thawed

recipeInstructions.text: The Sear: In a large skillet, brown the sausage over medium-high until no pink remains. Add the bell pepper and scallion whites; sauté for 3 minutes. Let cool slightly.
The Emulsion: In a massive bowl, whisk eggs, heavy cream, mustard, hot sauce, salt, and pepper until very frothy.
Combine: Fold in the sausage mixture, 1 1/2 cups of the cheese, and the thawed hash browns.
Assemble: Pour into a greased 9x13-inch baking dish. Smooth into an even layer.
Stage 1: Cover with foil. Bake at 350°F for 50 minutes.
Stage 2: Remove foil. Top with the remaining 1/2 cup cheese. Increase oven to 400°F. Bake for 10-15 minutes until the top is deep golden and the center is firm.
Serve: Let rest for 10 minutes. Garnish with scallion greens and serve.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, holiday, comfort-food, bake, saute, no-cook

recipes.name: Sausage, Shrimp & Quinoa Skillet
recipes.description: Onion, pepper and celery provide the trinity base for the Creole seasoning. Heat the cooked quinoa before adding the shrimp so the shrimp can finish without waiting for a frozen block of grain.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb medium shrimp, raw, peeled, deveined and thawed if frozen
6 oz spicy chicken sausage, labeled fully cooked, sliced
3 1/2 cups cooked quinoa, frozen prepared according to package, or properly refrigerated leftovers
1 cup onion, pepper and celery blend, chopped
fresh parsley, for garnish, rinsed and chopped
black pepper, a pinch, to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Brown sausage and soften vegetables: Use spicy chicken sausage, onion, pepper and celery blend, and neutral oil for this stage. Heat the oil over medium-high heat in a large skillet. Add the fully cooked sliced sausage and chopped vegetables; cook, stirring, until sausage is browned and vegetables are tender, beginning checks around 5–7 minutes. Lower heat if the pan scorches.
Add seasoning: Stir in Creole seasoning briefly until fragrant, about 30 seconds, without burning it.

Heat the cooked grain: Add cooked quinoa, breaking up clumps. Stir until hot throughout; for refrigerated leftovers check 165°F / 74°C in several places. Follow frozen-product heating instructions rather than treating two minutes as sufficient for every frozen load.

Cook shrimp: Add medium shrimp. Turn through the hot grain mixture until the thickest shrimp is firm, pearly and opaque through its center. Start checking around 2–3 minutes; size, starting temperature and pan load change the time. Keep cooking if centers are translucent.

Finish: Use fresh parsley, salt, and black pepper for this stage. Taste only after the shrimp are fully cooked. Add the listed salt and pepper allowances if needed, garnish with all the parsley and divide among the listed portions. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, spicy, acidic, herbaceous, weeknight, quick-lunch, meal-prep, fry, saute

recipes.name: Sauteed Mushrooms with Thyme
recipes.description: A loose single layer gives mushroom surfaces room to brown. Divide the measured oil across the batches, then bring all mushrooms together for the full butter, garlic and thyme finish.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs Mixed Mushrooms (cremini, shiitake, oyster), cleaned and sliced
2 tbsp Dry Sherry or White Wine

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Clean mushrooms, using a brief rinse under running water if needed, then dry their surfaces well. Trim tough shiitake stems and tough oyster bases; slice usable mushrooms into even roughly 1/4-inch pieces. Wash and dry the thyme and parsley.

Brown in batches: Divide the listed olive oil across the number of batches your skillet needs. Heat a share over medium-high heat until shimmering, not smoking; add a loose single layer of mushrooms. Cook undisturbed about 3–4 minutes until the underside browns, then turn and cook about 2–3 minutes. If released liquid pools, let it evaporate before judging browning. Transfer to a plate and repeat with remaining mushrooms and shares of the same oil; do not spend the full oil amount anew each round.

Butter and aromatics: Return all mushrooms and their collected juices to the pan; use more vessels if needed for tossing and divide the measured finish among them. Reduce heat to medium. Add all butter, garlic and thyme leaves. Toss about 1–2 minutes until garlic is fragrant and lightly golden; lower heat if butter or garlic darkens quickly.

Deglaze: Add all the measured sherry or white wine. Stir and scrape loosened browned bits until the sharp wine aroma mellows and no free puddle remains; about 30 seconds is an initial check, not a guarantee of complete evaporation or alcohol removal. Add all measured salt and black pepper.
Finish: Remove from heat and distribute all parsley over the mushrooms. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: French, American, umami, savory, earthy, rich, weeknight, date-night, saute

recipes.name: Savory Oatmeal with Egg
recipes.description: Oatmeal does not have to be sweet. Cooking oats in broth instead of water and topping them with a runny fried egg, scallions, and a drizzle of soy sauce creates a deeply satisfying savory bowl that feels more like congee than breakfast cereal.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Water or Low-Sodium Chicken Broth
2 Scallions, thinly sliced (white and green parts separated)
Optional: shredded cheddar, crumbled bacon, hot sauce, sliced avocado

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the Oats: In a saucepan, bring water or broth and salt to a boil. Stir in the oats. Reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the oats are creamy and tender but not mushy.

Fry the Eggs: While the oats cook, heat olive oil in a small nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. When the oil shimmers, crack in the eggs. Cook for 2-3 minutes until the whites are fully set and the edges are lacy and crisp, but the yolk is still runny. Season with salt and pepper.
Finish the Oats: Remove the oats from heat. Stir in butter, soy sauce, and sesame oil. The butter should melt and make the oats glossy.
Assemble: Divide the oats between two bowls. Top each with a fried egg, sliced scallions (both white and green parts), and a pinch of red pepper flakes.
Serve: Eat immediately, breaking the yolk so it runs into the oats and creates a rich, silky sauce. Add optional toppings as desired.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, umami, rich, weeknight, comfort-food, simmer, fry

recipes.name: Savory Thai Turkey Lettuce Wraps
recipes.description: Fish sauce, lime, cilantro and mint season the turkey filling. Let excess pan liquid reduce before filling the lettuce cups so the leaves stay crisp.
recipeIngredient: 2 medium bell peppers, seeded and chopped
1/4 c. packed fresh mint leaves, chopped
Lettuce cups, washed and dried; as needed for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Cook filling: In a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat, cook all the bell peppers in all the measured vegetable oil for about 3 minutes. Add all the garlic and cook about 30 seconds, then add all the ground turkey and fish sauce. Break up the meat and start checking after about 5 minutes; continue until the turkey reaches 165°F / 74°C on a thermometer before adding herbs. If liquid pools, let excess liquid reduce while stirring, keeping the filling moist. Use more loads or vessels for a larger batch, dividing the full measured ingredients proportionally.

Finish and serve: Stir in all the cilantro, mint and lime juice. Spoon the cooked filling into washed, dried lettuce cups using clean utensils. Offer the listed Sriracha and hoisin separately as wanted. Assemble promptly so the leaves stay crisp.

recipes.keywords: Thai, saute

recipes.name: Sazerac
recipes.description: The Sazerac is one of America's oldest cocktails, created in New Orleans in the 1830s, and it's been the city's official cocktail since 2008. Originally made with Cognac, it switched to rye whiskey when the phylloxera epidemic devastated French vineyards in the 1870s.
recipeIngredient: 2 oz rye whiskey (or Cognac for the original recipe)
Absinthe or dry anise-flavored spirit for rinsing

recipeInstructions.text: Chill an Old Fashioned: glass by filling it with ice water or placing it in the freezer.
In a mixing glass,: combine the rye whiskey, simple syrup, and bitters with ice. Stir well for 20-30 seconds.
Discard the ice water: from the chilled glass. Add a small amount of absinthe (about 1/4 oz) to the glass and swirl to coat the inside, then discard the excess absinthe.
Strain the stirred whiskey: mixture into the absinthe-rinsed glass (no ice).
Express a lemon peel: over the drink by twisting it to release the oils. Discard the peel or rest it on the rim (traditionally, it's discarded).
Serve immediately.:

recipes.keywords: American, rich, savory, herbaceous, entertaining, date-night, comfort-food, no-cook

recipes.name: Scallion-Shallot Oil with Crisp Alliums
recipes.description: Gently fried shallot and scallion in a strained aromatic oil, with the crisp solids kept for finishing.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup (240 ml) neutral oil, such as canola
100 g peeled shallots, sliced evenly about 1–2 mm thick
50 g scallion whites and pale greens, washed, thoroughly dried and thinly sliced
5 g peeled fresh ginger, cut into two thin slices, optional
1/8 tsp fine salt, for the fried solids

recipeInstructions.text: Set up before heating: Slice shallots evenly and dry the washed scallions thoroughly. Place a fine metal sieve over a stable dry heatproof bowl and line a tray with paper towels. Choose a small heavy saucepan with enough headroom for bubbling; ingredients and oil should occupy well under half its depth.

Begin with shallots: Put oil, shallots and optional ginger in the cold pan. Heat over medium until steady bubbles develop, stirring to separate rings. Reduce to medium-low as needed to maintain a gentle fry without smoking. Cook about 8–12 minutes, until shallots soften and begin to lose their raw white appearance.

Add scallions and watch closely: Add the dry sliced scallion whites and pale greens carefully. Continue frying about 5–10 minutes, stirring frequently, until shallots are pale golden and scallion pieces begin to color. Lift out any golden pieces early with a dry slotted spoon; do not wait for every piece to turn the same shade. If pieces are still pale and wet, allow more time at controlled heat rather than raising it sharply.

Separate promptly: Turn off the heat and carefully pour through the metal sieve. Spread the drained solids on the lined tray, discard ginger slices and sprinkle the measured salt over the alliums. Let them cool in one thin layer. Keep the hot oil on a stable surface out of the working area until safe to handle.

Measure and store: Expect roughly 180–210 ml strained oil and about 1/2 cup loose fried solids, with variation. Once cool enough to package, place oil and solids in separate clean, dry containers, date them and refrigerate promptly. Use within four days or freeze as directed; do not leave the garnish on the counter for several days.

recipes.recipeYield: About 3/4 cup oil plus 1/2 cup fried alliums
recipes.keywords: Chinese-inspired, aromatic, savory, sweet, nutty, crispy, everyday, meal-prep, make-ahead, fry, infuse

recipes.name: Seafood-Chorizo Tacos
recipes.description: Fresh Mexican-style chorizo seasons these shrimp-and-squid tacos with its full rendered fat. Cook the sausage before adding the seafood so its endpoint does not force a longer seafood cook.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb fresh uncooked chorizo, casings removed and meat crumbled
salt, a pinch, for the chorizo
black pepper, a pinch, for the chorizo
1/2 lb raw medium shrimp, shelled, deveined and chopped
1/2 lb cleaned small squid, cut into thin rings

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the Chorizo: Use extra-virgin olive oil, fresh uncooked chorizo, salt, and black pepper at the sausage stage. Heat the oil in a large skillet over moderately high heat, then add the chorizo and its initial salt and pepper. Break up the chorizo as it browns; about 4 minutes is an early check, not guaranteed doneness. Cook fresh pork/beef chorizo to 160°F, or 165°F if its label identifies poultry. Keep the full oil and rendered fat in the pan. Use enough pan area for the actual load, or cook separate proportionate batches with their own full supplies.
Soften the Onion: Add small red onion and ground cumin and cook about 2 minutes, until onion begins to soften.
Add the Garlic: Add garlic clove and sauté for 30–45 seconds, until fragrant.

Cook the Seafood: Add raw medium shrimp, cleaned small squid, and Mexican lager and toss over moderately high heat. Begin checking around 3 minutes; continue as needed for the seafood to reach 145°F. Shrimp should be firm, pearly and opaque, and squid cooked through. Raw size, thin rings and pan loading determine the time; do not stop solely because 3 minutes have passed.
Finish the Filling: Once sausage and seafood are cooked, stir in fresh lime juice, salt, and black pepper, season to taste and take the skillet off the heat.

Serve: Use corn tortillas, avocado, fresh cilantro, sour cream, and lime wedges for serving. Warm or char the tortillas in a dry skillet or carefully over a suitable flame, then fill with all the seafood-chorizo mixture and top with the avocado, cilantro and sour cream. Keep the toppings cold until assembly and serve the lime wedges alongside.

recipes.name: Seared Salmon with Summer Vegetables
recipes.description: Small strips of seared salmon with garlicky spinach, corn and shiitakes, finished with a rich balsamic butter sauce.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb center-cut salmon fillet, pin bones removed
6 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed and chilled, for finishing the sauce
2 tbsp unsalted butter, for the sauce aromatics
3 tbsp unsalted butter, for mushrooms and corn
1 tbsp unsalted butter, for searing salmon
2 cloves garlic, thinly sliced, for the sauce
1 clove garlic, peeled and left whole, for the spinach
1/4 lb whole shiitake mushrooms, stems reserved and caps quartered
1/3 cup water, plus a little only if needed to loosen the sauce
1 tbsp olive oil, for searing salmon
1 lb fresh spinach, washed and drained
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Michael Romano’s recipe at Food & Wine.

itemListElement.text: Prepare the components: Slice the salmon crosswise into similar strips for the intended number of portions. Pat dry and keep cold. Separate the shiitake stems from the quartered caps. Measure each butter and oil allocation, keeping the sauce-finishing butter chilled. Prepare a colander, warm serving plates and a bowl for straining sauce.

Soften and reduce: Melt the aromatic butter in a nonreactive saucepan over medium-low. Add onion, sliced garlic, mushroom stems, tomato, peppercorns and bay leaf. Cook about 10–12 minutes, stirring, until softened without browning. Add balsamic vinegar and the measured water. Simmer over medium to medium-high about 4–8 minutes, stirring more often near the end, until syrupy but still moist; do not let it scorch dry.

Finish the sauce: Turn heat to very low or move off heat if the pan is very hot. Whisk in the chilled sauce butter a few cubes at a time, letting each addition blend before adding more. If butter stops softening, briefly return to low heat; do not boil. Strain into the bowl, pressing lightly, and discard solids. Season with salt and pepper. Hold briefly above warm water, with the bowl not touching the water, and stir occasionally while finishing the meal.

Wilt spinach: Heat the spinach oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the whole garlic clove and spinach in handfuls, turning with tongs until wilted, about 3–5 minutes. Remove the garlic, season and transfer spinach to the colander. Let excess liquid drain; keep covered briefly while cooking the next components.

Cook mushrooms and corn: Carefully wipe the skillet clean. Melt the vegetable butter over medium heat. Sauté mushroom caps about 3–4 minutes until softened, then add corn and cook about 3 minutes until hot and tender. Season with salt and pepper and transfer to a warm bowl. Do not keep heating solely to force charring.

Sear salmon: Wipe the skillet if needed and heat the searing oil and butter over medium-high, reserving a proportional share of both for each additional batch. Season fish with salt and pepper. When butter foams without scorching, lay in the strips with space between them, in batches if necessary. Cook about 2–3 minutes on the first side, turn gently, then cook about 2–4 minutes more, adjusting for thickness. Check representative thick centers from the side for 145°F / 63°C; lower the heat if the surface browns before the center is ready. Remove each strip as it finishes.

Plate promptly: Divide drained spinach, corn and mushrooms among the intended portions, add salmon, then spoon over balsamic butter sauce. Sprinkle with chives. Serve immediately; this sauce is intended for a short finish at the stove, not extended warm holding.

recipes.keywords: American, acidic, rich, date-night, entertaining, light-and-fresh, sear, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Seared Scallops with Corn & Avocado Relish
recipes.description: Dry sea scallops and a dry surface help the pan brown them, but a golden crust does not establish that the centers are cooked. The corn relish uses the full cooked bacon and avocado; sauté the corn and onion in neutral oil, then fold in the bacon and avocado off the heat.
recipeIngredient: 12 strips bacon, fully cooked and chopped
1 tbsp neutral oil, for the corn skillet
Neutral oil, as needed to coat the scallop skillet
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste, for the relish
Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste, for the scallops

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the Relish: Use an upside-down small bowl inside a large bowl as a stand to cut corn kernels off the cobs. Add diced onion, bell pepper and half the measured parsley. Have the fully cooked chopped bacon and diced avocado ready. Pat the scallops dry with paper towels and keep them refrigerated until searing.

Sauté: Heat the measured corn oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the corn mixture for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the onion begins to soften; caramelization is optional, not a stopping requirement. Use more pan space or separate proportional batches if crowded. Take off the heat and let cool for about 2 minutes before folding in the avocado.

Finish the Relish: Fold all the diced avocado and fully cooked bacon into the warm corn mixture. Season with the relish salt and pepper to taste. Keep the relish and serving utensils away from raw scallops.

Sear the Scallops: Wipe the skillet and coat with the separate searing oil over medium-high heat. Season scallops with their salt and pepper allowance. Add in a single uncrowded layer; use additional pans or batches as needed. Sear until the underside develops a golden crust, then turn. Check the center of a thick scallop with an instant-read thermometer inserted from the side; cook to 145°F. The flesh should be firm, pearly, and opaque throughout. Lower the heat if the crust darkens before the center is done. Remove each scallop as it finishes; size and pan heat determine the time. Let them stand on a clean plate while you divide the relish.

Assemble: Divide all the warm corn-avocado-bacon relish among the portions, then add the measured scallops. The original batch plans four scallops per portion; portion sizes depend on actual scallop size.
Finish: Squeeze the measured lemon over the scallops and garnish with the remaining half of the parsley. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, herbaceous, smoky, date-night, entertaining, comfort-food, saute

recipes.name: Seasoned Bean Sprouts (Kongnamul Namul)
recipes.description: Kongnamul has larger yellow bean heads than mung bean sprouts. Give those heads time to cook through, then drain before seasoning.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb soybean sprouts (kongnamul), rinsed and drained
1/2 tsp fine sea salt, divided and added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Rinse sprouts, discard damaged or spoiled ones and drain. Put them in a medium pot with the measured cooking water and a small pinch taken from the measured salt.

Cook thoroughly: Cover and heat over medium-high until bubbling and steaming, then maintain steady steam without boiling dry. Allow roughly 10 minutes of covered heating and cooking, continuing until the soybean heads are tender and the sprouts are steaming hot throughout and above 165°F / 74°C. Check the sprouts themselves with a food thermometer and follow any longer package cooking directions; do not deliberately leave the sprouts lightly cooked. Open the lid if needed to check water or doneness, keeping your face away from steam.
Drain: Drain in a clean colander and let excess steam escape briefly. Use clean utensils for the cooked sprouts.
Season: Toss with the sesame oil, garlic, green onion and sesame seeds. Add the remaining measured salt gradually to taste; it need not all be used.

Serve or chill: Serve warm as a small side, or spread in a shallow container and refrigerate promptly for a chilled banchan. People at higher risk of foodborne illness should avoid raw or lightly cooked sprouts.

recipes.keywords: Korean, savory, umami, weeknight, light-and-fresh, steam

recipes.name: Sesame-Roasted Shelled Edamame
recipes.description: Shelled edamame roasted until drier and lightly browned, then finished with toasted sesame. A fresh side or snack, not a shelf-stable crunchy bean.
recipeIngredient: 450 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, prepared according to the package before roasting
2 tsp toasted sesame oil, for finishing
1/8 tsp fine salt, only if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the beans: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C. Read the edamame package. If it requires cooking, cook as directed before roasting; drain afterward. If it is explicitly ready to eat, thaw as directed or overnight in the refrigerator and drain. Do not assume every frozen product has the same preparation status.

Dry and season: Spread beans on a clean towel, blot thoroughly and let steam escape briefly if hot. Toss with neutral oil, soy sauce and garlic powder. Spread in a single layer on a parchment-lined rimmed half-sheet pan.

Roast and check: Roast about 30–40 minutes, stirring after 15 minutes and checking regularly thereafter. Stop when the surface is drier with light brown patches and a cooled sample bean has a pleasant firm center. Some edges may crisp; do not keep baking solely to make every bean hard and crunchy.

Finish: Toss warm beans with toasted sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds and optional pepper flakes. Taste and add the measured salt only if needed. Divide into four side portions and serve soon. Refrigerate leftovers promptly rather than leaving them out as a pantry snack.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, savory, nutty, salty, weeknight, snack, entertaining, roast

recipes.name: Sesame Tomato Salad
recipes.description: Ripe tomatoes with a generous soy, sesame and olive-oil dressing, finished with fresh basil.
recipeIngredient: 3 lb mixed ripe tomatoes, large tomatoes cored and sliced or chopped, small tomatoes halved
Flaky salt, only if needed after tasting

recipeInstructions.text: Mix dressing: Whisk olive oil, toasted sesame oil, soy sauce, vinegar, garlic and sugar until the sugar dissolves and the liquids combine. Set aside; whisk again before using if separated.
Prepare tomatoes: Wash and dry tomatoes, core large ones and slice or chop them; halve small tomatoes. Arrange on a wide shallow platter without piling them deeply.
Dress and rest: Spoon about half the dressing over the tomatoes. Let stand about 5 minutes so the tomato juices mingle with it. Keep the rest of the dressing in a separate serving bowl.
Finish: Scatter with basil and black pepper. Taste a dressed tomato before adding any flaky salt; it may not need more. Serve promptly with the remaining dressing on the side.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, herbaceous, light-and-fresh, entertaining, weekend-project, no-cook

citation.name: Adapted from The New York Times, Sesame Tomato Salad

recipes.name: Shakshuka
recipes.description: Shakshuka is a North African dish of eggs poached in spiced tomato sauce that has become a staple across the Middle East, especially in Israeli cuisine. The sauce must be thick enough to cradle the eggs -- if it is too thin, the whites spread and cook unevenly.
recipeIngredient: 1 (28 oz) can Crushed Tomatoes (San Marzano preferred)
1/4 cup Fresh Cilantro or Parsley, chopped

recipeInstructions.text: Build the Base: Heat olive oil in a large (10-12 inch) skillet over medium heat. Add onion and bell pepper. Cook for 5-6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and the onion is translucent.
Bloom Spices: Add cumin, paprika, coriander, and cayenne. Stir for 1 minute until very fragrant -- the spices should darken slightly and smell toasty. Add garlic and stir for 30-45 seconds.

Simmer the Sauce: Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add sugar and salt. Stir well and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce has thickened and reduced slightly. You should be able to drag a spoon through it and see the bottom of the pan for a moment.
Create Wells: Using the back of a large spoon, make 6 evenly spaced wells in the sauce. Crack one egg into each well.

Poach the Eggs: Cover the skillet with a lid. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cook for 5-8 minutes depending on your preference: 5 minutes for very runny yolks, 7-8 minutes for yolks that are jammy and just set. Check at 5 minutes -- the whites should be fully opaque.
Finish: Remove from heat. Scatter with cilantro and feta. Serve immediately, straight from the skillet, with crusty bread for scooping.

recipes.keywords: Middle Eastern, Mediterranean, savory, acidic, spicy, umami, weekend-brunch, weeknight, comfort-food, saute, simmer

recipes.name: Shaved Brussels Sprout Salad
recipes.description: Shave Brussels sprouts into thin strands so a short dressed rest softens them without losing all their crunch. Set aside a little dressing for the apple before tossing the sprouts, then combine everything gently and add the full measured Pecorino.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup Pecorino Romano, finely grated (about 3 oz)

recipeInstructions.text: Mix dressing: Whisk apple cider vinegar and honey in a large bowl, then drizzle in the oil while whisking. Add the listed salt and pepper to taste, remembering that Pecorino will add salt. The dressing can separate during standing; whisk again when needed.

Prepare apple: Core the apple and cut fine matchsticks. Move a small portion of the prepared dressing into a separate bowl (about 1 tbsp at the original batch) and toss with the apple. Keep this apple bowl aside; its dressing is taken from the measured total.
Shave sprouts: Trim tough bases and damaged leaves from washed, dried Brussels sprouts. Use a mandoline with its guard or a sharp knife to shave thinly; discard large hard core pieces.
Dress and rest: Toss sprouts with the dressing remaining in the large bowl until evenly coated. Let stand 15 minutes, or cover and refrigerate for that interval if preparing ahead.
Finish: Add the apple and all its reserved dressing to the sprouts, then add the full measured finely grated Pecorino. Toss gently to distribute.
Serve: Taste before adding any extra salt or pepper. Serve now, or keep refrigerated if waiting; serve cool if preferred without treating additional chilling as part of the 30 minute schedule.

recipes.keywords: Italian, sweet, acidic, rich, entertaining, potluck, light-and-fresh, holiday, no-cook, toss

recipes.name: Shaved Fennel Citrus Salad
recipes.description: Paper-thin fennel and juicy citrus with a light honey-lemon dressing, optional olives and shaved Parmesan.
recipeIngredient: 2 large fennel bulbs, stalks removed, tender fronds reserved
2 large navel or Cara Cara oranges
1 tbsp reserved citrus juice, collected while preparing the oranges or grapefruit
1/4 tsp kosher salt, added gradually to taste
2 tbsp shaved Parmesan; choose vegetarian-rennet cheese for a vegetarian version, or omit for vegan
1/4 cup pitted Castelvetrano olives, halved, optional
Cold water and ice, only if crisping the shaved fennel

recipeInstructions.text: Shave fennel: Wash the bulbs and fronds. Trim stalks and damaged outer layers, halve the bulbs lengthwise and cut out the hard core. Shave thinly with a sharp knife or a guarded mandoline. If the ribbons need crisping, immerse in ice water for 5–10 minutes while preparing the citrus; drain and spin or pat thoroughly dry.

Segment citrus: Cut the tops and bottoms off the oranges and optional grapefruit. Set on a flat cut end and slice away peel and white pith. Over a bowl, cut between membranes to release segments. Squeeze the remaining membranes to collect juice, and measure the listed amount for the dressing. Reserve any excess juice for another use, rather than pouring it all over the salad.

Whisk dressing: Whisk olive oil, lemon juice, the measured reserved citrus juice, honey or agave, pepper and half the salt. Taste with a fennel ribbon. The dressing should be bright but not harsh; the cheese and optional olives will add more salt.

Assemble and taste: Spread dried fennel on a broad platter and arrange citrus segments over it. Add optional olives. Drizzle about half the dressing, turn gently and taste a complete bite with a little Parmesan if using. Add more dressing and the remaining salt only as needed. Offer unused dressing separately. Finish with the Parmesan and reserved tender fronds and serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Italian, Mediterranean, acidic, sweet, fresh, aromatic, herbaceous, weeknight, light-and-fresh, holiday, date-night, no-cook

recipes.name: Roasted Chicken, Broccoli and Cheddar Bake
recipes.description: Chicken and broccoli roasted separately, then combined with a smooth broth-based Cheddar sauce and measured panko topping.
recipeIngredient: 680 g (1 1/2 lb) boneless skinless chicken thighs, cut into 1 1/2-inch pieces
450 g broccoli florets, cut into even 1 1/2-inch pieces, washed and dried

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the trays and topping: Heat oven to 425°F / 220°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Toss chicken on one tray with 1 tbsp oil and half the salt and pepper. Toss dry broccoli on the other tray with the remaining tablespoon oil and salt/pepper. Spread both out. Mix panko with its separate tablespoon oil.

Roast independently: Roast both trays, swapping rack positions once. Start checking broccoli at 15 minutes and chicken at 18 minutes. Remove broccoli when barely tender with browned tips, usually 15–20 minutes. Chicken may need 18–25 minutes; check thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C. Remove each tray when ready rather than waiting for them to match.

Make sauce during roasting: Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low. Whisk in flour and cook 1–2 minutes without darkening. Add broth gradually, whisking smooth after each addition. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 3–4 minutes, stirring, until thickened enough to coat a spoon. Remove from heat, wait for bubbling to subside and stir in Cheddar a handful at a time, then garlic powder.

Assemble: Put roasted chicken and broccoli in a 3-quart baking dish. Pour over the sauce and fold gently to coat. Scatter the oiled panko evenly over the top. Use a dish deep enough to contain the sauce without packing the food tightly.

Bake and serve: Return to the 425°F oven for about 10–15 minutes, until panko is golden, edges bubble and the center reaches 165°F / 74°C. If the topping colors early, shield it loosely with foil. Let stand about 5 minutes before portioning into four servings; handle the hot dish carefully.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, weeknight, comfort-food, kid-friendly, meal-prep, bake, roast

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Chicken Fajitas
recipes.description: Lime-seasoned chicken breast, three colors of peppers and red onion roasted on two pans, with warm tortillas and fresh cilantro. A brief optional broil adds browned edges.
recipeIngredient: 2 lb (907 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, trimmed
1 red bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
1 yellow bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
1 green bell pepper, stemmed, seeded and sliced
1 tbsp olive oil, for coating the filling
1 tsp olive oil, for the two pans
1 1/2 tsp ground ancho chile, without salt or other seasonings
Ripe avocado, sliced, optional, for serving
Salsa or hot sauce, optional, for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oven and prepare toppings: Heat the oven to 375°F / 190°C with racks in the upper and lower thirds. Lightly coat the two rimmed pans, or their foil liners, with the separate teaspoon of oil, dividing it equally. Chop cilantro and set out the tortillas; keep the avocado whole until near service.

Cut and season: Slice peppers into 1/4-inch-wide strips and onion into 1/4-inch slices, separating the layers. Pat chicken dry and cut across the grain into strips about 1/2 inch thick and 2–3 inches long; split very thick breast sections horizontally first. Mix all eight seasonings in the large bowl with the filling's tablespoon of oil and half the lime juice. Add chicken, peppers and onion and toss thoroughly. Roast as soon as the oven is ready, or cover and refrigerate briefly while it finishes heating.

Load both pans: Divide the filling evenly between the pans, keeping chicken strips separate and flat. Spread the vegetables around them in a loose layer rather than a heap. Each pan holds about half the chicken, peppers and onion. Wash the raw-food bowl, utensils and preparation surface before they touch cooked food or toppings.

Roast and check: Roast for about 20–25 minutes, turning the filling and exchanging the upper and lower pans after about 10 minutes. Begin checking chicken at 15 minutes. Insert a thin-tip thermometer sideways into the thickest part of several substantial strips on each pan; every checked strip must reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue cooking any unfinished pan and recheck. The peppers should be tender but still hold their shape. Transfer done chicken to a clean covered bowl if the vegetables need longer.

Optional browning: Once the chicken is safely cooked, remove it to the clean bowl if not already there. Leave the vegetables spread on their pans, spooning off a large pool of juice if necessary. Broil one pan at a time about 6–8 inches from the element for roughly 1–3 minutes, watching continuously for browned edges. Keep the other pan and chicken out of the broiler. Skip this step if the vegetables already have enough color. Recombine the hot filling and add the remaining lime juice.

Warm tortillas: While the finished filling is covered for this brief step, microwave the tortillas in stacks of four between lightly damp paper towels for about 30–45 seconds per stack, adding short bursts until hot and flexible. Follow the package if it gives a different method. Wrap the warm stack in a clean towel. For a skillet, warm one or two tortillas at a time in a dry pan over medium-high, about 10–30 seconds per side; allow several extra minutes for all twelve.

Serve: Slice the optional avocado. Divide the filling among twelve tortillas and add the cilantro and avocado, serving two fajitas per person. Offer any remaining filling alongside; do not overfill a tortilla until it tears. Offer salsa or hot sauce if desired. Rice, beans and guacamole have their own preparation times in the complete dinner plan.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, American, savory, smoky, tangy, aromatic, family-meal, entertaining, roast, broil

citation.name: Adapted from Natalie Mortimer at The Modern Proper

recipes.name: Balsamic Chicken with Tomatoes and Feta
recipes.description: Even chicken breasts roasted with red onion and tomatoes, with a restrained honey-balsamic finish and softened feta.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, divided into 4 portions and evened to about 3/4 inch thick
180 g red onion, cut into 1/2-inch wedges
150 g block feta, drained and cut into 4 slabs
1/4 tsp fine salt, for the chicken

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat the oven to 425°F / 220°C. Cut and weigh the vegetables, drain feta, and even the four chicken portions to about 3/4 inch thick. In a clean bowl, whisk balsamic vinegar, honey, Dijon, oregano, garlic powder and 1 tbsp of the oil. Reserve this mixture away from raw meat.

Arrange: Use the remaining 1 tbsp oil to coat the chicken, onion and 400 g of the tomatoes on a rimmed half-sheet pan. Season chicken with its measured salt and pepper. Spread everything with gaps, keeping vegetables beside rather than piled over the meat. Wash hands and raw-meat utensils.

First roast, then finish: Roast for twelve minutes. Add the remaining 200 g tomatoes and the four feta slabs in the spaces. Spoon the reserved clean balsamic mixture across chicken, vegetables and cheese. Do not use a raw-contact marinade as a late drizzle.

Measure: Return to the oven for roughly 13–18 minutes. Start checking the thickest center of every chicken piece from the side after about twenty minutes total roasting, and remove pieces individually once they reach 165°F / 74°C. Continue as needed. Tomatoes should be juicy with some collapsed and some still holding shape, and onion should be tender. If those need longer, leave them in after removing the chicken.

Rest and serve: Rest cooked chicken five minutes, then divide it with the vegetables, feta and tomato pan juices among four plates. Scatter the two tablespoons basil. Pair with a starch or a simple green salad as needed; an additional whipped-feta dip duplicates the cheese component.

recipes.keywords: Mediterranean, sweet, savory, acidic, rich, herbaceous, weeknight, meal-prep, roast

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Italian Sausage Dinner
recipes.description: This is the ultimate Tuesday night dinner: everything roasts on one pan, the broccoli steams while you wait, and store-bought rolls round it out. The key is getting the potatoes in the oven first - they need a head start to get crispy while the sausages just need to cook through and brown.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 lbs Italian Sausage Links (sweet or hot, your preference)

recipeInstructions.text: Prep: Preheat oven to 425°F. Line a large sheet pan with parchment.
Season Potatoes: Toss halved potatoes with olive oil, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper. Spread in a single layer on the sheet pan.
Start Potatoes: Roast potatoes alone for 15 minutes to get a head start on crisping.
Add Sausage: Remove pan, push potatoes to one side. Add sausage links, piercing each a few times with a fork. Return to oven.
Roast Together: Roast for 20 more minutes, flipping sausages halfway, until sausages are browned and cooked through (160°F internal) and potatoes are golden and crispy.
Steam Broccoli: While everything roasts, steam broccoli (about 5 minutes in a steamer basket or microwave).
Serve: Slice sausages on the bias. Serve with crispy potatoes, steamed broccoli, warm rolls, and mustard on the side.

recipes.keywords: Italian, American, savory, herbaceous, weeknight, comfort-food, roast

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Pancakes
recipes.description: A single 9-by-13-inch rimmed pan replaces individual griddle batches. Divide the toppings into four areas and keep the batter depth even so all portions bake together.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 tablespoons seedless strawberry jam , slightly warmed
maple syrup, butter, or powered sugar , for serving
Nonstick spray, for greasing the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F. Coat a 9×13 rimmed sheet pan with nonstick spray, making sure to get the sides and corners. Set aside.
Mix: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, brown sugar, granulated sugar, baking powder, and salt. Whisk in the eggs, milk, butter, and vanilla until combined and smooth.
Continue: Pour batter onto the prepared pan. Tap the pan on the counter a few times to even out and flatten the batter.
Continue: Now imagine the batter divided into four equal sections.
Continue: In one section, dollop teaspoons of the strawberry jam, then swirl into the batter using a toothpick, making a marbled pattern. Top with sliced strawberries.
Continue: In another section, sprinkle with the blueberries.
Continue: In another section, sprinkle chocolate chips.
Continue: For the last section, whisk together the melted butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon. Dollop teaspoons of the mixture, then swirl into the batter using a toothpick, making a marbled pattern.
Cook: Bake for 15-18 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean and the pancake springs back to the touch.
Finish: Allow to cool for a minute or so, then slice into portions.
Finish: Serve with your choice of syrup, butter, powdered sugar, or all three!

recipes.keywords: American, bake

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Pesto Chicken Bowls
recipes.description: Make the pesto mixture before handling raw chicken, and keep its bowl and spoon clean. Only measured portions go onto the roasting food; the rest is a separate clean reserve for another meal.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Fresh Broccoli, cut into florets

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Keep raw chicken cold until preparation and thaw frozen chicken in the refrigerator. Prepare all the vegetables as listed. Use rimmed pans and parchment rated for 400°F, with enough space to spread the complete load without piling it up; use additional pans for larger batches.

Make and reserve the clean mixture: Before handling raw chicken, mix all the listed prepared basil pesto, Parmesan, garlic and 2/3 of the olive oil, with salt and pepper to taste. At the original batch this is 2 tbsp of the 3 tbsp oil. With a clean spoon, measure out the two roasting additions into separate small dishes:2 tbsp of the finished mixture for the first stage and another 2 tbsp for the second stage at the original batch, scaled proportionally. Cover and refrigerate all the remaining clean mixture for another meal. Do not dip a raw-contact spoon back into this reserve.

First roasting stage: Toss all the diced chicken and mushrooms with the remaining 1/3 of the olive oil and the first measured pesto-mixture addition. At the original batch this is 1 tbsp oil and 2 tbsp finished mixture. Spread over the pans and roast for about 10 minutes; the chicken is not yet assumed cooked.

Add the vegetables: Add all the broccoli, zucchini and cherry tomatoes, and toss with the second measured finished-mixture addition. At the original batch this is 2 tbsp; it comes from the separate clean dish, not a raw-contact reserve. Spread the complete load out again, using another pan if needed.

Finish roasting: Start checking after another 10 minutes. Continue until each chicken piece reaches 165°F in its thickest part and the vegetables are tender to your liking. Check several pieces in each pan; wet vegetables and crowding can lengthen cooking. If chicken finishes first, move it with clean utensils to a clean plate and continue the vegetables; any vegetable or liquid that contacted raw chicken must also reach 165°F before serving.

Serve or store: Divide all the roasted chicken and vegetables among the listed bowls. Pasta or rice is a separate accompaniment. Use refrigerated portions within 3–4 days and reheat to 165°F. Freeze later portions; vegetables may soften after reheating. Refrigerate both the meal and the separate clean pesto reserve within 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F, at 40°F or below. Use the reserve within the shorter of its pesto product instructions and 3–4 days, or freeze it; it is not included in the served bowl allocation.

recipes.keywords: Italian, umami, herbaceous, meal-prep, weeknight, snack, bake, roast

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Pineapple Shrimp Tacos
recipes.description: These Mexican-inspired tacos keep shrimp, pineapple and onion in separate areas of the tray. Check the shrimp before waiting for browned pineapple: finished shrimp can come out while the fruit and onion roast longer.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled, deveined and tails removed
2 cups fresh pineapple, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
2 tbsp fresh lime juice, for the shrimp
1 tsp kosher salt, for the shrimp
1/2 cup fresh cilantro, for the slaw
corn tortillas, as needed to serve the filling
fresh cilantro, for serving, chopped, optional
radish, for serving, thinly sliced, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Use raw shrimp, fresh lime juice, garlic cloves, kosher salt, 1/4 of the extra-virgin olive oil, chili powder, ground cumin, and cayenne for the marinade. Pat the thawed shrimp dry, then whisk the marinade oil, lime juice, garlic, salt and spices together before adding the shrimp and tossing to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. Heat the oven to 425°F while you prepare the tray and slaw.

Prepare the Tray: Use fresh pineapple, medium red onion, 1/2 of the extra-virgin olive oil, and water for the onion and pineapple zones. Divide this pan share of oil equally between them; all the water goes with the onion. Spread the marinated shrimp in a third zone, with all its coating. Use additional rimmed trays if the shrimp or vegetables would overlap; divide the full supplies proportionally rather than adding oil.

Roast: Bake about 12–15 minutes, checking early. The thickest shrimp should reach 145°F with firm, pearly, opaque flesh throughout. Remove finished shrimp with clean utensils to a clean plate. If the pineapple and onion need longer, return their sections to the oven; do not delay the shrimp for a browning target.

Dress the Slaw: Toss 1/4 of the extra-virgin olive oil, green cabbage, fresh cilantro, lime, and kosher salt together while the tray roasts, using all the juice from the slaw lime, then refrigerate until serving. Keep this ready-to-eat mixture away from the raw-shrimp bowl and utensils.
Assemble: Warm corn tortillas, then divide the slaw, shrimp, roasted onion and pineapple among them. The taco count depends on tortilla and shrimp size.
Finish: Top with avocado, sour cream, lime wedges (if using), fresh cilantro (if using), and radish (if using) and serve.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, spicy, sweet, acidic, rich, weeknight, bake, roast, no-cook

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Shrimp Fajitas
recipes.description: Peppers and onions take longer than shrimp. Roast the vegetables first, then add the shrimp and cook only until opaque.
recipeIngredient: 1.5 pounds raw jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 bell peppers, seeded and thinly sliced
1 large red or sweet onion, thinly sliced

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Heat oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment rated for that temperature, or use a suitable bare rimmed pan. Mix all the measured spices in a small bowl. Thaw frozen shrimp in the refrigerator and pat dry; remove tails if preferred for tacos.

Roast the Vegetables: Toss sliced peppers and onion with half the measured oil and about half the seasoning. Spread in one layer, using additional pans if crowded, and roast about 12–15 minutes, until beginning to soften.

Add the Shrimp: Toss peeled, deveined shrimp with the remaining oil and seasoning and all the measured lime juice. Add to the vegetables, spreading shrimp in one layer; use a second pan if crowded. Divide the full supplies proportionally across the pans.

Finish: Roast about 6–10 minutes more, checking early, until the thickest shrimp reach 145°F with pearly, opaque flesh throughout. Remove as soon as done. Warm the measured tortillas separately and serve with all the shrimp and vegetables and optional lime wedges.

recipes.keywords: Mexican, roast

recipes.name: Shoyu Tuna Poke Bowl
recipes.description: Cold tuna in a mild soy, sesame and ginger dressing over lightly seasoned rice, with cucumber, edamame and avocado. Raw fish requires informed sourcing and handling.
recipeIngredient: 450 g boneless, skinless yellowfin tuna suitable for intended raw service; see sourcing note
4 cups freshly cooked [Plain Short-Grain White Rice](/mise/recipes/steamed-white-rice)
300 g English cucumber, ends trimmed and thinly sliced
150 g frozen unsalted shelled edamame, cooked according to the package and chilled
2 tbsp prepared sriracha mayonnaise, optional; check the label

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the rice and edamame: Follow Plain Short-Grain White Rice; its batch starting with 300 g dry rice should provide approximately the four cooked cups needed here, with any extra reserved separately. During soaking/cooking, prepare shelled edamame according to its package, drain and chill promptly in a shallow container. Thaw-only directions apply only to a product explicitly ready to eat.

Season the rice: Dissolve the rice vinegar, tablespoon of sugar and fine salt together, warming gently if necessary. Measure four cups hot plain rice and fold in this mixture. Spread gently in a wide bowl and let steam escape until the rice is barely warm, about 10 minutes. This brief cooling is part of final preparation, not an extended room-temperature hold.

Prepare the toppings and sauce during the rice process: While rice soaks or cooks, slice cucumber and scallion using clean equipment. Dice avocado near assembly, before switching to fish. Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, teaspoon of vinegar, ginger, half teaspoon sugar and scallion in a separate bowl. Taste the clean dressing before it touches fish.

Cut and dress the tuna while rice cools: During the final rice cooling period, on separate clean equipment, cut the cold tuna into 1/2-inch cubes. Fold into the dressing and refrigerate for about 5–10 minutes while setting out the bowls. Exact minute limits are not a safety control, and texture varies with the fish and dressing.

Assemble and eat promptly: Divide rice, tuna, cucumber, chilled shelled edamame and avocado among three bowls. Lift the fish from its dressing, adding only a little of its coating to each bowl; keep it away from communal toppings. Scatter sesame seeds and offer the measured optional mayonnaise separately. Add fish to rice only when each diner is ready to eat.

recipes.keywords: Hawaiian-inspired, Japanese-inspired, umami, savory, sweet, weekend-dinner, no-cook, assemble

recipes.name: Shrimp & Avocado Summer Rolls
recipes.description: Shrimp, creamy avocado and three fresh herbs wrapped in rice paper, with a sweet chile-lime dipping sauce. Drain the filling well and let each damp wrapper soften on the work surface before rolling.
recipeIngredient: 18 medium raw shrimp, fully thawed, peeled, tails removed and deveined
6 round rice paper wrappers, 8–8.5 inches across, plus spares for tears
1 Hass avocado, peeled, pitted and thinly sliced
1 Fresno chile, seeded and minced, or Thai bird chile to taste
Salt, to taste, for cooking water and dipping sauce
Asian chile-garlic sauce, optional, for serving

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the noodles: Cook or soak the rice vermicelli according to its package instructions until tender without a hard center. Drain, rinse under cool running water and drain thoroughly. Snip very long strands into manageable lengths; do not try to dry the noodles until hard.

Cook and cool the shrimp: Bring a saucepan of water to a boil and season lightly with salt. Add the thawed shrimp and reduce to a gentle simmer. Start checking after about 2 minutes; continue until firm, pearly and opaque throughout, checking 145°F / 63°C in the thickest part with a suitable thin probe. Transfer to a clean ice-water bath just until cold, then drain and pat dry. Halve lengthwise using clean utensils.

Make the sauce: Stir the sugar into the measured warm water until dissolved. Add lime juice, minced chile and garlic. Season with a small pinch of salt to taste. Serve the optional chile-garlic sauce separately.

Portion the fillings: Slice the avocado and prepare the herbs. Divide all noodles, avocado, cilantro, mint, chives and shrimp equally among the wrappers. Each roll gets six shrimp halves at any batch size. Keep fillings chilled if you pause before assembly.

Wet a wrapper: Fill a wide shallow dish with water at the temperature recommended on the wrapper package. Briefly wet both sides of one sheet, then lay it flat on a clean smooth work surface. Let it become pliable and slightly tacky before folding; do not leave it soaking until limp.

Fill and roll: Arrange one portion of noodles, avocado and herbs in a compact strip across the lower third, leaving space at the sides. Arrange its shrimp halves curved side down near the filling. Fold the bottom over, fold in both sides and roll snugly without stretching. Repeat with all fillings; use a spare wrapper if one tears or the filling will not fit comfortably.

Serve: Keep rolls separate so they do not stick, and serve with the dipping sauce. The stated batch makes six substantial side rolls; for four diners, cut them in half and share three halves per person.

recipes.keywords: Vietnamese, sweet, savory, acidic, herbaceous, light-and-fresh, boil, no-cook

recipes.name: Shrimp and Corn Chowder
recipes.description: The key to chowder without heavy flour is grating an unripe green plantain directly into the stock. This introduces a natural starch that thickens the soup into a velvety consistency as it simmers.
recipeIngredient: 2 lbs Medium Shrimp, peeled and deveined
2 tbsp Fresh Lime Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Marinate: Toss shrimp with garlic, scallions, lime juice, and salt. Refrigerate for 1 hour.
Corn Milk: In a food processor, puree half the corn with the milk. Strain through a coarse sieve, pressing to extract all the liquid.
The Base: In a large pot, heat the oil. Sauté onion, pepper, and cumin for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes.
Simmer: Add the corn milk, stock, grated plantain, and remaining whole corn kernels. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 20 minutes until thick and aromatic.
Refine: For the Kitchen Standard texture, ladle 2 cups of the soup into a blender and pulse until smooth, then return to the pot.
The Crunch: Add the shrimp and its marinade. Cook for 2-3 minutes until just opaque.
Serve: Stir in cilantro and cayenne. Serve in warmed bowls.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Grits
recipes.description: Tender shrimp, crisp bacon and scallion-lemon pan juices over rich cheddar grits. The grits package determines the cooking schedule; cook the shrimp only when the base is ready.
recipeIngredient: 1 cup dry regular stone-ground grits, with package instructions matching the ratio and simmer time below
4 cups (950 ml) water, for the grits, with package-specific adjustment if needed
1 cup (240 ml) additional hot water, for loosening the grits as needed
1/2 tsp fine salt, for the grits, divided and partly added to taste
2 cups (225 g) sharp cheddar, freshly grated
1 lb (450 g) raw peeled, deveined, tail-off shrimp, weighed after thawing and draining; about 31–40 shrimp in this net quantity
1/2 tsp freshly ground black pepper, divided
1 cup (100 g) thinly sliced scallions, white and green parts separated
1/4 cup (60 ml) water, for the shrimp pan
4 tsp fresh lemon juice, divided and partly added to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare before cooking: Check that the grits package matches the stated liquid ratio and simmer time. Heat the four cups grits water in a 3-quart heavy saucepan while grating cheddar, dicing bacon and preparing scallions, garlic, parsley and lemon. Heat the additional cup of water in a kettle or microwave and keep covered for adjusting the grits; rewarm if needed. Keep white and green scallion parts separate. Pat thawed peeled shrimp dry and keep refrigerated. Set aside half the black pepper for grits and half for shrimp.

Cook the grits: Bring the water to a boil, whisk in grits and half the measured salt, then reduce to a gentle low simmer and cover. Stir thoroughly across the bottom every few minutes to prevent sticking. For grits with the stated package method, begin tasting at twenty minutes and allow about twenty to twenty-five; continue longer if the centers are still firm. If it gets thick before tender, add hot water from the listed additional cup in small amounts. The grains should feel tender in a cooled spoonful, not merely absorb all the water.

Cook bacon and finish the base: While grits simmer, cook diced bacon in the 12-inch skillet over medium heat for about eight to ten minutes, stirring until browned and crisp. Transfer bacon to a plate; carefully measure one tablespoon of rendered fat into a small heatproof cup and pour off the excess, leaving a thin film in the skillet. Discard or separately save the excess fat. Once grits are tender, take them off heat and fold in butter, cheddar and their half of the pepper. Taste before adding the remaining grits salt. Loosen with a little listed hot water if needed so the grits spread softly rather than stand in a firm mound. Cover and keep gently warm while cooking shrimp.

Cook the first shrimp batch: Heat the skillet with half the reserved tablespoon bacon fat over medium-high heat; keep the other half aside. Add half the shrimp in one layer and cook about one to two minutes per side. Check the thickest centers as described in the next step, then transfer cooked shrimp to a clean plate. They will return only briefly for coating, not simmer through the sauce preparation.

Cook the second batch and check: Add the remaining reserved fat and shrimp. Cook and turn as before, until the flesh is firm, pearly and opaque through the center. Check several of the largest shrimp with a thin-tip thermometer inserted into the thickest part for 145°F / 63°C; continue any larger or still-translucent pieces until done. Typical cooking is about three to four minutes per batch, but thickness determines it. Transfer this batch to the clean plate.

Make a brief pan coating: Reduce heat to medium-low. Add scallion whites to the fat film and stir for about one minute, then add garlic for about thirty seconds without browning it. If the pan looks dry, use a teaspoon from the measured pan water while the scallions soften. Add the rest of the separate quarter-cup pan water and scrape up brown, not black, residue; simmer for thirty to sixty seconds. Turn off heat and stir in three teaspoons lemon juice, most of the scallion greens, parsley and the shrimp's half of the pepper. Return shrimp and any juices just long enough to coat. Taste a shrimp with a little grit and add the remaining teaspoon lemon only if needed. Do not salt the topping automatically; bacon and cheese already contribute seasoning.

Serve promptly: Divide grits among four bowls, top with shrimp and the light pan juices, then scatter over crisp bacon and the reserved scallion greens. Distribute shrimp evenly, roughly eight to ten per bowl for the stated size. Serve a vegetable alongside; the grits provide the starch for the plate.

recipes.name: Shrimp & Mango Tacos
recipes.description: Mango stays in small pieces rather than being cooked down into a smooth glaze. Toasted cumin seasons the shrimp, and the full lime juice goes in after cooking.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb small shrimp, raw, peeled, deveined and patted dry
salt, to taste for the shrimp
2 tsp cumin seeds, lightly toasted and ground
1 large ripe mango, peeled, pit removed and finely chopped
1/4 cup fresh cilantro, washed and chopped
water, enough for the steamer below the basket, if steaming, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Prepare all the filling ingredients before heating the pan. If the cumin is not already toasted, stir the seeds in a dry pan over moderate heat until fragrant, then cool briefly and grind. Keep the measured cumin total unchanged.

Warm the tortillas: Warm corn tortillas and water (if using): heat tortillas in a towel in short microwave intervals until flexible, starting around 45–60 seconds for the original batch, or char them briefly on a hot dry skillet, turning as needed. For direct-flame warming: use tongs to turn each tortilla briefly over a gas flame until lightly charred and flexible. Keep wrapped and warm. For steaming, set the wrapped tortillas above about 1 inch of boiling water, cover and steam for 1 minute, then turn off the heat and leave covered for 15 minutes; water must not touch the tortillas. More tortillas may need separate loads.

Start the shrimp: Use neutral oil, small shrimp, salt, and garlic cloves. Heat the measured oil in a large heavy skillet or wok over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and the shrimp-seasoning salt. Stir about 1–2 minutes until they begin to color, adding all the garlic during the last 30–45 seconds so it does not scorch. Use a pan that lets you move the shrimp freely, or divide the whole filling across batches.

Add cumin and chili: Stir in cumin seeds and serrano chilies and cook about 1 minute until fragrant, reducing heat if the garlic is darkening. Continue cooking shrimp as needed rather than using pink edges as the final test.

Add mango and cilantro: Fold in large ripe mango and fresh cilantro and cook about 1 minute, until the mango edges soften but pieces remain. Cook until the thickest shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; FDA guidance is 145°F for seafood when checking with a suitable thermometer. Pink color or a fixed minute count alone does not establish doneness.

Finish and serve: Off heat, stir in fresh lime juice and salt, adding the finishing salt only as needed after tasting cooked filling. Divide all the filling among all the warm tortillas; the original batch provides eight tortillas for four planning portions. Serve promptly, with separately prepared Mexican Red Rice if wanted.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Snow Pea Noodles
recipes.description: Rice noodles with shrimp and crisp snow peas in a sweet chili, soy, ginger and garlic coating.
recipeIngredient: 8 oz raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
8 oz fresh snow peas, strings removed, sliced diagonally
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
Water, for noodle preparation and a small splash if needed in the pan

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare noodles: Follow the package instructions for stir-fried rice linguine. For a product calling for a hot-water soak, use a heatproof bowl and expect roughly 25 minutes; separate clumps gently with a fork. Drain when nearly tender, rinsing only if directed, and drain thoroughly.

Marinate and prepare: While noodles hydrate, pat shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Toss with one-fifth of the sweet chili sauce and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Trim and slice peas, grate ginger and mince garlic. Mix the remaining four-fifths of the sweet chili sauce with the measured soy sauce in a clean bowl.

Cook shrimp: Heat half the oil over medium-high. Lift shrimp from the marinade, letting excess drip away; discard the raw-contact marinade. Cook in a single layer about 1–2 minutes per side, as needed, until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate. Lower heat if the sweet coating darkens rapidly.
Cook vegetables: Add remaining oil, snow peas and ginger. Stir-fry about 2 minutes until the peas brighten and retain a little bite. Add garlic and stir for about 30 seconds without letting it burn.

Finish noodles: Add drained noodles and the clean chili-soy mixture. Lift and turn gently for about 2–4 minutes until hot and tender; use a small splash of water if they stick or need further softening. Avoid vigorous stirring that tears the strands.

Combine: Return shrimp and plate juices only long enough to warm through, about 30 seconds. Taste before adding any further salt and pepper. Divide noodles and the actual shrimp count evenly among bowls and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Shrimp & Sweet Potato Noodle Stir-Fry
recipes.description: This shrimp stir-fry combines Korean sweet potato glass noodles with soy, lime and ginger. The noodles stay chewy when cooked to the package’s endpoint and drained well.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
4 green onions, whites and greens separated, sliced
Gochugaru or red pepper flakes (optional, for heat)
2 tbsp high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), divided
Water, for cooking noodles according to the package

recipeInstructions.text: Coat and stage: Pat the prepared raw shrimp dry with paper towels. Toss large shrimp, soy sauce, and cornstarch until evenly coated. Keep chilled during the 10-minute stand while preparing the other ingredients; cook promptly after preparation. Keep coating and sauce soy sauce separate.

Cook noodles: Have sweet potato glass noodles (dangmyeon), toasted sesame oil, and water ready for the noodles. Boil the noodles following the package for water, timing and any rinse instruction, checking for pliable, springy noodles without a hard center. Drain thoroughly and toss with their measured sesame oil. Start checking around 6–7 minutes only if consistent with the actual package.
Whisk sauce: Whisk soy sauce, fresh lime juice, honey, toasted sesame oil, and fish sauce until the honey disperses; keep beside the stove.

Start shrimp: Heat a wok or heavy skillet over medium-high to high heat appropriate to the pan, following its preheating instructions; keep the oil below its smoke point. Add 1/2 of the high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), reserving the other half of this oil for aromatics. Spread the coated shrimp into a single layer, using batches and dividing this oil allowance across them if needed. Cook about 1 minute per side as an initial check, until the surface changes color; transfer immediately to a temporary dish for further cooking in step 7. Do not taste partly cooked shrimp.

Cook aromatics: Add 1/2 of the high-smoke-point oil (avocado or grapeseed), garlic cloves, fresh ginger, the green-onion whites, and gochugaru or red pepper flakes (if using) to the pan. Keep all green-onion greens for finishing. Stir about 30 seconds until fragrant, reducing heat if garlic begins to brown too quickly.

Cook vegetables: Add large carrot and snow peas, carrots first for about 2 minutes, then snow peas for another 1–2 minutes, stirring until crisp-tender. These are first checks, not fixed endpoints for every cut.

Toss and finish cooking: Return all noodles, shrimp and collected shrimp juices to the pan. Add all the sauce and lift/toss to distribute it, starting to check after 1–2 minutes. Cook until the thickest shrimp are firm, pearly and opaque throughout; FDA guidance is 145°F for seafood when checking with a suitable thermometer. Pink color or a fixed minute count alone does not establish doneness. The sauce should coat the noodles without dry starch patches. A larger batch needs separate complete pan loads; do not crowd the final toss after batching shrimp.

Finish: Finish with the green-onion greens, lime, and toasted sesame seeds: fold in all green-onion greens, scatter sesame seeds as wanted, and offer the lime wedges for squeezing to taste. This lime is separate from the measured sauce juice. Transfer to a clean serving dish and serve promptly.

recipes.name: Shrimp Fettuccine Alfredo
recipes.description: Prepare the full linked Alfredo batch and cook the shrimp just until firm and pearly opaque through their thickest centers. Pasta, shrimp and sauce can overlap, but the scratch sauce needs its own preparation time.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Raw Jumbo Shrimp, peeled and deveined
Water, as needed to boil pasta
1/2 cup Pasta cooking water, reserved before draining; one shared supply for sauce and final toss
Water, a little as needed when reheating leftovers

recipeInstructions.text: For the scratch version, read the complete Alfredo Sauce first and grate its Parmesan. Make one full linked batch for this original four-serving pasta recipe, matching the same scaling factor for both recipes. Use its full butter, cream and Parmesan amounts. Bring pasta water to a boil, using part of the listed salt allowance, and cook fettuccine according to its package. Reserve the listed pasta-water supply before draining.

Use raw peeled, deveined shrimp; if frozen, thaw in the refrigerator first and drain. Toss with the garlic powder and some of the remaining salt and black pepper. Keep the raw-shrimp bowl and utensils separate from the cooked-shrimp plate.

Heat some of the total olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook shrimp in uncrowded loads, dividing the same total oil across loads. Turn as needed, beginning checks around 2 minutes per side; time depends on size and pan heat. Continue until the thick centers are firm and pearly opaque. Move fully cooked shrimp to a clean plate.

For scratch sauce, follow the linked complete butter–cream–garlic stage in the shrimp skillet. Before the offheat Parmesan stage, simmer the cream base as directed and verify it reaches at least 145°F /63°C so liquid in the raw-contact pan is heated as well; then melt the Parmesan gently as the linked recipe directs. Alternatively, prepare that same complete batch in a separate clean saucepan. The sauce recipe can use up to ¼ cup of the original ½-cup shared pasta-water reserve; keep the rest for the final toss. Do not add the sauce allowance on top of the pasta reserve.

Toss the hot pasta and fully cooked shrimp with the sauce. Add remaining shared pasta water a little at a time if needed to loosen; not all of it may be necessary. Adjust with the remaining salt and pepper allowance without adding another fixed dose.
Top with the chopped parsley and serve immediately.
