recipes.name: Shrimp Linguine with Fresh Tomato, White Wine & Basil
recipes.description: Fresh spinach linguine with shrimp, grated Roma tomatoes, white wine and basil, finished with butter and an optional crisp breadcrumb topping.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw large shrimp, weighed after peeling and deveining, shells reserved
1 tsp kosher salt, for seasoning shrimp
1 tsp olive oil, for shell stock
1 tbsp olive oil, for cooking shrimp
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
1 lemon, finely zest the whole fruit and juice half
Extra-virgin olive oil, optional, for finishing
2 cups reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
1 clove garlic, grated, for the optional topping
1 tbsp olive oil, for the optional topping

recipeInstructions.text: Peel and season: Peel and devein shrimp, reserving shells. Toss peeled meat with the measured shrimp salt and optional baking soda. Refrigerate for 15–30 minutes while preparing the stock and vegetables. Wash raw-contact tools and pat shrimp dry just before cooking.

Make shell stock: Heat the oil labeled for stock in a small saucepan over medium heat. Stir shells for about 2–3 minutes until pink and aromatic. Add a small splash taken from the measured wine and all the stock water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 15 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh strainer, pressing shells, then discard shells. Measure the liquid and reduce to half the starting water volume if necessary; add a little water if reduced below that target.

Prepare optional topping: If using it, warm the topping oil in the skillet over medium-low. Toast panko, stirring, until beginning to turn golden, about 2–3 minutes. Add the grated topping garlic and a little salt and stir about 30–60 seconds more until fragrant and golden. Transfer to a bowl. Meanwhile have tomatoes grated, shallots and garlic prepared and pasta water heating.

Cook shrimp: Add the oil labeled for shrimp to the skillet over medium-high. Cook shrimp in a single layer about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Use batches if crowded, sharing the oil. Transfer to a clean plate.

Soften aromatics: Lower heat to medium. Add shallot oil and one-fifth of the butter. Cook shallots about 4–5 minutes until softened, then add sliced garlic and crushed red pepper and stir about 30–45 seconds until fragrant without darkening.

Build tomato sauce: Add all remaining measured wine and simmer about 2–4 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Add grated tomatoes with their juices and the measured finished stock. Simmer gently about 10–15 minutes until lightly thickened and flowing. Taste before adding salt and pepper.

Cook pasta: When sauce is ready, stir in baby spinach until wilted. Cook fresh linguine in salted boiling water according to its package, checking early and stopping just short of fully tender. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining. Do not assume every fresh noodle cooks in two minutes.

Finish off heat: Add pasta to sauce and turn gently, using a small splash of reserved water if needed. When the pasta is tender, remove from heat and add remaining four-fifths of the butter in small pieces, tossing until the coating is smooth. Fold in cooked shrimp and their juices only to warm through.

Season and serve: Add lemon zest, juice from half the lemon gradually to taste and most of the measured basil. Taste before adding further salt or pepper. Divide into bowls and finish with the remaining basil, optional olive-oil drizzle and optional breadcrumbs. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Shrimp with Lobster Sauce
recipes.description: This dark, pork-and-douchi version follows a Boston-Chinese style; it contains shrimp, not lobster. Pour beaten egg over gently simmering sauce and give the ribbons time to form before folding.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), quickly rinsed, drained and mashed
1 lb shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined
green onions, washed and chopped, as wanted for garnish

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare slurry: Whisk cornstarch and cold water smooth in a small bowl. Have the prepared beans, garlic, shrimp and beaten egg ready before cooking.

Cook pork: Cook neutral oil and ground pork: warm the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat, add pork and break it into small crumbles. Cook until browned, beginning to check around 5 minutes; a crisp surface or disappearance of pink is not the final endpoint. Keep cooking promptly through the following steps.
Add aromatics: Stir in garlic cloves and fermented black beans (douchi) and cook about 1 minute until fragrant, reducing heat before the garlic scorches.
Start shrimp: Add shrimp and stir-fry about 2 minutes until the outside changes color. The shrimp continue cooking in sauce; pink alone is not the endpoint.

Simmer and thicken: Pour in chicken stock, soy sauce, and dark soy sauce and bring to a simmer. Re-stir the prepared slurry and stir all of it into the simmering sauce. Simmer about 1 minute, until the starch is cooked and the sauce coats a spoon; continue as needed rather than promising immediate gloss.

Set egg ribbons: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer. Pour large egg in a thin stream over the surface; let the ribbons begin to set before folding gently. Continue cooking until the pork and egg sauce reach 160°F / 71°C and the thickest shrimp have firm, pearly, opaque centers. Keep heat on as needed; a 30-second off-heat stand does not certify cooking.
Serve: Garnish with green onions and serve promptly over separately prepared white rice if wanted.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, savory, umami, comfort-food, weeknight, quick-lunch, fry, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Shrimp Scampi with Linguini
recipes.description: Linguine with shrimp in a generous lemon, white-wine and butter sauce, finished with parsley and Parmesan.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw large shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
1/2 cup unsalted butter, cold and cut into small pieces
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for cooking shrimp
1 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for shallots and garlic
2 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing the sauce
1 large lemon, juiced, juice added gradually to taste
Kosher salt and black pepper, to taste
1 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and start pasta: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it. Prepare garlic, shallots, parsley and lemon; pat the shrimp dry and season lightly with salt and pepper. Cook linguine about 1 minute short of its package al dente time, coordinating it with the sauce below. Reserve the listed cooking water before draining.

Cook shrimp: Heat the oil labeled for shrimp over medium to medium-high. Add shrimp in a single layer; use batches if crowded, sharing that oil. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side, continuing as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

Soften aromatics: Lower heat to medium and add the oil labeled for shallots and garlic. Cook shallots about 4–5 minutes until softened. Add garlic and pepper flakes and stir about 30–45 seconds until fragrant without darkening.

Reduce wine: Add wine and scrape the pan. Simmer about 2–4 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Add the drained pasta and a small splash of reserved water; toss over low heat until the pasta is tender with a little bite.

Finish off heat: Remove the pan from heat. Add cold butter a few pieces at a time while tossing, then drizzle in the finishing oil. Add more reserved water in small splashes if needed for a coating that clings. Fold in half the lemon juice, parsley, shrimp and plate juices. Warm very briefly over low heat only if necessary.

Taste and serve: Taste a strand with sauce before adding remaining lemon juice, salt or pepper. Divide shrimp and pasta evenly among plates and offer Parmesan at the table. Serve promptly rather than holding the pasta over heat.

recipes.name: Shrimp Vodka Pasta
recipes.description: Rigatoni, shrimp and broccoli in a tomato-vodka cream sauce, with basil stirred in and scattered over the top.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
1 large broccoli crown, cut into bite-size florets with thin stems
2 tbsp olive oil, divided into three equal portions
1/2 tsp kosher salt, added to taste, plus salt for pasta water
1 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
Water, a small splash if needed to finish broccoli

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and start pasta: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it. Cut broccoli, mince garlic, chop basil and dry shrimp. Cook rigatoni about 1 minute short of the package al dente time, coordinating it with the sauce. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining.

Cook broccoli: Heat one-third of the oil over medium heat. Add broccoli and sauté about 5–7 minutes until stems yield with a little resistance. If needed, add a small splash of water and cover briefly to finish the stems; uncover to evaporate free water. Transfer to a plate.

Cook shrimp: Add another third of the oil and arrange shrimp in a single layer. Cook about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

Start sauce: Lower heat to medium-low. Add remaining oil and garlic and stir about 30 seconds until fragrant. Take the pan away from the burner, add measured vodka carefully, then return to medium-low heat. Simmer gently for about 2–3 minutes, without deliberately igniting it.

Simmer and combine: Add marinara, cream, half the basil, black pepper and only as much of the measured salt as needed after tasting the prepared sauce. Simmer gently about 5 minutes. Add pasta and broccoli and toss over low heat until pasta is tender with a little bite, using reserved water in small splashes if necessary.
Finish shrimp: Fold in shrimp and their juices only long enough to warm through. Turn off heat, scatter with remaining basil and serve promptly. Avoid holding the finished pasta over heat.

recipes.name: Shrimp with Black Bean Sauce
recipes.description: Fermented black beans season this dark gravy, which also contains ground pork and egg ribbons. Blanching the pork is a preliminary preparation step; it still cooks in the sauce.
recipeIngredient: 12 oz shrimp, raw, peeled and deveined, 21/25 size
water, enough to cover pork for blanching
1 1/2 tbsp fermented black beans (douchi), quickly rinsed, drained and mashed slightly
1/4 cup green bell pepper, finely diced
additional water or chicken stock, a little at a time only if needed to loosen sauce, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Rinse the black beans and mash slightly. Whisk chicken stock, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, sugar, and white pepper. Have all aromatics chopped and shrimp prepared before pan cooking. In a separate bowl, stir the measured slurry cornstarch and cold water until smooth; keep it separate from the stock mixture.

Blanch pork: Prepare ground pork and water. Bring enough water to cover the pork to a boil, then add the pork, breaking up clumps, and blanch for about 1 minute. Drain and set aside for immediate further cooking; this blanch is not the final doneness check. Empty and dry the wok before adding oil.

Cook aromatics and start shrimp: Use shrimp, vegetable oil, garlic clove, fresh ginger, fermented black beans (douchi), green bell pepper, and Shaoxing wine: heat the oil over medium-high heat, then sauté garlic, ginger, peppers, black beans and the blanched pork for about 30 seconds. Add shrimp and Shaoxing wine and stir-fry about 30 seconds. Continue immediately into the sauce stage; these brief stages do not establish doneness.
Heat stock mixture: Pour in all the stock mixture and bring to a rapid boil, then reduce to a simmer.

Thicken gradually: Use cornstarch, cold water, and additional water or chicken stock (if using). Re-stir the prepared slurry, then add it gradually while stirring the simmering sauce. Stop when the sauce coats a spoon; you may not need all the slurry. Thin with a little water or stock if needed. Keep unused raw-contact slurry separate from ready-to-eat food and discard it after cooking.

Set egg ribbons: Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer. Pour large egg across the surface and let the ribbons begin to set before folding gently. Continue cooking until the pork and egg sauce reach 160°F / 71°C and the thickest shrimp have pearly, opaque flesh. Ten seconds alone is not a doneness test.
Serve: Garnish with scallion and serve immediately over separately prepared steamed jasmine rice if wanted.

recipes.name: Shrimp Wonton Soup
recipes.description: Cantonese wontons rely on a filling that's sticky and cohesive, achieved by stirring ground pork and shrimp vigorously in one direction until proteins bind into a tacky paste. This traditional technique prevents the filling from crumbling during boiling.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil, for the filling
Additional Toasted Sesame Oil, a few drops per serving bowl
1 tbsp Light Soy Sauce, for the filling
4 tsp Light Soy Sauce, for the bowls, or less to taste
1 lb prepared Wonton Wrappers; use as many as needed for the filling
4 cups prepared [Cantonese Wonton Broth](/mise/recipes/cantonese-wonton-broth), plus extra to taste
Water, for sealing wrappers and boiling wontons
Baby Bok Choy or Spinach, as desired
1 tbsp Black Vinegar, for serving, optional

recipeInstructions.text: The Filling: In a large bowl, combine pork, shrimp, ginger, scallions, egg white, the filling soy sauce, and the filling sesame oil. Stir vigorously in one direction for 3 minutes until sticky.

Assemble: Place 1 tsp filling in the center of a prepared wonton wrapper. If making Fresh Wonton Wrappers, allow their preparation and resting time separately. Dab edges with water, fold into a triangle, and pinch the corners together.

The Base: Heat the prepared broth in a saucepan. Divide the nori among four serving bowls and add a few drops of sesame oil to each. Add up to 1 tsp of the bowl soy sauce per bowl, tasting with a little broth first because the broth is already seasoned.

Boil: Bring a separate pot of water to a gentle boil. Add the wontons in batches without crowding. Start checking after 3-4 minutes; floating alone does not establish doneness. Check several wontons with a thin-tip thermometer inserted into the center of the filling and continue until they reach 165°F / 74°C. Cook the greens in the hot broth until tender.
Bind: Ladle 1 cup of the hot prepared broth into each serving bowl to "wake up" the seasonings.
Serve: Transfer the cooked wontons and greens to the bowls. Garnish with fresh coriander and offer the black vinegar at the table. Refrigerate unused wrappers according to their package instructions.

recipes.name: Shruff's End
recipes.description: Shruff's End comes from the modern craft cocktail movement, representing the bold, spirit-forward style popularized by bars like Death & Co in New York. The name likely references Shruff House from the Harry Potter series, fitting for a drink that combines magic-like alchemy.
recipeIngredient: 1 oz heavily peated 10-year Islay single-malt Scotch
0.5 oz French honeyed herbal liqueur (40% ABV)
Orange peel or lemon peel for garnish (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: Add the Scotch, apple brandy, French honeyed herbal liqueur, and New Orleans-style anise-forward bitters to a mixing glass filled with ice.
Stir well for 20-30: seconds until properly chilled and diluted.
Strain into a chilled: coupe or rocks glass over a large ice cube (if serving on the rocks).
Express an orange or: lemon peel over the drink and garnish if desired.
Serve immediately and enjoy: the complex interplay of smoke, fruit, and herbal notes.

recipes.name: Zucchini Soup
recipes.description: Gently cooked zucchini, onion and garlic blended with stock, butter and olive oil, finished with raw zucchini matchsticks.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 lb zucchini, halved lengthwise and sliced about 1/4 inch thick
Additional raw zucchini, cut into fine matchsticks, for garnish
Salt and white pepper, to taste

recipeInstructions.name: Directions
recipeInstructions.description: Adapted from Grant Achatz’s Silky Zucchini Soup at Food & Wine.

itemListElement.text: Soften onion: Melt butter with olive oil in a saucepan over medium-low. Add onion and garlic with a little salt and white pepper. Cook about 7–8 minutes, stirring, until soft without browning.
Cook zucchini: Add the measured sliced zucchini and cook about 10 minutes, stirring frequently, until softened. Lower heat if the bottom starts browning.

Simmer: Add stock and all the measured water. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook about 10 minutes, until zucchini crushes readily with a spoon. While it cooks, wash and finely cut the additional raw garnish zucchini.

Blend: Remove from heat and let active bubbling stop. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping its guard submerged and stopping before lifting it. Alternatively, cool to your countertop blender’s permitted temperature and blend in as many small batches as its hot-liquid fill limit requires, with the lid and steam vent arranged exactly as its instructions specify. Start low; do not use a sealed personal cup for hot soup.

Finish and serve: Stir in the measured lemon juice, then taste for salt and white pepper. Warm gently if needed and divide into the intended soup portions. Add raw zucchini matchsticks just before serving.

recipes.keywords: American, sweet, acidic, rich, comfort-food, saute, simmer, blend

citation.name: Adapted from Grant Achatz, Food & Wine

recipes.name: Dry-Brined Roast Turkey with Cider
recipes.description: A smaller whole turkey seasoned a day ahead, with weighed salt, dry skin, herb-cider pan aromatics and doneness checks in both breast and leg meat.
recipeIngredient: 1 whole turkey, 10–12 lb (4.5–5.4 kg), fully refrigerator-thawed, not kosher, pre-brined or enhanced with a salt solution
25 g salt, weighed regardless of crystal size
1 lemon, finely zested, then cut into wedges
12 garlic cloves, lightly smashed and peeled
1 onion (about 200 g), peeled and cut into wedges
1 bottle (330 ml) dry hard apple cider
1 cup (240 ml) water, plus up to 2 cups (480 ml) hot water for the roasting pan if needed

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the thawed bird: Remove packaging, neck and giblet bags, checking both cavities. Reserve those parts separately under appropriate refrigerated storage or discard. Pat the turkey dry with disposable towels; do not wash it in the sink. Put breast-side up on a rack over a deep rimmed tray or roasting pan that fits in the refrigerator.

Season twenty-four hours ahead: Mix the weighed salt with black pepper and the lemon zest. Distribute it evenly over the bird, using some directly over the breast and upper leg meat under gently loosened skin; avoid tearing the skin or depositing the mixture in one pocket. Refrigerate uncovered for twenty-four hours at 40°F / 4°C or below, protected from contact with other foods. Refrigerate the zested lemon separately for the pan. Do not rinse off the seasoning before roasting.

Prepare the oven and pan: Heat the oven to 325°F / 163°C with space for the turkey on a lower rack. Keep the bird refrigerated while the oven heats. Put garlic, onion, lemon wedges, thyme, rosemary and sage in the roasting pan beneath the rack. Add the cider, wine and initial cup of water. Set the turkey on the rack breast-side up, keep its cavity empty, tuck the wing tips underneath and brush the skin with all the melted butter in a thin coat. Use a clean brush; no repeated basting is needed.

Roast and manage the drippings: Roast at 325°F / 163°C. Begin checking the pan after about an hour, then periodically; carefully add a little of the listed hot water before the bottom dries out. Keep a shallow layer rather than submerging the bird. If skin colors strongly before the meat is ready, shield that area loosely with foil. Do not repeatedly open the oven just to wet the skin.

Measure every required site: Begin temperature checks after about 2 1/2 hours; plan roughly 2 3/4–3 1/4 hours total roasting, with additional time possible. A leave-in breast probe helps track progress, but use an instant-read thermometer to check the thickest part of each breast, the innermost part of each thigh and the innermost wing areas, clear of bone. Continue roasting until all reach at least 165°F / 74°C. Check again in a nearby spot if a reading seems implausible. A single thigh reading, clear juices and browned skin are insufficient.

Rest and carve: Move the bird to a clean carving board and rest thirty minutes, loosely tented if needed. Carve breasts from the bone and slice across the grain, then separate legs and thighs. Divide among about ten diners with sides; this is not a promise of ten identical meat weights or abundant leftovers. Strain the pan liquid, discard spent aromatics and taste before deciding whether to use it in a separate gravy. Do not serve burned or excessively salty pan deposits.

recipes.name: Korean Spinach Salad (Sigeumchi Namul)
recipes.description: Sigeumchi namul is a simple spinach banchan. Cool the wilted leaves promptly, then remove excess water with a gentle squeeze.
recipeIngredient: 250 g fresh spinach, roots trimmed and leaves washed
1 tsp fine sea salt, for blanching water
1/4 tsp fine sea salt, for seasoning, added to taste
Cold water, as needed for cooling

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Bring the measured water and blanching salt to a boil. Set out a colander and cold water for cooling.
Blanch: Add washed spinach and stir it under the water. Start checking at 30 seconds; remove it when the leaves have wilted and stems are tender, allowing longer for thick stems.
Cool: Drain and rinse under cold running water or transfer to fresh cold water until cool enough to handle.
Drain gently: Lift out small handfuls and squeeze gently to remove excess water. Do not wring the leaves bone-dry. Cut long stems and leaves into bite-size lengths; baby leaves can remain whole.

Season: Mix sesame oil, garlic, scallion and part of the seasoning salt in a bowl. Separate the spinach, add it with the sesame seeds and toss gently. Taste before adding the remaining seasoning salt.
Serve: Divide into the listed small side portions (four in the original batch), or cover and refrigerate promptly until serving.

recipes.name: Skillet Biscuits with Berries
recipes.description: These butter-rich biscuit mounds steam over berries before a brief broiler finish. Keep the lid on over very low heat until the biscuit centers are cooked, then watch the broiler closely for lightly browned tops against the soft fruit.
recipeIngredient: 12 tbsp (1 1/2 sticks) unsalted butter, cold, cut into small cubes

recipeInstructions.text: Mix the dough ingredients: In a large bowl combine the dough’s all-purpose flour, light brown sugar, baking powder, and salt.
Cut in the butter: Cut the unsalted butter into the dry mixture with a pastry blender or fingertips until the mixture is coarse with small pieces of butter still visible.

Shape the mounds: Stir in the half-and-half just until evenly moistened. Scoop one loose mound per listed portion, keeping the mounds approximately the original size; the original batch makes eight. Set them on a parchment-lined tray and keep the dough cool while the berries cook.

Simmer the berries: Position an oven rack about 6 inches below the broiler and preheat the broiler according to its instructions. In a large, deep skillet approved for broiling, combine the berries’ raspberries, blackberries, granulated sugar, water, finely grated orange zest, and cinnamon stick. Bring to a vigorous boil, then reduce to a moderate simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 10 minutes until the berries are juicy and just broken down.

Steam the biscuits: Arrange the dough mounds over the bubbling fruit in a single layer with room to expand. The original batch uses eight mounds; for a different quantity use a suitably smaller skillet or additional skillets rather than crowding or increasing mound size. Cover with a fitting lid and simmer over very low heat for about 15 minutes, until the biscuit tops are springy and the centers are cooked through. Check a center biscuit for moist crumb rather than raw dough; if needed, cover and continue simmering before broiling.

Brown the tops: Remove the lid and sprinkle the biscuits with additional granulated sugar. Broil about 6 inches from the heat for up to 5 minutes, watching continuously and shifting the pan as needed, until lightly browned in spots. Stop sooner if they brown quickly; broiling does not replace cooking the centers.

Cool slightly and serve: Let the skillet cool slightly, remove and discard the cinnamon stick, then serve biscuits and berries warm with sweetened whipped cream. Handle the hot skillet and handle with oven mitts.

recipes.name: Skinny Broccoli Mac & Cheese
recipes.description: Lighter mac and cheese works when you lean on technique instead of just cutting fat. The roux here uses less butter than a classic béchamel, but the combination of skim milk and chicken broth creates a sauce with real body - the broth adds savory depth that low-fat cheese alone can't deliver.
recipeIngredient: 2 cups Skim Milk + 1 cup Chicken Broth

recipeInstructions.text: The Pot: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta. 2 minutes before the pasta is al dente, add the broccoli florets. Drain.
The Roux: In a large skillet, melt butter. Sauté onion for 2 minutes. Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute until golden.
Emulsify: Slowly whisk in the milk and broth. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Season with salt and pepper.
Bind: Remove from heat. Stir in the cheddar until molten. Fold in the cooked macaroni and broccoli.
Bake: Transfer to a greased baking dish. Sprinkle with breadcrumbs and Parmesan.
Finish: Bake at 375°F for 15-20 minutes. Broil for 2 minutes until the top is crispy and the cheese is "Snappy."

recipes.keywords: American, savory, umami, rich, weeknight, kid-friendly, comfort-food, meal-prep, bake, saute, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Cheesy Mushroom Quinoa
recipes.description: Using a strict 1:2 ratio of quinoa to liquid and cooking on High for a shorter duration (2-3 hours instead of 4-5) ensures each grain maintains its texture and distinct curly tail rather than turning to porridge. Adding cream cheese cubes at the very end creates risotto-like silkiness that standard shredded cheese cannot achieve - the residual heat melts it into a smooth, creamy sauce.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: Add quinoa, mushrooms, broth, red pepper, garlic, and herbs to the slow cooker. Stir well.
Cook: Cover and cook on High for 2-3 hours (or Low for 4-5 hours) until the liquid is fully absorbed.
Emulsify: Open the lid. Add the cream cheese cubes. Stir vigorously for 1 minute until the cream cheese has melted and emulsified with the grain.
Bind: Top with the Italian cheese blend. Cover and cook for another 15 minutes until molten.
Finish: Stir once more. Garnish with fresh green onions for the mandatory High Note.

recipes.keywords: American, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, slow-cook, blend

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Chicken Noodle Soup
recipes.description: A thyme-scented chicken and vegetable broth with shredded thigh meat and separately cooked fusilli that stays distinct in the bowl.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, added gradually to taste

recipeInstructions.text: Load the cooker: Place onion, small carrot and celery pieces, garlic, thyme, rosemary and pepper in a 6-quart slow cooker. Add thawed chicken and stock. Cover and start cooking immediately; do not use a delayed start with raw chicken.

Cook and check: Cook on LOW about 5–6 hours, or HIGH about 3–4 hours, until several thick chicken pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and the carrots are tender. Extend as needed. Keep the lid closed between checks.

Cook pasta near service: Once the soup is close to ready, bring the pasta water to a boil in a separate pot. Cook fusilli according to its package until just tender, then drain. Cook a proportional amount if serving only part of the soup.

Shred the chicken: Transfer fully cooked chicken to a clean board, let stand briefly until safe to handle, and shred into bite-sized pieces. Return it to the hot soup and warm through. Avoid leaving it out while doing unrelated preparation.
Balance: Taste the fully cooked broth. Add measured salt gradually only if needed. Stir in parsley and start with half the lemon juice, adding more to taste.
Assemble bowls: Divide pasta among six bowls, then add chicken, vegetables and broth. Serve promptly. Keep any remaining pasta separate from the soup for storage.

recipes.keywords: American, savory, herbaceous, bright, comfort-food, slow-cook, boil

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Chicken Ramen with Miso
recipes.description: Chicken-leg broth with shiitake and a brief kombu infusion, finished with miso, bok choy, fresh ramen noodles and measured toppings.
recipeIngredient: 1.35 kg bone-in skin-on chicken whole legs, fully thawed
2 liters water, plus hot water only to adjust strained broth volume
15 g dried shiitake mushrooms, rinsed briefly to remove grit
100 g white miso paste, added gradually to taste
2 tbsp tamari or light soy sauce, added gradually only if needed
450 g baby bok choy, washed, stems sliced 1/2 inch thick and leaves cut into bite-sized pieces
600 g fresh ramen noodles, seasoning packets discarded if included
1 sheet toasted nori, cut into 10 pieces, optional
2 liters water, for cooking noodles and eggs as described
Ice and cold water, for cooling cooked eggs

recipeInstructions.text: Start the broth: Put thawed chicken legs, 2 liters broth water, scallion whites, garlic, shiitake and mirin in a 6-quart slow cooker. Cover and start immediately. Keep scallion greens refrigerated for serving.

Cook chicken: Cook on LOW about 5–6 hours or HIGH about 3–4 hours until each leg reaches 165°F / 74°C away from bone and the meat pulls away readily. Extend if needed. Transfer chicken to a clean tray and mushrooms to a small bowl; let chicken cool only enough to handle.

Strain and infuse: Strain broth into a 4-quart saucepan and discard spent scallion and garlic. Skim excess surface fat. Aim for about 1.8–2 liters broth, adding a little hot water if needed. While the broth is steaming hot but not boiling, add kombu and leave off heat for about 10 minutes, then remove it. During the infusion, discard chicken skin/bones and shred meat; discard tough mushroom stems and slice the caps.

Prepare optional eggs and noodles: Bring the noodle/egg water to a boil in a separate pot. If using eggs, lower them in carefully and simmer gently about 11–12 minutes until whites and yolks are firm. Transfer to ice water for 5 minutes, then peel and halve. Return the pot water to a boil and cook ramen according to its package, draining just before assembly. If omitting eggs, simply cook the noodles near serving.

Cook greens and warm meat: Bring the strained broth back to a gentle simmer. Add bok choy stems and cook about 2–3 minutes; add leaves, chicken and mushrooms and cook until stems are tender, leaves wilted and chicken is heated through to 165°F / 74°C. Turn off heat.

Finish with miso: Whisk about three-quarters of the miso with a ladleful of hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot. Taste and add remaining miso and tamari gradually only as needed. Do not boil the seasoned soup for a long hold.

Assemble: Divide noodles among five large bowls. Add chicken, mushrooms, bok choy and about 350–400 ml broth per bowl. Finish with sliced scallion greens and the optional egg halves, two nori pieces and a little sesame per bowl. Serve promptly.

recipes.keywords: Japanese, sweet, savory, comfort-food, slow-cook, simmer, boil

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Cilantro Lime Chicken
recipes.description: Shredded chicken with black beans, corn and salsa, finished with fresh cilantro and lime for six tortilla servings.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken breasts, fully thawed, left whole
1 can (15 oz / 425 g) black beans, rinsed and drained, about 255 g drained total
1 can (10 oz / 283 g) diced tomatoes with green chiles, with juices
150 g corn kernels, fresh or thawed frozen
150 g red onion, cut into 1/4-inch dice
1 jalapeño, seeds removed and finely diced, optional
1 tsp mild chili powder blend, not pure hot chile powder
1/2 cup loosely packed chopped fresh cilantro, reserved for finishing
3 tbsp fresh lime juice, added gradually to taste
1/4 tsp fine salt, only if needed
Water, a small splash only if needed while finishing the onion
12 small corn tortillas, about 6 inches across
1 large ripe avocado, about 200 g edible flesh, sliced just before serving

recipeInstructions.text: Load: Combine drained beans, tomatoes and their juices, corn, salsa verde, finely diced onion, optional jalapeño, cumin, chili blend and pepper in a 4-quart slow cooker. Nestle in fully thawed whole breasts and spoon some sauce over them. Cover and start immediately. Keep cilantro and avocado for serving.

Cook and check: Cook on LOW about 3–4 hours, beginning checks around 2 1/2 hours, or HIGH about 2–3 hours. Check several thick breast centers for 165°F / 74°C. Remove fully cooked chicken to a clean board even if the onion needs longer; check a piece of onion separately.

Finish the filling base: If onion is still firm or the base is watery, transfer the bean mixture to a wide saucepan and simmer, stirring gently, about 5–10 minutes or until onion is tender and excess liquid has evaporated. Add a small splash of water only if the onion needs more cooking and the pan is dry. Meanwhile shred the chicken into bite-sized pieces.

Combine and season: Fold chicken and its juices back into the hot filling and warm briefly through. Turn off heat. Add cilantro and half the lime juice, taste, then add remaining juice and measured salt only as needed.

Warm tortillas: Heat a dry skillet over medium heat. Warm tortillas in batches, about 20–30 seconds per side or following their package, until pliable and lightly spotted. Wrap in a clean towel as each batch finishes; do not char them until brittle.

Serve: Slice avocado just before serving. Divide filling among six diners, with two warm tortillas and one-sixth of the avocado each. Spoon excess cooking liquid sparingly so the tortillas stay manageable.

recipes.keywords: Tex-Mex, spicy, acidic, comfort-food, slow-cook, simmer

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker General Tso–Style Chicken
recipes.description: Tender chicken thighs in a tangy ginger-chile sauce, thickened on the stove just before serving.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, left whole
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus a little only if needed to loosen the finished sauce
1 tbsp granulated sugar, added gradually to taste
1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, or less to taste
2 tbsp cold water, for the slurry

recipeInstructions.text: Load: In a 3-quart slow cooker, stir hoisin, soy sauce, 120 ml water, 1 tbsp of the vinegar, ginger, garlic and pepper flakes. Add fully thawed whole thighs and turn to coat. Cover and start immediately.

Cook and check: Cook on LOW about 3–4 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, until several thick pieces reach 165°F / 74°C and are tender. Keep the lid closed between checks. Transfer chicken to a clean plate and cover loosely while finishing the sauce.

Set sauce volume: Pour cooking liquid into a saucepan, scraping in the garlic and ginger. Skim excess surface fat. Aim for roughly 300–350 ml liquid: simmer briefly if much more remains, or add a little water if very concentrated. Taste only after the chicken has completed cooking; avoid reducing an already salty sauce further.

Thicken: Mix cornstarch with its 2 tbsp cold water until smooth. Bring sauce to a simmer. Re-stir the slurry and whisk in half, simmering about 1 minute. Add more slurry gradually only if needed, letting each addition thicken. Stop when the sauce lightly coats a spoon and remains pourable.

Balance and return chicken: Add 1 tbsp of the remaining vinegar and half the sugar. Taste, then add the remaining vinegar and sugar only as needed. Cut or pull chicken into large bite-sized pieces, return it and its plate juices to the sauce, and warm gently through without a long boil.
Serve: Divide into four main portions and scatter over scallions. Serve with separately prepared plain rice and vegetables. This chicken is tender and saucy; it has no crisp fried coating.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-American, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, meal-prep, comfort-food, weeknight, slow-cook, simmer

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Hoisin Garlic Chicken
recipes.description: Tender pulled chicken thighs with a garlic-hoisin sauce reduced separately and finished with balsamic vinegar.
recipeIngredient: 900 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, excess surface fat trimmed
1/2 cup (120 ml) water, plus a little only to adjust the finished sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Combine: Stir hoisin, tomato paste, 120 ml water, 2 tsp balsamic vinegar, minced garlic and optional pepper flakes in a 3–4-quart slow cooker. Add thawed whole thighs and turn to coat. Cover and start cooking immediately.

Cook: Cook on LOW about 4–5 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, checking that several thick thighs reach 165°F / 74°C and pull apart readily. Extend if needed for tenderness. Transfer chicken to a clean platter and cover loosely.

Reduce carefully: Pour liquid and garlic into a wide saucepan and skim excess fat. Bring to a lively simmer, stirring regularly, until it lightly coats a spoon, usually about 8–12 minutes. Roughly 250–300 ml is a useful target, not a reason to oversalt it: taste as it reduces and stop earlier if already concentrated. Add a little water if too sticky or salty.

Pull and coat: Pull the chicken into large strands, discarding any unwanted gristle. Stir the reserved 1 tsp balsamic into the sauce gradually to taste. Add chicken and plate juices, then fold over low heat just until hot and coated.

Serve: Divide into six modest main portions with separately prepared rice and broccoli, and finish with the sliced scallions. The recipe does not include an additional batch of rice or lettuce-wrap ingredients.

recipes.keywords: Chinese-inspired, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, comfort-food, meal-prep, weeknight, slow-cook, simmer

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Korean Beef
recipes.description: Chuck cubes need long cooking for tenderness. The soy, ginger and brown-sugar sauce thickens with a cool cornstarch slurry near the end; keep its water separate from the broth.
recipeIngredient: 3 lb boneless beef chuck roast, fully thawed, cut into 1-inch cubes
cooked jasmine rice, as wanted for serving, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Keep fully thawed beef refrigerated until preparation. Check the actual 6-quart cooker’s load instructions, then cut the chuck into the listed 1-inch cubes. Start promptly after loading; do not use a delayed timer.

Mix the sauce: Whisk beef broth, low-sodium soy sauce, light brown sugar, garlic cloves, toasted sesame oil, rice wine vinegar, fresh ginger, Sriracha, onion powder, and white pepper in a bowl until the sugar is dispersed. Sriracha enters this sauce, rather than being required again at finishing.

Slow cook: Put boneless beef chuck roast in the cooker and add all the sauce. Cover and cook on LOW for 7–8 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours as planning ranges, until the chuck is fork-tender and pulls apart easily. Check beef has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with a three-minute rest before serving; tender chuck commonly needs substantially more cooking than the minimum. Keep covered except for necessary doneness checks.

Thicken at the end: Whisk cornstarch and water smooth in a small bowl immediately before adding; cornstarch settles while standing. Stir all the slurry into the hot beef and sauce. Cover and cook on HIGH, starting to check around 30 minutes; continue until the sauce is hot and thickened enough to coat the beef, allowing longer if still thin.

Serve: Use scallions, sesame seeds (if using), and cooked jasmine rice (if using): distribute the scallions over the beef and add the measured sesame seeds if wanted. Serve with the separately prepared rice. Rice cooking time is additional if it is not already ready.

recipes.keywords: Korean, spicy, sweet, savory, acidic, umami, comfort-food, slow-cook

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Mongolian Beef
recipes.description: Slice the flank steak across its visible muscle fibers, then distribute all the measured cornstarch over the slices. This is a shorter-cooking flank-steak recipe, distinct from the chuck-roast Korean beef.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/2 pounds flank steak thinly sliced against the grain
1/2 cup green onions cut into 1/2 inch pieces

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Use fully thawed flank steak kept refrigerated until preparation. Slice thinly against the grain. Check the cooker’s load instructions before starting; use a cooker suitable for the listed load.
Coat: Toss all the measured steak and cornstarch in a bowl until the slices are evenly coated. Transfer the coated steak and any remaining measured coating to the cooker.
Add sauce: Add all the sesame oil, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar and measured water. Stir to coat the meat, cover and start promptly.

Cook: Cover and cook on HIGH for 2–3 hours or LOW for 4–5 hours as planning ranges. Start with fully thawed beef. Check tenderness and that beef has reached at least 145°F / 63°C with three minutes rest before serving. The sauce should be thickened and the thin slices tender; continue as needed rather than rely only on the clock.
Finish: Stir in all the measured green onions, then divide among the listed portions and serve.

recipes.keywords: Chinese, slow-cook

recipes.name: Slow-Cooker Chicken Tortellini Soup
recipes.description: Chicken and spinach in a lightly creamy tomato broth, with cheese tortellini cooked separately for a reliable pasta finish.
recipeIngredient: 680 g boneless skinless chicken thighs, fully thawed, left whole
6 cups (1.44 liters) low-sodium chicken broth, divided
2 cans (14.5 oz / 411 g each) petite diced tomatoes, with juices
1/2 tsp fine salt, added gradually only if needed
140 g fresh spinach, washed, thick stems removed

recipeInstructions.text: Soften the base: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook onion about 5–7 minutes until softened. Add garlic and basil and stir about 30 seconds, then add tomato paste and cook another minute, stirring.
Disperse flour: Sprinkle flour over the mixture and stir for 1 minute. Gradually stir in 1 cup of the measured broth until the paste is smooth and pourable, scraping the bottom.
Load: Transfer the base to a 6-quart slow cooker. Add remaining measured broth, tomatoes and juices, pepper and fully thawed thighs. Stir gently, cover and start immediately.

Cook chicken: Cook on LOW about 4–5 hours or HIGH about 2–3 hours, until several thick thighs reach 165°F / 74°C and shred readily. Remove to a clean board, shred coarsely and return to the hot soup. During the last 20 minutes of the chicken cook, heat the separate pasta water.

Boil tortellini: Cook frozen tortellini in the boiling pasta water according to their package until seams are tender and centers are hot, meeting any stated filling-temperature requirement. Drain gently. Time this to finish near the soup's final stage.

Finish broth: With chicken fully cooked and returned, add spinach to the hot broth and stir until wilted, about 2–3 minutes. Turn off heat. Mix cream with a ladleful of broth, then stir it back into the pot with Parmesan. Taste and add salt only if needed. Avoid a prolonged boil after this finish.

Assemble: Divide tortellini among six large bowls, then ladle over chicken, spinach and broth. Serve promptly. For planned leftovers, cook only the tortellini portions needed and keep any cooked pasta separate from stored broth.

recipes.keywords: Italian-American, umami, rich, herbaceous, comfort-food, saute, slow-cook, boil

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Vegetable Korma
recipes.description: Soft cauliflower, carrots, green beans and peas in a coconut-and-almond curry, finished with a little yogurt for tang.
recipeIngredient: 900 g cauliflower florets, weighed after removing leaves and the tough core; cut into roughly 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm pieces
300 g carrots, weighed after trimming and peeling; cut into 1/4-inch / 6 mm half-moons
150 g onion, peeled and finely chopped
300 ml full-fat unsweetened canned coconut milk, stirred together before measuring
2 tbsp mild, salt-free Indian-style curry powder
2 tbsp finely ground almond meal or blanched almond flour, not defatted almond powder
1/2 tsp fine salt, reserved for the final seasoning; use only as needed
1/4 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional
125 g fresh green beans, weighed after trimming; cut into 1 1/2-inch / 4 cm lengths
1/4 cup (60 g) plain whole-milk yogurt, unstrained
1/4 cup (60 ml) hot water, reserved only if the sauce begins to catch before the vegetables soften

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare the vegetables: Wash the vegetables, trim and weigh them, then cut as listed. Put the carrots and onion in the bottom of the slow cooker, scatter over the garlic and add the cauliflower. Keep the prepared beans refrigerated. Leave the peas frozen and the yogurt chilled for now.

Coat and start cooking: Stir the coconut milk thoroughly before measuring 300 ml. Whisk it with the curry powder, garam masala, ground almonds, the first teaspoon of fine salt and optional pepper flakes. Pour over the vegetables and gently turn the cauliflower to coat it, leaving most carrots underneath. Cover and start on High immediately. Do not add the reserved water automatically; this is a coated vegetable curry, not a pot of submerged vegetables.

Check and add beans: After about 3 hours, check a carrot and a thick cauliflower stem with a small knife. When both are nearly tender, gently fold the green beans into the hot sauce, replace the lid and continue on High. Allow about 45–60 minutes total for the beans, beginning checks after 30–45 minutes so the peas can cook during the final part of that window. If the carrots are still distinctly hard at the first check, continue covered and check again in 20–30 minutes before adding the beans. Avoid frequent stirring that breaks up the florets.

Cook the peas and check the whole pot: When the beans are nearly tender, stir in the frozen peas. Cover and continue on High for about 10–15 minutes, until the peas are steaming hot throughout and all the vegetables are tender; follow any longer cooking requirement on the pea package. This final pea period overlaps the end of the bean cooking time. Expect roughly 3 3/4–5 hours total on High, with some cauliflower edges softening into the sauce. Stop when the vegetables are ready rather than keeping a fast batch cooking for five hours.

Hold briefly or finish: If dinner is running late, keep the fully cooked curry covered on Warm before adding the yogurt, checking that it stays at least 140°F / 60°C. Aim to serve within an hour for better vegetable texture. Warm holds cooked food and does not finish undercooked vegetables. When ready to serve, thicken a loose sauce before adding yogurt, as described in troubleshooting. Turn the cooker off and uncover for about 5 minutes, until active bubbling stops. Whisk a few spoonfuls of hot sauce into the yogurt in a bowl, then gently fold all of it back into the curry. Taste and add the reserved fine salt a pinch at a time, only as needed. The sauce should coat a spoon and the vegetables, with a little fine almond texture.
Serve: Divide among six bowls with rice or naan. The batch makes about 7–8 cups, enough for roughly 1 1/4 cups per person.

recipes.name: Slow Cooker Lentil Tortilla Soup
recipes.description: Dry red lentils soften and thicken this soup alongside fully cooked canned beans, corn and the onion-and-pepper base. Add optional cream near the end and choose toppings per bowl.
recipeIngredient: 1 tsp avocado oil or olive oil
1 jalapeño pepper, diced; reduce or omit for a milder soup
1 can (15 oz) tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes
1/2 cup salsa verde or another chosen salsa
1 can (15 oz) black beans, fully cooked canned beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, fully cooked canned beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup corn kernels, fresh, drained canned, or frozen; follow package preparation
3/4 cup dry red lentils, sorted and rinsed
half-and-half, to taste, instead of heavy cream, optional
cream cheese, to taste, instead of heavy cream, optional
black pepper, to taste after cooking
fresh lime juice or lime wedges, as wanted for finishing and serving
crushed tortilla chips, as wanted per bowl, optional
shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese, as wanted per bowl, optional
sliced or diced jalapeños, as wanted per bowl, optional
chopped red onion, as wanted per bowl, optional
pico de gallo, as wanted per bowl, optional
diced avocado, as wanted per bowl, optional
fresh cilantro, as wanted per bowl, optional
sour cream or Greek yogurt, as wanted per bowl, optional
additional vegetable broth or tomato sauce, a little at a time to loosen if wanted, optional
corn tortillas torn into pieces, as wanted to thicken near the finish, optional

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Check the cooker’s load instructions. Drain and rinse the measured canned black and pinto beans; do not replace them with dried beans in this route. Sort and rinse the dry red lentils and dice the vegetables. Choose salsa/jalapeño heat deliberately; for a milder soup, reduce or omit jalapeño/cayenne. Follow any frozen-corn package preparation directions.

Load the base: Stir onion, avocado oil or olive oil, bell pepper, jalapeño pepper, vegetable broth, tomato sauce or crushed tomatoes, salsa verde or another chosen salsa, tomato paste, black beans, pinto beans, corn kernels, dry red lentils, chili powder, garlic powder, ground cumin, and cayenne pepper together in the cooker, distributing the tomato paste. Keep dairy, finishing seasoning and toppings separate. The measured oil belongs to this loaded base; no preliminary sauté is required for the slow-cooker route.

Cook the lentils and vegetables: Cover and cook on HIGH for 4–6 hours or LOW for 7–8 hours as planning ranges. Check that the lentils are soft throughout without a chalky center and the vegetables are tender. Red lentils may break down and thicken the soup; they do not have to vanish completely. Continue covered if still firm, rather than judge only by thickness.

Finish and adjust: Use heavy cream (if using), half-and-half (if using), cream cheese (if using), salt, black pepper, additional vegetable broth or tomato sauce (if using), and corn tortillas torn into pieces (if using) as wanted. Choose one optional dairy finish near the end: use the measured heavy cream from its listed range (¼ cup or the fuller ½ cup option in the original batch), or replace it with half-and-half or cream cheese added gradually to taste. Warm the chosen dairy through and melt cream cheese fully. If loosening, add the extra broth or tomato sauce a little at a time; torn tortillas can thicken the soup. Warm through and taste before adding the finishing salt and pepper. For the existing smoother option, remove from heat and use an immersion blender only if its instructions allow hot soup, keeping the blade submerged to prevent splashing; leave some texture rather than promise a fixed pulse count.

Serve with chosen toppings: Use fresh lime juice or lime wedges, crushed tortilla chips (if using), shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese (if using), sliced or diced jalapeños (if using), chopped red onion (if using), pico de gallo (if using), diced avocado (if using), fresh cilantro (if using), and sour cream or Greek yogurt (if using). Taste and add lime juice at the finish if wanted, or serve wedges alongside. Divide the soup among the listed small portions, six at the original batch, and let each person choose toppings. For larger meal bowls, plan fewer portions and prepare accompaniments separately. Finished volume and bowl size are unmeasured. Extra jalapeño can stay on the side. Prepare avocado/lime/cilantro with clean utensils.

recipes.name: Smashed Cucumber Salad (Pai Huang Gua)
recipes.description: Cool, irregular cucumber pieces with garlic, vinegar, soy, and sesame. A short salt-and-drain step keeps the dressing from becoming diluted immediately.
recipeIngredient: 1 1/3 lbs (600 g) Persian or English cucumber, washed and ends trimmed
1 tsp vegan chili crisp, optional; check the label

recipeInstructions.text: Crack and cut: Set cucumbers on a stable board. If an English cucumber has a loose, watery seed core, halve it and scrape that part away. Cover with a clean towel to contain splashes and tap gently with a rolling pin until cracked. Cut into rough 1-inch pieces.

Salt and drain: Toss the pieces with the measured salt in a colander over a bowl. Let drain for 15 minutes, preferably chilled. Shake off the released liquid and gently blot the pieces; do not squeeze them into mush.
Mix dressing: While the cucumber drains, stir vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, garlic, and optional chili crisp together until the sugar dissolves.

Taste and toss: Taste a drained cucumber piece. If overly salty, rinse briefly and blot well, then begin with only half the dressing. Otherwise add the cucumber to the dressing and toss gently until coated. Taste and adjust the amount of dressing to suit the cucumber.
Finish: Fold in scallion and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Divide into four side portions and serve soon after dressing. Keep chilled if there will be a short delay.

recipes.name: Smoked Salmon Toast
recipes.description: Toast the bread until it is crisp enough to support the cream cheese and toppings. Spread the full measured cream cheese over the warm toast, then add cold smoked salmon in loose folds.
recipeIngredient: 2 slices Thick-Cut Sourdough or Pumpernickel Bread
2 tbsp Red Onion, very thinly sliced

recipeInstructions.text: Toast: Use cold-smoked salmon labeled ready-to-eat for uncooked serving; follow its refrigeration, opening and use-by instructions. Keep salmon cold while preparing the bread. Soften only the listed cream cheese needed for this batch. Rinse the dill, red onion and lemon under running water before cutting or juicing, and drain well. Toast all the bread until golden and firm enough to support the toppings, without scorching.
Spread: Divide all the listed cream cheese across the toast, spreading it gently to the edges.
Salmon: Divide all the salmon across the toast in loose folds. This preparation does not cook the salmon.
Top: Divide all the drained capers, sliced onion, dill and measured lemon juice over the toast. Add the black-pepper allowance to taste.
Finish: Use the optional everything-bagel seasoning allowance if desired.
Serve: Eat promptly after assembly, while the toast is crisp. Larger batches need more toaster cycles; hold the fish and dairy refrigerated rather than assembling early and leaving them warm.

recipes.name: Spanish Rice and Chickpeas
recipes.description: This Spanish-inspired rice dish draws from paella technique. Frying dry rice in onion-garlic oil for 3 minutes before adding liquid toasts the starch, creating distinct, individual grains rather than sticky clumps - a technique called socarrat in traditional paella.
recipeIngredient: 1 can (19 oz) Chickpeas, rinsed and drained

recipeInstructions.text: Foundation: In a large deep skillet, heat 2 tbsp oil. Sauté onion for 7 minutes cook until golden brown and softened. Add garlic, paprika, and oregano; sauté for 30-45 seconds until the spices bloom.
The Toast: Add the dry rice. Stir constantly for 3 minutes until the grains are coated in the red oil and smell nutty.
The Simmer: Stir in the tomatoes, chickpeas, and broth. Bring to a boil.
The Finish: Reduce heat to low. Cover tightly. Simmer for 20-22 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
The Steam Cycle: Remove from heat. Do not open the lid. Let sit for 6 minutes (mandatory for structure).
Finish: Fluff with a fork. If adding shrimp, nestle them into the rice during the final 5 minutes of simmering. If adding spinach, stir it in during the steam cycle.

recipes.name: Snickerdoodles
recipes.description: What separates a Snickerdoodle from a standard sugar cookie is Chemistry. The Cream of Tartar provides the signature tangy flavor and reacts with the baking soda to create a uniquely chewy, pillowy texture that prevents the cookie from becoming too crisp.
recipeIngredient: 2 tsp Cream of Tartar (The essential ingredient)

recipeInstructions.text: Cream: Beat the butter, 1 1/2 cups sugar, and eggs until very light and fluffy.
Sift: In a separate bowl, whisk together the flour, cream of tartar, baking soda, and salt.
Mix: Gradually add the dry ingredients to the butter mixture until just combined.
Chill: Refrigerate the dough for 30 minutes. This makes it easier to roll and prevents excessive spreading.
Roll: Shape dough into walnut-sized balls. Roll each ball in the cinnamon-sugar mixture until fully coated.
Bake: Place on a baking sheet 2 inches apart. Bake at 400°F for 8-10 minutes. The cookies should be set at the edges but still appear soft in the center.

recipes.name: Soba Noodles with Shiitakes & Tofu
recipes.description: Soba noodles are made from buckwheat, making them more delicate than wheat pasta. Rinsing them under cold running water for 1 minute immediately after boiling removes surface starch and prevents them from becoming gummy.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Soy Sauce + 1 tbsp Shaoxing Wine
2 tsp Toasted Sesame Oil (The complex flavor)

recipeInstructions.text: The Sauce: In a small bowl, whisk stock, soy sauce, wine, ginger, and garlic.
Blanch: Boil baby broccoli for 1 minute. Shock in ice water. Drain and pat bone-dry.
Boil Soba: Cook soba noodles for 4-5 minutes until al dente. Drain and rinse under cold water for 1 minute. Toss with 1 tsp sesame oil.
The Sear: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok until smoking. Sear tofu for 2 minutes until golden. Remove.
The Crunch: Add 1 tbsp oil and the red pepper flakes. Sauté shiitakes and scallions for 2 minutes. Add the blanched broccoli.
Bind: Add the noodles, tofu, and the stock mixture. Toss vigorously over high heat for 2 minutes until the liquid has emulsified into a glossy glaze.
Serve: Stir in the cilantro and sesame oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Soft Batch Chocolate Chip Cookies
recipes.description: Use the edge color to judge these soft cookies: remove them when the edges are just starting to brown and the centers have set while staying soft. This dough uses equal cup measures of brown and granulated sugar.

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare and dry mix: Start preheating the oven to 375°F. Line baking sheets with parchment and set out a cooling rack. Whisk the flour, baking soda, baking powder and sea salt together.
Cream: Beat the softened butter and both sugars until combined and light, about 2 minutes, scraping the bowl. Beat in the eggs and vanilla until evenly mixed.
Combine: Add the dry mixture just until no flour pockets remain, then distribute all the chocolate chips through the dough.
Shape: Roll about 2 tablespoons of dough into each ball and place 2 inches apart on the prepared sheets. Keep waiting dough covered and refrigerated; do not load dough onto a hot sheet.

Bake: Once the oven reaches 375°F, bake for 8–10 minutes per tray. Remove when the edges are just beginning to brown and the centers have set but remain soft. If the center is still liquid or raw-looking, continue baking and check again.

Cool: Rest on the sheet for about 2 minutes, then transfer carefully to a rack once the cookies hold together. Allow more pan time if they are too fragile to lift. Cool completely before packing. Repeat with the remaining dough on cooled sheets.

recipes.name: Soy Ginger Dipping Sauce
recipes.description: Soy sauce, rice vinegar and sesame oil form a 4:2:1 base by volume. Dissolve the sugar before adding finely grated ginger, garlic and green onion so each small dipping portion carries the same seasoning.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 tsp Chili Garlic Sauce or Sriracha (optional)

recipeInstructions.text: The Mix: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and sugar until sugar dissolves.
The Aromatics: Stir in grated ginger, minced garlic, and sliced green onion. Add chili sauce if you want heat.
The Rest: Let rest for 10 minutes to let flavors meld, or refrigerate for a longer wait. Taste and adjust seasoning - add more vinegar for tang or sugar to balance saltiness.

The Serve: Divide into small individual dipping dishes; keep the unused batch separate from sauce that has been dipped into. Refrigerate the unused sauce promptly at 40°F / 4°C or below and use within 3–4 days. Do not leave it out longer than 2 hours total, or 1 hour above 90°F / 32°C. Soy sauce and vinegar do not establish a shelf-stable mixture once fresh aromatics are added. Stir before serving; there is no need to warm the whole stored batch to room temperature.

recipes.name: Soy Sauce Butter Pasta with Shrimp and Shiitakes
recipes.description: Thin pasta with shrimp and browned shiitakes in a savory soy-butter sauce with wine, Parmesan and parsley.
recipeIngredient: 10 oz dry thin spaghetti or angel hair
8 oz raw shrimp, peeled and deveined, tails removed
8 oz fresh shiitake mushrooms, tough stems removed, caps thinly sliced
1 tbsp olive oil, for cooking shrimp
1/2 cup reserved pasta cooking water, use only as needed
Salt, for the pasta water and final seasoning only if needed
Water, a small splash if needed for sticking shallots

recipeInstructions.text: Prepare: Bring pasta water to a boil. Slice mushrooms, mince shallots and garlic, chop parsley and grate Parmesan. Pat shrimp dry. Salt the pasta water moderately; soy and cheese will season the finished dish.

Cook shrimp: Heat olive oil over medium-high. Cook shrimp in a single layer, about 1–2 minutes per side or as needed until firm, pearly and opaque through the center; a fine-tip thermometer inserted into a thick shrimp should read 145°F / 63°C. Transfer to a clean plate.

Cook mushrooms and aromatics: Reduce heat to medium. Add one-third of the butter and the shallots; cook about 3 minutes until beginning to soften. Add mushrooms and cook about 5–7 minutes, turning, until softened with some brown edges. Add garlic for the last 30–45 seconds. If the pan dries and shallots begin catching, loosen with a small splash of water rather than burning them.

Reduce and cook pasta: Add wine and simmer about 2–3 minutes until reduced by roughly half. Meanwhile cook pasta about 1 minute short of its package al dente time; for very quick angel hair, start it only when the mushrooms are ready. Reserve the listed pasta water before draining.

Coat: Add pasta and soy sauce and toss over low heat until the pasta is tender with a little bite, using a small splash of reserved water as needed. Turn off heat. Add the remaining two-thirds of the butter and toss until melted into the sauce, then fold in Parmesan, parsley, shrimp and their juices. Add further water only if the coating is tight.
Serve: Taste before adding salt; it may need none beyond the soy and cheese. Add black pepper and divide the pasta and shrimp evenly. Serve promptly.

recipes.name: Sun-Dried Tomato Cream Spaghetti
recipes.description: Use the listed tomato-jar oil and butter in the sauté, then reduce the broth before gently adding sour cream and Parmesan. Put the prepared fresh spinach in a clean heat-safe colander and drain the hot pasta carefully over it.
recipeIngredient: 5 oz Fresh baby spinach, rinsed under running water unless labeled prewashed or ready-to-eat; coarsely chopped and drained
1/2 cup Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, slivered; reserve jar oil separately
1 tbsp Oil from the sun-dried tomato jar
Water, as needed to boil pasta
Salt for pasta water, as desired, separate from measured sauce salt
Water for reheating, a little as needed for leftovers

recipeInstructions.text: Cook pasta: From Dry whole-wheat spaghetti, Water, and Salt for pasta water, season the water with its salt allowance and bring it to a boil; then add the spaghetti and cook according to its package until al dente.

Wilt washed spinach: Prepare Fresh baby spinach in a clean heat-safe colander with room for the cooked pasta. Set it securely above the sink so food cannot touch sink surfaces. Drain the hot pasta and water carefully over the spinach, keeping hands clear of steam; toss to wilt and drain thoroughly. If some leaves remain crisp, finish wilting them during the final warm toss.

Soften the sauce base: In the same emptied pasta pot, heat Oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes, Oil from the sun-dried tomato jar, Red onion, and Unsalted butter over medium heat, adding onion and tomatoes once the fats are warm. Stir about 3 minutes until onion softens; allow longer as needed.
Season: Add Garlic cloves, Crushed red pepper, Salt, and Ground black pepper and stir about 45 seconds until fragrant, without scorching garlic.

Reduce broth by observation: Add Low-sodium chicken broth and simmer, stirring, until roughly half the starting broth remains. Use the change in liquid level as the cue and allow longer as needed. Pot width, heat and batch size change evaporation.
Finish gently: Reduce heat to low and stir in Sour cream and Parmesan cheese until the cheese melts and the sauce is smooth; take the pot off the heat if it bubbles hard.

Coat pasta and spinach: Return the drained spaghetti and spinach to the sauce. Toss gently over low heat until hot, the spinach is wilted and sauce clings to the strands. Do not cook until every drop of sauce is absorbed or the bottom dries out.
Serve and reserve leftovers: Serve hot. The listed Water for reheating is only for reheating leftovers, not an extra dose during this first cooking.

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Tofu Meatballs
recipes.description: Vegetarian "meatballs" have been made with nuts and grains for centuries, though tofu-based versions became popular in the 1970s and 80s. The key to firm texture is pressing the tofu bone-dry, then binding it with ground walnuts and breadcrumbs.

recipeInstructions.text: Foundation: In a large skillet, sauté onion, carrot, pepper, and garlic in olive oil for 10 minutes cook until golden brown and softened. Let cool slightly.
The Base: In a massive bowl, crumble the pressed tofu with your hands until it looks like ground meat.
Emulsify: Add the eggs, breadcrumbs, walnuts, herbs, mustard, sesame oil, and soy sauce to the tofu.
Combine: Add the sautéed vegetables. Mix vigorously with your hands until a sticky, uniform dough forms.
Shape: Form into 1.5-inch balls. Arrange on an oiled baking sheet.
Bake: Bake at 350°F for 20-30 minutes, flipping once, until the exterior is deep brown and "Snappy."
Serve: Add the meatballs to your favorite Roasted Tomato Sauce and serve over Fresh Egg Pasta.

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Clams & Braised Greens
recipes.description: Spaghetti with clams is a classic Italian coastal dish, typically made with white wine and garlic. This version adds pureed roasted red peppers to the clam-steaming liquid for a thicker, more colorful sauce - a modern American twist.
recipeIngredient: 1 lb Swiss Chard or Collard Greens, chopped
1 Lemon, zested and juiced (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: Steaming: In a large pot, heat 1/4 cup oil. Sauté half the garlic for 30-45 seconds. Add clams and wine. Cover and boil for 5-7 minutes until clams open.
The Puree: Transfer opened clams to a plate. Strain the liquid into a blender. Add roasted peppers and pulse until smooth.
The Greens: Wipe the pot. Heat 1/4 cup oil. Sauté remaining garlic and chili flakes for 30-45 seconds. Add the chard in batches; sauté for 3 minutes until wilted.
Boil: Cook spaghetti until very al dente.
Bind: Pour the pepper broth into the greens. Add the hot pasta and the cold butter.
Emulsify: Toss vigorously over medium heat. Add lemon juice, zest, and Parmesan. Stir until the sauce is glossy.
Serve: Return clams to the pot to warm through. Serve in shallow bowls with plenty of extra Parmesan.

recipes.keywords: Italian, spicy, acidic, umami, rich, comfort-food, date-night, entertaining, weekend-project, saute, boil, steam, blend

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Clams
recipes.description: Spaghetti alle vongole is a classic from the Campania region (Naples and the Amalfi Coast), where fresh clams are abundant. In Italy, they use tiny vongole veraci that are sweet and delicate; American littleneck clams are larger but work beautifully.
recipeIngredient: 1 tbsp Fresh Lemon Juice (The Acid Balance)

recipeInstructions.text: The Purge: Soak clams in a bowl of cold salted water for 20 minutes. Drain and rinse.
Boil: Cook pasta in a massive pot of salted water until very al dente (2 minutes less than directions).
Foundation: In a large wide skillet, heat olive oil over medium. Sauté garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute until fragrant but not brown.
The Crunch: Add the vermouth and the clams. Cover tightly. Shake the pan vigorously for 2-3 minutes until all clams have popped open.
Bind: Add the hot drained pasta directly to the skillet. Increase heat to medium-high.
Emulsify: Toss vigorously for 1 minute until the pasta has absorbed the clam liquor and the oil has emulsified into a glossy film.
Finish: Stir in the lemon juice and half the parsley.
Serve: Garnish with the remaining parsley and a final drizzle of oil. Discard any clams that did not open.

recipes.name: Spanish Rice with Chorizo and Chickpeas
recipes.description: Chorizo seasons the vegetables before the rice bakes in broth with chickpeas and raisins. This covered method uses Arborio rice.
recipeIngredient: 1/2 lb Spanish-style chorizo, cured, sliced into rounds; check product label
1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced
1/4 cup dry sherry or white wine
hot water, a little only if rice is firm and pan is dry

recipeInstructions.text: Render chorizo: Use Spanish-style chorizo for this stage. Preheat the oven to 400°F. Use a roomy oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven with a tight-fitting lid that holds the rice, full broth, chickpeas and chorizo with room to stir and without a brim-full load. Read the Spanish chorizo label: cured does not always mean ready-to-eat. Prepare any cook-before-eating pork sausage according to its package, checking 160°F / 71°C, before using this rendering route. A raw poultry product needs 165°F / 74°C and is not an assumed equivalent. Render the prepared rounds over medium heat until crisped and their red fat is released; remove to a clean plate. Keep the rendered fat for the current main route.

Soften vegetables: Add red bell pepper, yellow onion, and garlic cloves to the chorizo fat. Cook about 8–10 minutes until softened, stirring and lowering heat if garlic browns too quickly. Use chorizo that releases enough fat to cook the vegetables without catching. For the olive-oil version, choose the complete uncovered variation below.
Add paste and spices: Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika (pimentón), and saffron threads (if using) and cook about 1 minute until fragrant without scorching.
Coat rice: Add Arborio rice and stir about 2 minutes to coat the grains in the spiced fat.
Add wine: Add dry sherry or white wine, scrape the bottom and let bubble about 1 minute.
Bring to a boil: Add chickpeas, chicken broth, and raisins and all the reserved chorizo. Bring to a boil before moving to the oven.

Bake covered: Use hot water for this stage. Cover tightly and bake at 400°F about 20–25 minutes, then check absorbed liquid and a tender rice center. If the center is firm and the pan is dry, add a little hot water, cover and continue; if wet and firm, keep cooking before adding more liquid. Do not replace Arborio directly with Bomba or Calasparra or use the source variant’s uncovered method here.

Rest and serve: Rest off heat, covered, for 10 minutes, then fluff gently and divide among the listed portions. Allow about 80 minutes overall including 20 minutes preparation, roughly 50 minutes rendering/sautéing/heating/baking and the rest; extra batches or firm rice extend the estimate. Larger quantities need sufficient pan space or separate original-size pans, not proportional oven times.

recipes.name: Spatchcocked Roast Chicken (The Best Method)
recipes.description: Removing the backbone and flattening the chicken exposes more skin and can shorten roasting time. Breast and leg meat still differ in thickness, so check each required temperature site rather than assuming they finish together.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbsp Fresh Rosemary or Thyme (or 1 tbsp dried)
1 tbsp Olive Oil (for greasing the pan)
1/2 cup Water or Chicken Stock (for the pan)
Fresh Lemon (for serving, cut into wedges)
Fleur de Sel or Finishing Salt (optional, for the table)
Salt and black pepper, to taste for the optional pan sauce

recipeInstructions.text: Remove the backbone: Keep the fully thawed chicken cold until preparation. Place it breast-side down, with the backbone facing up. Cut along both sides of the backbone with sturdy kitchen shears or a suitable knife, and remove it. If saving it for stock, promptly refrigerate in a covered raw-poultry container for use within 1–2 days, or freeze it; stock can also be made without a backbone.

Flatten: Turn the chicken skin-side up and press firmly on the breastbone to flatten it. Use a board large enough to contain the bird and keep raw juices away from ready-to-eat food. Pat the skin dry with paper towels and discard the towels.

Apply the whole rub: Mix all the kosher salt, black pepper, garlic, herbs and optional paprika with all the listed rub olive oil. Rub all of this paste over the bird, including under gently loosened breast skin, the legs and the skin surface. The original batch uses 2 tbsp fresh rosemary or thyme, or its distinct 1 tbsp dried option; scale the chosen option proportionally. Keep the full rub quantity.

Optional refrigerated seasoning: Roast directly after preparation, or refrigerate the seasoned bird on a rimmed tray for 30–60 minutes or up to 8 hours. Leave it uncovered for drying only where it is protected from contamination and cannot drip onto other food. Do not use a counter warm-up as a substitute for refrigerator thawing.

Preheat and prepare the pan: Preheat the oven to 475°F with the rack in the lower-middle position. Use a rimmed metal pan or roasting pan rated for 475°F. If using an optional baking stone or steel, heat and position it according to its manufacturer’s instructions. Grease the roasting pan with all the 1 tbsp olive oil listed for the pan, and add all the ½ cup water or stock. These are original-batch amounts, scaled with the ingredients; pan geometry is a separate choice.

Roast skin-side up: Place the flattened bird skin-side up with room around it. Roast at 475°F and start checking after 35–45 minutes; actual birds and ovens can take longer. For larger batches, roast additional original-size 4–5 lb birds in enough rated pans with airflow, checking each separately. Ingredient scaling does not turn a fractional bird or larger bird into the same geometry or multiply the roasting clock.

Check all sites: Measure the thickest part of each breast and the innermost thighs and wings without touching bone. Every checked site must reach at least 165°F / 74°C before removal. Recheck cooler areas after further roasting; the timer and skin color do not establish doneness. If using the optional convection finish for skin color, follow the oven instructions and watch closely while the bird is still cooking; stop once all required sites reach 165°F rather than adding a mandatory 10–15 minutes after it is done.

Rest and make optional sauce: Transfer the cooked bird to a clean board with a lip and rest 10 minutes before carving. For the optional pan sauce, put the roasting pan on a burner only if its manufacturer permits stovetop use; otherwise carefully transfer the hot drippings and scraped browned bits into a saucepan. Heat the poultry-contact liquid to 165°F, then simmer, starting with 2–3 minutes, until slightly reduced. Taste with a clean spoon and use the separate optional sauce salt and pepper allowances if needed. Strain if desired.

Carve and serve: Carve into two leg quarters and two breast portions, or into smaller pieces as preferred. Serve with all the lemon wedges and the optional finishing salt, and spoon over the optional cooked pan sauce. Four portions are a planning yield for the original 4–5 lb bird, with sides; bird size and appetite vary. Refrigerate promptly in shallow covered containers at 40°F or below, within 2 hours (1 hour above 90°F). Use within 3–4 days, or freeze portions for later. Reheat hot leftovers to 165°F throughout. For reheated optional pan sauce, USDA also recommends bringing sauces and gravies to a rolling boil. Stir for even heating and avoid prolonged boiling that over-reduces the jus. These handling limits do not promise unchanged texture.
